articles.titulo: Rapid spread of nutritional Wolbachia symbionts across and within solitary bee species
articles.autores: Preuß L, Tischer M, … Gerth M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Maternally inherited, intracellular bacteria of the genus Wolbachia are extremely widespread among arthropods. Their evolutionary success is owed to frequent host shifts and rapid subsequent spread within host populations, often facilitated by Wolbachia-induced reproductive manipulations. Theory suggests that often, Wolbachia spread may also be explained by fitness benefits, the nature of which have remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that Wolbachia's success in many solitary bee species is strongly associated with the presence of a gene cassette enabling Wolbachia to synthesize biotin (vitamin B7). This ability is absent from almost all other Wolbachia strains but common among bee-associated strains. We show that Wolbachia occurs in up to 60% of all bee species and that strains carrying this rare genomic element have independently spread into numerous bee hosts recently. We further demonstrate that the presence of the biotin operon is associated with specialized diets in several bee species, suggesting a previously overlooked nutritional role of Wolbachia in this group of important pollinators. Overall, our results suggest that nutritional benefits provided by symbionts may represent a more widespread and important mechanism by which reproductive manipulators spread into new host species than previously appreciated.

articles.autores: Duron O (1 autor)

articles.titulo: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
articles.autores: Amato C, Graham R, … Wood W (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

articles.titulo: Epidemiology and Associated Risk Factors of Malaria Infection in Loka Abaya District, Sidama Region, Ethiopia
articles.autores: Melese M, Woldesenbet A, … Birmeka M (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Despite continuous efforts to manage malaria, it remains a deadly disease, particularly common in low-lying areas of Ethiopia. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence, trends, and risk factors associated with malaria infection in Loka Abaya district, Sidama region, Ethiopia.
A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out using house-to-house visits from April to June 2023. A total of 186 febrile patients were chosen using systematic random sampling. Those above the age of 18 were included in the study. Five health facilities and one primary hospital in the district provided retrospective data. A systematic questionnaire and microscopic analysis of blood films were used to gather data. The blood samples were evaluated in Hantate primary hospital. Univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the associated factors of malaria infection. Variables with p value less than 5% were considered statistically significant.
Of 34,613 suspected patients tested for malaria over the previous 5 years, 26.2% were positive. The lowest rate recorded at 20.3% in 2018, whereas 2020 was the highest rate at 30.1%. Among them, 47.4% and 52.6% were females and males, respectively. Age groups from 5 to 14 covered up 21.6%, adults aged over 15 take up to 57.2%, and children under age 5 were 21.2%. The infection distribution was 58.8% for Plasmodium falciparum, 38.8% for Plasmodium vivax, and 2.4% mixed infections. The highest rate of infection was recorded during September to November. Cross-sectional parasitological survey showed that 18.3% of individuals were infected. The identified risk of contracting malaria was significant for individuals who were closer to mosquito breeding sites (AOR, 13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), did not use a mosquito net while sleeping (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), did not use indoor residual spraying in the previous 12 months (AOR,13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), used a window without a screen (AOR, 2.78.3, 95% CI, 1.03-13.86, p < 0.02), used a thatched roof (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), and did not know how malaria is transmitted (AOR, 4.3, 95% CI, 2.36-22.6, p < 0.04).
The study indicated that malaria remains a health issue in the Loko Abaya district. Several factors, including low income, wall openings, proximity to mosquito breeding sites, lack of indoor residual spraying, and lack of bed net use, were important predictors of malaria.

articles.titulo: Viral Infections and Dysregulation of Neurotrophin Signaling: Potential impact in the Central Nervous System
articles.autores: Miteva MT, Protto V, … De Chiara G (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Viral infections can perturb neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system, with important consequences for neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, and long-term cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, and neurotrophin-4, mediate their actions primarily through tropomyosin receptor kinases (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC) and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR), activating intracellular pathways such as PI3K-AKT, MAPK-ERK, and PLC-γ. Growing evidence suggests that both neurotropic/neuroinvasive and non-classically neurotropic viruses can interfere with these pathways through multiple mechanisms, including those elicited by direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking required for sustained Trk signaling, and inflammation-driven alterations in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. This review summarizes current knowledge on how selected viruses affect neurotrophin availability and downstream signaling in experimental models and clinical settings. Specifically, the review focuses on: 1) viruses capable of establishing life-long latent or persistent infection such as i) herpesviruses (herpes simplex virus-1; Epstein Barr virus; human cytomegalovirus), and ii) human immunodeficiency virus; 2) other neurotropic viruses driving peculiar neuropathological profiles, such West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Zika virus, and Borna disease virus 1; 3) respiratory viruses, such as influenza A virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. For each virus group, we discuss convergent pathogenic mechanisms and receptor-level interference with neurotrophin signaling. We further highlight some gaps in current knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the underexplored role of viral co-infections and reactivations, and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation.

articles.titulo: TRIM5α, TRIM56 and TRIM69 differentially regulate dengue virus 2 infection through selective NS2B3-mediated antagonism
articles.autores: Paswan RR, Martins L, … Berthoux L (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus (DENV) is a major mosquito-borne human pathogen. Understanding the mechanisms of cellular resistance to the infection is vital to develop novel therapeutic tools. Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins contribute to antiviral innate immunity through direct restriction of viral replication and regulation of antiviral signaling, but current knowledge on DENV targeting by TRIM proteins remains preliminary. Previously, TRIM56 was found to inhibit DENV, whereas reports on whether TRIM69 is a DENV restriction factor are conflicting. Surprisingly, the broad-spectrum viral restriction factor TRIM5 was proposed to restrict tick-borne but not mosquito-borne flaviviruses. Here, we investigated the effects of TRIM5, TRIM56, and TRIM69 on DENV serotype 2 (DENV2) infection. Overexpression experiments showed that TRIM5 and TRIM56 restrict DENV2, whereas TRIM69 enhances it. Consistently, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated loss-of-function showed that knocking out TRIM5 or TRIM56 increases infection, while TRIM69 knockout decreases it. Restriction correlated with reduced viral RNA and viral protein levels in TRIM5- and TRIM56-expressing cells. Virus-free experiments showed that TRIM56 downregulates the DENV2 protease complex NS2B3 levels. Reciprocally, DENV2 NS2B3 reduced TRIM56 and TRIM69 abundance independently of protease activity. RING domain-mutated TRIM56 retained partial antiviral activity and the ability to reduce NS2B3 levels, and TRIM56-NS2B3 reciprocal downmodulation effects were not counteracted by proteasomal or lysosomal inhibition. Together, these findings establish TRIM5 as a DENV2 restriction factor, reveal TRIM69 as a positive factor in DENV2 infection, suggest that TRIM5? and TRIM56 inhibit DENV2 through distinct mechanisms, and hint at proteasome-independent TRIM56-NS2B3 reciprocal downmodulation.

articles.titulo: Loss of macrodomain catalytic activity modulates Chikungunya virus
articles.autores: Bardossy ES, Bergmann L, … Saleh MC (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Viral macrodomains are promising antiviral targets that counteract host ADP-ribosylation-mediated antiviral responses in mammals. However, their role in dual-host viruses within the mosquito vector remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the role of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) nsP3 macrodomain catalytic activity by mutating the active-site asparagine 24 (N24). N24 mutant viruses rapidly selected for compensatory second-site mutations at aspartate 31 (D31) in mammalian Vero cells, while interferon-competent human cells favored reversion at position 24 instead, suggesting adaptive responses to macrodomain functional impairment. Catalytically inactive double-mutant viruses replicated poorly in interferon-competent human cells but comparably to wild-type in mosquito cells. In Aedes mosquitoes in vivo, macrodomain mutations modulated CHIKV replication and infectivity in a mutation-specific manner: one mutant reduced them while another enhanced them. Biochemical and structural analyses confirmed that these phenotypes arise in the context of a catalytically inactive macrodomain that retains ADP-ribose binding capacity, with D31 mutations lining the substrate exit path. These findings demonstrate that macrodomain catalytic activity modulates CHIKV dissemination and transmission potential in Aedes mosquitoes, revealing fundamental differences in host-dependent evolutionary advantage for a catalytically inactive viral enzyme.

articles.titulo: Unconventional modulation of Na1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain
articles.autores: Zhou X, Wang H, … Liu Z (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Nav channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from Lychas mucronatus. LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Nav1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNav1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSDII) and the extracellular loop III (ECLIII) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3-S4II loop and displaces S0/S3II helices to trap VSDII within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSDII conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSDII trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECLIII engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECLIII region underlie the prominent species- and isoform-dependent activities of the toxin toward insect and mammalian Nav channels. Our study provides a structural basis for the dual-action mechanisms of β-scorpion toxins on Nav channels and presents a structural framework for understanding toxin binding, channel gating modulation, ecological adaptation, and rational drug design.

articles.titulo: Online extraction and preconcentration system employing a mini-column packed with 4-(2-thiazolylazo)-resorcinol-coated CoFe2O4 nanoparticles for the determination of lead in water samples by F AAS

articles.titulo: A "ready to move in" osteoporosis bone regeneration material
articles.autores: Deng S, Zhao C, … Li D (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The repair of osteoporotic bone defects remains challenging because of the hostile pathological microenvironment-resembling "barren soil"-characterized by excessive oxidative stress and persistent inflammation, which impair cell survival and tissue regeneration. To address this problem, we developed a "fertile soil" implant system as a ready-to-use platform for osteoporotic bone regeneration. It consists of: (1) a three-dimensional (3D) -printed β-tricalcium phosphate/gelatin methacryloyl (β-TCP/GelMA) composite scaffold as a structural "soil matrix," and (2) a Kaempferol-loaded ZIF-8 metal organic framework as an "intelligent nutrient bank" that responsively releases zinc ions and Kaempferol in acidic osteoporotic conditions.In vitro, the implant promoted a shift in macrophage polarisation from a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype towards a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. Mechanistic studies showed that this immunomodulatory effect was associated with improved mitochondrial function and reduced mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) accumulation, accompanied by suppression of the cGAS-STING-TBK1-NF-κB signaling pathway. The implant reversed inflammation-induced metabolic reprogramming in macrophages by reducing glycolytic activity and restoring oxidative phosphorylation, thereby favouring the re-establishment of immune homeostasis. In parallel, the implant directly enhanced the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells and inhibited osteoclastogenesis, helping to restore the balance of bone remodelling. Conditioned-medium experiments further demonstrated that scaffold-mediated macrophage reprogramming established a pro-regenerative microenvironment that indirectly promoted osteogenesis and restrained osteoclast formation. In osteoporotic bone defect models, implantation enhanced new bone formation, improved trabecular microarchitecture, tissue integration, and vascularisation, and reduced local inflammation.In summary, this "ready-to-move in" osteoporotic bone repair system remodels the hostile microenvironment through immunomodulation and direct cell regulation, providing a "fertile soil" that may enhance bone defect repair under osteoporotic conditions.

articles.titulo: Lymphatic filariasis-associated lymphedema: pathogenesis, diagnosis, management, and global elimination
articles.autores: Narahari SR, Rajkumar P, … Murugaiyan J (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: SUMMARYFilarial lymphedema (FL), a chronic consequence of lymphatic filariasis, represents one of the most neglected manifestations of helminth infection, despite affecting an estimated 120 million individuals across tropical and subtropical regions. More than 40 million people live with irreversible limb or genital disfigurement, accompanied by lifelong pain, disability, psychological distress, and social stigma. Unlike other causes of lymphedema, FL arises from sustained host-parasite interactions, in which prolonged immune modulation, microbial persistence, and secondary infections drive progressive lymphatic damage. Disease transmission and early pathology often remain clinically silent for years, allowing lymphatic injury to accumulate before overt swelling becomes apparent. Although global elimination efforts have reduced transmission, individuals with established FL remain largely neglected, highlighting a critical disconnect between parasite control and morbidity management. Current interventions are limited to hygiene-based care, infection control, and conservative limb management; no vaccine or curative therapy exists for established lymphatic failure. Diagnostic approaches primarily capture infection status rather than ongoing immune-mediated tissue damage, constraining disease staging, monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation in resource-limited settings. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the immunopathogenesis of FL, emphasizing the roles of chronic inflammation, genetics, immune dysregulation, microbial translocation, and lymphatic adipose tissue remodeling in disease persistence. We highlight emerging diagnostic biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and integrative management strategies, and outline critical gaps that hinder effective morbidity reduction. Advancing stage-specific diagnostic approaches and exploring intervention mechanisms will be essential to improve quality of life for affected individuals and achieve meaningful, sustainable elimination of lymphatic filariasis-associated morbidity.

articles.titulo: T/NK-cell remodeling and IFN-responsive myeloid activation delineate immunometabolic risk profiles in chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease
articles.autores: Cao Y, Zhou Z, … Zhang W (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease (CAEBV) is a rare EBV-associated T/NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by persistent viral infection, systemic inflammation, and highly variable clinical courses. Patients may develop HLH-like hyperinflammation, severe organ involvement, lymphoma transformation, or death, yet current assessment does not fully explain why patients with similar viral burden follow divergent trajectories.
We integrated PBMC single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from healthy controls and CAEBV samples with a retrospective cohort of 130 independent CAEBV patients to connect cellular immune remodeling with clinically measurable features.
Single-cell analysis identified T/NK remodeling toward cytotoxic, exhaustion-associated, senescence-associated, and metabolically altered states, accompanied by IFN-responsive, antigen-presenting myeloid programs. Ligand-receptor and receiver-side analyses prioritized candidate IFNγ-associated T/NK-to-myeloid communication within this IFN-responsive program, linking NK and CD8+ T-cell states with myeloid inflammatory activation. Guided by these findings, we mapped inflammatory, metabolic, coagulation, and lymphocyte-subset variables into a biology-informed clinical immunometabolic index reflecting inflammatory cytokine activation, metabolic stress, and adaptive immune contraction. Internally defined index strata were associated with increasing CAEBV+HLH, death, and severe-disease burden. Unsupervised clinical mapping further identified three exploratory but interpretable immunometabolic patterns, including immune-metabolically preserved, intermediate immune-contraction, and IFNγ-high immunometabolic high-risk, with distinct immune-cell, inflammatory, metabolic, and outcome profiles.
Together, these findings organize CAEBV heterogeneity around linked T/NK remodeling, myeloid activation, and systemic immunometabolic stress. This single-cell-informed clinical-pattern map complements EBV-DNA and organ-size assessment and supports prospective validation of clinically measurable, mechanism-guided monitoring and intervention strategies.

articles.titulo: Recent Developments in Sulfonamide-Based Anti-Malarial Agents: Structure-Activity Relationships and Future Perspectives
articles.autores: Kong SH, Chauhan S, … Qin HL (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Despite tremendous advancements in prevention and treatment, malaria continues to be one of the deadliest infectious illnesses in the world and a persistent public health concern. The critical need to find new chemotherapeutic drugs with better efficacy, selectivity, and resistance profiles is highlighted by the widespread rise of resistance to traditional anti-malarial drugs. Due to their exceptional structural adaptability, advantageous pharmacokinetic characteristics, and capacity to modulate several biological targets involved in the Plasmodium life cycle, sulfonamide-based compounds have garnered significant attention in anti-malarial drug discovery among the various classes of bioactive molecules. Many derivatives with strong action against drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant strains of Plasmodium falciparum have been produced via structural modifications of the sulfonamide pharmacophore. All things considered, this review offers insightful information about the medicinal chemistry of sulfonamide derivatives and a strategic framework for the logical development of novel anti-malarial treatments.

articles.titulo: Saponins and Sapogenins in Inflammation Therapeutics: Glycosylation-Dependent Mechanisms, Pharmacokinetics and Advanced Delivery Solutions
articles.autores: Qin M, Fu Y, … Gao X (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Saponins and their aglycones, the sapogenins, are the bioactive constituents of medicinal herbs such as Panax ginseng and Astragalus membranaceus, and they act on inflammation at several levels at once. The canonical nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome cascades are the best-replicated entry points, and beyond them these compounds modify non-coding RNA networks and post-translational regulation and reshape immuno-metabolic circuits by suppressing glycolytic enzymes and engaging AMPK-dependent energy sensing. Whether a given activity belongs to the glycoside or to the aglycone is often unclear, because orally administered glycosides are extensively deglycosylated by the intestinal microbiota, and this review therefore organises the evidence by glycosylation status and annotates every compound accordingly. Translation is constrained by poor aqueous solubility, low and variable bioavailability, structural instability, and dose-dependent toxicity, and stimulus-responsive nanocarriers, exosome-based systems, and microbiota-aware pharmacokinetic modelling are the most credible routes past these barriers. The mechanistic picture that emerges is coherent but still provisional, and progress now depends less on further pathway catalogues than on experiments that establish direct target engagement and on pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic data obtained in human-relevant models.

articles.titulo: Integrated metabolomics reveals nervonic acid-associated immunometabolic
articles.autores: Xu Y, Xu D, … Qin L (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits profound metabolic heterogeneity, yet the functional lipid metabolites driving tumor progression and immune microenvironment remodeling remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to construct a metabolomic atlas of HCC and identify clinically relevant metabolic vulnerabilities.
Untargeted metabolomic profiling was performed in 91 paired HCC and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Integrated metabolomic, transcriptomic, clinicopathological, and immune analyses characterized metabolic heterogeneity. Nervonic acid was evaluated in HCC cells, immunocompetent and immunodeficient mouse models, and knockdown and rescue experiments targeting ATP citrate lyase (ACLY).
HCC showed extensive metabolic remodeling with limited metabolite-gene concordance. Clustering identified four metabolomic subtypes. The high-risk subtype MS1 exhibited poor prognosis, pronounced very-long-chain fatty acid remodeling, and immunosuppressive features. Nervonic acid, a very-long-chain monounsaturated fatty acid, was enriched in MS1, increased in HCC tissues, and associated with unfavorable survival. It promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth. In immunocompetent models, nervonic acid reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and increased M2-like macrophage enrichment. Exploratory CD8 depletion suggested attenuation of the nervonic acid-associated tumor growth increment. Coordinated lipid remodeling included altered free fatty acid composition, enhanced fatty acid uptake, increased cholesterol abundance, and changes in membrane lipid order. Nervonic acid induced an ACLY-centered lipogenic program; in HCC cells, ACLY knockdown attenuated malignant phenotypes and lipid accumulation, and ACLY rescue restored these responses.
Nervonic acid marks an aggressive HCC subtype with distinct immune features. Knockdown and rescue in HCC cells implicate ACLY in lipid remodeling. The prognostic value of tumor nervonic acid requires independent validation.

articles.titulo: Understanding Nonreacting Substrate Analogs as Potential Scaffolds for Inhibitor Design Against Mycobacterium tuberculosis Cystathionine β-Synthase
articles.autores: Polepalli S, Roy A, … Dutta S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mycobacterium tuberculosis cystathionine beta-synthase (MtbCBS), a pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme, regulates sulfur metabolism and redox homeostasis, making it a model enzyme for inhibition studies and to understand scaffold behavior. Amino acids remains as an attractive scaffold for designing novel inhibitors having reduced cytotoxicity and improved properties for cellular uptake. This study integrates computational, biophysical, and structural approaches to provide for a potential scaffold that could be further modified to inhibit MtbCBS. Structure-based sequence alignment of CBS homologs identified seven conserved polar/charged regions critical for PLP-substrate interactions. Molecular docking of polar substrate analogs (threonine, histidine, glutamic acid, and arginine) at the conserved active site revealed distinct binding modes for histidine, glutamic acid, and arginine. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated persistent binding of histidine, stabilized by hydrophobic interactions relative to other analogs. Experimental studies revealed histidine's ability to form stable external aldimine adducts, modulating enzyme thermostability (ΔTm), akin to known reacting substrates. Finally, cryo-EM-based structural studies revealed two classes of MtbCBS, one with extra density suggesting the noncovalently bound histidine and the unbound WT MtbCBS maintaining internal aldimine. This suggests that exploration of the chemical modification space of the histidine moiety might provide us with a potential inhibitor against MtbCBS and enzymes of the RTS pathway.

articles.titulo: Case report: A worm's eye view: Fatal intraocular Dirofilaria immitis in a domestic cat from Georgia, USA
articles.autores: Jones H, Yared K, … Yabsley MJ (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dirofilaria immitis (canine heartworm) is a mosquito-transmitted nematode for which the domestic cat (Felis catus) is an aberrant host. Feline infections typically involve low worm burdens, unisex or developmentally arrested specimens, absent or transient microfilaremia, and unreliable antigen serology. Ectopic larval migration to the ocular anterior chamber is rarely reported. We describe a fatal case of intraocular D. immitis in a 6-year-old male neutered indoor/outdoor domestic shorthair from Walton County, Georgia, USA. The cat presented to a local veterinary hospital with lethargy, hyporexia, and an owner-observed organism in the right eye (OD); examination revealed anterior chamber opacity, and a presumptive diagnosis of ophthalmomyiasis interna likely due to a Cuterebra species. Prior to referral, the cat received selamectin/sarolaner (Revolution® Plus), epsiprantel (Cestex), and a rabies vaccine. At the referral center, the cat developed recurrent seizure-like episodes and died overnight despite supportive care. A SNAP Feline Triple Test (IDEXX) was negative for heartworm antigen, FeLV antigen, and FIV antibody. Post-mortem enucleation of OD revealed a single nematode (10.74 cm) within the anterior chamber. The worm was morphologically consistent with Dirofilaria and was confirmed to be D. immitis by sequence analysis of the COI and 18S rDNA gene targets. This case highlights the limitations of feline heartworm testing, initial clinical misidentification, morphologic limitations in aberrant host-tissue combinations, and the importance of pre-treatment microfilaremia assessment.

articles.titulo: Endoplasmic reticulum stress promotes ferroptosis in ventilator-induced lung injury by promoting HRD1-dependent GPX4 ubiquitination via the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway
articles.autores: Jiang Y, Ling M, … Ye L (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is a serious complication of mechanical ventilation. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) has been implicated in regulating ferroptosis, and we previously linked ERS to VILI-associated inflammation. However, how ERS mechanistically drives ferroptosis during VILI remains unclear.
C57BL/6J mice were pretreated with the IRE1α RNase inhibitor STF-083010 or the HRD1 inhibitor LS102 before high tidal volume (HTV) ventilation for 4 h. Mouse lung epithelial cells were transfected with sgGpx4, siHrd1, or corresponding controls and then subjected to 20% cyclic stretch (CS) with or without ferrostatin-1. Lung injury was assessed by H&E staining, wet/dry ratio, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) protein and cell counts. Inflammation was quantified by ELISA and qRT-PCR. Ferroptosis was evaluated by transmission electron microscopy and measurement of malondialdehyde (MDA), Fe²⁺, and reactive oxygen species (ROS). Protein abundance and localization were analyzed by immunoblotting and immunohistochemistry. HRD1/GPX4 interaction and GPX4 ubiquitination were examined by co-immunoprecipitation and ubiquitination assays.
HTV ventilation induced severe lung injury with ferroptotic features and reduced SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression. STF-083010 alleviated lung injury and inflammation, suppressed ferroptosis, and restored SLC7A11/GPX4, while attenuating HRD1 upregulation. GPX4 deletion markedly increased susceptibility to CS-induced cell death and was not rescued by ferrostatin-1. Mechanistically, HRD1 interacted with GPX4 and promoted its ubiquitination and degradation under injurious ventilation. HRD1 knockdown preserved GPX4 stability and reduced CS-induced ferroptosis. Consistently, LS102 mitigated ferroptosis, lung injury, and inflammatory responses in vivo.
ERS promotes ferroptosis in VILI through an IRE1α/XBP1-HRD1 axis that drives ubiquitin-mediated GPX4 degradation. Targeting HRD1 or upstream IRE1α RNase activity preserves GPX4, limits ferroptosis, and attenuates VILI, supporting this pathway as a therapeutic target.

articles.titulo: Urolithin A mitigates behavioural and synaptic deficits associated with epilepsy
articles.autores: Mishra S, Verma V, … Nongthomba U (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The persistence of drug-resistant epilepsy highlights the need for new therapies that target novel mechanisms while maintaining synaptic strength and minimizing side effects. Small molecules of natural origin with anti-epileptogenic potential can influence altered synaptic deficits and reducing seizure threshold, offering a strategy to restore cellular energy homeostasis and slow the progression of epilepsy and associated comorbidities.
We used a combination of approaches including behavioural assays, immunostaining and electrophysiological recordings to study the synaptic contributions to reduced seizure-threshold in both Drosophila and mouse models of epilepsy. In addition, we used affinity-purification with synthesized beads specific for our small molecule to identify its cellular partners.
We found that administration of Urolithin-A (UA), a small molecule of natural origin, mitigated behavioural and synaptic dysfunctions under chemically and genetically induced epileptic conditions in Drosophila. Additionally, chronic treatment with UA attenuated the altered single-cell and network synaptic transmission in PTZ-induced chronic kindling of mice. However, UA exerted no seizure-suppressive effects in in vitro epileptic conditions, suggesting the absence of acute anti-epileptic effects. In addition, we identified the direct interactor of UA as the complex of tubulin dimer and VDAC1. Molecular docking analyses also predicted that urolithin A interacts with VDAC1. Consistent with the neuroprotective role of VDAC1 downregulation reported in previous studies, neuron-specific knockdown of VDAC1 in Drosophila phenocopied the effects of UA.
Collectively, our data show that UA exerts disease-modifying anti-epileptic effects in both Drosophila and mouse models with VDAC1 identified as a critical functional mediator; however, direct functional modulation of VDAC1 and associated partners by UA will require further experimental validation. These findings provide the blueprint for future drug discovery targeting VDAC1-dependent pathways.

articles.titulo: Targeting endoplasmic reticulum-associated glucose-6-phosphate metabolism sensitizes glioblastoma to chemoradiotherapy
articles.autores: Vitale F, Losacco S, … Marini C (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Antioxidant capacity is a major determinant of glioblastoma (GBM) resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) and radiotherapy (RT). Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) metabolism, regulated by hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) and glucose-6-phosphatase 3 (G6PC3), sustains ER-linked nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) production and thereby supports glutathione (GSH)-dependent redox buffering; however, its clinical relevance and therapeutic exploitability in GBM remain poorly defined.
Public GBM transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to assess the prognostic relevance of H6PD and G6PC3 expression. U87 GBM cells were treated with TMZ and fractionated RT, with or without transient chlorogenic acid (CGA) exposure administered prior to irradiation. CGA was selected as a modulator of ER G6P metabolism due to its capability to inhibit G6P transport across the reticular membrane. Cell survival, oxidative stress, intracellular redox balance, and metabolic activity were evaluated.
High expression of H6PD and G6PC3 predicted poorer patient survival, with H6PD retaining independent prognostic significance, identifying ER-associated G6P/NADPH metabolism as an adverse metabolic signature in GBM. Transient CGA exposure significantly potentiated TMZ + RT cytotoxicity, increasing membrane damage and reducing cell survival after irradiation. CGA induced an early increase in oxidative stress followed by delayed depletion of reduced NADPH and GSH, amplifying redox imbalance under combinedchemoradiotherapy. Metabolic analyses indicated enhanced glycolytic engagement without further stimulation of mitochondrial respiration.
ER-associated NADPH metabolism represents a clinically relevant determinant of redox resilience in GBM, with H6PD emerging as an independent prognostic marker within this metabolic axis. In a U87 proof-of-concept model, transient, timing-based metabolic priming with CGA disrupts antioxidant buffering and amplifies oxidative vulnerability during chemoradiotherapy, thereby enhancing tumor in vitro. These findings provide a strong mechanistic and translational rationale for targeting ER-linked redox metabolism as an adjuvant strategy to improve GBM responsiveness to standard chemoradiotherapy.

articles.titulo: Validating regional insect pest phenology forecasts using published developmental data
articles.autores: San-Segundo Molina D, Stefanescu C, Morales-Castilla I (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: BACKGROUND: Crop losses caused by insect pests are expected to increase under global warming, highlighting the need for accurate phenology forecasts to support integrated pest management (IPM). Arthropod pests, as ectotherms, exhibit temperature-dependent development and phenology that can be described by thermal performance curves (TPCs). For decades, developmental models have predicted pest emergence through thermal accumulation approaches, yet it remains unclear to what extent experimentally derived development models can accurately predict field phenology across spatial and temporal scales. Here, we evaluate whether developmental TPCs and linear degree-day models fitted from published experimental data can predict large-scale pest phenology under a rate-summation approach. RESULTS: We compiled published developmental data for the widespread crucifer pest Pieris rapae and fitted several TPCs and linear degree-day models. Model predictions were validated against independent long-term monitoring data from the Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme for mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. Published experimental data accurately predicted large-scale pest emergence, with prediction errors generally below one week. However, predictive performance depended strongly on the spatial and temporal scale considered, with model rankings changing according to the scale and temperature resolution used. CONCLUSION: Published experimental thermal biology data can accurately predict regional insect pest phenology when developmental models are selected according to the intended forecasting scale. These findings provide practical guidance for improving pest alert systems and other decision-support tools, while demonstrating how decades of experimental research can be translated into operational phenology forecasting.

articles.titulo: Differential modulation of host cell Serine and Arginine-Rich (SR) protein and apoptotic factor BCL-2
articles.autores: Mandal D (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Regulation of alternative splicing (AS) is important in controlling cellular functions. More than 95% human genes are alternatively spliced and AS is regulated by close to 100 splicing factors. Line of evidences suggest that virus infections alter the AS pattern of numerous host genes. In this study we have investigated Chandipura virus (CHPV) induced alteration of host cell SR protein gene expressions and determined if these changes have any effect on apoptotic factor BCL-2 levels. CHPV is a negative stranded RNA virus which causes fever, brain encephalitis and death among young children with a case-fatality rate of 50%. Few studies were done in past to understand the roles of host factors in CHPV pathogenesis and no study was done on virus induced changes in AS. Our study showed that there is a down-regulation of SR proteins SRp55 and SRp75 expression levels significantly decreased in the CHPV infected Vero E6 cells compared to uninfected cells. For a comparison, we also looked at the levels of SRp55 and SRp75 in dengue virus (DENV) infected cells. Our results showed that SRp75 levels is unchanged whereas SRp55 levels increased in DENV infected cells. We have also determined the levels of large and small splice variants of apoptotic gene BCL-2 to find out possible correlation between the altered splicing factor expressions and virus infected cell death via apoptosis. Our data indicates that in CHPV infected cells, BCL-2 large splice variant expressions decreased as compared to uninfected cells. This is the first study of CHPV mediated alteration of splicing factor expressions and these results warrant further study with other viruses to better understand the global changes in host splicing events, cell survival, host immune response during virus infection.

articles.titulo: A DNA barcode reference library of the mosquitoes of Iran: insights into species boundaries and evolutionary relationships
articles.autores: Norouzi B, Oshaghi MA, … Azari-Hamidian S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) are the most significant arthropods in public health. In Iran, 73 species across eight genera are known to occur, including 35 species and seven genera in Guilan Province. Due to challenges in morphological identification, this study evaluated the utility of DNA barcoding for mosquito species identification in Iran. Sampling was conducted from 2022 to 2024 across five counties in Guilan Province. Species were initially identified morphologically, followed by molecular analysis using the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene. Sequences were compared with reference data in GenBank, and phylogenetic trees were constructed using the Maximum Likelihood method. A total of 13151 adult mosquitoes were collected and morphologically identified including 17 species, with COI sequences generated for 15 species, 10 of which are newly barcoded from Iran. Phylogenetic analysis of the genera and species of Aedes, Anopheles and Culex was performed. The analysis revealed a close genetic relationship between Cx. pipiens and Cx. quinquefasciatus (p-distance = 0.019); however, diagnostic nucleotide positions successfully differentiated Iranian specimens. Within the genus Anopheles, An. hyrcanus and An. pseudopictus formed closely related clades (p-distance = 0.023), underscoring the challenging debates of the Hyrcanus Group with the COI gene and the need for complementary markers. Overall, COI-based phylogeny supported the traditional classification of the genera, subgenera and species of Iranian mosquitoes. DNA barcoding clearly displayed the geographical and phylogenetic affinities of Iranian species and served as a suitable tool for tracing distributional routes, whether natural or anthropogenic.

articles.titulo: The targeted modulation of the inflammatory response to alleviate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via a biomimetic allicin delivery platform
articles.autores: Gao Y, Yin J, … Li X (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Reperfusion strategies, the clinical standard for acute myocardial infarction, inevitably trigger severe myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury. The acute phase of MI/R causes dual imbalance: excessive cardiomyocyte apoptosis and impaired macrophage phagocytosis. This pathological mechanism, the aberrant accumulation of apoptotic cells, triggers secondary necrosis, thereby serving as a critical driver of inflammatory storm and maladaptive cardiac remodeling. However, there is currently no targeted anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategy for this early pathological mechanism. To break these treatment limitations, we engineered a biomimetic stem cell membrane-camouflaged, allicin-loaded metal-organic framework nanoplatform (MOF-Al@NVs). Leveraging the nanovesicles' ischemic homing capability and the MOF's high drug-loading capacity and acidic degradation properties, this platform enables rapid, targeted delivery and release of allicin (which has anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory effects) within the ischemic myocardium. In vitro and in vivo investigations demonstrate that MOF-Al@NVs efficiently rescue dying cardiomyocytes by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) bursts and blocking the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Concurrently, the platform re-orchestrates cardio-immune homeostasis by cooperatively upregulating the efferocytic receptor axis (TREM2/MERTK) on macrophages via activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade. This dual coordinative effect accelerates the clearance of cellular debris and promotes the anti-inflammatory phenotypic transition from M1 to M2 macrophages, thereby attenuating the inflammatory storm, ameliorating acute-phase MI/R-induced cardiac dysfunction, and improving short-term prognosis. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics, integrated with multi-omics, confirms that MOF-Al@NVs effectively restore spatial immunometabolic homeostasis in the early infarct border zone. This biomimetic nanoplatform offers a promising strategy for targeted anti-inflammatory therapy in early MI/R injury.

articles.titulo: Cell-informed host-response profiling distinguishes neutrophil-like and PLA2G7-associated immunometabolic axes in systemic infection
articles.autores: Gu Y, Yu Y, … Ding S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Whole-blood host-response signatures can distinguish infection-positive from infection-negative systemic inflammation, but their signal combines changes in leucocyte composition with regulation within cells. We asked whether a retrospectively selected and subsequently fixed blood transcriptomic framework could relate candidate transcripts to granulocyte-associated and monocyte/macrophage-associated expression contexts rather than serve as another stand-alone diagnostic product.
A 12-gene framework was retrospectively derived from four contrasts across three studies (444 contrast-level observations; 443 unique arrays) and subsequently fixed for external evaluation using a single-sample transcriptome-rank score. Performance was examined separately across cohorts with different specimens, age groups and comparators. Transcript-score sensitivity analyses, donor-level whole-blood single-cell pseudobulk and cell-line qRT-PCR were used to assess candidate localization and cell-line expression-context concordance. Cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation were included as exploratory genetic context.
In the closest target-context cohort, GSE134347, the fixed score achieved an AUROC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.764-0.889) for sepsis versus non-infectious critical illness. Performance was lower in pediatric day-1 SIRS comparisons, indicating dependence on population and comparator context. Adjustment for alternative neutrophil-associated transcript scores produced a marker-dependent ordering, with SMPDL3A among the most attenuated and PLA2G7 among the least attenuated candidates; no candidate remained FDR-significant in the primary six-gene family. Donor-level single-cell analysis and qRT-PCR supported a monocyte/macrophage context for PLA2G7 and granulocyte-like localization of the diagnostic immune markers. Exploratory Mendelian randomisation did not support a susceptibility effect for the testable immunometabolism-associated candidates, and the HLA-DRB1 regional signal lacked evidence of a shared variant under single-variant colocalisation assumptions.
This study provides an auditable, cell-informed framework that relates granulocyte-associated transcription to PLA2G7-associated monocyte/macrophage localization within the whole-blood infection response. The framework is intended for biological prioritisation, and it defines testable candidates for future studies.

articles.titulo: Exploring Neem Phytochemicals as Potential Inhibitors of Trehalose-6-Phosphate Synthase
articles.autores: Bella-Omunagbe M, Adebayo AH, … Chinedu SN (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Increasing resistance to insecticides and their accompanying off-target effects call for the development of biodegradable insecticides with selective metabolism-based targets. Anopheles gambiae trehalose-6-phosphate synthase (AgTPS), the first enzyme in the trehalose metabolic pathway, is essential for key developmental processes in the organism but absent in vertebrates, making it an attractive insecticidal target. This study aims to evaluate the inhibitory potential of neem-derived compounds against AgTPS using in silico methods. The 3D structure was predicted, and its active-site residues were identified based on conserved TPS homologues. A library of 275 neem phytochemicals was compiled from IMPPAT and Dr Duke's databases, alongside known substrates and inhibitors. Molecular docking was performed using AutoDock Vina at the glucose-6-phosphate (G6P), UDP-glucose (UDPG), and combined binding sites. Protein-ligand interactions were analysed using LigPlot+, while insecticide-likeness and ADMET properties were evaluated using QEPest and pkCSM. Several neem-derived compounds exhibited stronger binding affinities to AgTPS than the natural substrates across all binding sites. Tannic acid showed a high binding affinity across all binding sites, with a range of -11.3 to -12.1 kcal/mol, showing interactions with conserved catalytic residues. Other compounds, including 1-cinnamoylmelianolone, nimbilin, 6-acetylnimbandiol, and 7-deacetyl-7-oxogedunin, also demonstrated strong and consistent binding, frequently outperforming known TPS inhibitors. ADMET analysis revealed that tannic acid possessed unfavourable pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles. In contrast, limonoids such as 1-cinnamoylmelianolone and nimbilin displayed a more favourable balance between potency, insecticide-likeness, and predicted safety. Neem-derived phytochemicals show significant potential as inhibitors of AgTPS, supporting AgTPS as a promising target for selective mosquito control. While tannic acid demonstrates strong binding affinity, its poor drug-likeness limits practical application. The limonoids, such as 1-cinnamoylmelianolone and nimbilin, thus emerge as more viable lead candidates. These findings provide molecular insights into neem's insecticidal activity and support further experimental validation for vector control applications.

articles.titulo: A Male-Specific Immunometabolic Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell Transcriptomic Signature in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
articles.autores: Bura A, Noh MY, … Kim SH (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) demonstrates well-recognized sex-related differences in incidence, age at onset, and clinical features, but the biological mechanisms underlying this heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Peripheral immune mechanisms have been proposed as potential contributors.
We performed sex-stratified transcriptomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from a clinically well-characterized cohort of 60 participants: 15 male ALS participants, 15 female ALS participants, and 30 sex-matched healthy controls. Differential gene expression and pathway enrichment were analyzed, followed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) validation and correlation with clinical parameters, including plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels.
PBMCs from male ALS participants exhibited extensive transcriptional alterations, with coordinated downregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation pathways and upregulation of the extracellular matrix and inflammatory signaling. In contrast, PBMCs from female ALS participants showed minimal and less-consistent transcriptomic changes. These findings were validated by qPCR. Notably, changes in mitochondrial and immune-related transcripts were not associated with the plasma NfL level, disease progression rate, or clinical severity.
This study has identified a male-specific peripheral immunometabolic transcriptomic signature in ALS that is independent of established biomarkers of neurodegeneration. These findings may help to explain sex-related differences in disease pathogenesis and clinical presentation, and they underscore the importance of considering sex as an influential biological variable in ALS.

articles.titulo: Vitamin D3 Attenuates Experimental Colitis with PPARγ-associated regulation of macrophage lipid accumulation
articles.autores: Lu J, Hu Q, … Zhang J (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) and its active metabolite calcitriol exert immunoregulatory effects, but their macrophage metabolic actions during intestinal inflammation remain incompletely defined. We examined oral vitamin D3 in experimental colitis and explored vitamin D receptor (VDR)-associated peroxisome proliferator-activated receptorγ (PPARγ) involvement in macrophage responses to calcitriol. In a dextran sulfate sodium-induced mouse model, oral vitamin D3 reduced disease activity, colonic injury, macrophage infiltration and inflammatory cytokine production, and partly normalized selected serum lipid parameters, with dose-related increases in serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25-(OH)2D3). In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages, calcitriol lowered IL-6 and IL-12/23p40, increased IL-10 and TGF-β, reduced M1-like/M2-like macrophage ratio, and decreased intracellular triglyceride, cholesterol and lipid-droplet accumulation. Oral vitamin D3 restored colonic PPARγ expression, PPARγ knockdown attenuated the effects of calcitriol on cytokine release and lipid accumulation. Murine colon microarray data linked myeloid Pparg deficiency to higher expression of inflammatory genes and lower expression of selected lipid-metabolism genes. Human UC macrophages with detectable VDR transcripts had higher PPARγ-target and lipid-metabolism module scores. These findings support anti-colitic effects of oral vitamin D3 and suggest VDR-associated PPARγ involvement in the macrophage response to calcitriol.

articles.titulo: Draper-mediated efferocytosis by Drosophila imaginal disc epithelial cells clears cellular debris during regeneration
articles.autores: Mathure SA, Maghinang K, … Smith-Bolton R (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Regeneration is a coordinated process that restores tissue integrity following damage. Following injury, tissues initiate early responses, including epithelial remodeling and clearance of cellular debris. However, how debris clearance is coordinated with regenerative growth to ensure efficient tissue repair remains poorly understood. To address how early damage responses, particularly debris clearance, are coordinated with regeneration, we used a genetic ablation system in Drosophila wing imaginal discs to induce apoptosis in the pouch region. Targeted damage generates cellular debris that localizes to both the apical and basal sides of the epithelium. We show that most cellular debris is cleared within two days after damage, although some debris persists apical to the regenerating epithelium. Our data indicate that residual debris consists of a heterogeneous mixture of cellular components, suggesting no preferential targeting by the clearance machinery. Notably, immune cells are not recruited to the damaged tissue due to restricted access by an intact basement membrane. Instead, we discovered that debris clearance is mediated by efferocytosis, whereby neighboring hinge epithelial cells activate JNK signaling and engulf debris via lysosomal formation. Reduction of efferocytosis by mutation of the phagocytic receptor Draper delays debris removal and increases debris persistence. This impairment has a modest impact on regeneration, as measured by adult wing size. Together, our results reveal a previously unappreciated role for epithelial cells as non-professional phagocytes for debris clearance during regeneration.

articles.titulo: Innate immune memory of past hepatic injury promotes ischemic cardiac inflammation.
articles.autores: Zhang S, Zhang Y, … Zhan Z (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hepatic disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular diseases, leading to worsened prognosis. However, the mechanisms of inter-organ communication and the impact of historical hepatic injury await elucidation. Here, we report that the historical liver damage triggers long-term reprogramming of the innate immune system, biases hematopoietic stem cells differentiation toward myeloid fate, and aggravates inflammatory injury during myocardial infarction (MI). This immune memory is transmissible in bone marrow transplantation and parabiosis models. Injured liver-derived palmitic acid is responsible for the metabolic rewiring of cardiac macrophages during memory formation and establishes persistent epigenetic signatures in the transcriptional regulatory regions of hepatic injury-associated memory ("HepMem") genes containing the activator protein-1 motif. The HepMem monocyte/macrophages are expanded in liver-injured mice and potentiate the post-MI inflammatory cascades and adverse cardiac remodeling. Therefore, the innate immune memory links the past hepatic injury with MI, guiding the promising therapeutic approaches for the inflammatory cardiac comorbidities.
articles.resumo_pt_v6: Lesão hepática antiga reprograma de forma duradoura o sistema imune inato, desvia a diferenciação de células-tronco hematopoéticas para a linhagem mieloide e agrava a inflamação no infarto do miocárdio; a memória é transferível por transplante de medula e parabiose. O ácido palmítico do fígado lesado rearranja o metabolismo dos macrófagos cardíacos e fixa marcas epigenéticas em genes com motivo AP-1 (assinatura HepMem).

articles.titulo: S1P1-mediated metabolic reprogramming promotes astrocytic mitochondrial dysfunction via histone lactylation in subarachnoid hemorrhage.
articles.autores: Zhang L, Pang J, … Jiang Y (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central event in the pathophysiology of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that mitochondrial function is vulnerable to metabolic alterations. While the role of neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction in SAH pathology is firmly established, less is known about mitochondrial dysfunction in astrocytes, the key regulators of brain homeostasis, especially its potential regulation by metabolic reprogramming after SAH. Hence, we aimed to define the metabolic reprogramming and its potential role in mitochondrial dysfunction in astrocytes post SAH.
We established in vivo and in vitro models of SAH. Glucose uptake, lactate production, and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) measurement were employed to profile the metabolic alterations in astrocytes after SAH. ATP level, mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, oxygen consumption rate (OCR), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were applied to assess the structural and functional integrity of astrocytic mitochondria. Lentivirus carrying short hairpin RNA (shRNA) and adeno-associated virus (AAV) were used to knockdown sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1P1) to explore the role of S1P1 in astrocytic metabolism switch. Additionally, ChIP-qPCR was utilized to elucidate the epigenetic mechanism of S1P1-mediated metabolic reprogramming in regulating the mitochondrial function of astrocytes post SAH.
We provided new evidence that astrocytes underwent metabolic switch with enhanced glycolysis in the early stage of SAH which was mediated by S1P1 through mammalian target of rapamycin/hypoxia-inducible factor 1ɑ (mTOR/HIF1ɑ) activation. Notably, enhanced glycolysis-derived lactate accumulation in astrocytes promoted mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, we found that the enhanced glycolysis facilitated mitochondrial fission factor (MFF) transcription by elevated H3K9la, resulting in excessive mitochondrial fission and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction in the early stage of SAH.
Our findings demonstrate that S1P1-driven glycolysis enhancement promotes astrocytic mitochondrial dysfunction via histone lactylation and provide a potential therapeutic strategy for SAH.

articles.titulo: Circadian Gating of Neuroimmune Memory: A Shared Persistence-and-Gating Hypothesis for Chronic Pain, Depression, and Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction.
articles.autores: Song X, Feng M, … Luan Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic pain, depression, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction provide distinct settings in which inflammatory responses and persistent vulnerability may intersect. Evidence for specific cytokine, synaptic, and microglial mechanisms differs across these conditions and does not establish a single comorbidity mechanism. We examine whether circadian context influences the formation or later expression of neuroimmune memory. Circadian regulation of inflammatory responses and innate immune memory each have experimental support, while their coupling in disease-relevant microglia remains unresolved. Human BCG vaccination studies provide a peripheral timing-and-training precedent, which cannot be assumed to operate in the brain. We distinguish immune memory from ongoing inflammation, neuronal chromatin regulation, and sustained symptoms, and separate cell-autonomous microglial timing from rhythmic environmental inputs. The framework generates distinct tests of imprint formation, maintenance, recall, and reversal. A convincing test requires a resolved first challenge, control of initial inflammatory exposure and recall phase, and cell-resolved molecular measurements coupled to altered secondary-response function. Failure to reverse an established imprint would not exclude a role for timing during its formation. Perioperative studies offer a defined exposure but must distinguish delirium from longer-term cognitive decline. This evidence-calibrated hypothesis specifies what must be demonstrated before circadian interventions can be linked to prevention or modification of neuroimmune memory.

articles.titulo: Microglial SUCNR1 senses metabolic state to regulate whole-body homeostasis.
articles.autores: Repollés-de-Dalmau M, Asimakidou E, … Fernández-Veledo S (31 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Peripheral metabolic cues influence central energy control through incompletely understood pathways. Succinate, a Krebs cycle-derived metabolite elevated during nutrient excess and inflammation, signals via the G protein-coupled receptor SUCNR1; however, its central nervous system (CNS) role remains poorly defined. Using integrated mouse, human, and cellular approaches, we investigated how the succinate-SUCNR1 axis regulates peripheral energy balance in normal and high-fat diet states. Cerebrospinal fluid succinate dynamics were dissociated from plasma levels yet reflected systemic metabolic status, supporting a distinct central succinate compartment dynamically associated with peripheral metabolic state. Multi-omic and functional analyses identified microglia as the principal CNS targets of succinate, characterized by high SUCNR1 expression and functional dependence on this signaling pathway. Microglial Sucnr1 deletion altered peripheral energy regulation, conferring resistance to diet-induced metabolic stress while disrupting physiological energy balance, including leptin responsiveness and fasting-refeeding behavior. These findings establish the microglial succinate-SUCNR1 axis as a key immuno-metabolic mechanism linking systemic metabolic signals to the hypothalamic control of energy homeostasis.

A deleção de Sucnr1 na microglia deu resistência ao estresse metabólico por dieta rica em gordura e alterou a resposta à leptina e o comportamento de jejum/realimentação.

articles.titulo: When location makes oxidative stress lethal: mitoxyperilysis at the immunometabolic stress interface.
articles.autores: Zhang Y, Xia XP, Zhao L (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mitoxyperilysis is a proposed lytic death pathway in which oxidatively damaged mitochondria become membrane-lethal when retained at the plasma membrane. In founding models, TLR stimulation plus carbon restriction engaged MYD88-dependent innate signalling and BAX/BAK1/BID-dependent mitochondrial oxidative stress, while mTORC2-RhoA-actin remodelling prolonged peripheral mitochondrial retention. Mitoxyperiosis denotes prolonged mitochondria-plasma membrane association and localised oxidative membrane injury, whereas mitoxyperilysis denotes the subsequent plasma membrane rupture and lytic cell death. In these models, NINJ1 contributed to terminal rupture and LDH/HMGB1 release without being required for cell death. The damaging oxidant, physical tether, and mechanism linking local injury to membrane failure remain unresolved. Sepsis may reproduce upstream metabolic-redox conditions, but direct evidence for the complete spatial sequence in patient-derived cells is lacking. This review separates founding-model findings from disease-relevant observations and untested steps.

Os autores dizem que oxidante, ancoragem e ligação entre dano local e falha de membrana seguem sem resolução.

articles.titulo: Cytosolic and Mitochondrial CaImaging in Drosophila Dopaminergic Neurons.
articles.autores: Inoshita T, Imai Y (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The ATP-producing organelle, mitochondrion, controls cellular or synaptic Ca2+ concentrations through temporal uptake of Ca2+ outside of the mitochondria. Although intracellular Ca2+ influx occurs during neuronal activity, a persistently higher concentration of intracellular Ca2+ is neurotoxic. Healthy mitochondria ensure rapid Ca2+ uptake, which is necessary for proper neuronal activity. Mitochondrial Ca2+ buffering activity decreases in aged or sick neurons. In this chapter, we will introduce our protocol for evaluating Ca2+ buffering activity through the mitochondria during neuronal activity of dopaminergic neurons.

articles.titulo: Structural basis of CO2 valence coding in Drosophila
articles.autores: Javorski D et al. (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In the olfactory system, glomerular sensory channels of single receptor identity support reliable odor recognition for appropriate approach or avoidance behaviors. For many olfactory stimuli, the assigned sensory value is innate but weighted by the internal state and previous experiences. How context-dependent modulation of innate valence coding supports distinct behavioral responses is poorly understood. Here we show that CO2 sensory information in Drosophila, intrinsically aversive but modified by attractive food signals, diverges from the canonical glomerular channel already in the antennal lobe via the polarized local interneuron LN23. LN23 relays sensory input via an extraglomerular CO2 pathway and manipulation of LN23 activity revealed a dominant role in CO2-induced avoidance behavior. The extraglomerular CO2 pathway projects to the posterior lateral protocerebrum (PLP) adjacent to the canonical Lateral Horn (LH) olfactory processing center and segregates into anatomically distinct valence channels. Connectome data together with functional characterization showed the convergence of parallel CO2 channels onto two interconnected 3rd order neurons which integrate additional sensory modalities via distinct mechanisms: while the glomerular CO2 pathway converge with food relay neurons onto separated dendritic domains of the PD5 interneuron in the LH, the extraglomerular pathways integrating CO2 information with antennal humidity and temperature modalities establish antagonistic inputs onto the PLP interneuron PV9. This early anatomical divergence of a defined olfactory channel followed by separated multimodal integration provides a structural basis for context-dependent valence coding and appropriate behavioral responses.

articles.titulo: Analysis of Dopaminergic Functions in Drosophila.
articles.autores: Inoshita T, Takemoto D, Imai Y (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dopaminergic (DA) neurons regulate various physiological functions, including motor function, emotion, learning, sleep, and arousal. Degeneration of DA neurons in the substantia nigra of the midbrain causes motor disturbance in Parkinson's disease (PD). Studies on familial PD have revealed that a subset of PD genes encode proteins that regulate mitochondrial function and synaptic dynamics. Drosophila is a powerful model of PD, whereby genetic interactions of PD genes with well-conserved cellular signaling can be evaluated. Morphological changes in mitochondria, along with dysfunction and degeneration of DA neurons, have been reported in many studies using Drosophila PD models. In this chapter, we will describe imaging methods to visualize mitochondria in DA neurons and to evaluate spontaneous neural activity of DA neurons in the Drosophila brain.

articles.titulo: Neuronal activity regulates glycolysis to sculpt synaptic transmission
articles.autores: Theisen EK et al. (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Neuronal computation imposes rapid, localized changes in energy consumption, yet how energy production is regulated at such fine spatiotemporal scales is incompletely understood. Using two photon imaging of neuronal activity and energy metabolism in Drosophila , we show that neurons recruit glycolysis in less than a second, with cell-type and subcellular specificity. This coupling scales with neuronal activity and is regulated by AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Activity-induced glycolysis is tightly correlated with presynaptic sites in cholinergic neurons, and is required for cholinergic but not glutamatergic neurotransmission. In cholinergic neurons, glycolysis supports both energetic demand and acetylcholine biosynthesis, with ATP citrate lyase linking these functions by both activating acetylcholine biosynthesis and disinhibiting glycolytic flux. These findings establish glycolysis as a previously unrecognized regulator of cell-type specific computation.

articles.titulo: Rhodopsin 7 is an ancestral non-canonical photoreceptor that shapes light-responsive behavior.
articles.autores: Kirsch V, Reinhard N, … Senthilan PR (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Animals rely on light not only for vision but also to adapt behavior to their environment through non-image-forming pathways. In Drosophila, most rhodopsins mediate retinal image formation, but Rhodopsin 7 (RH7) is widely expressed in the brain and optic lobe, acting as a non-canonical light sensor reminiscent of mammalian melanopsin. We combined expression mapping, behavioral assays, and phylogenetic comparisons to investigate its function. RH7 detects temporal changes in luminance, guiding rapid behavioral responses, and regulating daily activity patterns. Flies lacking RH7 are less active during the dark phase, while strains with constitutively active RH7 show increased activity. Phylogenetic analyses suggest that RH7 is an ancient rhodopsin present across panarthropods, representing an intermediate between G protein-coupled receptors and specialized rhodopsins, highlighting a key step in the evolution of non-visual light perception. These findings show that RH7 functions as a melanopsin-like sensor, shaping behavior, and illuminating the origins of light detection.

articles.titulo: Corpora amylacea and synaptic organization in the human brain analyzed by volume electron microscopy.
articles.autores: Cano-Astorga N, Merchan-Perez A, DeFelipe J (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The presence of corpora amylacea in the brain is a frequent finding in normal aging and in a broad spectrum of neurological disorders, yet the significance of these deposits for the organization of human cortical circuits remains unclear. Here, we combined complementary light and electron microscopy approaches to analyze temporal lobe epilepsy biopsy specimens with and without corpora amylacea. Samples containing corpora amylacea showed marked alterations in synaptic circuit microorganization, which were not restricted to areas of corpora amylacea accumulation but extended throughout the cortical tissue. These changes were characterized by neuronal loss, gliosis, reduced synaptic density, an increased proportion of inhibitory synapses, and larger synapses. Integration of these structural findings with clinical data from the same patients further supports the view that corpora amylacea are associated with disease-related pathological processes. Together, these findings provide a basis for understanding the potential significance of corpora amylacea in human brain circuit dysfunction and may help to inform future research studies focusing on disease mechanisms.

articles.titulo: A short embedding protocol for diagnostic electron microscopy: long-term implementation and diagnostic outcomes in a high-volume clinical series.
articles.autores: Zhou H, Zhou XJJ (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epoxy resin polymerization is a lengthy step in tissue preparation for transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We evaluated whether reducing the polymerization step alone to 40 minutes at 120 °C, with upstream processing unchanged, could maintain diagnostic quality. The protocol has been the sole routine method in a high-volume, accredited clinical TEM laboratory for more than 10 years. Among more than 30,000 consecutive cases, no embedding-related diagnostic inadequacy was identified in consultant pathologist sign-out records. In a prospective, blinded, split-specimen comparison of renal biopsies, both pathologists scored 4 or 5 on every feature for both methods. Nearly all scores were at the upper end of the scale, indicating comparable performance but not establishing statistical equivalence. Glomerular basement membrane thickness was closely similar (mean difference -12.7 nm, ~4%), within measurement variability and below diagnostic detection thresholds. Because curing behavior depends on the resin formulation and oven conditions, local validation is required before implementation.

articles.titulo: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development.
articles.autores: Wang X, Zeng J, … Zhang R (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission.

Perturbar os microtúbulos e trocar a isoforma de hemoglobina indicou que essa associação é necessária para organizar os SPMT e para a maturação do gametócito.

articles.titulo: Thermodynamic, Kinetic, and Structural Basis of Polyspecificity in the Malaria Sugar Transporter PfHT1
articles.autores: Paul A et al. (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum relies on the polyspecific sugar transporter PfHT1 for survival in diverse nutrient environments, making the molecular basis of its polyspecificity a potential avenue for antimalarial drug discovery. However, the structural, thermodynamic and kinetic basis of the emergence of polyspecificity in membrane transporters are not established in literature. Despite advances in AI for protein engineering, the design of selective/promiscuous membrane transporter proteins remains challenging as it requires connecting substrate recognition to the energetics of the transport cycle. Here, we examine the molecular origins of polyspecificity in PfHT1 transporter using molecular dynamics simulations of substrate transport and experimental validation of the key residues that tune specificity. From a structural viewpoint, we hypothesize that polyspecific membrane transporter contains flexible structural elements that could reshape the binding pocket in a substrate-dependent manner. For PfHT1, the cracking of the extracellular helix TM7b allows flexible reshaping of the binding pocket similar to the promiscuous enzymes. The thermodynamic signature of polyspecificity emerges in the form of the substrate dependent stabilization of transport-competent states. From a kinetic perspective, this stabilization asymmetrically alters transition kinetics and channels the flux through diverse conformational pathways that facilitate the conformational transitions from outward to inward facing states. To investigate the contribution of the underlying interaction network to sugar specificity, we used graph-attention learning to prioritize mutant transporters with distinct substrate preferences. Distinct glucose- and fructose-dependent growth phenotypes identify positions with differential effects on sugar utilization, providing functional evidence relevant to substrate specificity within the polyspecific transporter. Together, these findings support a mechanism in which structural, thermodynamic and kinetics observables connect polyspecificity to conformational energetics, kinetics, and structural plasticity.

articles.titulo: The heteromeric Plasmodium falciparum pantothenate kinase has only one active site and does not require Pf14-3-3I for activity.
articles.autores: Liu X, Spry C, Saliba KJ (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Coenzyme A (CoA) is an essential molecule for the intraerythrocytic stage of Plasmodium falciparum. Pantothenate kinase (PanK) catalyses the first step of the CoA biosynthesis pathway and functions as a homodimer in most organisms investigated thus far. P. falciparum possesses a novel heteromeric PanK complex composed of PfPanK1, PfPanK2 and Pf14-3-3I. Using a mutagenesis approach, we generated 10 PfPanK mutants and demonstrate that the PfPanK complex has only one functional active site, with both PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 required for activity by the complex. We also show that PfPanK2 is essential for normal intraerythrocytic parasite proliferation using a conditional knockdown system. 14-3-3 binding motifs generally contain a phosphoserine/threonine residue. Mass spectrometry analyses of phospho-peptide enriched, immunoprecipitated PfPanK samples revealed phosphorylation sites in both PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 that were additional to the previously reported sites. To investigate the role of specific sites in PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 that may be involved in Pf14-3-3I binding, five additional mutants were generated. Mutagenesis of four predicted Pf14-3-3I binding sites in PfPanK1 resulted in a significant reduction in the amount of Pf14-3-3I bound to the PfPanK complex. Heterologous expression of the PfPanK complex in an insect cell system yielded a small amount of soluble protein that assembled in situ into a functional complex. Combined results from heterologous expression and P. falciparum mutagenesis suggest that Pf14-3-3I may not be essential for PfPanK activity but may be important for stabilising the PfPanK complex.
