articles.titulo: Multistage Insecticidal Activity of Juniperus phoenicea Essential Oil Against Culex pipiens, a Major West Nile Virus Vector: Biochemical and Histopathological Effects, Molecular Docking, and Non-target Selectivity.
articles.autores: Madani F, Haleche I, … Tail G (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Given the need for environmentally sustainable alternatives for mosquito control, this study aimed to assess the biocidal potential of Juniperus phoenicea essential oil (EC) against developmental stages of Culex pipiens, a major vector of West Nile virus and other pathogens, while elucidating its biochemical and histopathological effects, interactions with acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and effects on two non-target aquatic organisms, Daphnia magna and Cloeon dipterum.
Egg-hatching inhibition, larvicidal, and pupicidal bioassays were conducted to determine IC₅₀ and LC₅₀ values, as appropriate. The chemical composition of the essential oil (EO) was characterized using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Changes in protein, carbohydrate, and lipid contents, as well as histopathological alterations in the midgut, were assessed. Molecular docking was performed to investigate the potential interactions of all identified EO constituents with AChE. The toxicity of EO to D. magna and C. dipterum was also evaluated.
GC-MS analysis identified 101 compounds, with α-pinene (21.12%), trans-calamene (4.87%), and 1,10-di-epi-cubenol (3.69%) as the predominant constituents. The EO inhibited egg hatching and exhibited larvicidal and pupicidal activities, with an IC50 of 130.4 µL/L for egg-hatching inhibition and LC50 values of 56.15 and 107.2 µL/L for larvae and pupae, respectively. Larvae exhibited the lowest LC50 among the tested life stages. Exposure induced metabolic disturbances and marked midgut alterations. Manooloxide showed the most favorable predicted binding energy for AChE (- 8.2 kcal/mol). In D. magna, mortality remained below 30% at the tested concentrations, whereas no mortality was observed in C. dipterum.
To our knowledge, this study provides the first integrated assessment of J. phoenicea essential oil against the egg, larval, and pupal stages of C. pipiens, integrating biochemical and histopathological analyses with molecular docking predictions involving AChE and an assessment of toxicity to non-target aquatic organisms. Its activity across multiple developmental stages and the limited mortality observed in the tested non-target species suggest potential for further investigation as a botanical insecticide for integrated vector management, pending further evaluation of its ecological safety and selectivity.

articles.titulo: PDE4B Inhibition Attenuates Intestinal Inflammation with Reducing Glycolysis in Macrophages.
articles.autores: Mao H, Lu Y, … Wang Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Accumulating evidence underscores that PDE4B expression is significantly upregulated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, its therapeutic potential and the underlying molecular mechanisms in pediatric IBD remain poorly defined. In this study, multiple public datasets were analyzed to characterize PDE4B expression in pediatric IBD. This was followed by therapeutic evaluation in mice colitis models to validate the efficacy of PDE4B inhibition in vivo. Analysis of public datasets revealed a marked elevation of PDE4B in pediatric IBD cohorts. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that a PDE4B inhibitor effectively suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory responses in primary blood samples from pediatric patients. In murine models, pharmacological inhibition of PDE4B significantly attenuated intestinal inflammation in both DSS- and LPS-induced colitis models. Furthermore, treatment with the PDE4B inhibitor successfully alleviated established chronic mucosal injury and preserved goblet cell integrity in spontaneous Il10-/- mice. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated that PDE4B inhibition was associated with a partial restoration of gut microbiota diversity and a reduction in specific bacterial dysbiosis. At the molecular level, the inhibitor promoted the activation of the anti-inflammatory mediator p-CREB while concurrently abrogating pro-inflammatory p-STAT3 signaling. Notably, the suppression of pathological glycolysis by the inhibitor was closely accompanied by the metabolic reprogramming and enhanced anti-inflammatory function. In conclusion, these findings suggest that targeting PDE4B represents a potential therapeutic approach for pediatric IBD by modulating macrophage immunometabolism and restoring intestinal homeostasis.

articles.titulo: Native architecture of a mitochondrial oxphosome
articles.autores: Melnik M et al. (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mitochondrial cristae are the primary bioenergetic units of eukaryotic cells, yet the molecular principles that dictate their morphologies remain largely unknown. Using in situ cryo-electron tomography and integrative modeling, we resolve the native organization of the respiratory machinery in the diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum. Unlike previously studied animals and green algae, diatoms possess tubular crista, a conserved membrane architecture found in diverse and globally relevant species. We identify several native supercomplexes assemblies, including an oxphosome comprising the entire respiratory chain. Our results, together with molecular dynamics analyses, reveal that these supercomplexes assemble through a lipid-mediated mechanism. We propose that tubular cristae are shaped by the interplay between membrane-bending ATP synthase oligomers that bud the hemispherical crista tips and supercomplexes that act as molecular roadblocks to constrain ATP synthase propagation, thereby balancing membrane curvature and allowing cristae body extension. Furthermore, we show that the diatom Complex I retains ancestral subunits related to fatty acid synthase. Beyond illuminating diatom bioenergetics, our findings reveal a fundamental principle of mitochondrial morphogenesis where ATP synthase-driven membrane curvature is spatially fine-tuned by respiratory supercomplexes.

articles.titulo: Comparative effectiveness of tirzepatide versus GLP-1 receptor agonists on the risk of incident infection and severe infection-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes.
articles.autores: Wu JY, Lee KW, … Lin YM (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at increased risk of infection-related morbidity and mortality. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) may exert immunomodulatory effects beyond glycemic control. Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide and GLP-1 receptor agonist, has demonstrated superior metabolic efficacy, but its association with infection-related outcomes remains unclear.
We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX research network including adults with T2DM between January 2022 and November 2025. New users of tirzepatide were compared with new users of GLP-1RAs. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced demographic characteristics, comorbidities, medications, and laboratory variables. The primary endpoint was a composite of infection-related events within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included pneumonia, skin infection, and all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
After matching, 143,288 patients were included in each group. Tirzepatide initiation was associated with a modestly lower risk of composite infection-related events compared with GLP-1RAs (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.99). Lower risks were observed for pneumonia (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98), skin infection (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.99), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.98). Results were consistent across most prespecified subgroups and sensitivity analyses, including landmark analyses and a negative control outcome. No significant differences were observed for acute pyelonephritis or gastrointestinal infection.
In this large real-world cohort of patients with T2DM, tirzepatide use was associated with a modestly lower risk of infection-related outcomes compared with GLP-1RAs. These findings suggest that dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonism may be associated with differences in infection-related outcomes, although prospective studies are needed to confirm causality.

articles.titulo: Geospatial risk mapping and time-series forecasting of malaria transmission among under-fives in Bauchi and Oyo States, Nigeria.
articles.autores: Nkeiruka OJ, Taiwo OJ, … Kaduru C (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with marked geographic and seasonal variability influencing transmission dynamics. Understanding spatial and temporal heterogeneity is essential for optimising malaria control strategies and improving the targeting of interventions. This study investigated under-five malaria transmission patterns in two epidemiologically distinct Nigerian states using integrated time-series forecasting and Bayesian geospatial risk mapping.
A two-stage analytical framework was applied to monthly confirmed under-five malaria cases obtained from the District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2) between January 2014 and December 2024. At the state level, autoregressive integrated moving average models with exogenous variables (ARIMAX) were developed using climatic variables obtained from the NASA Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) database. Candidate lag structures were identified using cross-correlation analysis, and competing models were compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Final models were validated using out-of-sample data before generating forecasts for January-December 2025. At the Local Government Area (LGA) level, Bayesian Besag-York-Mollié (BYM) models were used to estimate annual relative malaria risk.
Bauchi exhibited a substantially higher malaria burden and stronger seasonal transmission than Oyo throughout the study period. One-month lagged rainfall improved forecasting performance in both states, whereas temperature did not improve predictive accuracy and was excluded from the final models. Forecasts for 2025 projected continued seasonal transmission, with substantially higher malaria incidence in Bauchi than in Oyo. Bayesian spatial analysis identified persistent high-risk LGAs in Bauchi, particularly Warji, despite declining risk over time, while Ido remained the principal persistent hotspot in Oyo.
Integrating ARIMAX forecasting with Bayesian geospatial risk mapping provides a comprehensive framework for characterising malaria transmission dynamics and identifying persistent transmission hotspots. The findings highlight the value of combining routine surveillance data with climate information to strengthen malaria early warning systems and support geographically targeted malaria control strategies in Nigeria.
Not applicable.

articles.titulo: Peripheral and Uterine NK Cell Immunometabolic Concordance: A Minimally Invasive Approach to Endometrial Receptivity Assessment.
articles.revista: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.autores: Celik O, Celik S (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) occurs even after euploid embryo transfer, indicating a maternal determinant beyond embryo quality. A landmark meta-analysis showed that peripheral NK (pNK) cell numbers do not correlate with endometrial NK (uNK) cell numbers and called for functional rather than numerical assessment.
Narrative synthesis of immunometabolism, reproductive immunology, endometrial tissue metabolism, and uterine luminal sampling evidence to develop a testable model.
We propose that pNK cells may exhibit immunometabolic states correlated with, but not identical to, those of endometrial uNK cells (immunometabolic concordance). Concordance does not imply functional equivalence: pNK cells are predominantly cytotoxic, whereas uNK cells are angiogenic and immunomodulatory. We propose three axes, ΔΨm, mtROS, and intracellular lipid load, as measurable determinants of uNK function. Among minimally invasive routes, uterine luminal fluid currently has the most direct feasibility evidence, whereas cervical mucus remains hypothesis-generating and unproven. Assay-specific confounders, including P-glycoprotein-mediated dye efflux, are explicitly addressed. Six testable predictions and a prospective validation protocol are presented.
If validated, the model could reduce reliance on endometrial biopsy; if not, it will show that functional NK assessment requires compartment-specific analysis.

articles.titulo: Screening of open-source libraries from the Medicines for Malaria Venture using Bunyamwera virus as a model reveals inhibitors of Oropouche virus infection.
articles.autores: Cassani NM, Pearson HM, … Jardim ACG (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Arboviral infections remain a major public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions, where environmental and socioeconomic conditions facilitate the circulation of diverse RNA viruses, including over 350 members of the recently renamed Peribunyaviridae family. In this regard, Oropouche virus (OROV) has caused explosive outbreaks in the Amazon region and shows wider distribution in Brazil, with confirmed neurological infections and fatalities in 2024. The absence of effective antiviral therapies highlights an urgent need for the discovery of anti-OROV drugs. In this work, we evaluated the antiviral potential of the Pandemic Response Box and Global Health Priority Box libraries from the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) against OROV, using a well-established Bunyamwera virus (BUNV) system, widely used as a prototype of the Peribunyaviridae family, expressing the reporter gene enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP). A screening protocol based on fluorescent reporter gene detection by live cell imaging was employed. Nine compounds were identified with significant activity against BUNV-eGFP, with three being highlighted as the most promising hits: Trimetrexate, GSK-983 and MMV1634385. These compounds were validated by testing for activity against OROV, and in these assays, GSK-983 exhibited the lowest EC50 value and consequently the highest selectivity index. Future studies should evaluate the antiviral efficacy of GSK-983 and assess its pharmacokinetic profile. Furthermore, our results indicate that our approach employing BUNV-eGFP as a model against OROV provides an efficient route to prioritize candidate compounds from large libraries, thereby establishing a practical screening route for future antivirals against Oropouche fever.

articles.titulo: Spatiotemporal epidemiology of dengue fever across all 64 districts of Bangladesh: a retrospective ecological analysis of reported hospital admissions.
articles.autores: Nabed IA, Daiby AT, … Hayat T (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Bangladesh has experienced increasingly widespread dengue activity, with hospital admissions reported beyond the historical concentration in Dhaka. District-level evidence is needed to support preparedness, but nationwide-analyses combining temporal patterns, population-standardised reported admission rates, and spatial clustering remain limited.
We conducted a retrospective ecological spatiotemporal analysis of reported dengue hospital admissions across all 64 districts of Bangladesh using daily Directorate General of Health Services Health Emergency Operations Centre reports from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2025. The analytical dataset contained 93,504 district-day observations after imputing 19 missing dates using district-wise linear interpolation. Annual reported admission rates per 100,000 population were computed using district mid-year population projections from the 2022 census. Temporal patterns were assessed descriptively, with exploratory Seasonal Mann-Kendall assessment and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Spatial clustering was evaluated using Global Moran's I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Getis-Ord Gi* under queen-contiguity weights, with K-nearest-neighbour (k = 6) sensitivity analysis. Additional sensitivity analyses examined the impact of missing-date handling.
DGHS yearly totals reported 62,382 dengue admissions in 2022, 321,017 in 2023, 101,214 in 2024, and 102,861 in 2025. Corresponding totals in the interpolated dataset were 62,034, 320,943, 100,803, and 102,929, respectively, reflecting minor differences attributable to interpolation of missing dates. Reported admissions increased sharply from 2022 to 2023, declined substantially in 2024, and remained stable in 2025. Dhaka district's share of national admissions fell from 63.5% to 31.5% between 2022 and 2025, while Barishal Division's share increased from 5.1% to 21.1%. In 2025, Barguna recorded the highest reported admission rate (959.5 per 100,000 population). Spatial autocorrelation was strongest from 2023 onward, with weak positive autocorrelation detected in 2022. Dhaka was not identified as a statistically significant LISA or Gi* hotspot core, unlike spatially coherent southern clusters emerging 2023 onwards.
Reported dengue hospital admissions show an apparent redistribution beyond Dhaka, with repeated concentration in several southern districts after 2023. Because the analysis is based on hospital-reported admissions, a study-period of four years, and facility-location rather than residence-location data, the findings should be interpreted as suggestive evidence of changing dengue-admission patterns.

articles.titulo: LC-MS-Based Chlorine-Signature Query Engine Strategy for Automated Discovery of Phosphate-Containing Metabolites.
articles.autores: Chen X, Li Y, … Wu JL (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Comprehensive profiling of phosphate-containing compounds (PCCs) in untargeted metabolomics remains challenging due to their high hydrophilicity, poor separation, and low stability, which hampers high-throughput screening from large-scale liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) datasets. Herein, an LC-MS-based chlorine-tagging strategy integrated with a Chlorine Signature Query Engine (Cl-SQE) was established for the rapid identification of potential PCCs in complex matrices. The novel derivatization reagent, [5-(2-chlorophenyl)isoxazol-3-yl]methyl amine (ClXIMA), can react with phosphate groups on PCCs, such as nucleotides, sugar phosphates, glycerophosphates, and nucleotide sugars under mild conditions, thereby markedly enhancing reversed-phase retention and separation resolution. More importantly, the incorporation of chlorine, identifiable by its characteristic isotopic peak pattern, provides a unique digital signature in the mass spectra. Leveraging these features, Cl-SQE, a data mining program, was developed to systematically and automatically extract candidate PCCs from large-scale datasets. By applying this strategy to liver tissues from a mouse model of cholestasis, 318 potential ClXIMA derivatives were screened out, and 189 metabolites were identified or tentatively assigned. Statistical analysis revealed significant disturbances in nucleotide metabolism, addressing a critical gap in phospho-metabolomic profiling for cholestatic disease and revealing dysregulated nucleotide homeostasis as a potential feature of cholestasis-associated metabolic remodeling. Overall, this platform facilitates the discovery of PCCs in complex matrices and provides new insights into the pathogenesis of cholestasis and other clinical diseases.

articles.titulo: Immunomodulatory Effects of Dodelate C against Plasmodium by Reshaping Macrophage Function.
articles.autores: Wu J, Cang LQ, … Jiang B (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study investigated the effect and molecular mechanism of Dodelate C, a sesquiterpenoid isolated from Dobinea delavayi, in regulating macrophage function during malaria. Its antiplasmodial activity was tested in vitro against Plasmodium falciparum 3D7, and macrophage regulatory effects examined in vivo in Plasmodium yoelii-infected mice. Cytokine levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA); macrophage polarization was analyzed via flow cytometry, with proliferation and phagocytosis measured by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and neutral red uptake assays. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations identified potential targets, with key protein expression validated by Western blot. Dodelate C exerted robust antiplasmodial activity both in vitro and in vivo. In infected mice, it significantly reduced serum interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and nitric oxide (NO) levels, increased total macrophages, and markedly decreased the M1/M2 ratio. At non-cytotoxic concentrations in RAW 264.7 cells, Dodelate C enhanced macrophage phagocytic function and regulated macrophage polarization: it downregulated CD86 and pro-inflammatory factors (NO, tumor necrosis factor-alpha [TNF-α], and interleukin-1 beta [IL-1β]) to suppress the M1 phenotype, while upregulating CD206 and interleukin-10 (IL-10) to promote M2. Additionally, Dodelate C elevated Beclin-1 and the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3)-II/LC3-I ratio, modulating peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling by upregulating PPARγ/retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα) and reducing insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R)/Akt/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) phosphorylation. These findings show Dodelate C modulates macrophage function by balancing polarization and regulating autophagy, driving its antimalarial efficacy.

articles.titulo: Ferroptosis as an Immunometabolic Regulator in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.autores: Ahmed Z, B H (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Autoimmune diseases involve persistent immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and progressive tissue injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and impaired antioxidant defences, may contribute to these processes.
This review examines the immunological relevance of ferroptosis in autoimmune diseases, focusing on iron homeostasis, lipid peroxidation, GPX4 (glutathione peroxidase 4), system xc- (cystine/glutamate antiporter), inflammatory pathways, immune-cell dysfunction, biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies.
Ferroptosis has been implicated in synovial inflammation and fibroblast-like synoviocyte dysfunction in rheumatoid arthritis, and in neutrophil abnormalities, oxidative injury, and lupus nephritis in systemic lupus erythematosus. Related mechanisms are also being explored in multiple sclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease, and other autoimmune conditions.
Ferroptosis may represent a shared but context-dependent immunometabolic process in autoimmunity, with potential diagnostic and therapeutic relevance. However, disease heterogeneity, cell-specific effects, limited human validation, and the need for biomarker-guided precision approaches remain important challenges.

articles.titulo: A multipathogen view of Epstein-Barr virus pathogenesis and tumorigenesis.
articles.autores: Tang J, Zhong L, … Zhang X (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects more than 95% of the global population and contributes to multiple human cancers and autoimmune diseases. Co-infection with pathogens including Helicobacter pylori, human immunodeficiency virus, human papillomavirus, and Plasmodium falciparum can reshape host immunity and the EBV latency-lytic balance and, in some settings, promote reactivation. Collectively, these interactions may exacerbate chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and epigenetic dysregulation to accelerate disease progression and tumor formation. Existing clinical treatments control only the active pathogens but fail to target latent EBV. Emerging strategies such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) gene editing and EBV-targeted immunotherapy aim to eliminate latent viral reservoirs. This review outlines the synergistic mechanisms of EBV co-infection in oncogenesis, highlighting that further research on pathogen interactions is vital for developing better prevention and treatment options.

articles.titulo: Distribution of kdr-west and kdr-east resistance alleles in Anopheles gambiae s.l. across contrasting transmission settings in central and southern Senegal.
articles.autores: Diop M, Diagne NS, … Niang EHA (25 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The effectiveness of malaria vector control in sub-Saharan Africa is increasingly threatened by insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.). Knockdown resistance (kdr) mutations L1014F (kdr-west) and L1014S (kdr-east) are key target-site mechanisms associated with resistance to pyrethroids, the primary insecticide class currently approved for long-lasting insecticidal nets. This study assessed insecticide susceptibility and compared the distribution and phenotypic associations of kdr-west and kdr-east mutations in An. gambiae s.l. populations from two health districts in Senegal.
Larvae were collected from four sites in Nioro and Velingara health districts and reared to adulthood. Adult females (3-5 days old) were tested against permethrin, deltamethrin, alphacypermethrin, bendiocarb, and pirimiphos-methyl using WHO susceptibility assays. Molecular identification of sibling species and detection of kdr mutations were performed by PCR. Allelic frequencies were compared between sites and species, and associations between kdr alleles and pyrethroid resistance phenotypes were assessed using odds ratios.
Populations of An. gambiae s.l. from both districts exhibited high resistance to permethrin (9.18%; 13.08%), deltamethrin (46.08%; 48.08%) and alphacypermethrin (75%; 56%) in Nioro and Velingara, respectively. While remaining fully susceptible to bendiocarb (99.06%; 100%) and pirimiphos-methyl (100%; 100%) in Nioro and Velingara, respectively. Anopheles arabiensis was the predominant species in both districts, with higher proportions of An. gambiae sensu stricto (s.s.) and An. coluzzii in Velingara. A total of 85 and 90 An. gambiae s.l. specimens were genotyped to determine kdr-west and kdr-east alleles frequencies, respectively in Nioro and Velingara. Both kdr-west and kdr-east alleles were detected, with marked spatial and species-specific variation. The kdr-west allele was significantly associated with pyrethroid resistance in both Nioro (OR = 5.68, p < 0.01) and Velingara (OR = 2.81, p < 0.01), indicating that mosquitoes carrying kdr-west allele are more likely to survive exposure to pyrethroids than those that do not carry it. Whereas no significant association was observed for the kdr-east allele.
Pyrethroid resistance is widespread in An. gambiae s.l. populations from central and southern Senegal and is significantly associated with the kdr-west mutation. The limited association between kdr-east and resistance phenotypes suggests the involvement of additional resistance mechanisms. These findings highlight the need for resistance-informed vector control strategies and support the integration of complementary interventions in areas with high pyrethroid resistance.

O alelo kdr-west se associou à resistência (OR 5,68 em Nioro e 2,81 em Velingara); kdr-east não.

articles.titulo: Detection of Jamestown Canyon Virus in Mosquito Populations, Northeastern Illinois, USA, 2024.
articles.autores: Mackay AJ, Cara C, … Stone C (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Jamestown Canyon virus (JCV) is an underreported mosquitoborne arbovirus that can cause viral encephalitis in humans. To determine whether humans in greater Chicago, Illinois, USA, were at risk for JCV infection, we conducted surveillance on mosquito populations in suburban forest preserves with seasonal wetland habitats likely to sustain enzootic transmission. We documented the diversity and abundance of putative vector mosquito species to determine their prevalence for JCV infection. Of 11 predominantly mammalophilic mosquito taxa screened, we detected JCV in 5 species. The highest JCV prevalence was in Anopheles punctipennis, followed by Aedes stimulans group, Ae. canadensis, Ae. trivittatus, and Coquillettidia perturbans mosquitoes. Most detections were from mosquitoes collected in June and early July, and earliest detections were limited to Ae. stimulans group female mosquitoes. Our findings indicate substantial potential for human JCV exposure where urban development encroaches on natural habitats in northeastern Illinois. We urge continued surveillance for JCV.

articles.titulo: Biological Embedding of Social Experience Over Genomic and Neural Time Scales
articles.autores: Peng et al. (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The "Neurons for Today, Genes for Tomorrow model" (NTGT) predicts how the brain's neural and molecular control systems interact to regulate biological embedding, whereby social experience alters the brain to shape future behavior. We report here on the first test of this model, using honey bee queen retinue pheromone (QRP) and behavioral, single-nucleus transcriptomic, and electrophysiological analyses. Consistent with theory, weaker exposure triggered a simple attraction response and transcriptomic changes primarily in the antennal lobes (AL), whereas stronger exposure induced transcriptomic changes in the mushroom bodies, a brain region affecting more complex behavior. In addition, AL electrophysiological responses to QRP were enhanced after stronger exposure, also consistent with theory. We also showed how individual differences in biological embedding can be explained by NTGT, with individual differences in brain gene regulatory network topology, especially in specific sensory cell clusters, supporting a new mechanistic framework for behavioral regulation.

articles.titulo: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Childhood Malaria Risk in Rwanda, 2014-2023: A Spatial Study of DHS and MIS Surveys.
articles.autores: Rudasingwa G, Ishimwe NC (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria remains a leading cause of childhood morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa. Rwanda offers a valuable epidemiological case study, having experienced marked control gains, a documented resurgence, and subsequent recovery. We characterised spatial and temporal patterns of Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia among children aged 6-59 months across four nationally representative surveys (2014-2023) to quantify national trends and identify sub-national areas of relatively high risk.
Geocoded data from the 2014-15 DHS, 2017 MIS, 2019-20 DHS, and 2023 MIS were analysed (43,313 children; 1,332 clusters). RDT-confirmed parasitaemia was the primary outcome. National and stratum-specific prevalence was estimated using the full complex survey design (stratification, clustering, and sample weights) with Taylor-linearised 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Global spatial autocorrelation was assessed with Moran's I (k = 8 nearest neighbours; 999 permutations) and local clusters with Getis-Ord Gi*. Deterministic triangulated interpolation produced continuous prevalence surfaces; areas of relatively persistent high prevalence were defined as top-quartile interpolated prevalence in ≥3 of 4 waves.
Design-based prevalence was 4.1% (95% CI 3.5-4.7%) in 2014-15 DHS and 1.2% (0.9-1.6%) in 2019-20 DHSa 71% reduction between the two methodologically comparable DHS waves. The two MIS rounds, which use a different testing protocol, recorded 9.5% (7.7-11.8%) in 2017 and 1.0% (0.7-1.5%) in 2023 and are reported as descriptive cross-design comparisons. Significant positive spatial autocorrelation was detected in both DHS waves (Moran's I = 0.168 and 0.141; both two-sided p < 0.001) but not in the MIS waves. A relatively persistent zone of higher interpolated prevalence was identified in the Southern Province (Gisagara, Nyanza, Ruhango).
Childhood malaria parasitaemia declined substantially over the study period, most robustly evidenced by the 71% DHS-to-DHS reduction. Spatially patterned residual transmission is concentrated in a southern corridor that warrants further programme investigation and targeted surveillance as Rwanda pursues malaria elimination.

articles.titulo: A social bee (Bombus terrestris) learns to associate a novel odor with social context.
articles.autores: Amsalem E, Hefetz A (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Many pheromone responses are hardwired into the insect's nervous system and are essential for critical behaviors such as mating, alarm signaling, and trail following. Workers of social species are assumed to respond innately to queen pheromones, affecting their behavior and reproductive physiology. However, accumulating evidence suggests that learning and experience may also shape responses to social chemical cues. To examine if the response to queen-associated odors can be learned, we exposed Bombus terrestris workers to a novel odor by treating the queen daily with unfamiliar floral scents, either anisyl alcohol or methyl anthranilate. We allowed perfumed queens to establish colonies and examined worker attraction and egg laying following exposure to these odors in the absence of the queen, either with or without brood as context. In a two-choice olfactometer, workers preferred the queen odor they learned during colony development. Exposure of workers to the queen-associated odor in the absence of the queen influenced worker egg laying only in the presence of brood, surprisingly resulting in increased egg laying. Our study demonstrates that workers can learn novel odors that are associated with their queen or nest, which in turn function as context-dependent social cues that modify their social and reproductive behavior.

articles.titulo: Salidroside decreases lipid abundance, mitochondrial function, and expression of the mitochondrial citrate transporter SLC25A1 via miR-1343-3p in gastric cancer.
articles.autores: Cao M, Zhang Z, … Wang X (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To investigate the potential mechanisms by which salidroside regulates mitochondrial function, SLC25A1 expression, and lipid abundance in gastric cancer (GC) cells via miR-1343-3p.
Transcriptome sequencing was performed on MGC-803 cells before and after salidroside treatment to identify differentially expressed miRNAs and mRNAs. Bioinformatic analysis was then used to screen for candidate molecules. The interaction between miR-1343-3p and SLC25A1 was validated by dual-luciferase reporter assay, sequence alignment, and RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP). Mitochondrial morphology and function were examined by transmission electron microscopy and fluorescent probes. MGC-803 and AGS cells were used to assess the effects of salidroside, miR-1343-3p modulation, and SLC25A1 silencing on mitochondrial citrate export, lipid abundance, and cell proliferation. Furthermore, a nude mouse xenograft model was established to evaluate the effects of salidroside and a miR-1343-3p agomir on tumor growth, the expression of miR-1343-3p and SLC25A1, and tumor metabolic status.
Transcriptome sequencing revealed 44 differentially expressed miRNAs and 1,384 differentially expressed mRNAs in MGC-803 cells following salidroside treatment. Among them, miR-1343-3p was significantly upregulated as a tumor-suppressive miRNA, while SLC25A1, a mitochondrial citrate transporter, was significantly downregulated. RT-qPCR and Western blot results demonstrated that salidroside significantly increased the expression of miR-1343-3p while decreasing the mRNA and protein expression of SLC25A1. Dual-luciferase reporter, sequence alignment, and RIP assays confirmed that miR-1343-3p directly targets SLC25A1. Further studies showed that salidroside treatment, miR-1343-3p overexpression, and SLC25A1 silencing could all cause the accumulation of mitochondrial citrate, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, increased ROS production, and decreased the levels of NADH, ATP, acetyl-CoA, free fatty acids, cholesterol, and triglycerides, while significantly inhibiting GC cell proliferation. However, after knocking down miR-1343-3p, the opposite results were observed, which were efficiently rescued by salidroside. In vivo, both salidroside treatment and the miR-1343-3p agomir administration significantly reduced tumor volume and weight. Tumor tissues from these groups showed increased miR-1343-3p expression, decreased SLC25A1 expression, and lipid metabolic changes consistent with those observed in vitro.
Salidroside inhibits GC cell proliferation and tumor growth by upregulating the tumor-suppressive miR-1343-3p, which directly targets and downregulates the mitochondrial citrate transporter SLC25A1. Meanwhile, decreased mitochondrial citrate export, impaired mitochondrial function, and reduced lipid abundance are observed. These findings indicate that miR-1343-3p and SLC25A1 may be promising therapeutic targets for metabolic intervention in gastric cancer.

articles.titulo: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict.
articles.autores: Bodas D, Demirci Ş, … Rezaval C (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

articles.titulo: Oropouche Fever Outbreak, Havana, Cuba, June-September 2024.
articles.autores: Martínez-Rodríguez A, Rodríguez EC, … Guzmán MG (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Oropouche fever emerged nationwide in Cuba in 2024. We investigated the outbreak in Havana; of 549 suspected cases, 189 (34.4%) were confirmed. No cases were severe. Incidence was 8.9/100,000 population and was highest in adults 27-59 years of age (10.2/100,000 population). Three infants tested positive. Dengue cocirculation challenged surveillance.

articles.titulo: Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State.
articles.autores: Coelho-Rocha E, Fernandes LN, … Lima-Camara TN (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The 2016-2019 sylvatic yellow fever epidemic in Brazil spread into the peri-urban areas of São Paulo State, raising concerns about the potential resurgence of urban yellow fever transmission in the Americas. In Alberto Löfgren State Park (PEAL), Serra da Cantareira, one of the world's largest urban forests, southern brown howler monkeys became locally extinct in early January 2018 following a short-lived outbreak.
To investigate mosquito feeding patterns during and after the yellow fever outbreak, we collected 5,001 female mosquitoes between December 2017 and March 2020, and screened 143 blood-engorged specimens using Nanopore sequencing.
Vertebrate hosts were identified as the source of blood meals in 74.8% (107/143) of samples, revealing that mosquitoes fed predominantly on mammals (83.2%, 89/107), but also on birds (10.3%, 11/107), and on multiple hosts (6.5%, 7/107). Humans accounted for 76.6% (82/107) of identified blood meals. Other hosts included non-human primate, dog, opossum, mouse and passerine birds. Among Haemagogus leucocelaenus, the primary yellow fever virus (YFV) vector at PEAL, 94.6% (35/37) of blood meals were human-derived, while 5.4% (2/37) contained non-human primate blood. Additionally, two engorged Haemagogus capricornii (100%, 2/2), another YFV vector, fed on humans. Untargeted sequencing recovered a complete YFV genome from an Hg. leucocelaenus specimen with human blood, providing direct evidence of active viral circulation within PEAL.
Sylvatic YFV vectors captured in urban forest fragments of the Serra da Cantareira exhibited marked anthropophilic feeding behaviour. Our findings underscore the risk of mosquito-mediated spillover into densely populated São Paulo, emphasising the urgent need for sustained vaccination together with entomological and virological surveillance to track and respond to yellow fever outbreaks in peri-urban settings.
articles.resumo_pt_v6: Em 143 fêmeas ingurgitadas do Parque Estadual Alberto Löfgren (SP), o sequenciamento Nanopore identificou o hospedeiro vertebrado em 74,8% (107/143); 76,6% desses repastos eram humanos e, em Haemagogus leucocelaenus, 94,6% (35/37). O sequenciamento não direcionado recuperou um genoma completo do vírus da febre amarela de um espécime com sangue humano.

v6.implicacao: Xenovigilância (Rio + portos) (fonte-repasto): mesma prova de conceito do programa, mosquito ingurgitado como amostra de sangue e de patógeno, com taxa de recuperação de hospedeiro (74,8%) e de genoma viral em plataforma portátil; vale como referência de desempenho.

O sequenciamento não direcionado recuperou um genoma completo do vírus da febre amarela de um espécime com sangue humano.

articles.titulo: Beyond cytokines in inflammatory bowel disease: targeting the epithelial microbiome-mitochondria-immune axis to restore metabolic homeostasis.
articles.autores: Torossian T, Choufany E, … Echtay KS (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Inflammatory bowel disease is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by mucosal immunity dysregulation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and gut microbiome dysbiosis. While cytokine-targeted therapies have improved clinical outcomes, many patients remain refractory or relapse, emphasizing the need for additional therapeutic approaches. Recent evidence suggests that mitochondrial metabolism in the intestinal epithelium regulates mucosal homeostasis, immune cell recruitment, and susceptibility to inflammation. However, it remains controversial whether mitochondrial dysfunction is a cause or a consequence of intestinal inflammation. Epithelial energetic deficiency and barrier dysfunction are associated with impaired oxidative phosphorylation, defective short-chain fatty acid utilization, redox imbalance, and faulty mitochondrial quality control. Indeed, impaired mitophagy promotes mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release through voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1) oligomerization and mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening. Extracellular mtDNA acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern, activating cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes, toll-like receptor 9, and NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 inflammasome pathways that amplify mucosal inflammation. These metabolic changes alter luminal oxygen and microbiome composition, whereas microbial metabolites, particularly tryptophan-derived indoles and kynurenines, modulate epithelial mitochondrial function through aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling. These findings support a bidirectional microbiome-mitochondria-immune axis that potentiates intestinal inflammation. In this review, we summarize the current evidence of how epithelial mitochondrial dysfunction associates with intestinal inflammation. We discuss how mitochondrial metabolism interfaces with microbial ecology and immune regulation to shape disease pathogenesis. We also discuss therapeutic strategies targeting this axis: mitochondrial-targeted antioxidants (eg, MitoQ), VDAC1 inhibitors, bile-acid derivatives (eg, tauroursodeoxycholic acid), and metabolite-based therapies to restore microbial tryptophan metabolism. These approaches target mitochondrial bioenergetics and microbial metabolic cross-talk with the potential to restore microbiome-immune homeostasis, preserve barrier integrity, and complement conventional immune-directed therapies.

articles.titulo: Plasmodium infection inhibits angiogenesis and induces autophagy in melanoma through the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
articles.autores: Zhao Y, Fang C, … Chen X (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Melanoma is a highly malignant and metastatic skin tumor, and current treatments exhibit limited efficacy in advanced cases. Plasmodium infection can activate the human immune system. Previous studies have found Plasmodium infection has therapeutic effects on lung cancer and breast cancer. However, this treatment method has never been used on melanoma therapy. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway is crucial for regulating tumor cell autophagy and angiogenesis. Whether this signaling pathway plays a role in malaria parasite infection for treating melanoma remains unclear.
A mouse B16F10 melanoma model was established. The subjects were randomly divided into a control group (Mel) and a Plasmodium infection group (Mel + Py). Transmission electron microscopy was employed to examine the morphology of autophagosomes. Hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining, along with immunohistochemistry(IHC), was utilized to assess histopathological changes in the tumor. Additionally, RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses were performed to evaluate the expression of autophagy-related factors (LC3-II, Beclin-1, Atg5, P62) and angiogenic factors (HIF-1α, VEGF), as well as to measure the phosphorylation levels of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
Plasmodium infection significantly inhibited melanoma growth, as indicated by a reduction in tumor volume (p < 0.05). This infection also induced autophagosome formation and autophagic cell death, demonstrated by the up-regulation of LC3-II, Beclin-1, and Atg5 expression, along with the degradation of P62. Concurrently, the infection down-regulated the expression of HIF-1α VEGF and CD31, thereby inhibiting tumor angiogenesis. Mechanistically, the infection specifically decreased the phosphorylation levels of AKT and mTOR (p-AKT and p-mTOR) without altering the total protein levels, suggesting inhibition of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
Plasmodium infection demonstrates antimelanoma effects by inhibiting the phosphorylation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, synergistically inducing autophagic cell death, and suppressing angiogenesis. This investigation offers a novel molecular foundation for Plasmodium-based therapy and may provide new insights into melanoma treatment.

articles.titulo: Diethylhexyl Phthalate Impairs Liver Health in Epinephelus coioides via Metabolic Dysregulation and Autophagy.
articles.revista: Bulletin of environmental contamination and toxicology
articles.autores: Xu Z, Chen Z, … Li Y (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Diethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) is a common plasticizer that readily leaches from plastic products into the environment, posing potential threats to aquatic organisms. In this study, Epinephelus coioides were gavaged with DEHP (0, 10 and 40 µg/g BW/day) for 14 days. The results showed that DEHP exposure caused hepatic inflammatory infiltration, tissue damage, fat vacuolation, and glycogen deposition. The 10 µg/g group exhibited activated glycolysis, the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), and fructose/mannose metabolism. In contrast, the 40 µg/g group showed suppression of all these metabolic processes. DEHP exposure increased malondialdehyde (MDA) content and inhibited superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, indicating antioxidant system impairment, and significantly upregulated the expression of autophagy-related genes. In conclusion, DEHP induces tissue damage in E. coioides by disrupting redox homeostasis, interfering with energy metabolism, and inducing autophagy. This study elucidates the hepatotoxic effects of DEHP in E. coioides, providing a scientific basis for ecological risk assessment in aquaculture.

articles.titulo: Confocal Live-Cell Imaging Under Ultralow Irradiance Using Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensor
articles.autores: Okano C et al. (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Confocal laser scanning fluorescence microscopy (CLSFM) is widely used for three-dimensional live-cell imaging. However, high irradiance is required to overcome dark counts in photodetectors, often leading to observation bias. In this study, we examine whether a CLSFM system equipped with a virtually dark-count-free superconducting transition-edge sensor (TES) can enable live-cell imaging under low irradiance, thereby mitigating observation bias. Using green fluorescent protein-tagged HeLa cells, we determined the minimum laser power required for live-cell imaging and demonstrated suppression of photobleaching and cell-division arrest during long-term observation. Innate fluorescence signature analysis revealed that TES-CLSFM could discriminate between two oleaginous yeast species with different lipid productivities at ca. 1/400 the irradiance required by conventional CLSFM. These results establish TES-CLSFM as a minimally invasive imaging modality for the quantitative physiological assessment of living cells.

articles.titulo: Winding-up of fibrin fibers as a novel mechanism of platelet-mediated fiber compaction.
articles.autores: Grichine A, Kovalenko T, … Sadoul K (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study reveals an unrecognized mechanism by which platelets retract and compact fibrin fibers. Using a newly developed 2D fiber-retraction assay, we observed a 'gearwheel' pattern of actomyosin in spread platelets with associated, extracellular fibrin patches that appear to initiate fibrin fiber attachment and rearrangement. The outcome of this process results in two morphologically different platelet populations. Spread platelets with coiled fibers around and above their pseudo-nucleus. Other, only partially spread platelets have tightly packed fibers around bulbous protrusions ('bulbs'), mirroring the architecture of platelets and adjacent fibers within a retracted clot. Thus, the observed compaction process might take place during clot retraction to reduce clot volume, stiffen the clot, and enhance wound repair. Apart from pulling on fibers like on a rope, platelets actively wrap them into compact structures, similar to balls of wool. Using a combination of 3D clot- and 2D fiber-retraction assays, expansion and electron microscopy, live imaging, and mathematical modeling, we show that platelets use an actomyosin-driven motion to loop fibrin fibers around the base of bulbs, which form when platelets get trapped between fibrin fibers during 3D clot- or 2D fiber-retraction assays. These findings complement existing models of platel-mediated fibrin retraction, offering new insight into how platelets mechanically organize fibrin fibers.

articles.titulo: CRISPR-Cas Systems in Protozoan Parasites: Genome Editing, Functional Genomics, Gene Regulation and Emerging Applications.
articles.autores: Ganguly N, Thakre BJ (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Protozoan parasites possess complex genomes, unusual DNA-repair mechanisms, multiple developmental stages, and, in several species, intracellular or vector-dependent life cycles that complicate functional genetic studies. CRISPR-Cas9 has become a central tool for functional genomics in these organisms, enabling targeted gene disruption, replacement, tagging, nucleotide modification and genome-wide functional screening. However, editing efficiency and outcomes vary substantially among parasite species and depend not only on Cas9-mediated double-strand break formation but also on target accessibility, guide design, delivery method, parasite stage, DNA-repair capacity, donor availability, selection and the biological cost of the induced lesion. This review focuses primarily on experimentally established Cas9-mediated genome editing in Plasmodium, Leishmania, Toxoplasma gondii, Trypanosoma, Babesia, Theileria and Cryptosporidium. We compare plasmid-based and transient expression, ribonucleoprotein (RNP) delivery, electroporation/nucleofection, stage-specific delivery, guide and donor design, selection strategies, editing outcomes, and molecular and functional validation. Particular emphasis is placed on homology-directed repair (HDR), canonical non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) and single-strand annealing (SSA), which determine whether editing results in indels, precise sequence replacement, tagging or larger genomic deletions. Species-specific differences are illustrated by efficient NHEJ-mediated disruption in Toxoplasma, donor-dependent repair in Plasmodium and Cryptosporidium, SSA-associated repair in Leishmania, efficient homologous recombination in trypanosomatids, precise editing in Babesia, and stage-specific delivery constraints in Theileria. The review further examines the progression from single-gene editing to marker-free manipulation, base editing, conditional approaches and genome-wide functional screens. Cas12a, CRISPRi/a, prime editing and related systems are discussed as emerging extensions. Overall, this repair- and delivery-centred framework explains why CRISPR editing differs among protozoan parasites and identifies the experimentally validated limitations that currently shape their genome-engineering potential.

articles.titulo: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons.
articles.autores: Martin-Solana E, Carter SD, … Freyberg Z (30 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

articles.titulo: A fractographic and numerical assessment of dental zirconia implant fractures.
articles.revista: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
articles.autores: Lohbauer U, Belli R, … Wartzack S (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
This study investigated fracture mechanisms, complementing a prospective clinical trial reporting a 16.7% five-year fracture-related failure rate.
Four retrieved, horizontally fractured ZV3 zirconia implants were examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), surface profilometry, and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). Finite element analysis (FEA) assessed stress distribution under horizontal loading, considering parametric variations of different bone level support as well as variations of occlusal contact loading angles, relative to the implant axis.
All implants fractured palatal-to-buccal, originating at the root of the first endosseous thread. SEM revealed pressing-related volumetric defects and pronounced surface damage from milling and grinding. Mean surface roughness (Rz) was 10-20 μm, while micro-CT showed volume defect sizes peaking at approximately 30 μm and reaching 50-70 μm. FEA predicted peak stress of 750.85 MPa under a 600 N horizontal load, increasing to 3963.30 MPa with 3-mm simulated marginal bone loss under worst-case conditions. A 1-mm buccolingual crown shift towards the implant axis reduced the maximum principal stress in the root of the first endosseous thread by 123.03 MPa.
Fracture mechanics calculations indicated that critical defects could substantially reduce the fracture strength, potentially allowing clinically relevant masticatory forces to initiate fracture. Thread-root stress concentration, bone loss, and off-axis loading conditions further contribute increasing the fracture susceptibility.
Implant fractures resulted from manufacturing defects interacting with a stress-concentrating thread geometry, exacerbated by marginal bone loss and off-axis loading. These findings highlight the importance of manufacturing quality, fracture-resistant implant design, and appropriate surgical and prosthetic planning.

articles.titulo: Defining host factors required for dengue virus NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability and endothelial glycocalyx layer disruption
articles.autores: Tjang LV et al. (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne positive-sense RNA virus belonging to the Flaviviridae family that poses a significant threat to global health. Clinical manifestations of DENV infection range from febrile to severe disease characterized by vascular leakage. The secreted DENV nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) contributes to endothelial dysfunction through interactions with endothelial cells, leading to disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx and intercellular junction complexes (IJC). However, host factors required for NS1-triggered endothelial dysfunction are not well understood. It is also unclear if NS1 highjacks different host factors and signaling pathways for glycocalyx and IJC disruption. To address these questions, we used a targeted genetic approach to identify host factors required either for NS1-triggered endothelial glycocalyx layer (EGL) disruption, as assessed by immunofluorescence assays, or for IJC disruption, as measured by transendothelial electrical resistance. After demonstrating the decoupled nature of EGL and IJC disruption in our models, we genetically depleted host factors with known roles in regulating endothelial barrier function and/or involvement in NS1 pathogenesis, including heparanase, cathepsin L, sialidases, and the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and {beta}-catenin signaling pathways. Our results reveal a complex genetic landscape where NS1-induced disruption of EGL and IJCs involves both unique and shared host factors. Further, our data identify a direct role for {beta}-catenin in NS1-induced endothelial dysfunction in vitro and in vivo. Overall, this work advances understanding of host factors required for DENV NS1-triggered endothelial dysfunction, revealing distinct intracellular pathways that are highjacked by NS1 to modulate barrier function, thus providing new insights into dengue-associated vascular leak.

articles.titulo: Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins inhibit dengue virus replication and remodel host-cell metabolism
articles.autores: Jimenez-Posada EV et al. (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Flaviviruses reprogram host-cell metabolism to support viral replication. In previous work, we showed that Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins inhibit dengue virus replication and were predicted to interact with viral enzymes. Here, we investigated whether S01, a purified solid from Solanum ovalifolium containing predominantly two characterized spirostane saponins, also modulates host-cell metabolism in association with reduced permissiveness to dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). We performed untargeted GC-QTOF-MS metabolomics in Vero cells under four conditions, including untreated control, S01 treatment, DENV-2 infection, and DENV-2 infection with S01 treatment. Quality-control samples clustered tightly, supporting analytical reproducibility. Principal component analysis revealed separation among experimental groups, and PERMANOVA confirmed significant global metabolic differences (F = 27.567, R{superscript 2} = 0.827, p = 0.001).  S01 also retained strong antiviral activity, producing 99.9% inhibition under the metabolomics conditions. DENV-2 infection was associated with alterations metabolites related to amino acid, carbohydrate, lipid, and sphingolipid metabolism. Pathway analysis highlighted glutamate metabolism, arginine and proline metabolism, glycolysis-related pathways, fatty-acid oxidation and carnitine-associated metabolism, phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis, and sphingolipid metabolism. In uninfected cells, S01 induced a distinct metabolic profile (OPLS-DA R{superscript 2}Y = 0.951, Q{superscript 2} = 0.851; permutation p = 0.002), characterized by increased carbohydrate-related metabolites, including the unresolved Talose/D-glucose feature, gluconic acid, 2-keto-L-gulonic acid, and D-mannitol, together with decreased abundance of selected lipid-related metabolites. During infection, S01 induced a distinct metabolic (OPLS-DA R{superscript 2}Y = 0.928, Q{superscript 2} = 0.841), characterized by lower abundance of several fatty-acid-related and organic-acid metabolites and higher abundance of carbohydrate-related metabolites, while modifying selected DENV-2-associated metabolic alterations. These findings associate S01 antiviral activity with substantial remodeling of host-cell metabolism. Together with previous docking predictions of interactions with viral targets, the results support a model in which the antiviral activity of Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins may involve complementary effects on viral and host-associated processes.

articles.titulo: The impact of childhood obesity on the developing skeleton.
articles.autores: Baran E, Wójcik M (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Childhood obesity is an increasingly prevalent global health concern associated with significant metabolic, endocrine, and skeletal consequences. During critical periods of growth and peak bone mineralisation, excessive adiposity may impair skeletal development by disrupting bone formation and remodeling. The effects of obesity on bone metabolism are complex and multifactorial, involving altered mechanical loading, hormonal dysregulation, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Key mediators, including insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and disturbances in calcium-phosphate-magnesium-vitamin D homeostasis, contribute to impaired osteoblastic and osteoclastic activity. Additionally, gut microbiome dysbiosis and reduced nutrient absorption may exacerbate skeletal fragility and abnormal mineralisation. This review provides an integrative overview of current evidence regarding the impact of obesity on the developing skeleton. It discusses (I) methods of bone assessment in children with excess body weight and associated diagnostic challenges, (II) biomarkers relevant to bone metabolism and obesity-related skeletal alterations, (III) the role of dietary factors, nutrient intake, and physical activity in bone development, and (IV) future research directions aimed at reducing fracture risk and improving skeletal health outcomes in paediatric populations.

articles.titulo: Heterogeneous short-term plasticity reformats latent temporal information into an explicit population clock
articles.autores: Buerkle NP, Jeanne JM (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Short-term plasticity (STP) supports diverse synaptic-level computations, but how its organization across a circuit shapes emergent, network-level dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we first characterize STP across sparse inputs to Kenyon cells in the Drosophila mushroom body, revealing an unstructured and near-random organization that could not be explained by either pre- or postsynaptic cell identity. Rather than representing biological noise, an experimentally constrained network model instead shows how this heterogeneous organization reformats temporal information embedded in presynaptic spike rate trajectories into a behaviorally relevant population clock. Although an ideal observer could recover the same degree of temporal information from most alternative models, only the STP-mediated transformation made that information accessible to a biologically realistic decoder. Together, our results identify heterogeneous STP as a distributed biophysical mechanism that collectively functions as a temporal basis set to support circuit computations across variable input statistics.

articles.titulo: Targeting sphingolipid metabolism to inhibit insulin-like growth factor signaling-driven glioma growth.
articles.autores: Liu P, Xia S, … Wanggou S (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Insulin-like growth factor (IGF) signaling drives progression of glioblastoma (GBM), the most aggressive brain cancer. While sphingolipid metabolism is implicated in gliomagenesis, the mechanism by which it regulates GBM growth and therapy response is poorly understood.
Through bioinformatic analyses of human gliomas, we identified sphingolipid metabolism genes with potential functional significance in glioma. Using patient-derived cells, a Drosophila glioma model, and xenograft mouse models, we investigated the functional role of Dihydroceramide desaturase 1 (DEGS1). Lipidomics profiling and RNA sequencing were performed in patient-derived cells to reveal the mechanism by which DEGS1 regulates glioma growth. Additionally, we tested the effect of a DEGS1 inhibitor on GBM cell growth and their resistance to IGF1R-targeted therapy.
Our data demonstrate that the expression of sphingolipid metabolism gene DEGS1 is associated with aggressive glioma biomarkers and worse patient survival. DEGS1 is required for glioma growth in patient-derived cells, a Drosophila glioma model, and xenograft mouse models. Lipidomics profiling reveals that DEGS1 deficiency results in reduced ceramides and complex sphingolipids and accumulation of their precursors. Disrupted sphingolipid homeostasis impairs lipid raft biogenesis and lipid raft-associated IGF signaling. Targeting DEGS1 decreases GBM cell growth and their resistance to IGF1R inhibition.
These findings establish that targeting DEGS1-regulated sphingolipid metabolism is a viable avenue to inhibit IGF signaling-driven GBM growth.

articles.titulo: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
articles.autores: Wang G, Sun P, … Wang S (18 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim-5kb) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim+/-5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

articles.titulo: A Standardized Rearing Procedure for Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae): Implications for Laboratory-Based Vector Competence and Control Studies.
articles.autores: Asgarian TS, Moosa-Kazemi SH, … Sedaghat MM (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Aedes aegypti is a major vector of numerous arboviruses, including dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever. This study aimed to establish a standardized and practical procedure for maintaining and propagating an Ae. aegypti colony under controlled insectary conditions in Bandar Abbas, Iran.
Environmental parameters were routinely monitored. Larvae were reared with an appropriate diet under a regular feeding schedule, while adult mosquitoes were provided with a sucrose solution and blood meals. The correlation between the duration of egg paper drying and the hatching percentage was evaluated. Hatching rates were compared across three media: cooled boiled water, yeast and larval food.
A strong negative correlation was observed between drying duration and hatching percentage, with a Pearson correlation of -0.818 (p< 0.001). Gradual drying of egg papers over a period of two days resulted in a hatching rate of over 90% without any hatching stimulant. No significant differences in hatching rates were found among the three media, as indicated by F= 0.601 (p= 0.578). In a novel observation, female mosquitoes were found to deposit approximately 20-30% of their eggs directly on the water surface inside ovitraps under insectary conditions in Iran.
This study provides a reliable, low-cost model for rearing Ae. aegypti in research insectaries and facilitates future studies on vector control.

articles.titulo: Entomological survey for potential Anopheles malaria vectors and their insecticide resistance status in agricultural and peri-urban sites of Central and Southern Greece.
articles.autores: Balaska S, Parnassa V, … Kioulos I (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Greece has eliminated malaria for several decades now, however the ecological settings as being transformed in response to climatic crisis and the current geo-political situation may pose an epidemiological risk. Evidence on Anopheles vector species occurrence and their insecticide resistance (IR) profile in the country is limited and this study aims to narrow this gap. To this end, Anopheles collections were performed in selected agricultural and peri-urban sites throughout Greece, during 2021-2024. Α sub-set of the populations was assessed for their response to insecticides commonly used in the country, showing evidence of resistance to deltamethrin in Corinthia and Boeotia, and possible resistance for the Phthiotis collection, based on CDC guidelines, while all the characterized populations showed a tendency towards susceptibility to the bacterial larvicide Bti (WHO larval bioassays). A multi-locus DNA barcoding approach identified totally five Anopheles species, with distinct abundances and distribution patterns, including epidemiologically relevant malaria vectors, such as An. sacharovi, Αn. labranchiae and An. claviger. In parallel, monitoring of common pyrethroid resistance-associated mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene revealed the exclusive presence of the wild-type allele L1014. Lastly, a Plasmodium parasite detection assay was applied in the adult Anopheles specimens from Phthiotis producing negative results. In all, our survey updates the Anopheles species distribution map of central and southern Greece and provides valuable evidence on populations' IR status, to support future vector control targeted initiatives. The presence of malaria competent vector species, along with sporadic deltamethrin resistance records, stress the importance of systematic monitoring practices to maintain malaria transmission elimination.

articles.titulo: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations.
articles.autores: Piccinno R, Madec Y, … Malacrida AR (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Aedes albopictus is one of the world's most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. This study investigates whether and how the complex dynamics of these diverse genetic backgrounds have shaped variations in vector competence for CHIKV, DENV, and Zika (ZIKV) viruses.
Using highly polymorphic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers, we genotyped Ae. Albopictus samples from an ancestral population (Guangzhou, China) and ten adventive populations across five Mediterranean regions (Southern Switzerland, Northern/Central Italy, the Balkans, and Greece). Genetic ancestry and demographic histories were inferred using Bayesian STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) and DIYABC-RF. The association between population ancestry and vector competence for CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1, and ZIKV (PE243) was assessed using infection rate, dissemination efficiency, and transmission efficiency indices, analyzed via univariate and multivariate models.
Combining historical records with demographic models revealed that the establishment of Ae. Albopictus in the Mediterranean was driven by chaotic, discontinuous lineage introductions and admixture events, resulting in high spatial and ancestry heterogeneity. Notably, this genetic heterogeneity significantly influences vector competence, in particular for CHIKV and DENV. Interestingly, populations in neighboring geographical areas with distinct ancestries exhibited drastically different competence profiles, whereas geographically distant populations sharing genetic ancestry displayed similar vector competence for CHIKV and DENV.
Our findings demonstrate that the complex population dynamics and colonization history of Ae. Albopictus contributes to variation in vector competence, altering the geographical landscape of arboviral risk. These results underscore the urgent need for localized, geographically tailored vector control strategies in Europe, a region facing a rising trend of both imported and autochthonous arboviral infections.

Essa ancestralidade explica diferenças de competência para CHIKV e DENV: populações vizinhas com ancestrais distintos diferem muito; populações distantes com mesma ancestralidade se parecem.

v6.implicacao: Para Epidemiologia de Precisão: no estudo comparativo de competência vetorial de Aedes aegypti nos seis recortes do município, a ancestralidade genética da população local é um confundidor a medir antes de atribuir diferença de competência a ambiente ou Wolbachia.

articles.titulo: Profiling Histone Modifications in Harpegnathos saltator Brains by CUT&Tag.
articles.autores: Kuang M, Antonova A, … Bonasio R (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Harpegnathos saltator ants are a powerful model for studying socially induced adult brain plasticity. In this species, adult workers can transition into reproductive gamergates, which is accompanied by extensive behavioral, physiological, and gene regulatory changes arising from a single genome. Understanding the chromatin mechanisms that regulate these transitions requires epigenomic methods that are sensitive enough to profile small organs such as insect brains. Cleavage under targets and tagmentation (CUT&Tag) is a genome-wide chromatin profiling method that can be used to map histone modifications at high resolution from low-input samples by using an antibody-directed protein A/G-Tn5 transposase to perform targeted, in situ DNA tagmentation, substantially improving the signal-to-noise ratio compared with other chromatin profiling approaches. Here, we provide a CUT&Tag protocol that has been optimized for profiling histone modifications in Harpegnathos brains. We describe the steps for nuclei isolation from insect brains, followed by antibody incubation, transposase binding and tagmentation, and library preparation for high-throughput sequencing. This protocol is further adaptable to single-cell multiomic assays, enabling high-resolution profiling of the epigenomic landscape in social insect brains and other organs.

articles.titulo: NET-Inhibiting Bio-Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence.
articles.autores: Li F, Li X, … He XT (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Maladaptive trained immunity (MTI) establishes pathogenic innate immune memory that amplifies the immune response to recurrent chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, but erasing this memory remains challenging. In this study, we identified neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) as key mediators of periodontitis-induced MTI that reprogrammed bone marrow epigenetics and transcriptomics to amplify inflammation upon secondary challenge. Thus, we designed a NET-inhibiting bioengineered platform (tPA@AGNs-DNase I) to erase MTI and prevent recurrent inflammation. This platform was constructed by encapsulating tPA within activated gelated neutrophils (AGNs) and conjugating DNase I onto the surface by glycoengineering and click chemistry. Leveraging the inflammation-homing property of AGNs, the platform enabled co-delivery of two enzymes: DNase I degraded the DNA scaffold of NETs, while tPA disrupted fibrin‒neutrophil engagement to block NETosis, thereby achieving synergistic NET clearance. Local periodontal administration of tPA@AGNs-DNase I not only resolved primary inflammation but also reversed established MTI by restoring aberrant bone marrow epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming, thereby markedly attenuating recurrent hyperinflammation and alveolar bone loss in a religature-induced periodontitis model. Collectively, this work provides a bioengineered platform that erases central MTI via in situ NET clearance, offering a paradigm-shifting strategy to control chronic inflammatory disease recurrence.
