articles.titulo: From reactive control to precision environmental health: a One Health-based scoping review of vector management strategies in China
articles.autores: Guo X, Lin Q, … Guo L (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Climate change, urbanization, and global travel have accelerated the resurgence of Aedes-borne diseases, posing growing public health threats. Conventional vector control remains largely reactive and chemical-dependent and is increasingly challenged by climate-driven changes in vector habitats. Using China as a case study, this scoping review examines the shift toward precision environmental health under a One Health framework. We trace surveillance advances from manual vector indices to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled ecological sensing and examine multisource early-warning approaches integrating meteorological, biological, and human-related data for dynamic risk classification. We also consider how technological interventions, including drone-assisted precision control and biological control, can be integrated with social governance to support climate-resilient health systems. Drawing on these experiences, we propose a Layered Technology framework intended to support adaptable, environmentally sustainable vector management in resource-constrained settings, particularly in the Global South. Finally, we call for coordinated international data sharing and collaboration to address cross-border environmental and public health threats.

articles.titulo: Advancing a tool for Aedes aegypti breeding-site surveillance: validation of manual identification of trash and tires on unmanned aerial imaging
articles.autores: Woo KE, Tarpenning MS, … Rosser JI (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Trash accumulations and discarded tires can retain water and may provide habitat for Aedes aegypti, but the reproducibility of identifying and classifying these features from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery has not been established.
We evaluated manual trash mapping in two Kenyan settings, Ukunda and Kisumu. Raters delineated visible trash polygons on high-resolution UAV orthomosaics and assigned categories using a seven-category scheme and a collapsed three-group scheme (low-risk trash, high-risk trash, and tires). Classification agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha. Spatial inter-rater and intra-rater consistency were evaluated from polygon overlap and unique area metrics.
Pairwise inter-rater agreement for classification was strong (mean unweighted Cohen's kappa = 0.80, 95% CI 0.75-0.86; mean weighted kappa = 0.80, 95% CI 0.61-0.97). Three-rater Fleiss' kappa was 0.80 (95% CI 0.77-0.83) and increased to 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.93) for the collapsed risk groups. Standard and fuzzy Krippendorff's alpha values were 0.76 (95% CI 0.71-0.81) and 0.94 (95% CI 0.91-0.96), respectively. Spatial analyses showed overlap in major trash areas but meaningful differences in detection and boundary placement. Intra-rater feature-specific unique area ranged from 4.7 to 18.5%; pooled across all seven features, unique area was 31.1% (95% CI 29.8-32.4).
Manual interpretation of UAV imagery is reproducible for image-based identification and classification of visible trash and tires, particularly for visually distinctive features such as tires. The method measures potential habitat proxies rather than confirmed Aedes aegypti breeding productivity; entomological ground validation remains necessary. Standardized annotations may also support future automated image classification approaches.

articles.titulo: Needle in a haystack: Fluorescence-guided 3D targeting for FIB milling in high-pressure-frozen samples
articles.autores: Koczy O, Tollervey F, … Mattei S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rare subcellular structures are difficult to retain during lamella preparation for cryo-electron tomography, particularly in high-pressure-frozen specimens. Here we introduce two complementary workflows for three-dimensional fluorescence-guided milling on a commercial cryo-focused ion beam-scanning electron microscope with integrated fluorescence imaging. Iterative fluorescence correlation uses repeated rounds of imaging and milling to refine the target position, whereas bidirectional fluorescence correlation images a lifted-out block from two orthogonal directions. We validated both by targeting centrosomes in waffle-frozen early Caenorhabditis elegans embryos, each of which occupy approximately 0.007% of the embryo volume. We recovered recognizable centrosomes in 83% and 67% of lamellae examined by transmission electron microscopy, respectively, compared with 25% using a refined, 2D-guided high-throughput SOLIST workflow, run as a benchmark. Neither method requires hardware modification or fluorescent fiducial beads. These workflows provide accessible strategies for targeting rare subcellular structures during lamella preparation, with or without a lift-out hardware.

articles.titulo: In vitro evaluation of sliding contact wear performance in direct resin-based composites with varying inorganic filler loadings
articles.revista: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
articles.autores: Cinelli F, Rocca GT, … Saratti CM (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To evaluate the two-body wear performance and behavior of commercially available direct resin-based composites (RBCs) spanning a broad range of inorganic filler loadings.
144 disc-shaped specimens (5 mm × 2 mm) were prepared from six commercial RBCs selected according to manufacturer-reported filler loading (vol%): ELS (E), 49%; Tetric EvoCeram (T), 53-55%; Filtek Z250 (Z), 60%; Inspiro (I), 65%; Grandio (G), 71.4%; and Clearfil Majesty Posterior (M), 82%. Specimens underwent two-body wear testing in a dual-axis chewing simulator (CS-4.8) against stainless-steel antagonists (5°C/55°C, 49 N, 1.8 Hz) for 150,000, 300,000, or 600,000 cycles (n = 8/group). Volume loss was measured by confocal optical profilometry; digital microscopy and scanning electron microscopy provided qualitative assessment. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) estimated the inorganic filler mass fraction (wt%). Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA and linear regression (α = 0.05).
Volume loss increased with cycle count. Two-way ANOVA revealed significant effects of composite type and cycle count and a significant interaction (all p < 0.001). At 600,000 cycles, mean (SD) volume loss ranged from 2.896 (0.292) mm3 for Grandio to 6.502 (0.948) mm3 for ELS. Higher inorganic mass fractions were associated with lower volume loss at all cycle counts (p < 0.001; R2 = 0.234-0.655), with regression slopes differing across loading intervals (p < 0.001). Microscopy revealed subsurface microcracking; no micro-pitting was observed.
Under the tested conditions, wear performance differed significantly among the six commercial RBCs, and higher inorganic mass fractions were associated with lower volume loss. The independent contribution of filler content could not be isolated from other compositional and microstructural differences among the commercial formulations.

articles.titulo: Advances toward high-throughput and accurate mosquito age prediction using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) and artificial neural networks (ANNs)
articles.autores: Gao Z, Wu X, … He L (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Accurate mosquito age estimation is critical for vector surveillance and targeted disease intervention. In this study, we present a rapid, standardized sample preparation workflow combining 70% ethanol extraction, bead disruption, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), and artificial neural networks (ANNs) for predicting mosquito age. Solvent screening on 18-day-old mosquitoes established 70% ethanol as the optimal extraction medium. Across mosquitoes aged 3, 10, and 18 days, parallel bead disruption consistently yielded higher peak prominence-to-noise ratios than sequential sonication, markedly improving spectral definition. Crucially, parallel bead homogenization processed 12 specimens in 45 s compared to 12 min with sequential sonication, a 16-fold increase in disruption throughput. Initial spectrum-level ANN classification achieved 86.0% accuracy for a 3-age Aedes aegypti dataset (Thailand-origin; TH-origin), 92.7% for a 5-age Culex tarsalis dataset, and 84.2% for a 7-age Ae. aegypti dataset (Lakewood). Corresponding regression models demonstrated high predictive accuracy, with Pearson correlation coefficients (R) of 0.95-0.99 and root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 1.60-3.58 days. Further evaluation using three ordered hold-out splits with mosquito-level majority voting confirmed robust performance across multiple age classes. This streamlined workflow supports efficient batch preparation and accurate spectroscopic age prediction, providing a foundation for future field validation.

articles.titulo: Assessing the impact of absence of coordination in malaria intervention strategies: A modeling study
articles.autores: Iggidr Y, Ruktanonchai N, … Champagne C (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria control programs are increasingly tailored at subnational scales; however, neighboring areas remain connected through human mobility, allowing parasite importation that may undermine independently timed interventions. Although the spatial targeting of control has been the focus of extensive research, the epidemiological consequences of temporal misalignment in intervention deployment across interconnected regions remain to be elucidated. We investigate how asynchronous timing of malaria interventions affects transmission dynamics using a two-patch susceptible-infected-susceptible metapopulation model. We compare synchronous and asynchronous intervention schedules and quantify their impact using measures of excess cumulative incidence attributable to asynchrony. The measure that will be used for this purpose is referred to as Asynchrony-Induced Growth (AIG). Across a range of 10,000 parameter combinations, asynchronous implementation has generally been observed to result in higher incidence compared to synchronized deployment, though the impact is typically negligible in most endemic settings. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the impact is most significant when interventions are highly effective, infectious duration is brief, and transmission intensity approaches the elimination threshold. In such circumstances, asynchrony has the potential to substantially inflate case numbers, delay transmission interruption, or even prevent elimination entirely. In illustrative scenarios that reflect realistic settings, synchronizing interventions has been shown to avert large numbers of infections and shorten elimination timelines by years to decades. These findings demonstrate that, beyond spatial targeting, temporal coordination of interventions across connected areas can meaningfully enhance malaria control and elimination. Coordinated timing may be particularly valuable for cross-border or near-elimination programs and should be considered in operational planning and resource allocation.

articles.titulo: In silico evaluation of antimalarial compounds derived from the stem bark of Senegalia polyacantha (Willd.) Seigler & Ebinger (Fabaceae) against the validated target: Plasmodium falciparum prolyl-tRNA synthetase
articles.autores: Ouédraogo RJ, Leutcha PB, … Ditchou YON (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Our previous preliminary in vitro studies indicated that extracts and isolated compounds (1-24) from the stem bark of Senegalia polyacantha (S. polyacantha) exhibit antimalarial properties associated with cytotoxicity profiles that are suitable for subsequent in vivo investigations in animal models. Advancing these in vivo studies, however, requires prior insight into the potential mechanism of action of the plant's major chemical constituents. In this context, the present study was undertaken to assess the stability of chemical compounds isolated from the trunk bark of S. polyacantha against a validated therapeutic target for malaria. Twenty-four compounds (1-24) previously shown to be active against chloroquine-sensitive and multidrug-resistant strains of Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) were subjected to molecular docking using Maestro-13.9 against P. falciparum prolyl-tRNA synthetase (PfcProRS) (PDB ID: 7QC1). Their molecular dynamics (MD) were subsequently evaluated in GROMACS over 0.1 ns, 5 ns, and 110 ns to predict the most stable hits. Molecular docking on PfcProRS suggested that hits 6-10, 14, and 17-24 could interact favourably with the target (S <- 7 kcal/mol). During the 0.1 ns of simulation, hits 6-8, 10, and 22 were unstable (RMSD > 2 Å). At 5 ns, compounds 9, 19, and 23 also showed instability (RMSD > 3 Å). In silico cross-reactivity analysis shows that compounds 14, 17, 20-21, and 24 interact strongly with the Halofuginone binding site on Homo sapiens (Hs)ProRS, revealing a lack of clear selectivity at the initial docking level. Overall, these findings highlight compounds 14, 17, 20-21, and 24 as the most promising hits for rational structural optimization to engineer parasite-specific selectivity, and provide a theoretical rationale to support subsequent in vitro PfProRS enzyme inhibition assays compared to HsProRS, then in vivo studies to further assess their safety and therapeutic potential against malaria.

articles.titulo: Shikonin in Cardiovascular Inflammatory Injury: Immunometabolic Regulation, Mitochondrial Homeostasis, and Regulated Cell Death
articles.autores: Wang Y, Du L, … Gao W (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cardiovascular inflammation is sustained by reciprocal changes in immune-cell metabolism, mitochondrial function, and stress-responsive cell death. Shikonin, a naphthoquinone derived from the roots of Lithospermum erythrorhizon and related medicinal plants, is widely used experimentally as an inhibitor of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) and also modifies redox and stress-response signaling. Cardiovascular studies now extend from endothelial cells and vascular smooth muscle cells to experimental atherosclerosis, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardiac remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, cardiotoxicity, and thrombosis. The strongest cardiovascular evidence concerns PKM2-dependent glycolysis: shikonin suppresses inflammatory metabolic activation in macrophages and lymphocytes, reduces foam-cell formation and vascular smooth muscle-cell proliferation, and attenuates metabolic remodeling in cardiac and pulmonary vascular models. Mitochondrial membrane potential, reactive oxygen species, NRF2-dependent antioxidant responses, and fission-related proteins are also responsive to shikonin in cardiovascular models. Apoptosis and inflammasome-associated signaling show context-dependent activity, while other regulated cell-death pathways require interpretation within the specific experimental system. Emerging liposomal and hydrogel formulations offer avenues for tissue-selective delivery, with vascular reactivity and hemostatic safety central to cardiovascular translation. Overall, shikonin represents a promising preclinical scaffold for immunometabolic modulation and formulation-specific cardiovascular investigation.

articles.titulo: Quantifying Organelle-Specific Membrane Lipid Dynamics at the Cell Population Scale Using Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer-Based Biosensors
articles.autores: MacKenzie SN, Oh C, … Pemberton JG (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET) is a versatile live-cell technique that can monitor molecular interactions with high spatial and temporal resolution. By enabling the detection of transient or weak interactions that are difficult to capture using conventional biochemical or imaging methods, BRET is particularly powerful for detecting membrane lipid dynamics using the expanding palette of lipid-sensitive protein domains. Among the major classes of structural and signaling lipids, polyphosphoinositides (PPIns) are particularly important for coordinating cellular metabolism and membrane homeostasis. As a result, this chapter outlines the design principles, experimental applications, and basic workflow for a unique detection strategy called bystander BRET. This technique facilitates the kinetic measurement of PPIn levels at specific organellar compartments by combining a membrane-targeted fluorescent resonance energy transfer (RET) acceptor with a complementary bioluminescent RET donor, which is tagged to a PPIn-specific lipid-binding domain. Overall, bystander BRET-based approaches enable the real-time quantification of localized PPIn dynamics, enzymatic activity, or molecular complex formation, making them powerful tools for studying membrane and PPIn biology in living cells.

articles.titulo: Lactate-Lactylation Signaling at the Macrophage-Disc Cell Interface: Immunometabolic Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities in Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
articles.autores: Li H, Zheng J, … Feng M (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) develops within an avascular, hypoxic, and lactate-rich microenvironment in which metabolic stress converges with cellular senescence, ferroptosis, oxidative injury, and chronic inflammation. Lactate is not only a glycolytic end product and signaling metabolite but also a substrate for lysine lactylation. This narrative review evaluates lactate-driven lactylation at the macrophage-nucleus pulposus (NP) cell interface and distinguishes disc-supported findings from correlative observations and cross-tissue mechanistic inference. Disc studies link AMPKα lactylation to impaired autophagy and senescence; H3K18 lactylation and ACSL4 K412 lactylation to ferroptosis; THBS1-associated H3K18 lactylation to inflammatory transcription; and SOD1 K123 lactylation to defective antioxidant defense. No study using intervertebral disc tissue has yet demonstrated NP-to-macrophage lactate transfer, lactate-induced lactylation in disc macrophages, or a complete macrophage-NP feed-forward loop. The possible reprogramming of disc macrophages by NP-derived lactate is therefore inferred mainly from other hypoxic and inflammatory tissues and requires direct testing in disc models. These observations motivate a proposed bidirectional lactate-lactylation interaction as a testable model while distinguishing disc-supported NP-intrinsic mechanisms from an unresolved immune arm. This framework highlights pharmacologically tractable nodes in lactate production and transport, lactylation writers and erasers, ACSL4-dependent ferroptosis, SOD1 dysfunction, senescence, and macrophage state control. It also emphasizes the risks of suppressing physiological NP glycolysis and the need for disc-restricted delivery. Cell-type-resolved validation in human tissue will be essential before lactylation-directed interventions can be translated into disease-modifying therapy.

articles.titulo: Protection Against Rabies Virus by a Bacterium-Like Particle-Based Subunit Vaccine Displaying the Glycoprotein
articles.autores: Cong H, Li J, … Feng N (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic disease caused by the rabies virus (RABV) and remains a major global public health concern. Although currently available rabies vaccines provide reliable protection, their widespread application is limited by complicated immunization schedules and relatively high production costs. Therefore, the development of safe, effective and economically accessible next-generation vaccines is urgently needed. In this study, we developed a novel rabies subunit vaccine based on a bacterium-like particles (BLPs) delivery platform. Recombinant RABV glycoprotein fused with a peptidoglycan anchor protein (G-PA) was expressed in insect cells using the baculovirus expression system and successfully displayed on the surface of BLPs, generating the G-BLPs vaccine candidate. Surface localization of the recombinant G protein was confirmed by transmission electron microscopy and western blot analysis. Immunization in mice demonstrated that both G-BLPs and adjuvant-formulated G-BLPs (Adj-G-BLPs) induced high titers of virus-neutralizing antibodies, reaching 13.25 IU/mL and 27.25 IU/mL, respectively, together with enhanced T-cell cytokine responses. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed significant enrichment of the IL-17 signalling pathway and marked upregulation of Ccl2, indicating activation of multiple immune-related pathways. Both G-BLPs and Adj-G-BLPs provided complete protection against RABV CVS-24 challenge and significantly reduced viral loads in brain tissues. These findings demonstrate that the BLP-based platform can effectively display the RABV glycoprotein and induce both humoral and cellular immune responses, offering a promising and potentially scalable strategy for the development of next-generation rabies vaccines.

articles.titulo: Rapidly Progressive and Severe Hemolytic Anemia Associated With Epstein-Barr Virus: A Case Report
articles.autores: Torijano A, Tole MC, … Vigoda I (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is rarely associated with severe hemolytic anemia. We report a case of a 41-year-old woman with sickle cell trait who developed rapidly progressive hemolytic anemia following travel to Guinea. She presented with fever, jaundice, abdominal pain, and splenomegaly. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe hemolysis, with hemoglobin declining from 11.4 g/dL to 4.6 g/dL, complicated by hemodynamic instability and acute kidney and liver injury. Despite a reported history of malaria, repeated blood smears and Plasmodium polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing were negative. The initial direct antiglobulin test (DAT) was negative, but repeat testing became positive for complement C3d, while cold agglutinin testing remained negative. EBV serology and polymerase chain reaction findings raised suspicion for EBV-associated hemolysis, although a definitive causal relationship could not be established. The patient required multiple red blood cell transfusions, corticosteroids, and supportive care, with gradual clinical improvement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of severe hemolytic anemia with evolving immunohematologic findings. It emphasizes the importance of repeat DAT testing and the consideration of EBV as a potential associated infection.

articles.titulo: SEVI fibrils are induced by bacterial surface molecules and exert antimicrobial activity against ESKAPE pathogens
articles.autores: Vogel V, Olari LR, … Spellerberg B (18 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Semen-derived enhancer of viral infection (SEVI) is an amyloid fibril formed from PAP248-286, a fragment of prostatic acid phosphatase naturally occuring in seminal plasma. Beyond its role in HIV transmission, SEVI may contribute to innate immunity. Since many amyloids display antimicrobial effects, we investigated its antibacterial activity against ESKAPE pathogens and urogenital bacteria.
We evaluated SEVI's antibacterial activity in radial diffusion and survival assays against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella quasipneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, Streptococcus agalactiae, Listeria monocytogenes, Staphylococcus aureus, and Enterococcus faecium. The role of fibril structure was examined using epigallocatechin gallate, while lipopolysaccharide and lipoteichoic acid induced fibril formation was evaluated kinetically. Mechanisms were investigated through electron microscopy, membrane-disruption assays, and analysis of intracellular polyphosphate granules.
SEVI exhibited direct, dose-dependent antibacterial activity against most ESKAPE pathogens, at concentrations estimated to occur in seminal plasma. Lipopolysaccharides and lipoteichoic acid induced SEVI fibril formation, whereas epigallocatechin gallate abolished antibacterial activity, indicating that fibrils are required. Electron microscopy showed limited membrane disruption and intracellular polyphosphate granule accumulation in some P. aeruginosa cells, suggesting bacterial stress.
SEVI may have a physiological antimicrobial function in addition to its role in HIV transmission. Its activity against urogenital pathogens suggests a potential contribution to vaginal mucosal innate immunity. The dependence on fibril structure and induction by bacterial surface molecules imply that bacteria may promote formation of an antimicrobial SEVI conformation. Limited membrane damage and polyphosphate granule accumulation suggest that SEVI acts partly through intracellular stress responses rather than extensive membrane lysis. Further studies should clarify its molecular mechanism and in vivo relevance.

articles.titulo: A rare imported mixed Plasmodium falciparum and P. malariae infection: The indispensable role of microscopy. A case report
articles.autores: Yapalak ZL, Bedir O, … Koru Ö (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria remains a clinically important diagnosis in non-endemic countries, where mixed-species infections are easily overlooked. We report an 18-year-old man who presented with a four-day history of intermittent fever after returning from Guinea and developed marked thrombocytopenia (platelet nadir 64,000/mm³). A rapid diagnostic test was positive only for Plasmodium falciparum; however, microscopic examination of thin and thick blood films revealed a mixed infection with both P. falciparum and P. malariae. The patient was treated with artemether-lumefantrine plus single-dose primaquine and recovered fully. This case underscores that microscopy remains indispensable for detecting mixed Plasmodium infections that rapid diagnostic tests may miss, ensuring complete species identification and appropriate management.

articles.titulo: Regioselective esterification of ginsenoside Rg_1_ yields anti-DENV derivatives with reduced viral NS3 expression
articles.autores: Chen H, Pang P, … He YP (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus (DENV) poses a major global health burden, and clinically approved antiviral drugs remain scarce. Leveraging a regioselective esterification strategy of ginsenoside Rg1, we synthesized nineteen derivatives (I1-I19) and evaluated their anti-DENV-2 activity using the New Guinea C strain. Among them, I6 and I17 reduced extracellular DENV RNA levels in Vero cells, with the responses approaching a non-zero plateau at higher concentrations, with EC50 values of 17.77 ± 2.79 μM and 5.50 ± 0.70 μM (ribavirin, the assay control: 98.35 ± 5.84 μM). The compounds also showed low cytotoxicity, with CC50 > 400 μM. Western blotting and immunofluorescence assays demonstrated that both compounds reduced DENV NS3 protein expression in infected cells. These results identify I6 and I17 as promising Rg1-derived anti-DENV candidates and provide a foundation for further optimization of natural-product-derived antiviral scaffolds.

articles.titulo: Storage-enabled microbiomes for low-carbon wastewater treatment: Linking carbon capture and retention to electron allocation and process control
articles.autores: Wang H, Weng H, … Peng Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Carbon-limited wastewater treatment is often interpreted as a shortage of biodegradable organic matter, yet treatment performance also depends on when influent carbon is captured, how long it is retained, and how effectively its reducing equivalents are directed to target reactions. Intracellular storage decouples substrate uptake from later electron use by retaining carbon as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) and glycogen, while polyphosphate cycling supports energy conservation and phosphorus transformations. This Review develops a mechanistic framework for storage-enabled microbiomes in low-C/N wastewater treatment. We distinguish three constraints that can be hidden by similar bulk C/N ratios: insufficient electron inventory, premature carbon loss, and weak coupling between reserve mobilization and terminal respiration. We then connect reserve turnover with central metabolism, respiratory electron carriers, denitrifying reductases, and community-level division of labour. Across post-anoxic denitrification, partial denitrification-anammox, denitrifying phosphorus removal, sulfur-assisted nitrogen removal, and PHA recovery, process performance depends on matching reserve formation, retention, and mobilization with reaction-specific electron and energy demand. We further establish an evidence framework that separates temporal association, stoichiometric plausibility, population or pathway assignment, and perturbation-supported causality. By strengthening intracellular carbon accumulation, preserving reserve-derived electron potential across redox stages and directing subsequent electron release toward target reactions, storage-enabled microbiomes can improve the effective utilization of influent carbon under low-C/N conditions. The engineering benefits of this strategy should be evaluated through nutrient-removal performance, nitrogen-product profiles, N₂O emissions, aeration demand, sulfate and alkalinity balances, sludge production, resource-recovery trade-offs, and disturbance resilience.

articles.titulo: Aqueous Extract of Guiera senegalensis J. F. Gmel. Galls (Combretaceae) Improves Malaria-Induced Cognitive Abnormalities in Suppressive Study: A Pilot Investigation
articles.revista: Advances in pharmacological and pharmaceutical sciences
articles.autores: Walbadet L, Gounoue R, … Boyom FF (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cerebral malaria is the deadliest complication of malaria, and the treatment remains a great challenge for the control of the disease. Galls from the plant Guiera senegalensis are currently used in traditional medicine for treating symptoms associated with cerebral malaria. This study aimed to scientifically validate the traditional use by investigating the suppressive antiplasmodial and neuroprotective effects of the aqueous extract of the G. senegalensis galls in a rat model of malarial infection induced by Plasmodium berghei ANKA in rats. The in vitro antiplasmodial activity was assessed against Plasmodium falciparum strains PfDd2 and Pf3D7 using the SYBR-green assay. Cytotoxicity was determined on Vero cells. Antioxidant effects were evaluated using DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP radicals. The in vivo suppressive test was conducted on infected male Wistar rats, followed by nervous behavioral analysis (Y-maze and novel object recognition test). Biochemical analyses measured oxidative stress markers and the neurotransmitters acetylcholine (ACh) and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) in the brain. Annotated compounds were characterized using UHPLC/MS analysis. The extract exhibited potent in vitro antiplasmodial activity with inhibitory concentrations 50 of 5.84 ± 0.94 μg/mL and 5.48 ± 0.95 μg/mL to PfDd2 and Pf3D7, respectively. The extract showed low cytotoxicity against Vero cells (CC50 > 250 μg/mL), resulting in a high selectivity index (SI > 43). Antioxidant effects on radicals tested were observed. In vivo, the extract significantly suppressed (p < 0.001) parasite growth, achieving inhibition percentages of 83.79% (350 mg/kg) and 84.50% (700 mg/kg) by Day 8 postinfection, and prevented (p < 0.001) the occurrence of neurological damage of malaria infection. Furthermore, extract significantly protected animals from plasmodium-induced memory and behavioral disorders (p < 0.001) by increasing the concentration of the neurotransmitters Ach and GABA in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus. Treatment also restored oxidative status and reduced histopathological damage in brain tissues. Bioactive compounds annotated, including β-amyrin, vanillic acid, epigallocatechin, epigallocatechin 3-O-gallate, flavone, and rhamnetin, are thought to mediate these effects. These results conclusively indicate that the aqueous extract of G. senegalensis galls possesses significant dual antiplasmodial and neuroprotective properties, primarily by mitigating neurological deficits associated with cerebral malaria. This provides preliminary evidence supporting its traditional use and potential as a source for new drug leads.

articles.titulo: Multi-omics and single-cell profiling characterize the protective effects of indole-3-acetic acid in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury
articles.revista: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.autores: He Y, Guan Z, … Guo W (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of liver dysfunction after hepatic surgery and transplantation. Sterile inflammation, myeloid-cell recruitment, and metabolic disturbance contribute to hepatic IRI, but effective immunometabolic interventions remain limited. Indole-3-acetic acid (3-IAA) is a natural plant auxin found in Arabidopsis thaliana shoot apices and young leaves and is also produced by microorganisms. Whether 3-IAA affects hepatic IRI is unknown.
We integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling to identify changes associated with hepatic IRI. We then evaluated 3-IAA pretreatment in a murine hepatic IRI model. Serum transaminases and histopathology were used to assess liver injury. CyTOF and single-cell RNA sequencing characterized immune-cell composition, functional signatures, and inferred intercellular communication.
Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified 3-IAA among the metabolites showing lower hepatic abundance after IRI. 3-IAA pretreatment lowered alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels and reduced histological injury. CyTOF showed lower relative abundances of macrophages and neutrophils after 3-IAA treatment. Single-cell analysis identified fewer Ero1a+Bnip3+ macrophages and more C1qa+C1qb+ macrophages. These changes were accompanied by differences in maturation- and phagocytosis-related signatures. Neutrophil-associated transcriptional programs and inferred CCL, CXCL, MIF, TNF, complement, and galectin signaling also differed between groups.
Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified lower hepatic 3-IAA abundance after IRI, and pretreatment with exogenous 3-IAA attenuated liver injury in mice. Protection was associated with changes in macrophage and neutrophil abundance, cell states, and inferred immune communication.

articles.titulo: Study on the mechanism of Yishen Tongluo Formula in improving asthenospermia based on mitochondrial autophagy dysfunction induced by oxidative stress
articles.autores: Li X, Zhu Z, … Yuan Z (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
This study explored the mechanism by which Yishen Tongluo Formula improves asthenospermia (AS) based on oxidative stress-induced mitochondrial autophagy dysfunction.
Serum pharmacochemistry was used to identify the blood-entering components of Yishen Tongluo Formula. A tripterygium glycosides (TG)-induced rat model of AS was established, and rats were treated with low, medium, or high doses of Yishen Tongluo Formula. Western blotting and quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to detect the protein and mRNA expression levels of oxidative stress- and mitophagy-related markers. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to observe the mitochondrial ultrastructure of Sertoli cells.
Eighty blood-entering components were identified, mainly including terpenoids and flavonoids. Yishen Tongluo Formula improved the gonadal index, sperm quality, and seminiferous tubule morphology in TG-induced AS rats. Compared with the model group, Yishen Tongluo Formula restored testicular mass, testicular index, testicular volume, epididymal mass, and epididymal index to varying degrees, increased sperm concentration, sperm motility, and number of progressively motile sperm, and decreased number of immotile sperm (P<0.05). It also increased the Johnsen score and seminiferous tubule diameter (P<0.05). Mechanistically, Yishen Tongluo Formula upregulated superoxide dismutase 2, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), and heme oxygenase-1 expression (P<0.05). Meanwhile, it downregulated PTEN-induced putative kinase 1 (PINK1), Parkinson disease protein (Parkin), microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3, and lysosomal-associated membrane protein 2 and upregulated sequestosome 1 (P<0.05), suggesting that it may inhibit excessive mitophagy. TEM showed improved mitochondrial ultrastructure.
Yishen Tongluo Formula may improve sperm motility by regulating the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense system and the PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy pathway, providing an experimental basis for treating AS with traditional Chinese medicine.

articles.titulo: Resolving the Role of Phosphoinositides in Cell Migration
articles.autores: Mehrabi A, Camardi C, … Antonescu CN (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cell migration is fundamental to development and adult tissue homeostasis, while also central to progression of diseases such as cancer. Many different cellular processes contribute to cell migration, including focal adhesion complex dynamics, cytoskeleton dynamics, membrane traffic, and signaling. Notably, each of these processes is critically regulated by specific phosphoinositides, including phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate, phosphatidylinositol-3,4-bisphosphate, phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate, and phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate. Understanding the cell physiological implications and impact of phosphoinositide dynamics relies on the ability to measure a range of cell behaviors, among the most important being cell migration. Here, we describe a method for measuring two-dimensional cell migration based on tracking cells with a fluorescent nuclear stain. This method allows systematic resolution of the impact of perturbations of phosphoinositide dynamics on cell migration.

articles.titulo: Molecular Diagnosis of Rickettsial Meningoencephalitis With Concurrent Herpes Simplex Virus Type 2 Infection in a Young Female Presenting With Acute Febrile Encephalopathy: A Report on a Rare Case
articles.autores: Chichhal K, Dwivedi A, … Pandey P (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rickettsial CNS infections have been increasingly reported in tropical countries, including India, and are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Early diagnosis is challenging due to nonspecific presentations, absent rash/eschar, and limited sensitivity of conventional serological tests in the acute phase. Concurrent CNS infection with herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) is exceedingly rare and further complicates clinical diagnosis and management.  This report presents the case of a 28-year-old previously healthy female from Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, who presented with a 10-day history of intermittent fever, headache, vomiting, decreased appetite, and progressively worsening altered sensorium. Four days before admission, she developed recurrent seizure-like episodes characterized by upward deviation of the eyeballs and jaw clenching. On admission, a neurological examination revealed a Glasgow coma scale (GCS) score of E2V2M5 with neck rigidity suggestive of meningeal irritation. Owing to progressive neurological deterioration and impaired airway protection, she required endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. Laboratory investigations demonstrated mild neutrophilic leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, elevated alanine aminotransferase levels, and hypoalbuminemia. A CSF analysis revealed normal glucose and protein concentrations with minimal pleocytosis, while Gram stain and bacterial cultures were negative. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) and MRI demonstrated only a small calcified occipital granuloma without evidence of acute inflammatory changes. Extensive investigations for common bacterial and tropical infections, including malaria, dengue, enteric fever, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and bacterial meningitis, were negative. Multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) performed on peripheral blood detected Rickettsia spp. DNA. Subsequent molecular analysis of CSF also demonstrated Rickettsia spp. DNA, confirming CNS involvement, while real-time PCR simultaneously detected HSV-2 DNA, establishing the diagnosis of concurrent Rickettsia spp. meningoencephalitis and HSV-2 encephalitis. The patient initially received empirical intravenous ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir. Following molecular confirmation of Rickettsia spp. infection, doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) was initiated while antiviral therapy was continued. The patient demonstrated progressive neurological improvement with recovery of sensorium and a favorable clinical outcome. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges associated with rickettsial CNS infection, particularly in patients lacking classical clinical features and presenting with normal CSF biochemistry and nonspecific neuroimaging findings. Simultaneous molecular detection of Rickettsia spp. in peripheral blood and CSF together with HSV-2 in CSF emphasizes the importance of considering mixed infectious etiologies in patients presenting with acute febrile encephalopathy. Early application of molecular diagnostics enabled prompt institution of targeted therapy and contributed to successful clinical recovery. To the best of our knowledge, this represents one of the very few reported cases of concurrent molecularly confirmed Rickettsia spp. meningoencephalitis and HSV-2 encephalitis worldwide and is likely the first such case reported from India.

articles.titulo: Compatibility and Insecticidal Responses of Bacillus thuringiensis in Tank Mixtures with Spray Adjuvants against Spodoptera frugiperda
articles.autores: Peterlini E, Machado FP, … da Costa Ferreira M (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda, is a major agricultural pest whose management increasingly relies on Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)-based bioinsecticides. However, tank-mix applications with adjuvants may alter Bt performance. This study evaluated the in vitro compatibility of Bt (Xentari) combined with five commercial adjuvants (Li-700, Fighter, Wetcit Gold, Protac, and Tween 80) and compared the insecticidal responses of these mixtures in laboratory bioassays. In vitro compatibility was assessed using nutrient agar to determine vegetative growth and sporulation, while pH variation was measured in laboratory spray solutions over time. Insecticidal response was evaluated through bioassays on artificial diet with second-instar S. frugiperda, using two complementary approaches: spore suspensions derived from in vitro assays and laboratory assays with spray solutions applied at 0, 2, 6, and 24 h after preparation. Tween 80 increased vegetative growth, whereas Li-700 reduced vegetative growth but enhanced sporulation. Wetcit Gold and Protac completely inhibited Bt development in vitro. Protac reduced solution pH below 2.5, indicating strongly acidic conditions. Under the laboratory conditions evaluated, microbiological compatibility observed in vitro did not consistently correspond directly to the insecticidal responses obtained in the artificial-diet bioassays. All Bt-containing spray solutions resulted in final mortality above 80%. Within the Wetcit Gold treatment, final mortality at 2 h was lower than at 6 and 24 h, while no significant differences among Bt-containing treatments were detected within individual resting times. These findings indicate that microbiological compatibility assays and laboratory bioassays provide complementary information for interpreting Bt-adjuvant interactions.

articles.titulo: [Common mechanisms and protective strategies against cardiomyocyte injury induced by three multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors]
articles.revista: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.autores: Yang ZM, Liu D, … Han YL (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Objective: To investigate the common mechanisms of cardiomyocyte injury induced by three multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI)-sunitinib, sorafenib, and regorafenib. Methods: The GSE146096 dataset was obtained from the GEO database, and differentially expressed genes (DEG) in cardiomyocytes treated with the three TKIs were extracted. Overlapping DEGs were subjected to GO functional enrichment and KEGG pathway analyses. The common DEGs were intersected with an endoplasmic reticulum stress-related gene set to screen for intersecting genes. H9C2 rat cardiomyocytes were treated with different concentrations of sunitinib, sorafenib, and regorafenib, with cells treated with an equal volume of dimethyl sulfoxide as the control group. Cell viability was detected by the CCK-8 assay; Western blotting was used to detect the expression levels of key endoplasmic reticulum stress proteins (binding immunoglobulin protein (BIP), C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), and activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4)); and the ultrastructure of the endoplasmic reticulum was observed under a transmission electron microscope. Functional rescue experiments were performed using the endoplasmic reticulum stress inhibitor 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) and the nuclear protein 1 (NUPR1) inhibitor ZZW-115. Western blot and real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) were used to examine the protein and mRNA expression levels of the common regulatory target NUPR1. Results: A total of 248 common DEGs were identified among the three TKIs, and enrichment analysis showed that the DEGs were mainly enriched in protein folding disorder-related pathways. CCK-8 assay results showed that after treatment of H9C2 cells with sunitinib, sorafenib, and regorafenib, cell viability was lower than that of the control group in a concentration-dependent manner. Transmission electron microscopy revealed ultrastructural damage typical of endoplasmic reticulum stress, including endoplasmic reticulum dilation and vesiculation. Western blot results showed that in H9C2 rat cardiomyocytes, compared with the control group, the protein expression levels of BIP, ATF4, and CHOP were higher in the sunitinib, sorafenib, and regorafenib treatment groups (all P<0.05). Functional rescue experiment results showed that the cell viability of the groups treated with drugs combined with different concentrations of 4-PBA was higher than that of the TKI-alone groups to varying degrees (all P<0.05). NUPR1 was the only intersecting gene. In H9C2 rat cardiomyocytes, quantitative PCR results showed that compared with the control group, NUPR1 mRNA levels were higher in the sorafenib and regorafenib groups (both P<0.05), while the sunitinib group showed an increasing trend but the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.145). Western blot results were consistent with the mRNA levels, and NUPR1 protein expression was also significantly upregulated in the sorafenib and regorafenib groups (both P<0.05), while there was no statistically significant difference between the sunitinib group and the control group (P=0.884). ZZW-115 treatment significantly restored the viability of damaged cardiomyocytes in the sorafenib and regorafenib groups (both P<0.05). Conclusion: All three TKIs could induce cardiomyocyte injury by activating endoplasmic reticulum stress, and inhibition of endoplasmic reticulum stress could effectively alleviate this toxic effect; NUPR1 may serve as an important molecular node mediating this common endoplasmic reticulum stress response.

articles.titulo: Double-Fluorescent Immunoblot Detection of Phosphoinositide-Protein Complexes
articles.autores: Chen M, Ren C, … Anderson RA (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Protein-lipid interactions, particularly those involving signaling phosphatidylinositol phosphate (PIP, also known as phosphoinositide), are fundamental to cellular regulation but remain technically challenging to study due to the low abundance and dynamic nature of lipids. In this chapter, we describe a comprehensive protocol that provides an integrated workflow to investigate specific protein-lipid interactions, such as those between a nuclear protein (e.g., p53) and PIP signaling lipids. The method begins with the culture and transfection of mammalian cells to express the protein of interest, followed by cell lysis and immunoprecipitation to isolate native complexes. Detection is achieved via a double-fluorescence immunoblot, which allows simultaneous, quantitative analysis of the immunoprecipitated bait protein and its associated lipid-binding partner from a single blot using spectrally distinct infrared dyes. This approach combines physiological relevance with biochemical validation and is particularly powerful for assessing dynamic interactions under different cellular conditions.

articles.titulo: Thiochromene Analogues as Antiparasitic Chemotype: Synthesis, Antiplasmodial and Antitrypanosomal Profiling, Experimental Validation, and Computational Insights into Trypanothione Reductase Inhibition
articles.autores: Malik J, Kirad S, … Sankaranarayanan M (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The emergence of drug resistance and the limited availability of effective therapeutics continue to hinder the treatment of protozoal diseases, highlighting the need for new chemotypes with broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. In the present study, a series of nitro and trifluoromethyl-substituted thiochromene carboxamides, previously identified as antileishmanial agents, were further explored for their broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. Biological screening identified several compounds with promising activity and favorable selectivity against Plasmodium falciparum (D10 and W2 strains) and Trypanosoma brucei (AnTat1.1E strain). As the synthesized analogues exhibited a more favorable antitrypanosomal activity and selectivity profile, representative analogues were subsequently evaluated for trypanothione reductase (TryR) inhibition to investigate their potential mechanism of action, as TryR is a validated and highly conserved drug target across kinetoplastid parasites. Among the synthesized molecules, compound 5p showed the highest antiplasmodial potency (D10 EC50 = 2.1 μM), whereas compounds 5c and 5r were the most potent antitrypanosomal analogues (EC50 = 1.8 μM). Structure-activity relationship analysis demonstrated that piperidine and piperazine-containing carboxamide is a key pharmacophoric feature for broad-spectrum activity, whereas incorporation of a nitro substituent enhanced the activity against T. brucei. To investigate the potential mode of killing, representative compounds were evaluated for inhibition of TryR, identifying compound 5v as the most potent enzyme inhibitor. Enzyme kinetic studies established an uncompetitive mode of inhibition (k i ≈ 29.5 μM), suggesting interaction at an allosteric site rather than the active catalytic site. Consistent with these findings, SiteMap analysis identified a druggable allosteric pocket at the dimer interface of substrate-bound TryR, where the active compounds exhibited favorable binding affinities and interaction profiles. Collectively, these results demonstrate that thiochromene carboxamides constitute a promising scaffold for the development of broad-spectrum antiprotozoal agents and support allosteric inhibition of TryR as a viable strategy for antitrypanosomal drug discovery.

articles.titulo: Emerging and Re-Emerging Viruses: Global Threats, Virological Mechanisms, and Preparedness Strategies
articles.autores: Shaheen MNF (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Emerging and re-emerging viral diseases represent one of the most significant threats to global health security in the 21st century. Viruses, and RNA viruses in particular, exploit distinctive evolutionary mechanisms-including high mutation rates, recombination, and reassortment-to cross species barriers, adapt to novel hosts, and achieve pandemic potential. This narrative review examines the virological underpinnings of viral emergence and re-emergence, with particular focus on RNA virus biology, host adaptation dynamics, zoonotic spillover events, and the anthropogenic drivers-deforestation, agriculture, mining, and urbanisation-that create opportunities for spillover. Evidence was identified through a structured narrative search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2000-October 2026). We analyse five case studies-SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (with emphasis on H5N1 in cattle), Ebola virus disease (including the 2026 Bundibugyo virus epidemic), Nipah virus, and Zika virus-to illustrate how genomic plasticity and ecological disruption interact to generate novel threats. The review critically evaluates the WHO R&D Blueprint priority pathogen framework-which prioritises viral threats including Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus, filoviruses, coronaviruses (MERS-CoV, SARS), henipaviruses (Nipah, Hendra), Lassa fever virus, Rift Valley fever virus, Zika virus, and the placeholder 'Disease X'-and assesses current global surveillance, genomic sequencing, artificial-intelligence (AI)-enabled analytics, and preparedness strategies. We identify critical gaps including inequitable access, fragmented One Health governance, underdeveloped broad-spectrum antiviral pipelines, and the uneven deployment of AI-enabled surveillance. We recommend integrating virological intelligence into pandemic preparedness frameworks to enable earlier and more targeted responses to emerging viral threats.

articles.titulo: Laser-Induced Graphene Modified with Gold Nanoparticles for Dengue Biomarker Detection: Toward Portable and Flexible Biosensing Platforms for Early Diagnosis
articles.autores: Teixeira da Silva T, Bernardes Sequalini I, … Vieira NCS (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue remains a major public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, where early detection can support timely clinical management. Nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), released during the acute phase of infection, is an important biomarker for early dengue detection. Here, we report a flexible electrochemical immunosensor based on laser-induced graphene (LIG), a hierarchically porous three-dimensional carbon material produced by laser irradiation of polyimide and functionalized with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) through a simple electroless deposition process. The incorporation of AuNPs reduced the impedance of the LIG electrode, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and increased the electrochemically accessible surface area. Structural, morphological, electrochemical, and surface wettability characterizations confirmed the successive modification steps of the sensing platform. The resulting biosensor exhibited a logarithmic response to DENV-2 NS1 over the experimentally evaluated concentration range of 10-1000 ng/mL, with a calculated limit of detection of 3.3 ng/mL. The sensor showed reproducible responses and low cross-reactivity toward Zika virus NS1 under the investigated conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining porous LIG and AuNPs for electrochemical NS1 detection and provide a basis for the further development of flexible electrochemical biosensors for dengue NS1 detection.

articles.titulo: Where the clone is selected: stage-specific selection from hematopoietic stem cells to plaque macrophages in clonal hematopoiesis
articles.autores: Ueno K, Nakayama Y (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) raises cardiovascular risk, yet the size of a clone in blood does not by itself explain how that clone contributes to disease. We argue that selection acts not once but at three dissociable checkpoints: competition among hematopoietic stem cells, myeloid lineage output, and entry, niche occupancy and local proliferation in tissue. Blood variant allele frequency (VAF), the measurement on which the clinical literature rests, is the product of the first two and therefore does not report the mutant fraction among stem cells; because lineage bias is gene-dependent, VAF-matched comparisons across drivers are not equivalent. Evidence from TET2, DNMT3A, ASXL1, JAK2 and Trp53 models shows that an advantage at one checkpoint need not carry to the next, and that the checkpoints separate gene by gene. At checkpoint 1, cardiovascular risk factors and tissue injury act on stem cells both directly and by remodeling the bone marrow niche, but whether cardiovascular stress selects mutant clones specifically through defined niche changes remains unresolved. At checkpoint 3, human cross-sectional data have not demonstrated preferential recruitment of mutant macrophages into cardiovascular tissue and cannot separate recruitment from retention, niche occupancy or local proliferation, and irradiated transplantation chimeras measure how a clone fills a vacated niche rather than how it competes for an occupied one. Existing pharmacology - canakinumab, colchicine, metformin - is read out at checkpoints 1 and 2 alone. Genotype-resolved, spatial and longitudinal measurements are needed to make the framework testable.

articles.titulo: SlitOBP9 contributes to cis-3-hexenol recognition and larval orientation in Spodoptera litura
articles.autores: Yao WC, Li JB, … Zhang YN (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cis-3-hexenol is a typical green leaf volatile (GLV) that plays an important regulatory role in plant-insect interactions. Spodoptera litura is a globally significant agricultural pest whose larvae cause severe damage to a wide range of crops, yet the olfactory molecular mechanism underlying larval recognition of this volatile has remained unclear. Two-choice behavioral assays showed that a low dose (0.1 µg) of cis-3-hexenol exerted a significant attractive effect on S. litura larvae. Tissue-specific expression analysis identified an odorant-binding protein, SlitOBP9, that is highly expressed in the larval antennae. Fluorescence competitive binding assays confirmed that SlitOBP9 binds cis-3-hexenol, with the highest binding affinity at neutral pH (7.4); binding capacity was lost under acidic (pH 5.0) or alkaline (pH 9.0) conditions. RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated silencing of SlitOBP9 significantly reduced larval chemotactic behavior toward cis-3-hexenol. Relative to siNC controls, siOBP9-injected larvae showed a marked decrease in food intake on maize and cabbage, together with highly significant reductions in body-weight gain, and frass production. These results indicate that SlitOBP9 contributes to the perception of cis-3-hexenol and provide a systematic account of the olfactory mechanism by which S. litura larvae recognize this ecologically important volatile. These findings may provide a basic mechanistic lead for future studies, but further work is needed before any practical pest-control application can be considered.

articles.titulo: miR-132-3p-Enriched Exosomes Modulate Axonal and Mitochondrial Markers in Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion Rats
articles.autores: Doozandeh Juibari A, Mortazavi Y, … Aboutaleb N (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological disability, but effective neural repair strategies remain limited. Mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-derived exosomes may offer therapeutic potential because of their low toxicity, limited immunogenicity, and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Among their bioactive cargo, miR-132-3p is implicated in axonal growth and neuronal survival. This study aimed to investigate whether miR-132- 3p-enriched exosomes improve early outcomes and modulate axonal and mitochondrial markers after experimental ischemic stroke.
In this randomized experimental animal study, 115 adult male Wistar rats were assigned to the sham, middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), exosome-treated (Exo), or miR-132-3p-enriched exosometreated (Exo-miR-132) groups (n=5 per group). Focal ischemia was induced by 90 minutes of intraluminal MCAO. Human umbilical cord MSC-derived exosomes were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and characterized using transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. miR-132-3p was loaded into exosomes by electroporation, with the optimal concentration selected based on brain Nefh expression. Animals received Exo or Exo-miR-132 intravenously at 0 and 24 hours after MCAO. At 48 hours, six behavioral assessments were performed. Infarct volume, BBB permeability, brain water content, and neuronal cell death were assessed, whereas axonal and mitochondrial markers were evaluated by immunofluorescence.
Exosomes showed characteristic morphology and expressed CD9, CD63, and CD81. The 5-nmol loading concentration produced the greatest increase in brain Nefh expression. Compared with Exo, Exo-miR-132 was associated with higher NF-H and mitofusin-2 expression and lower peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase D, cytochrome c, dynamin-1-like protein, and p21 expression. Exo-miR-132 also reduced infarct volume, BBB permeability, cerebral edema, neuronal cell death, and neurological deficits, with greater effects than Exo for several outcomes.
miR-132-3p-enriched exosomes modulated axonal regeneration-associated markers and mitochondrial fission/fusion balance, alongside reduced injury and improved early neurological outcomes. Direct evidence of axonal regrowth and long-term functional recovery requires further investigation.

articles.titulo: Microglial lipid metabolic reprogramming in ischemic stroke: temporal immunometabolic switches, lipid mediators, and therapeutic opportunities
articles.autores: Yiping J, Guang T, … Jiangwei S (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ischemic stroke begins as an acute vascular and bioenergetic event, but the later course of tissue injury and recovery is shaped by neuroinflammation in which microglia play a central role. Emerging evidence indicates that lipid metabolism is an under-integrated layer of microglial biology after stroke. This review proposes a temporal immunometabolic switch framework: in the acute phase, lipid storage and metabolic adaptation may help microglia tolerate excess fatty acids and contain injury, whereas in the chronic phase, unresolved lipid accumulation, cholesterol overload, and oxidized lipid signaling drive foamy microglia, defective resolution, and persistent neuroinflammation. We synthesize evidence on microglial lipid droplets, cholesterol metabolic reprogramming, phospholipid imbalance, sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling, and ferroptosis-related lipid peroxidation. On this basis we outline stage-specific therapeutic opportunities: limiting lipid peroxidation and inflammatory lipid mediator amplification acutely, promoting pro-resolving lipid mediator pathways and effective phagocytosis in the subacute phase, and restoring cholesterol turnover and lipid disposal, exemplified by CYP46A1 activation, during chronic recovery. Finally, we critically appraise the evidence underlying the protective-versus-detrimental interpretation of lipid droplets, discuss safety considerations of lipid-directed interventions, and propose how lipidomics-guided stratification could match lipid-directed therapies to the dominant lipid program at each disease stage.

articles.titulo: Accurate identification of medically important Aedes mosquito species using low-cost imaging and geometric wing morphometrics
articles.autores: Sauer FG, Jöst H, … Lühken R (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Accurate species identification is crucial to assess the medical and veterinary relevance of a mosquito specimen, but it requires high taxonomic expertise of the respective organism group and well-equipped laboratories. This study aimed to evaluate whether low-cost imaging in combination with geometric wing morphometrics can provide accurate identification of invasive, morphologically similar Aedes species. The right wings of 670 female specimens covering 184 Ae. aegypti, 156 Ae. albopictus, 166 Ae. j. japonicus and 164 Ae. koreicus, were dissected, mounted and photographed using a professional stereomicroscope (Olympus SZ61; Olympus, Tokyo, Japan) with a macro lens (Apexel-24XMH; Apexel, Shenzhen, China) attached to a smartphone (iPhone SE 3rd Generation; Apple Inc., Cupertino, CA, USA). The coordinates of 18 landmarks on the right wings were digitalized by a single observer for each image. In addition, the landmarks of 20 randomly selected specimens per species and imaging device were digitalized by six different observers to assess the degree of the observer error. The superimposed shape variables were used to compare the species classification accuracy of linear discriminant analysis (LDA), support vector machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost. In the single-observer landmark data, the LDA achieved the best classification results with a mean accuracy of 95% for landmarks from microscope images and 92% for those obtained from smartphone images. In the multi-observer landmark data, the reduction in the accuracy was more pronounced for smartphone images than for microscope images. This pattern was associated with a higher degree of observer error for smartphone images, as confirmed by a landmark-wise comparison across all landmarks. Geometric wing morphometrics provides a reliable method to distinguish the most common invasive Aedes species in Europe. Thereby, smartphones equipped with a macro lens provide adequate image quality and represents a cost-effective alternative to professional microscopes. However, due to the greater degree of observer variation for smartphone images, landmark coordinates for such images should ideally be collected by a single observer.

articles.titulo: Impact of a point-of-care rapid diagnostic test on the dengue diagnostic cascade in an emergency department in a non-endemic setting: A before-after study (RaDDEO)
articles.autores: Robin L, Foulongne V, … Boullé C (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Timely recognition of dengue is increasingly important in non-endemic regions, where imported viremic cases may trigger local transmission. We evaluated whether introducing a combined point-of-care rapid diagnostic test (RDT; NS1/IgM/IgG) shortened the time to dengue diagnosis in an emergency department; secondarily, we (a) assessed its impact on length of stay, admission and notification, (b) reconstructed the diagnostic cascade to identify excessive time lapses and missed opportunities, and (c) evaluated its diagnostic performance.
Single-center retrospective before-after study in Montpellier University Hospital, southern France. Adults undergoing dengue testing were compared between pre-RDT (10/2022-07/2024) and post-RDT (08/2024-05/2026) periods. The primary endpoint was the time from arrival to availability of the diagnostic result. RDT performance was assessed against the clinical diagnosis.
Among 88 patients (36 pre-, 52 post-RDT), 28 had dengue, all of them returning travelers, and 57% had sought healthcare before ED presentation. After RDT implementation, time to diagnosis decreased from 24.3 to 2.5 h (median gain 19.6 h, 95%CI 13.9-44.8; p < 0.001). The most time-consuming step was laboratory turnaround (median 25.6 h). While no significant differences were observed in terms of length of stay, hospital admission, and mandatory notification, the study was underpowered to assess these outcomes. RDT sensitivity was 100% and specificity 70.3%; all false positives were antibody bands, primarily in patients with imported malaria.
The RDT shortened time to diagnosis by 20 h without missing any cases of acute dengue. However, it did not accelerate downstream clinical or public-health processes, highlighting a need to raise frontline clinician awareness in view of ensuring timely notification.

articles.titulo: Epilepsy landscape in the Democratic Republic of Congo: A narrative review
articles.autores: Kazadi P, Adjoglo JU, … Sander JW (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epilepsy is a major public health problem in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), disproportionately affecting a young population in a context of limited resources. In this narrative review, we synthesise available epilepsy data from the DRC published between 1990 and 2025. No nationwide, population-based study has been conducted, and existing data come from heterogeneous sources, mostly hospital-based or small regional surveys. The overall epilepsy prevalence is estimated to be between 0.7 % and 1.8 % nationally, representing approximately 700,000 to 1,900,000 people living with epilepsy in a population of 105-109 million. The predominant epilepsy risk factors for epilepsy in DRC include perinatal encephalopathies, central nervous system infections, particularly cerebral malaria, neurocysticercosis, onchocerciasis, meningitis, and traumatic brain injuries. Recent clinic-based data suggest that the average age of seizure onset is 13.1 years +/- 11.2 years, with a wide range spanning from 5 days, and male-to-female ratios ranging from 1.1 to 1.9. Convulsive seizures dominate the clinical picture in the available series. The therapeutic gap remains considerable, with an estimated 75-80 % of people with epilepsy lacking access to appropriate care, a situation exacerbated by persistent sociocultural stigma, a shortage of neurologists (10 per 109 million inhabitants), and the scarcity of diagnostic and monitoring facilities. These findings underscore the urgent need for national management strategies that integrate prevention of avoidable causes, decentralised diagnostic services, improved access to antiseizure medication, and sustained community awareness campaigns.

articles.titulo: Prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis in patients with Sjögren disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.autores: Chen A, Luo Z, … Wang X (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Sjögren disease (SjD) and autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) may coexist, but the prevalence of AIH in SjD patients is unclear. This study investigated the prevalence and association.
Databases (Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, CNKI, Wanfang, CBMdisc, VIP) were searched up to November 14, 2025. Quality was assessed using NOS and JBI scales. Meta-analysis was performed with R 4.5.2 (PROSPERO: CRD420251233495).
Fourteen studies (3697 SjD patients) were included. Overall prevalence of AIH in SjD was 2.55% (95% CI: 1.52%-4.26%). Prevalence varied by study type (retrospective cohort: 4.58%, cross-sectional: 1.72%, prospective cohort: 1.67%) and by country (China: 6.16%, Japan: 2.51%, Spain: 2.49%). Stratified by SjD diagnostic criteria (1993 European, 2002 AECG) and AIH scoring (1993 IAIHG), prevalence was approximately 2%.
Prevalence of AIH in SjD patients varies significantly by study design and region. Early diagnosis and treatment of AIH may improve quality of life and prognosis in SjD patients.
This meta-analysis provides the first pooled estimate regarding the prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) in patients with Sjögren disease (SjD): 2.55% (95% CI 1.52%-4.26%; 14 studies, 3697 patients). Subgroup analyses indicated that AIH prevalence was influenced by study design, whereas estimates stratified by SjD and AIH diagnostic criteria were of similar magnitude (approximately 2%). Regional estimates showed numerical differences, but the differences were not statistically significant; the numerically higher estimates may reflect differences in genetic susceptibility, selection bias, environmental factors, and medical screening strategies, as well as referral and detection bias. Given the observational and largely cross-sectional design of the included studies, these estimates only motivate a hypothesis-generating immunometabolic framework, rather than permitting causal or mechanistic inference. In this framework, the liver may serve as a source of autoantigens through modifications of oxidation, glycosylation, and lipidation, including the hepatocyte β2GPI-PON1 axis; this mechanism remains to be tested in the SjD-AIH overlap.

articles.titulo: Genomic Epidemiology of Dengue Virus in Ivory Coast Reveals Five Decades of Viral Circulation with Repeated Introductions from Burkina Faso
articles.autores: Tao X, Kadjo HA, … Trovao NS (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue fever is a rapidly emerging mosquito-borne disease in Africa, yet the continent remains critically underrepresented in genomic surveillance efforts. This disparity is especially pronounced in West Africa, despite phylogenetic studies being concentrated in only a few countries, such as Burkina Faso. Within this broader regional gap, researchers have yet to systematically characterize the dengue virus (DENV) lineages circulating in the Ivory Coast. In this study, we present 24 newly sequenced DENV genomes from Ivory Coast, spanning serotypes DENV-1, DENV-2, and DENV-3, collected between 2017 and 2023. Combined with publicly available sequences, we assembled the most comprehensive dataset to date for the country. We performed maximum-likelihood and Bayesian phylogeographic analyses using global background datasets and reconstructed the spatial and temporal dynamics of dengue virus circulation in Ivory Coast. Our findings reveal multiple independent introductions of DENV into Ivory Coast, predominantly from neighboring Burkina Faso. We identify five introductions of DENV-1 between 2017 and 2019 and four introductions of DENV-2 between 2015 and 2016. DENV-3 showed two separate introductions, one in 2015 and another in 2018. Notably, we also identified an early DENV-1 introduction from India around 1977, suggesting long-distance historical viral movement likely linked to colonial and post-colonial military presence. These results underscore the need for sustained genomic surveillance to monitor viral evolution and inform regional public health responses aimed at controlling dengue outbreaks in West Africa.

articles.titulo: Origin tracing and detection lag in the first Aedes albopictus invasion of mainland Australia and a long-term genomic dataset of mosquito incursions
articles.autores: Schmidt T, Muzari O, … Ehlers G (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Proactive management of invasive species aims to prevent and eradicate new incursions before they establish. Genomic data can assist proactive management around how to deploy resources and when to change strategies, and has been used effectively in managing Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito) in the Australian Northern Peninsula Area over the past decade. This study characterises the first major incursion of Ae. albopictus on the Australian mainland, and contrasts this with long-term genomic monitoring of this species within the Torres Strait Islands (TSI). First, we genomically traced the mainland incursion, which was detected in Cape York, Queensland, to the nearest infested island, Muralug (Prince of Wales). Strong genetic drift patterns in the incursion are suggestive of recent inbreeding, and point to a lag between incursion and detection of at least two mosquito generations. This stands in stark contrast with incursions within the TSI, which showed no evidence of inbreeding, suggesting no detection lag in the TSI. We genomically traced n=63 incursions detected in the TSI between 2019-2026, including n=44 newly sequenced samples; this used an expanded reference databank containing samples from one island, Muralug, that had not been available in previous tracing. Including Muralug greatly improved tracing success from ~50% to 77.8-92.1%. We observed no reduction in tracing success when whole genome and reduced representation sequencing datasets were combined in analysis, indicating composite approaches are viable. Together these findings demonstrate the value of genomic databanks for long-term incursion monitoring, provided these capture a sufficient proportion of genetic variation.

articles.titulo: Chikungunya virus dynamics and persistence in body fluids-Nanning, Guangxi Province, China, 2025
articles.autores: Chen Y, Liang C, … Xu B (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
In 2025, China experienced its largest outbreak of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an acute infectious disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. This study aims to analyze the dynamic changes, developmental trends, and persistence of CHIKV in body fluids, based on infection data collected from Nanning, China.
A total of 506 specimens were longitudinally obtained from 53 hospitalized patients in Nanning, China. Positivity rates among different specimen types were compared using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, while the Kruskal-Wallis test was applied to evaluate differences in cycle threshold (Ct) values. To estimate the probability of viral detection, generalized estimating equations (GEE) were employed, and parametric survival analysis was conducted to examine the duration of viral persistence in human body fluids.
Serum had the highest positivity rate (81.20%), followed by plasma (72.50%), while urine (4.73%) and saliva (11.03%) were much lower. In the first four days following the onset of symptoms, the median Ct values for serum and plasma were lower compared to those for saliva and urine. According to GEE analysis, saliva showed the quickest decline in the likelihood of a positive test result, decreasing from 52.2% on day 1 to just 0.7% by day 7. Serum and plasma followed, with positivity rates dropping from over 85% on day 3 to around 30% by day 7. Urine consistently had low positivity rates and did not show a statistically significant relationship with the number of days since symptoms began. Parametric survival analysis indicated similar median durations of serum (5.8 days, 95% CI: 4.8-6.9) and plasma (5.8 days, 95% CI: 4.7-7.1), while saliva had a shorter median duration of 3.5 days (95% CI: 3.0-4.1). Urine was not included in this analysis due to an insufficient number of positive samples.
Blood is the preferred sample for detecting the chikungunya virus and accurately assessing the duration of the virus in the body; additionally, compared to urine, saliva is more sensitive for detecting the virus during the acute phase of the disease, which is important for subsequent transmission and public health control measures.

articles.titulo: The critical role of N-glycosylation in mediating arbovirus-host interactions
articles.autores: Wang L, Zhou H, … Zhao L (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Glycosylation is a major post-translational modification that regulates protein folding, stability, trafficking, and recognition in biological systems. During viral replication, many viruses exploit host glycosylation machinery to modify their own proteins and thereby shape virus-host interactions. Among the major forms of protein glycosylation, N-linked glycosylation has a particularly important role in viral glycoprotein folding, virion assembly, receptor engagement, membrane fusion, tissue tropism, vector competence, and immune evasion. Current studies have revealed diverse functions of viral protein glycosylation in the infection processes of several pathogens, including Zika virus, dengue virus, West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, duck Tembusu virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, and other medically or veterinary important arboviruses. Here, we review the biological significance of N-glycosylation in mediating interactions between arboviruses and their hosts, with emphasis on conserved mechanisms, virus-specific glycosylation sites and their contributions to viral replication, pathogenesis, host adaptation and immune escape. We also discuss unresolved questions and potential applications of glycosylation-targeted strategies in antiviral research and vaccine development.
