articles.titulo: In Situ Detection of Phosphoinositide-Protein Interactions Using Fluorescence Proximity Ligation Assay
articles.autores: Chen M, Tang Y, … Anderson RA (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The proximity ligation assay (PLA) is a well-established technique for detecting in situ interactions between two epitopes with high spatial resolution and specificity. Beyond its widespread application in studying protein-protein interactions, PLA has proven to be a powerful approach for characterizing and validating protein posttranslational modifications (PTMs) by combining one antibody directed against the protein of interest with another recognizing the modified residue. Building on this principle, PLA can be adapted to detect specific interactions between endogenous phosphoinositides, also known as phosphatidylinositol phosphates (PIPs), and their cognate binding proteins within cells. Notably, we have successfully and reproducibly detected nuclear PLA signals between PIPs and their effector protein p53, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of this approach. This method complements conventional strategies for studying PIP-protein interactions by providing precise subcellular localization and robust quantitative readouts. Here, we describe a fluorescence-based PLA protocol for detecting in situ PIP-protein interactions in cultured cells, which enables semi-quantitative assessment of signaling-regulated interactions.

articles.titulo: CsrA-dependent RNA accessibility landscapes prioritize new mRNA and sRNA targets and link CsrA to polyphosphate homeostasis
articles.autores: Buchser R, Taylor K, … Contreras LM (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The global RNA-binding protein CsrA (Carbon Storage Regulatory Protein A) regulates diverse physiological processes in Gammaproteobacteria, but the full set of RNAs through which it actuates and how they intersect with small RNA (sRNA) regulation and stress physiology remain incompletely defined. We asked how CsrA shapes RNA accessibility across 431 untranslated mRNA regions and 87 sRNAs in Escherichia coli. Using a previously published RNA accessibility profiling method (INTERFACE), we compared wild type and CsrA mutant (csrA::kan) strains. Permissive screening for accessibility peaks at GGA/AGA motifs nominated 87 5'UTRs, 32 3'UTRs and 28 sRNAs as candidate responsive RNAs but did not pass a permutation null (p=0.43), however it can be used to guide selection of candidates for validation. Eleven 5'UTRs had no prior experimental evidence, and all 3'UTRs and most sRNAs were nominated manually because of limited probe numbers in these targets. In reporter assays, six of nine RNAs tested showed CsrA-dependent expression (mdtE, ribB, patA, metC, ppk and proS) including three candidate activated-targets, although only two of five reporters from the primary candidate list responded. CsrA bound the sRNAs SsrA and RalA in vitro, and reporter assays suggested CsrA-dependent modulation of previously identified ArrS-ribB and GcvB-crp interactions. Mutating sequence elements in the ppk 5' UTR altered CsrA-dependent expression, and loss of CsrA-activity was associated with reduced polyphosphate and fewer Hfq-containing HP-bodies during nitrogen starvation. Together, these findings expand the CsrA regulon and its overlap with sRNA networks, and support accessibility profiling to prioritize RNA-binding protein targets for follow-up characterization.

articles.titulo: The Immune-Architectural Construction of Symbiont Niches in Insects
articles.autores: Lemaitre B, Li X (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Insects commonly harbor bacterial symbionts within diverse anatomical niches, including the gut lumen, midgut crypts, bacteriomes, and cuticular reservoirs. These specialized structures have long been viewed as passive containers, whereas immunity has been considered as means for host tolerance but not as a way of actively controlling symbiont populations. Here, we review studies on insect symbiont-niche formation, arguing that host anatomy and localized immunity are functionally inseparable components of a unified process of constructing a niche for symbionts. Drawing on comparative evidence from diverse insect systems -including flies, mosquitoes, tsetse flies, aphids, weevils, stinkbugs, bees, beetles, wasps, and others-, we present a framework integrating three primary modules: immune regulation and buffering, physicochemical niche properties, and symbiont-driven co-construction of the niche.

articles.titulo: Beyond urban ecology and evolution: socio-eco-evolutionary dynamics in insects and the importance of scales
articles.autores: Boullauazan Y, Govaert L, … Brans KI (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Urbanization drives rapid ecological and evolutionary change, creating opportunities for reciprocal feedback among insect phenotypes, ecological processes, and human societies. Yet, despite growing evidence for urban adaptation, empirical demonstrations of urban eco-evolutionary feedback remain rare, and their integration with societal processes is even less developed. Here, we review urban insect ecology and evolution through a socio-eco-evolutionary lens, focusing on pollinators, mosquitoes, and other indoor pests as particularly promising systems. Across these groups, urban environmental change can alter phenotypes through plasticity and evolution, with potential consequences for ecosystem services and disservices including pollination, biological control, pest outbreaks, and disease transmission. We propose a multiscale framework that separates but integrates biological organization, spatiotemporal extent, and urban scales. Phenotypic and evolutionary change can alter ecological processes and societal outcomes beyond the biological, urban, or spatiotemporal scale at which it arises, with resulting feedback propagating, dissipating, or being counteracted across scales. We introduce the concept of socio-eco-evolutionary hotspots, where phenotypic or evolutionary change meaningfully modifies ecological-societal feedback, and coldspots, where these feedback remain weak or fail to propagate. Linking urban insect eco-evolutionary dynamics to their societal consequences and governance scales provides a basis for identifying where biodiversity conservation, urban planning, pest management, and public-health interventions can most effectively shape urban socio-ecological outcomes.

articles.titulo: Biostable insect kinin mimetics in either blood or sugar meals deter feeding in the mosquito Aedes aegypti (L.)
articles.autores: Henriques-Santos BM, Pietrantonio PV (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In insects, kinins (leucokinins) regulate diverse physiological processes. Previously we found kinin mimetic 1728 elicits aversive behavioral responses in Aedes aegypti female mosquitoes of flying-, walking- or jumping away when offered in sucrose. The feeding effects of six insect kinin analogues with different EC50 on the recombinant mosquito kinin receptor, and containing aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) (1728, 1729, IK-Aib-12, IK-Aib-19, and IK-Aib-20) or β3-Pro (1460) for increased biostability, were investigated when offered in sugar or blood meals. We used a high-resolution, high-throughput feeding behaviors analysis device, the flyPAD, adapted for mosquitoes. Analogues 1728, IK-Aib-19, and IK-Aib-20 (1 mM) decreased the feeding behaviors towards both meals resulting in a reduction in sucrose volume ingested of 95%, 92%, and 33%, respectively, and reduced the volume of blood ingested by 95, 51 and 63%, respectively. Analogue IK-Aib-12 reduced blood volume ingested by 78%, having no effect on feeding behaviors towards sugar. Mimetics1728 and 1729 (1 mM) reduced the feeding behaviors towards blood, and the blood volume ingested by 95% and 91%, respectively. Analogues modulated feeding behaviors by mainly reducing the number of sips, feeding bursts, and activity bouts. Analogue 1728 reduced sugar volume ingested by 95% and its aversive behavioral effects were partially reversed by co-administration of a synthetic small molecule kinin receptor antagonist (SACC-0048555) that we discovered, as expected. However, the sugar volume ingested was still reduced by 73%. Co-administration of 1728 with suramin, a G protein decoupler, in contrast, restored both normal feeding behaviors and volume ingested. These results agreed with our previous finding that 1728 directly shuts down the sugar sensory neuron in the labella signaling through the kinin receptor, a GPCR.

articles.titulo: Blood-derived dietary protein promotes sleep in the mosquito Aedes aegypti
articles.autores: Zhang J, Tsujimoto H, … Keene AC (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Sleep is a ubiquitous, yet highly variable, behavior across species. The duration and timing of sleep are influenced by ecological demands and dietary context. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, a blood-feeding insect with specialized nutritional requirements, the relationship between feeding and sleep remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how blood-derived dietary protein influences sleep regulation. Using postural analysis, videography, and arousal-threshold assays, we established that immobility bouts of ≥10 min reliably define sleep in A. aegypti. Mosquitoes lacking the circadian clock gene cycle still maintained daily sleep rhythms but exhibited reduced sleep duration and heightened overall activity. Infrared activity monitoring revealed that blood-fed females showed a marked increase in sleep beginning immediately after feeding and persisting for several days, accompanied by reduced locomotor activity. Notably, this sleep elevation lasted well beyond the cessation of previously reported host-seeking phases, raising the possibility of distinct phases of opportunistic vs. targeted host pursuit. To determine the dietary basis of this effect, we tested mosquitoes fed a bovine serum albumin (BSA)-based diet. BSA feeding alone was sufficient to mimic the sleep-promoting and activity-reducing effects of blood, suggesting dietary protein is a major nutritional regulator. Moreover, RNAi-mediated knockdown of the leucokinin receptor (Lkr), which has previously been associated with fluid homeostasis and feeding behavior, resulted in enhanced sleep and reduced activity, implicating mosquito LK signaling in the modulation of postprandial sleep. Together, these findings demonstrate that blood-derived proteins drive sustained increases in sleep and reductions in locomotor activity in A. aegypti. This work positions A. aegypti as a model for dissecting nutrient-specific regulation of sleep and highlights potential adaptive functions of protein-induced quiescence, such as energy conservation and predator avoidance. More broadly, it provides insight into how specialized diets shape the neural and behavioral architecture of sleep.

articles.titulo: Assessment of natural filariae infections in the mosquitoes of Karen state, Myanmar: a cross-sectional PCR survey in six villages
articles.autores: Rongthong P, Kularbkeeree T, … Nosten F (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Filarial nematodes transmitted by mosquitos cause significant burdens and important stigma in the affected communities. Focal transmission of Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi was detected incidentally during blood surveys conducted for a program of malaria elimination in Karen state, Myanmar. The objective of this study was to assess filariae infections in selected mosquito species collected in these villages striving to identify the potential vectors, characterise their biting behaviours and estimate the entomological indices of transmission.
Cross-sectional entomological surveys were conducted in September 2019 in six villages. Mosquitos were captured over 24-h diel cycles using the human-landing catch and cow-baited trap collection methods, and identified with dichotomic morphological identification keys. A subset of the specimens of potential vector species was randomly selected and tested with a filariasis PCR assay targeting the parasites 5S rRNA gene. For positive Aedes specimens, correct identification of the filariae and vector species was confirmed with DNA sequencing of the filariasis and mosquito cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 PCR products.
Overall 5.2% (40/772) mosquito specimens had a positive filariasis PCR result. W. bancrofti DNA was found in half of the positive specimens. Three other zoonotic Brugia and Dirofilaria filariae species were also identified. W. bancrofti DNA was detected in known vector species including Anopheles barbirostris, An. hyrcanus, Downsiomyia harinasutai, Finlaya poicilia and Culex sitiens. Furthermore, it was also found in Aedes albopictus/pseudoalbopictus and Armigeres flavus. W. bancrofti entomological inoculation rate estimate was 0.094 infective bites/person-day (95%CI 0.049 to 0.164). Only 7.5% (3/40) of the positive specimens were captured indoors with the human-landing catch collection method between 9 PM and 5 AM. Specimens infected with zoonotic filariae were captured with the human-landing catch collection method highlighting the potential for zoonotic filariasis transmission in this area. Furthermore, infected specimens were collected in the cow-baited trap suggesting veterinary-based vector control interventions targeting livestock could be used to tackle filariasis transmission in this setting.
This study identified potential vectors of Wuchereria bancrofti and three zoonotic filariae species in Karen state. Mosquito bed nets may have only a limited efficacy against filariasis vectors in this area. Trials of vector control interventions preventing outdoor and early transmission are warranted.

articles.titulo: Trained Innate Immunity in Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Chronicity: Hematopoietic Memory and Failure of Inflammation Resolution
articles.autores: Yi F, Duan C (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Diabetes-related foot ulcers remain prone to non-healing and recurrence despite appropriate vascular, surgical, antimicrobial, and off-loading care. We evaluated whether trained innate immunity provides a coherent explanation for this chronicity and defined priorities for clinical translation. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched through August 5, 2026, for literature on trained immunity, diabetes, hematopoiesis, diabetic wounds, neutrophil extracellular traps, macrophages, efferocytosis, biofilm, epigenetics, immunometabolism, and inflammation resolution. Primary mechanistic studies, human translational studies, clinical guidance, and authoritative reviews were prioritized and classified as direct wound evidence, systemic contextual evidence, or hypothesis-level inference. Diabetes can produce persistent metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in hematopoietic progenitors and descendant myeloid cells. In diabetic wounds, excessive NETosis, macrophage dysfunction, impaired apoptotic-cell clearance, and recurrent microbial or damage signals can reinforce inflammation and disrupt vascular, stromal, and epithelial repair. Direct evidence supports components of this model, but the complete longitudinal bone-marrow-to-wound pathway has not been demonstrated in humans. Trained immunity should therefore be treated as a falsifiable mechanism of treatment resistance and recurrence, not as a clinical diagnosis. Clinically, this framework supports phase-aware biomarker sampling and confines immune-directed adjuncts to adequately perfused, source-controlled ulcers. Longitudinal cohorts with functional rest-and-rechallenge assays, lineage-aware epigenetic measurements, and rigorous adjustment for perfusion, infection, and off-loading are needed.

articles.titulo: People living with HIV have increased CD4+ T cell metabolic activity and reduced influenza-reactive cellular responses to vaccination
articles.autores: Oakes JM, Landeros-Reyes S, … Kalams SA (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: While antiretroviral therapy has improved health outcomes for people living with HIV (PLWH), individuals still experience chronic immune activation and increased incidence of comorbidities. This study investigated basal immunometabolic function and influenza vaccine-induced antibody and T cell responses in 13 PLWH on antiretroviral therapy with suppressed virus and 17 individuals living without HIV (PLWoH). We found similar serum hemagglutination inhibition antibody titers against influenza A (H1N1, H3N2) or influenza B (B-Victoria, B-Yamagata) antigens between PLWH and PLWoH pre- and postvaccination. While PLWH had higher baseline frequencies of influenza-reactive CD4+ T cells expressing OX40 and CD40L compared with PLWoH, only PLWoH had significantly increased frequencies of influenza-reactive CD4+ T cells in response to influenza vaccination. Naive and memory CD4+ T cells from PLWH exhibited higher basal metabolic activity with increased metabolic dysfunction compared with PLWoH. These findings suggest that while PLWH can mount humoral responses to influenza vaccination, increased CD4+ T cell activation and altered CD4+ T cell metabolism may influence cellular immune responses to vaccination. This highlights how the adaptive immune system in PLWH is affected even when HIV replication is controlled through ART.

articles.titulo: Creatine metabolic network and host immune interplay: from molecular mechanisms to regulatory strategies
articles.autores: Dai S, Wang S (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Emerging evidence indicates that creatine, long recognized as an energy buffer in muscle and neural tissues, also plays a critical role in immunometabolic regulation. Research on creatine metabolism and immune regulation spans multiple disciplines, yet a systematic theoretical framework remains lacking. Accordingly, this review proposes a three-dimensional framework of "creatine metabolic flux, immune cell subtype specificity, and microenvironmental regulation". Beginning with the molecular basis of the creatine metabolic network, we delineate the tissue distribution and functional characteristics of creatine de novo synthesis, transmembrane transport, and the phosphocreatine shuttle. We then analyze, across adaptive immunity, innate immunity, and neuroimmunity, the differential regulatory roles of creatine metabolism in processes including CD8+ T cell antitumor immunity, macrophage polarization, NK cell cytotoxicity, and inflammasome activation. Subsequently, we examine the bidirectional regulatory features of creatine metabolism in the tumor microenvironment and inflammatory microenvironment. Additionally, we synthesize recent advances in creatine metabolism related to anti-infective immunity, vaccine responses, and autoimmune diseases. Throughout, we distinguish direct experimental evidence from correlative observations and explicitly identify the inferential steps that remain to be validated. Through this review, we aim to facilitate a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms linking creatine metabolism and immune regulation, thereby providing new perspectives for the clinical translation of creatine-based interventions.

articles.titulo: Immunometabolic mechanisms across psoriatic disease: linking psoriasis to psoriatic arthritis
articles.autores: Romero Arocha SR, Gunawardana S, Coates L (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Psoriatic disease encompasses cutaneous and musculoskeletal inflammation. The mechanisms determining why some patients with psoriasis develop psoriatic arthritis while others do not remain incompletely understood. Current models emphasise the IL-23/IL-17 axis and tumour necrosis factor signalling, but cytokine-centric explanations do not fully account for tissue tropism, heterogeneous clinical trajectories, or preclinical musculoskeletal involvement. In this review, we examine immunometabolism as an additional regulatory layer linking systemic immune activation, tissue-specific susceptibility, and local inflammatory amplification across the psoriatic disease spectrum. We summarise evidence implicating glycolysis, mitochondrial dysfunction, amino acid metabolism, lipid metabolism, bile acid pathways, adipokines, and collagen-related metabolites in cutaneous, circulating, synovial, and entheseal compartments. We propose a multi-compartment model in which systemic immunometabolic priming interacts with pre-lesional skin dysregulation and receptive musculoskeletal niches to shape whether inflammation manifests in the skin, joints, entheses, or a combination. This model reframes psoriatic arthritis not simply as a downstream extension of cutaneous inflammation but as one manifestation of a broader systemic disorder in which metabolic and immune pathways converge. Finally, we consider clinical implications for risk prediction, diagnostic refinement, therapeutic stratification, and metabolic intervention, highlighting the need for longitudinal, multi-omics studies that integrate serum, skin, synovial, entheseal, imaging, and clinical data to identify patients at risk before irreversible musculoskeletal damage occurs.

articles.titulo: Antimicrobial peptides are differentially regulated in blood and visceral adipose tissue in obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction and linked to NLRP3-related signaling
articles.autores: Casado M, Gómez-Ambrosi J, … Catalán V (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation in which visceral adipose tissue (VAT) plays a central immunometabolic role. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) integrate host defense and inflammatory signaling, but their regulation across metabolic compartments in human obesity remains incompletely defined. We evaluated circulating AMP concentrations and gene expression levels in VAT and circulating leukocytes from 108 participants classified according to obesity and glycemic status. These analyses were complemented with mechanistic studies in human visceral adipocytes evaluating inflammatory and microbiota-related stimuli, effects of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)related modulation, and crosstalk with PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Obesity was associated with a selective circulating AMP profile characterized by higher cathelicidin, calprotectin, lipocalin-2 and neutrophil elastase together with lower α-defensin 6 and β-defensin 1. In VAT, obesity was accompanied by increased expression of several inflammatory AMP-related genes together with higher NLRP3 and NLRP6 expression and reduced DEFB1, with additional differences emerging across glycemic groups. Circulating leukocytes displayed a partially overlapping but distinct transcriptional profile, consistent with compartment-specific regulation rather than a generalized AMP response. In vitro, visceral adipocytes showed gene- and stimulus-dependent AMP responses to inflammatory and microbiota-related signals. NLRP3 silencing attenuated selected LPS-induced inflammatory and antimicrobial responses, whereas the glucose-lowering medication glibenclamide promoted complementary stimulus-dependent effects. Adipocyte-conditioned medium modified AMP expression in PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Collectively, these findings identify a selective, compartment-dependent remodeling of antimicrobial pathways in obesity and obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, with NLRP3-related mechanisms emerging as a potential contributor to the regulation of selected antimicrobial responses in visceral adipocytes.

articles.titulo: Spatial Immunometabolic Context of Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Ovarian Cancer: Evidence, Hypotheses, and Pharmacological Considerations
articles.autores: Wang Y, Wang P, … Zhang D (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), is characterized by marked spatial heterogeneity and limited benefit from immune-checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy. Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are organized lymphoid niches associated with immune-active tumor states, but their biological and clinical implications depend on maturation, anatomical site, cellular composition, and treatment context. This review evaluates how spatial metabolic conditions may be associated with TLS organization and B-cell function in ovarian cancer. To prevent overinterpretation, the evidence is classified into four levels: direct evidence from ovarian-cancer TLS, indirect evidence from ovarian-cancer immune or metabolic studies, evidence from other tumors or lymphoid systems, and author-generated hypotheses requiring validation. We distinguish TLS morphology from germinal-center activity, somatic hypermutation (SHM), class-switch recombination (CSR), B-cell receptor (BCR) clonality, antibody affinity, antigen specificity, and effector function. We further discuss the context-dependent roles of lactate transport and hypoxia, including evidence that physiological germinal-center hypoxia and MCT1-dependent pyruvate metabolism can support selected B-cell functions. Spatial metabolomics and imaging mass cytometry may help test these relationships, but they do not by themselves establish causality or therapeutic predictiveness. Accordingly, pharmacological strategies are presented as mechanistically relevant candidates rather than validated TLS-directed treatments.

articles.titulo: Itaconate: An Emerging Metabolic Regulator Linking Immunity and Ferroptosis
articles.autores: Li S, Chen Y, … Nan Y (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Itaconate, generated in activated myeloid cells by aconitate decarboxylase 1 (historically termed immune-responsive gene 1), coordinates immunometabolism, redox signalling and regulated cell death. Emerging evidence links this pathway to ferroptosis; however, interpretation is complicated by the frequent conflation of endogenous itaconate with exogenously administered native itaconate and electrophilic derivatives such as 4-octyl itaconate and dimethyl itaconate.
This review critically integrates the biosynthesis, transport and intercellular signalling of itaconate with its effects on ferroptosis. Evidence is examined across solute carrier family 7 member 11-dependent cystine uptake, glutathione supply, glutathione peroxidase 4 expression, stability and catalytic activity, iron-sulfur clusters, ferritinophagy, phospholipid remodelling, mitochondrial redox signalling and selective autophagy, distinguishing cell-autonomous effects in myeloid cells from cell-nonautonomous transfer to parenchymal and tumour cells.
The available evidence supports a context-dependent model: itaconate-related signalling can suppress ferroptosis and limit acute tissue injury, but may also preserve immunosuppressive myeloid populations or confer ferroptosis resistance on tumours; at high pharmacological exposures, selected compounds can instead promote ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis.
Clinical translation requires compound-resolved terminology, validated ferroptosis endpoints, cell-specific delivery, quantitative exposure and target-engagement biomarkers and careful assessment of infection- and tumour-related risks.

articles.titulo: The Lysine Metabolism-Protein Modification Axis in Tumor Immunity
articles.autores: Liu S, Xu Y, … Wu G (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The metabolic-epigenetic-immune tripartite regulatory network within the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) serves as a central hub governing tumor immune evasion and therapeutic response. Long regarded merely as an essential nutritional substrate, lysine has now emerged as a pivotal signaling molecule bridging metabolic reprogramming, protein post-translational modifications (PTMs), and immune cell fate determination. Tumor cells remodel immune cell function and foster an immunosuppressive microenvironment via three coordinated mechanisms: hijacking lysine transport, rewiring lysine catabolic metabolism, and disrupting acylation and methylation modifications at lysine residues. Herein, we propose a novel preclinical theoretical model coined "lysimetaboptenation," which we define as lysine metabolism-modification-coupled T cell exhaustion. This review systematically delineates lysine transmembrane transport, rewired lysine catabolism, and the lysine-centered PTM regulatory network, alongside the modulatory mechanisms underlying bidirectional crosstalk between tumor cells and immune cells. We further clarify the correlations between aberrant lysine axis signaling and patient prognosis, immunotherapeutic efficacy, and treatment resistance. Additionally, we summarize translational strategies targeting lysine transporters, catabolic enzymes, lysine PTM machinery, precision nutritional interventions, and combinatorial immunometabolic regimens. Finally, we highlight outstanding scientific questions, technical bottlenecks, and cutting-edge research frontiers, aiming to furnish theoretical frameworks and innovative avenues for overcoming resistance to immunotherapy and developing precision combinatorial metabolome-immunotherapy regimens.

articles.titulo: The fibrosis-targeting "Swiss Army Knife": a biomimetic nanomotor reversing pulmonary fibrosis via dual-pathway immunometabolic reprogramming
articles.autores: Wang H, Pu G, … Fan L (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In the realm of medical research, it is widely recognized that idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) constitutes a distinct subtype of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Its progression appears to be relentless, and it can be life-threatening. Moreover, the available treatment options for this condition are rather restricted in range, and to a certain degree, they mainly serve a palliative purpose. Dysregulated lipid metabolism and hyperactivation of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway are established key drivers of fibrotic progression. To address these pathological mechanisms, we developed a multifunctional nanomotor, PMPDA@HDL, consisting of HDL-loaded polydopamine nanoparticles camouflaged with a macrophage membrane functionalized with a collagen I-targeting peptide, where HDL represents the combined payload of H-151, DHA, and L-arginine. Upon NIR irradiation, L-arginine-derived NO enables nanomotor propulsion. The resulting nanomotors (∼300 nm) The nanoparticles exhibited excellent colloidal stability. Additionally, it demonstrated a reasonable and quantifiable level of biocompatibility. Moreover, when exposed to 808 nm near-infrared radiation, it showed a potentially potent and efficient photothermal reaction. This property enhances tissue penetration and the controlled drug release process. In vitro, PMPDA@HDL selectively bound to collagen-rich extracellular matrices, suppressing fibroblast activation, matrix contraction, and senescence phenotypes. In a bleomycin-induced murine IPF model, PMPDA@HDL accumulated preferentially in fibrotic lung tissue, significantly reducing collagen deposition, downregulating pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic mediators, and improving pulmonary function. Integrated RNA sequencing and mechanistic studies revealed that PMPDA@HDL orchestrates dual-pathway reprogramming, concurrently inhibiting the cGAS-STING-mediated senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and activating the KEAP1-NFE2L2 antioxidant pathway, thereby synergistically restoring immunometabolic homeostasis. Together, this collagen-anchored, macrophage-membrane-biomimetic nanomotor represents a potent, targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for multi-mechanistic intervention in IPF.

articles.titulo: Microbiota-Derived Butyrate as an Epigenetic and Immunometabolic Orchestrator of Cancer Immunity
articles.autores: Farah H, PadmaPriya G, … Alshmrty AI (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Among microbiota-derived metabolites, butyrate has emerged as a central regulator of cancer biology through its capacity to integrate epigenetic, metabolic, and immunological signaling. Acting primarily as a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor and metabolic substrate, butyrate orchestrates extensive transcriptional reprogramming that suppresses tumor proliferation, induces apoptosis, promotes differentiation, and limits metastatic dissemination. Beyond its direct antitumor activity, butyrate modulates the tumor immune microenvironment by enhancing cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell responses, influencing natural killer (NK) cell function in a context-dependent manner, and regulating dendritic-cell biology, macrophage polarization, and regulatory T-cell responses. These effects vary according to the immune-cell population, biological context, and experimental conditions. Preclinical evidence further suggests that butyrate can influence responses to immune checkpoint blockade, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy through distinct immunological, tumor-intrinsic, metabolic, and pharmacokinetic mechanisms; however, the clinical relevance of these effects remains to be established. Recent advances in microbiome engineering, next-generation probiotics, synthetic butyrate analogs, nanoparticle-based delivery systems, and precision microbial therapeutics have accelerated the translation of butyrate-based interventions into clinical oncology. This review integrates current advances in the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which butyrate regulates tumor development and antitumor immunity, critically evaluates its role in overcoming therapeutic resistance and enhancing treatment efficacy, and discusses emerging strategies for incorporating butyrate into precision cancer immunotherapy and microbiome-guided oncology.

articles.titulo: Applying functional MRI analysis techniques to whole-brain calcium-imaging data to investigate structural and functional relationships in Drosophila melanogaster
articles.autores: Okuno T, Woodward A, … Hata J (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Clarifying the relationship between structure and function is important for understanding the brain. In Drosophila melanogaster, FlyEM and FlyWire electron microscopy-based connectome data, and whole-brain calcium-imaging data are available. We applied pre-processing methods from functional magnetic resonance imaging to whole-brain calcium-imaging data and comprehensively investigated the optimal parameters. Then, we found that the FC-SC (functional and structural connectivity) correlation decreased linearly with region of interest count, and this trend was the same in flies and humans. We also developed a new, more robust method to quantify the degree of pre- and post-synaptic segregation, and investigated this in the fly whole-brain. This revealed that many neurons have unsegregated synapses. We extracted highly unsegregated synapses and compared them with random-extracted null SC matrices. Their FC-SC correlation was significantly higher, indicating that these synapses contribute to FC well. Conversely, highly segregated synapses showed significantly lower FC-SC correlation and contribute less to FC. Neurons with unsegregated synapses, like non-spiking neurons, are spread throughout the whole-brain, and they are thought to have a significant influence on FC.

articles.titulo: Neural correlates of facial recognition in a social wasp
articles.autores: Jernigan CM, Mammen LCC, … Sheehan MJ (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In humans and other primates, faces are special visual objects that are encoded by circuits selective to faces. If specialized circuits are the most efficient way to encode and discriminate among similar-looking objects of high relevance, then we expect that analogous circuits should evolve in other taxa with specialized visual individual recognition abilities. Thus, we surveyed the neural responses to visual objects across the brain of a wasp that has independently evolved specialized facial recognition, Polistes fuscatus. We found a localized population of neurons analogous to face cells, which we term "wasp cells," that selectively fire to front-facing wasp images. Some of these wasp cells encode information about facial patterns, which possibly underlie the unique visual recognition abilities of these wasps. These findings demonstrate high-level feature-selective tuning in an invertebrate and suggest that specialized circuits are an adaptive feature for nervous systems requiring complex visual recognition.

articles.titulo: A gut-brain axis for aversive interoception drives innate and anticipatory emesis in Drosophila
articles.autores: Karunakaran R, Choudhary P, … Das G (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The gut-brain pathways that transmit negative signals to the brain, influencing bodily functions and behavior, are not fully understood. We have identified a gut-brain axis in Drosophila that detects toxin-induced gut damage and triggers innate and learned, anticipatory emesis. Ingested toxins induce the midgut enterocytes to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). ROS are detected by TrpA1 channels in enteroendocrine cells, resulting in the release of neuropeptides that signal gastric malaise. We also find evidence for midgut and ROS-independent mechanisms of toxin detection. Gut-derived neuropeptides act on brain serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons, which then communicate with the brain's sensory integration and memory centers, the mushroom bodies (MBs). This circuit enables vomiting and facilitates the formation of aversive memories. We find that the persistent activity of dopaminergic neurons mediates aversive reinforcement. Such activity lends itself to pairing the gut-derived malaise signal with odor representations in the MBs, enabling the flies to learn that the paired odor predicts toxin ingestion and to exhibit anticipatory emesis. Many components of this interoceptive pathway are likely conserved, providing a genetic model for exploring how aversive gut-brain communication influences metabolism, feeding, stress responses, and neurodegeneration.

O circuito produz êmese inata e memória aversiva que antecipa a êmese.

articles.titulo: Malaria and the Coagulation System: A Narrative Review
articles.autores: Rolling T, Langer F, … Rolling CC (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria is a major global infectious disease, with Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) accounting for most severe and fatal cases. Severe malaria is also a disorder of the microvasculature in which parasite sequestration, endothelial activation, platelet responses, and coagulation pathways interact. During the erythrocytic stage, infected red blood cells express P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1, enabling cytoadherence to endothelial receptors such as CD36, ICAM-1, thrombomodulin, and the endothelial protein C receptor. This promotes microvascular sequestration, tissue hypoxia, and organ dysfunction, including cerebral and placental malaria. Endothelial activation is accompanied by marked release of von Willebrand factor and relative deficiency of ADAMTS13 activity, leading to accumulation of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers that support platelet adhesion, infected erythrocyte bridging, and microvascular obstruction. Platelets have context-dependent roles: they contribute to thrombocytopenia, vascular plugging, and cerebral pathology, but may also mediate antiparasitic immunity through platelet factor 4-dependent parasite killing. More recently, anti-platelet factor 4/polyanion antibodies and antiphospholipid antibodies have been implicated in malaria-associated platelet activation, anemia, and potentially microthrombosis. Tissue factor expression by endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, and infected placental tissue further links inflammation to fibrin deposition and severe organ manifestations. Clinically, this manifests as thrombocytopenia, prolonged coagulation profiles, and potential disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Because routine adjunctive anticoagulation is not recommended, management remains strictly focused on rapid antiparasitic therapy and supportive care. This review summarizes current concepts of hemostatic dysfunction in malaria and highlights unresolved questions regarding targeted modulation of coagulation pathways.

Não recomenda anticoagulação adjuvante de rotina.

articles.titulo: Environmental Factors Display Multiple Associations with West Nile Virus Risk Modeling in Kansas
articles.autores: Hinojosa I, Smith E, … Mulcahy ER (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
West Nile virus (WNV) persists as a significant vector-borne disease in the United States, yet risk prediction frameworks vary widely across the Midwest and often rely on sparse case data or limited mosquito surveillance. These challenges are amplified by the asymptomatic nature of WNV infection. Incorporating publicly available environmental and landscape variables-such as temperature, precipitation, drought indices, and land cover-may offer a more robust and scalable foundation for regional WNV risk assessment.
Seven years of human and equine WNV case data were integrated with Culex mosquito surveillance records, county-level land cover, and weekly temperature, precipitation, and drought indices for the state of Kansas. Mosquito abundance from 26 unique trapping sites was assessed using annual regression models, and case occurrence was evaluated using zero-inflated negative binomial models. Site-level trend assessments examined ecological patterns in relation to precipitation, drought, and habitat composition.
Lagged temperature and drought severity were the most stable environmental indicators of case occurrence, supported by trend-level contrasts between drought and nondrought seasons. Landscape composition shaped mosquito responses to precipitation and moisture availability. Although Culex abundance showed a significant monotonic association with WNV cases at a 3-week lag, regression models did not detect a linear relationship.
Publicly available, routinely updated, and geographically resolved environmental indicators can support a scalable WNV risk assessment framework. This study represents the first integration of these environmental, landscape, and surveillance factors for Kansas and provides a foundation for future work incorporating viral testing of mosquito pools, finer-scale land use data, and more consistent trap placement to strengthen predictive capacity.

articles.titulo: Relative Humidity Verification Over Vietnam in ECMWF Medium-Range Forecasts for a Dengue Early Warning System
articles.autores: Pérez-Fernández I, Sparrow S, … Main L (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue fever outbreaks impose a severe healthcare burden in Vietnam; therefore, the development of a Dengue early warning system is key to improve public health planning and mitigate this burden. This study assesses the ECMWF medium-range (up to 10 days) forecast skill for relative humidity in Vietnam-a key factor for vector-borne disease transmission-in re-forecasts between 2001 and 2020. Analysis focused on the rainy season (May-October) with ERA5 reanalysis as a reference dataset. Re-forecast data were pre-processed using a lead-time dependent quantile mapping technique to reduce the bias between forecasted and observational data, and skill was assessed using climatology and persistence as a reference. Rank histograms showed that the humidity forecast is reliable up to 10 days, and continuous ranked probability skill score (CRPSS) values show that the forecast is more skilful than the climatology up to 10 days. Nonetheless, when using persistence as a reference, CRPSS values are lower in South Vietnam, which was associated with the inaccurate representation of 2 m dew point temperature in the tropical regions, and the fact that persistence is a hard reference to beat in the tropics, hindering model forecast skill. Results from this study demonstrate that ECMWF ensemble forecasts of relative humidity are suitable to use as inputs for a Dengue early warning system up to 10 days in advance.

articles.titulo: Advances in Chikungunya Fever Prevention and Control: Antiviral Therapeutics, Vaccine Development and Integrated Intervention Strategies
articles.autores: Yu Y, Li J, … Shen C (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chikungunya fever (CHIKF) is an acute mosquito-borne disease caused by chikungunya virus (CHIKV). Driven by globalization, climate change and expanding vector habitats, its geographic range continues to widen; in 2025 it produced the largest outbreak ever recorded in China, with more than 25,800 locally transmitted cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities of Guangdong. Beyond acute fever, rash and arthralgia, a substantial proportion of patients develop chronic arthritis, which accounts for much of the disease burden. This review summarizes the etiological features, life cycle, epidemiology and ongoing evolution of CHIKV, and critically evaluates progress in antiviral drugs and vaccines, together with vector control, microbiome-based approaches and One Health governance. No specific antiviral has yet been approved: compounds targeting viral entry, RNA capping, protease activity and genome replication inhibit CHIKV selectively in cell culture but remain at preclinical or early clinical stages, and host-directed agents are further constrained by host toxicity. Two vaccines are now licensed-the live-attenuated vaccine Ixchiq, whose use has been progressively restricted following post-marketing safety signals, and the virus-like particle vaccine Vimkunya-while inactivated, chimeric, viral-vectored and mRNA candidates remain earlier in development. For all countermeasures, whether the envelope substitutions carried by recently emerged strains, including E2-L210Q and E2-I211 T within the immunodominant domain B, will erode protection remains experimentally unresolved. Collectively, CHIKV control still faces the absence of approved antivirals, incompletely defined long-term vaccine safety and breadth, and ongoing vector population expansion. Future work should prioritize broad-spectrum antivirals and next-generation vaccines, promote multidisciplinary collaboration, and strengthen integrated governance under the One Health framework.Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07555392..Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06669208..

articles.titulo: Efficient primer design for broad-range virus detection: A semi-automated workflow using sequence clustering and varVAMP
articles.autores: Johnston CM, Mingoli A, … Rasmussen TB (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Broad-range RT-qPCR assays are essential for detecting highly diverse viruses within virus families, but designing suitable primers remains challenging because of extensive sequence diversity and biases in public sequence databases. Here, we present a semi-automated workflow that combines sequence clustering and varVAMP, a tool for automated design of degenerate primers and probes from multiple sequence alignments, to streamline pan-RT-qPCR primer design. The workflow reduces sequence redundancy, improves the representation of viral diversity, and facilitates the identification of broadly reactive primer candidates. We demonstrate the workflow using the arboviral genera Orthoflavivirus and Alphavirus as proof-of-concept datasets. The resulting primer candidates were evaluated using dye-based RT-qPCR, demonstrating broad detection across representative viral panels. The workflow provides a practical, scalable, and reproducible framework for developing broad-range primer candidates and may support surveillance, diagnostics, and preparedness for emerging or divergent viruses.

articles.titulo: Fatal dengue cases in travellers from 1995 to 2025: A targeted review
articles.autores: Dinjer CS, Grobusch MP, … Steffen R (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in 136 countries and territories, with over 14 million cases and more than 10,000 deaths reported globally in 2024 alone. International travellers are at risk of infection when visiting endemic regions. While dengue in travellers is well described, dengue-related mortality in this population has not been comprehensively synthesised. We compiled and critically assessed available data on reports of fatal dengue cases among international travellers over a 30-year period.
A targeted review was conducted to identify dengue-related fatalities in travellers from non-endemic countries acquiring infection in endemic regions between 1995 and November 2025. PubMed searches using terms related to dengue, mortality, and travel were complemented by hand-searching conference proceedings, national and international surveillance reports, publicly accessible national infectious disease databases, media reports, and anecdotal notifications. Cases were classified as confirmed or probable based on diagnostic method and/or inclusion in surveillance systems. Data were extracted, cross-referenced to avoid duplication, and analysed descriptively.
Sixty-seven fatal travel-related dengue cases were identified, of which 55 were classified as confirmed/probable and 12 cases had limited information. Of the 55 confirmed/probable cases, 22 reported both country of residence and acquisition, spanning 14 endemic destinations. Confirmed/probable fatal cases occurred among patients aged <1-79 years; 25.5% were female, 21.8% were male, and in 52.7% sex was not documented. Where infection status was available, most were primary infections (9/16). Reported fatal manifestations included neurological, cardiac, haemorrhagic, and hyperinflammatory complications. Diagnostic and reporting heterogeneity was substantial, and surveillance gaps were evident.
Dengue-related mortality among travellers is rare but likely under-recognised and underreported. Strengthened diagnostic capacity and heightened clinical awareness may support earlier recognition and management of severe cases in travellers, while harmonised international reporting systems could improve case ascertainment and contribute to future prevention strategies.

articles.titulo: Parental intention to vaccinate children and adolescents against dengue fever in Vietnam: An analysis using the theory of planned behavior and selected health belief model constructs
articles.autores: Huynh G, Phan DQ, … Nguyen HV (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue fever (DF) is a major public health challenge for which no specific antiviral treatment is currently approved; therefore, prevention is the primary means of control. This study examined parents' intention to vaccinate children and adolescents with the first dengue vaccine approved in Vietnam and the factors associated with this intention.
A cross-sectional study was conducted from June to October 2025 among parents of children and adolescents aged 4-18 years in five schools in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire based on the Theory of Planned Behavior and selected Health Belief Model constructs and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Among 1,242 participants, 68.7% reported an intention to vaccinate their children against DF. Compared with parents of children aged 4-6 years, those with children aged 7-11 years had lower odds of vaccination intention (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.27, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.10-0.70). Lower self-perceived household income was associated with reduced intention (aOR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.32-0.85), whereas higher perceived mosquito density around the house (aOR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.43), favorable attitudes toward the vaccine (aOR = 2.05, 95% CI 1.53-2.75), stronger subjective norms (aOR = 1.32, 95% CI 1.17-1.49), greater perceived behavioral control (aOR = 1.36, 95% CI 1.26-1.47), and better DF prevention practices (aOR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.15-1.80) were independently associated with greater intention to vaccinate.
Parents' intention to vaccinate their children against DF was associated with financial, health-system, and social factors. These findings may inform strategies that address affordability, social support, service accessibility, and trusted health communication, particularly for parents of children aged 7-11 years and those in areas with high mosquito density.

articles.titulo: Convergent evolution of bt resistance in insects: Receptor mutations, non-receptor mechanisms and polygenic adaptation
articles.autores: Balaji A, Balakrishnan N, … Raghu R (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The extensive cultivation of transgenic Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) crops has constituted one of the largest human-mediated evolutionary selection experiments in modern agriculture. Although resistance is often attributed to specific management failures, accumulating global evidence shows that Bt-resistant populations repeatedly emerge across diverse agroecosystems and unrelated insect taxa, through comparable ecological conditions and a constrained set of adaptive mechanisms, indicating a central role for convergent evolution. This review integrates ecological, molecular and genomic perspectives into a single evolutionary framework. It argues that Bt resistance evolves through partially predictable trajectories shaped by convergent ecological pressures and constrained molecular pathways. At the ecological level, recurrent pressures such as prolonged Bt exposure, suboptimal toxin expression, inadequate refuge implementation and continuous host availability generate similar selection regimes in unrelated insect taxa. At the molecular level, convergence is most evident in receptor-gene modifications within ATP-binding cassette transporters, cadherins, aminopeptidases N and alkaline phosphatases, alongside non-receptor processes affecting toxin activation, sequestration and Bt susceptibility, including microbiota-associated effects. Genomic studies further demonstrate that resistance is not always explained by single major-effect mutations but can involve multilocus and polygenic architectures, as demonstrated by copy-number variation and standing quantitative-trait variation in Helicoverpa zea. The review also examines resistance to Vip3 toxins, considering reported genetic mechanisms and implications for Bt pyramids. These findings show how ecological pressures channel adaptation into a constrained set of molecular pathways, while diverse genetic architectures expand the evolutionary routes available to pest populations. We also discuss what molecular convergence means for resistance monitoring and management, and where the constraint may fail.

articles.titulo: Development of a novel osteotropic bone morphogenetic protein-2 carrier based on a polyphosphate diester
articles.autores: Hirai H, Kaito T, … Iwasaki Y (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Autologous bone grafting remains the clinical gold standard for bone regeneration but is limited by donor site morbidity and reduced availability and quality in elderly patients. Recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) provides strong osteoinduction; however, its conventional collagen sponge carrier allows rapid release, resulting in dose-dependent adverse effects and high costs. To address these limitations, we developed a bone-targeted delivery system using cholesterol-conjugated poly (ethylene sodium phosphate) (CH-PEP·Na), a polyphosphate diester with high bone affinity and dual biological activity that suppresses osteoclastogenesis and enhances early osteogenic gene expression. CH-PEP·Na formed stable complexes with BMP-2 (CHP-BMP-2) that were resistant to proteolytic degradation and exhibited sustained adsorption to hydroxyapatite. In vitro, CHP-BMP-2 enhanced osteogenic gene expression and matrix mineralization in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, while CH-PEP·Na inhibited osteoclast differentiation and showed reduced ERK phosphorylation in a single immunoblot experiment. In vivo, CHP-BMP-2 combined with allograft bone demonstrated prolonged fluorescence retention of labeled BMP-2, reduced bone resorption, and enhanced new bone formation compared with BMP-2 alone in a rat subfascial implantation model. Notably, in a posterolateral spinal fusion model, CHP-BMP-2-containing allografts achieved 100% fusion rates (12/12 evaluated sides in six rats) and generated high-density, trabecular-rich bone, whereas collagen sponge carriers produced bone of inferior structural quality. These findings demonstrate that CHP-BMP-2 enables spatially controlled delivery of BMP-2 via direct binding to bone graft surfaces. Clinically, this strategy may allow small amounts of autologous bone obtained during decompression procedures to function as a scaffold and growth factor depot, reducing BMP-2 dose, minimizing adverse effects and costs, and improving outcomes in spinal fusion and large-defect bone regeneration.
