articles.titulo: A One Health investigation of malaria infections in critically endangered eastern gorillas (Gorilla beringei) and national park employees in the highlands of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.autores: Kubala A, Warren K, … Linton YM (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Great apes across central Africa harbor many species of Plasmodium parasites, some of which, through cross-species transmission events, gave rise to malaria in humans. Concern has been raised that great apes could serve as a reservoir of infection for humans, while recent data suggest that malaria negatively affects the health and reproductive success of endangered great apes. Two subspecies of eastern gorillas, mountain (Gorilla beringei beringei) and Grauer's (Gorilla beringei graueri), live above 2000 m in the highlands of the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. To date, Plasmodium parasites have not been detected in these highland populations, but climate change is altering malaria transmission in this region, and Plasmodium vivax has been detected in nearby gorillas at lower altitudes. We used microscopic and molecular techniques to determine whether highland eastern gorillas and park employees are infected with Plasmodium parasites and whether bridge vectors are present in the highland eastern gorilla habitat. Highland gorillas had no Plasmodium infections. A small number of park employees were infected with human Plasmodium, but no gorilla Plasmodium parasites. The only Anopheles species captured at highland gorillas' night nests was Anopheles kingi. The most common Anopheles species captured below 2000 m, and within 17 km of endangered highland gorillas, were members of the Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles funestus complexes. Anopheles gambiae s.s. was infected with Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax. No vector captured above 1600 m was infected with Plasmodium parasites. This study is the first to report Rickettsia africae in gorilla blood.

articles.titulo: Setting the scene for the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine implementation programme in Kenya: a situational analysis of the health system, malaria burden, and immunization platform
articles.autores: Westercamp N, Kwambai TK, … Samuels AM (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Kenya has made notable progress in reducing malaria prevalence and improving child survival, yet the lake-endemic region continues to face high transmission and substantial malaria-related illness and death. To strengthen prevention, the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine was introduced in 2019 through Kenya's Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), leveraging a robust platform with decades of experience in rolling out new vaccines. This situational analysis provides a comprehensive description of the demographic, epidemiologic, and health system context in Kenya, with particular attention to the eight high-burden counties where the Malaria Vaccine Implementation Programme (MVIP) was launched. It highlights the organization of the health system, the burden of malaria, ongoing control strategies, and the strength of Kenya's immunization infrastructure as the backbone for vaccine introduction. By documenting the epidemiologic, health system, and immunization context, this paper provides the foundation for interpreting RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine implementation and evaluation findings and offers lessons for vaccine introduction in other malaria-endemic settings.

articles.titulo: Short-chain fatty acid enrichment, TLR4/MyD88/p-JNK inhibition, and gut metabolic modulation: a triple mechanism by which the probiotic ameliorates colorectal cancer
articles.autores: Madjirebaye P, Ullah N, … Wu X (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic intestinal inflammation is a major risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC). This study investigated the therapeutic potential of the probiotic Streptococcus thermophilus NCU074001 (ST) in a mouse model of colitis-associated CRC. ST supplementation reduced tumor number, preserved colon length, and alleviated clinical disease activity. ST suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and COX-2, while restoring the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 and the tight junction proteins ZO-1 and Claudin-1, indicating potent anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective effects. ST treatment inhibited the TLR4/MyD88/p-JNK pathway, reduced the CD117+FcɛRI+ immune population, and expanded CD25⁺Foxp3⁺ regulatory T cells, thereby rebalancing host immunity. ST also induced a significant microbiome reprogramming, partially ameliorating dysbiosis, enriching beneficial short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing genera (Odoribacter and Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group), reducing Escherichia-Shigella, and elevating SCFAs (butyrate, acetate, and propionate). A notable finding was that ST treatment correlated with reduced activity of proteolytic pathways (L-lysine fermentation and creatinine degradation) and increased abundance of pathways related to methanol oxidation (PWY-7616) and decaprenyl phosphate biosynthesis (PWY-6383), both of which are associated with barrier function and colonization resistance. Such functional alterations have rarely been reported in probiotic‑CRC research. Correlation network analysis further identified two opposing regulatory axes, a pathogen-driven pro-inflammatory axis and a protective SCFA-mediated axis, indicating that ST actively redirects the host immunometabolic landscape toward a protective state. Collectively, these findings position ST as a promising next-generation probiotic capable of modulating inflammation, epithelial barrier function, and microbial metabolism to disrupt the cycle of inflammation-driven colorectal carcinogenesis.

articles.titulo: Mitogenomic Evidence of Host Plasticity and Strict Phylogeographic Restriction in the Avian Malaria Parasite Plasmodium collidatum
articles.autores: Prompiram P, Mongkolphan C, … Poltep K (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Avian malaria parasites (Plasmodium spp.) are globally distributed pathogens that significantly affect host evolution and biodiversity. The rapid expansion-cancelation cycles that are characteristic of invasive lineages are well documented. However, the mechanisms maintaining the stability of endemic generalists remain poorly understood. This study aimed to resolve the evolutionary history and population genetics of Plasmodium collidatum (lineage pFANTAIL01) across three regions in Thailand with the use of a mitogenomic approach incorporating a 3315-bp concatenated dataset of cytb, cox1, and cox3. Phylogenetic reconstruction confirmed that P. collidatum was a robust monophyletic clade with substantial divergence (5.6%-5.7%) from its sister taxon (P. ashfordi). Results revealed a distinct phylogeographic paradox. In particular, although P. collidatum exhibited a high host plasticity across taxonomically diverse avian orders (Galliformes, Columbiformes, and Gruiformes), this genetic structure was strictly partitioned by geographic distance. The haplotype network analysis identified three site-specific haplotypes, indicating that the regional gene flow was constrained by localized vector communities rather than by host species barriers. The genetic diversity indices (pi = 0.00072, Hd = 0.80) and the non-significant neutrality tests (Tajima's D = 1.64, Fu's Fs = 0.952) showed a state of neutral equilibrium, thereby reflecting long-term demographic stasis and endemic integration. Based on these findings, P. collidatum maintains a stable endemicity via local ecological exploitation rather than via contemporary range expansion. This study underscores the need for high-resolution mitogenomic markers to elucidate the fine-scale transmission dynamics of generalist parasites. Further, it provides an important molecular baseline for avian conservation biosecurity in Southeast Asia.

articles.titulo: COVID‑19 nucleic acid vaccines, their many virtues, some deficiencies and unsuspected novel features. A reflection after pandemic resolution and present endemic SARS-CoV-2 circulation
articles.autores: Cassone A, Cauda R (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In the successful fight against COVID-19, there is little doubt that vaccines made with RNA or vectored-DNA have played a major role. However, their benefits are somewhat shadowed by their insufficiencies in fighting the viral infection, its transmission and, consequently, the lack of robust herd protection. Moreover, a few rare but significant side effects have caused some community worries. The main aim of this commentary is to provide a critical reflection on the above issues. We will also discuss some other nonspecific effects of these vaccines, potentially enlarging the spectrum of vaccination benefits but also involving intriguing inflammatory patterns in need of special consideration.

articles.titulo: Dynamics of parasitemia, symptoms and biomarkers during growth phase in malaria volunteer infection studies: implications for the development of highly sensitive Rapid Diagnostic Tests
articles.autores: Webb L, Marquart-Wilson L, … Britton S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Rapid diagnostic tests for malaria are based on two predominant biomarkers: Plasmodium falciparum histidine rich protein 2 (PfHRP2) and Plasmodium lactate dehydrogenase, the latter of which may be either genus specific (PanLDH) or Plasmodium vivax specific (PvLDH). However, these tests have reduced sensitivity at low parasitemia, and their relationship to early clinical symptoms is poorly understood.
Using longitudinal data from 24 participants from two volunteer infection studies, one P. vivax (n=8) and one P. falciparum (n=16), we characterised the relationship between parasitemia measured by qPCR and levels of PfHRP2, PfLDH, and PvLDH in early symptomatic malaria infection prior to treatment.
Symptoms attributed to malaria were observed in 87.5% of P. vivax and 43.8% of P. falciparum participants prior to treatment. In P. vivax infections, symptoms first presented between 6.1 - 8.8 days post-inoculation at parasitemias of 0.403 - 27.264 parasites/µL and PvLDH levels of 0.090 - 3.374 pg/µL. While in P. falciparum infections, symptoms first presented between 3.1 - 9 days post-inoculation at 0.012 - 184.891 parasites/µL with PfHRP2 levels of 0.004 - 7.144 pg/µL.
These results indicate that symptoms considered compatible with P. vivax and P. falciparum malaria can occur in malaria-naïve adults at parasite and biomarker concentrations below published analytical detection limits of currently available RDTs. This highlights the importance of the sensitivity of diagnostic tests for the early detection of malaria, especially in low-transmission settings.

articles.titulo: Factors associated with malaria prevention behaviours among residents in endemic areas of Tak Province, Thailand: a mixed-methods study
articles.autores: Chiraphatthakun P, Kanthawee P, … Azam M (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria remains a significant public health concern in Thailand, particularly in Tak Province along the Thailand-Myanmar border. Despite ongoing elimination efforts, persistent transmission in endemic communities highlights the need to better understand prevention behaviors and associated barriers. This study aimed to identify factors influencing malaria prevention behaviors among residents in endemic border areas using the Health Belief Model framework.
A convergent mixed-method study was conducted in four malaria-endemic villages in Khane Chue Subdistrict, Mae Ramat District, Tak Province, Thailand. Quantitative data were collected from 352 participants through face-to-face interviews using structured questionnaires. Qualitative data were obtained from in-depth interviews with 9 villagers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Fisher's exact test, and multivariable logistic regression. Qualitative data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis.
Overall, 77.3% of participants demonstrated effective malaria prevention behaviors, while 22.7% exhibited poor practices. Factors associated with poor prevention behavior included male gender (aOR = 2.00, 95% CI 1.00-4.02), previous history of malaria infection (aOR = 2.27, 95% CI 1.22-4.24), residence in bamboo housing (aOR = 21.48, 95% CI 2.38-193.99), low malaria knowledge (aOR = 5.45, 95% CI 2.28-13.03), low perceived benefits of malaria prevention (aOR = 11.40, 95% CI 1.96-66.33), and moderate perceived barriers to malaria prevention (aOR = 4.10, 95% CI 1.40-12.04) as well as high perceived barriers (aOR = 2.64, 95% CI 1.23-5.64) were significantly associated with poor malaria prevention behaviour. Qualitative findings provided context for these associations. Occupational exposure among males and structural housing vulnerability contributed to poor preventive practices. Previous malaria infection influenced preventive behaviors in different ways: some participants became more concerned and adopted preventive measures following infection, whereas others perceived malaria as a common and treatable illness, resulting in lower perceived severity and inconsistent preventive practices. A knowledge-behavior gap was also observed, while discomfort with preventive measures and limited access to protective tools remained major barriers.
Malaria prevention behaviors in endemic border communities are influenced by socio-demographic, environmental, and cognitive factors. Targeted interventions addressing behavioral barriers, risk perception, and structural vulnerabilities are essential to improve malaria prevention in high-risk border populations.

articles.titulo: Long COVID, chronic fatigue syndrome, and chronic lyme disease as Post-acute Infection Syndromes (PAIS): a translational synthesis
articles.autores: Sewell PE, Reddy R (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) comprise a heterogeneous group of chronic, multisystem conditions characterized by persistent or relapsing symptoms following resolution of an acute infectious illness, in the absence of ongoing pathogen replication detectable by standard diagnostics. Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), Long COVID, post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome, and related entities are increasingly recognized as part of a shared post-infectious disease spectrum. The COVID-19 pandemic has markedly expanded the global burden of PAIS and intensified investigation into their biological underpinnings.
This narrative translational review integrates clinical, epidemiologic, genetic, immunologic, metabolic, and neurovascular evidence to propose a unified framework for PAIS pathophysiology and management. We anchor the review in clinical phenomenology before turning to mechanism, then provide depth treatment of three core mechanism areas-cellular immune dysfunction with T-cell exhaustion and immunometabolic reprogramming, viral and antigen persistence with herpesvirus reactivation, and the genetic architecture revealed by the DecodeME 2025 GWAS and complementary studies. Convergent mechanisms across PAIS include T-cell exhaustion phenotypes, NK cell cytotoxicity defects, immunometabolic reprogramming with mitochondrial bioenergetic inefficiency, autonomic and endothelial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, altered tryptophan-kynurenine-NAD+ metabolism, viral or antigen persistence, autoantibody formation, and gut microbiome dysbiosis. Recent genome-wide association studies support heritable susceptibility involving immune regulation, mitochondrial maintenance, and neuroinflammatory pathways. Diagnostic paradigms remain primarily clinical, though emerging multi-omic and cellular biomarkers show translational promise. Tiered diagnostic and evaluation strategies are discussed to guide clinicians while minimizing harm, particularly post-exertional malaise.
PAIS represent biologically grounded, systems-level disorders with shared mechanisms and heterogeneous clinical expression. Integrating molecular insights with pragmatic clinical frameworks may accelerate development of precision-oriented diagnostic and therapeutic strategies to address the growing global impact of post-infectious chronic illness.

articles.titulo: Transient intracellular survival of Leptospira spp. within free-living amoebae
articles.autores: Luga A, Inizan C, … Thibeaux R (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Leptospirosis is a zoonotic disease caused by pathogenic Leptospira spp., which persist in soil and water environments for extended periods of time. The mechanisms enabling this environmental survival remain elusive. Free-living amoebae (FLA) are widespread protozoa that act as reservoirs or "Trojan horses" for numerous bacterial pathogens, protecting them from stress and contributing to their persistence. Whether pathogenic Leptospira exploit similar interactions with FLA has not been resolved.
Using live confocal microscopy, flow cytometry, and gentamicin protection assays, we investigated the interactions between pathogenic (Leptospira interrogans) and saprophytic (Leptospira biflexa) leptospires with three FLA species: Acanthamoeba castellanii, Dictyostelium discoideum, and Hartmannella vermiformis. While rapid internalization was observed, entry was only partially dependent on actin-driven processes and was enhanced by the presence of live bacteria. Following internalization, bacteria persisted for at least 48h as indicated by colony-forming assays. However, no evidence of intracellular replication was detected. The number of fluorescently labeled leptospires progressively declined over time, providing further evidence of leptospires survival without multiplication. Finally, analysis of environmental soils in New Caledonia showed co-occurrence of FLA and Leptospira. Soil-derived FLA also internalized pathogenic Leptospira in vitro, showing that these interactions extend to natural isolates.
Our results demonstrate that free-living amoebae internalize both pathogenic and saprophytic leptospires and that a fraction of internalized bacteria remains viable. These findings establish transient intracellular survival of Leptospira within FLA that may contribute to the ecological maintenance of Leptospira. These findings pinpoint FLA as potential components of the environmental phase of Leptospira that could play a role in shaping leptospires survival strategies relevant for transmission and host infection.

articles.titulo: The Histone Acetyltransferases Tip60 and CBP Differentially Regulate Alcohol-Induced Neuroadaptations in Drosophila Through the Ventrolateral Neurons
articles.autores: Del Valle-Colón CD, Morales-Cancio SI, … Ghezzi A (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a chronic neuropsychiatric condition characterized by impaired control over drinking, persistent cravings, cognitive dysfunction, and sleep disturbances. Growing evidence suggests that many of these symptoms arise from alcohol-driven neuronal adaptations that promote tolerance and dependence, mediated in part by epigenetic reprogramming of the neuronal circuits that shape alcohol-related behaviors. Recent work in Drosophila implicates the PDF-expressing ventrolateral neurons (LNv) as key regulators of alcohol tolerance and alcohol-induced sleep disruption. However, the molecular mechanisms by which these neurons drive alcohol-evoked neuroadaptation remain unclear. Here, we test whether histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity in these circadian neurons is required for ethanol-induced tolerance and sleep phenotypes. We used the UAS-Gal4 and GeneSwitch systems to manipulate the expression of two HATs previously implicated in alcohol-induced neuroadaptation-Tip60 and CBP-with spatial and temporal precision. We measured ethanol sedation tolerance and quantified sleep/activity rhythms in genetically modified flies, analyzing sedation recovery time, total sleep, and circadian anticipation. Knockdown of Tip60 in LNv neurons abolished ethanol tolerance, whereas knockdown of nejire (CBP) in the same neurons enhanced ethanol tolerance. Similarly, Tip60 but not nejire knockdown reduced both daytime and nighttime sleep and prevented ethanol-induced sleep promotion. In contrast, knockdown of nejire disrupted the effects of ethanol on morning and evening anticipatory behavior, while Tip60 knockdown had no effect. Together, these results identify Tip60 and CBP as contrasting epigenetic regulators of alcohol-driven behavioral plasticity in Drosophila clock neurons.

articles.titulo: Integrated serosurveillance to assess disease elimination in coastal Ecuador: Onchocerciasis, yaws, and trachoma
articles.autores: Simbaña L, Torres S, … Arnold BF (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Testing blood samples for antibodies with multiplex bead assays can assess elimination and identify residual foci of transmission for multiple pathogens simultaneously. In Ecuador, onchocerciasis and yaws are presumed eliminated, and the status of trachoma is unknown. We assessed their elimination status by measuring IgG antibodies in children aged 6-24 months.
In a birth cohort of 404 children measured between 2021-2024 in Esmeraldas province, Ecuador, we tested dried blood spots at ages 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months using a multiplex IgG assay that included antigens to Onchocerca volvulus (Ov16), Treponema pallidum (rp17, Tmpa), and Chlamydia trachomatis (Pgp3, Ct694). We estimated seroprevalence and incident seroconversion rates across an urban-rural gradient. Of 404 children enrolled, 369 contributed 1,574 samples. Seroprevalence was near zero for onchocerciasis (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.1% to 0.7%) and yaws (0.1%, 95% CI: 0.0% to 0.5%). Conversely, C. trachomatis Pgp3 child-level seroprevalence increased along the urban-rural gradient from the city of Esmeraldas (4.8%, 95% CI: 1.3% to 11.7%) to remote, river-accessible rural villages (47.5%, 95% CI: 31.5% to 63.9%), and incident seroconversion was common in rural villages (15.1 per 100 child-years, 95% CI: 10.1 to 21.0).
Serologic surveillance found no evidence of O. volvulus or T. pallidum transmission, consistent with elimination. High Pgp3 seroconversion rates suggest ongoing C. trachomatis transmission in rural villages. Results highlight the value of integrated serologic surveillance and motivate in-depth trachoma surveillance in Esmeraldas.

articles.titulo: PTC-assisted sustainable synthesis and integrated in silico evaluation of novel 2-oxo-nicotinonitrile derivatives as multitarget larvicidal agents against Culex pipiens L
articles.autores: El-Sayed MKF, Hekal MH, … Abbass EM (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study reports an operationally efficient and mild phase-transfer catalytic (PTC) synthesis of novel 2-oxo nicotinonitrile derivatives as potential larvicidal agents against Culex pipiens L. Compared with conventional reflux, the PTC protocol afforded markedly higher yields of 73-95% within 6-10 h, whereas the thermal method gave only 16-23% yields after 19-24 h. Larvicidal evaluation against third-instar larvae identified compounds 8, 2b, 10, and 4 as the most active derivatives, with LC50 values of 7.65, 9.92, 10.48, and 10.48 µg mL-1, respectively. Although their potency was lower than that of pyriproxyfen, these compounds showed promising activity as newly synthesized lead candidates. Molecular docking against Lymnaea stagnalis acetylcholine-binding protein and Aedes aegypti juvenile hormone-binding protein revealed favorable interactions consistent with a possible multitarget mode of action. DFT calculations showed that compound 8 possessed the lowest HOMO-LUMO energy gap and hardness and the highest softness among the synthesized candidates, supporting its superior activity within the series. SAR analysis highlighted the importance of molecular rigidity, substituent size, and hydrogen-bonding capacity. Compounds 4 and 8 also showed favorable predicted ADME and toxicity profiles, including lack of blood-brain barrier penetration, acceptable bioavailability, and relatively high LD50 values. Overall, PTC provides an operationally efficient and high-yielding route to biologically active nicotinonitrile derivatives, with compound 8 emerging as the most promising larvicidal lead.

articles.titulo: RNA-seq-based dissection of the OsPHR2-OsPHO2-OsPT1 pathway links Pi signaling to lipid metabolism-associated responses in rice
articles.autores: Kang M, Gho YS, … Jung KH (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Phosphate (Pi) use efficiency has long been a major challenge in agriculture, particularly for rice as a staple crop. In this study, we conducted a genome-wide analysis of the molecular mechanisms underlying phosphate deficiency tolerance in rice, focusing on the OsPHR2-OsPHO2-OsPT1 pathway. Through RNA sequencing, we identified 1000 up-regulated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the roots of OsPHR2-OX, 997 in ospho2, and 976 in OsPT1-OX. Integrated GO and KEGG analyses of the up-regulated DEGs in OsPHR2-OX and the ospho2 mutant revealed coordinated induction of genes involved in glycerophospholipid and glycerolipid catabolic pathways, indicating lipid metabolism-related transcriptional changes in OsPHR2-OX and ospho2.Consistent with this transcriptional change, Nile Red staining revealed genotype-dependent differences in lipid-associated fluorescence pattern, OsPHR2-OX and the ospho2 mutant roots exhibited increased green-channel Nile Red-positive puncta and reduced red-channel membrane-associated fluorescence. The upregulation of these genes highlights their potential in enhancing phosphate deficiency tolerance. Collectively, this work refines our understanding of the molecular basis of phosphate deficiency adaptation and provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms of phosphate deficiency stress adaptation for improving phosphate use efficiency in rice.

articles.titulo: Nano-structural analysis of zein-cellulose derivative composite films using AFM-Lorentz contact resonance and local thermal analyses
articles.autores: Zhang Y, Bonilla J, Lim LT (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study investigated nanoscale zein particle suspensions (ZPS) prepared from aqueous ethanol (90% w/w) by antisolvent precipitation. The zein particles had a volume-based median particle diameter (Dv50) of 0.208 as determined by light scattering. The ZPS was incorporated into either an ethanol-soluble ethyl cellulose (EC, 4% w/w) solution or a water-soluble hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC, 4% w/w) solution to form continuous composite films by casting. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed distinct particle distributions and morphologies in the two polymer matrices. SEM images showed a bilayer structure in the zein-HPMC film. In contrast, in the zein-EC film, the particles were dispersed throughout the cross-section, with an increased concentration towards the casting substrate. AFM in Lorentz contact resonance mode revealed two distinct stiffness regions in the zein-EC film, whereas only one phase was observed in the zein-HPMC film. Nano-thermal analysis detected two local softening temperatures in the zein-EC film, whereas only one temperature was detected in the zein-HPMC film. In summary, this study reports a method to prepare EC and HPMC microcomposites with controlled zein particle distribution and a distinct morphology, resulting from matrix-dependent zein-polymer interactions. These structural differences may provide a basis for tailoring the localization and mobility of active compounds in functional food films and packaging, although their potential effects on bioactive delivery performance require further validation.

articles.titulo: Routine suspected typhoid notification rates in Sierra Leone exceed African blood-culture surveillance estimates, 2019-2025
articles.autores: Ikoona EN, Namulemo L, … Sahr F (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Sierra Leone records suspected typhoid in the electronic Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (eIDSR) system as aggregate district notifications. The records are not linked to diagnostic method or microbiological result. We compared annual notification rates from 2019 to 2025 with 535 per 100,000 person-years, the upper 95% confidence limit of the highest adjusted all-age site estimate in the Typhoid Fever Surveillance in Africa Program. The comparison assessed how routine notifications relate to the country's underlying typhoid burden.
We analyzed 112 district-year records from all 16 health districts. Annual district and national notification rates were calculated from suspected typhoid counts and projected populations. A district-clustered Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) estimated annual notification rates, 95% confidence intervals, and rate ratios against that reference. Geographic analyses described district variation. A secondary negative-binomial GEE examined whether within-district changes in malaria notification rates were associated with changes in suspected typhoid notifications.
eIDSR recorded 1,016,325 suspected typhoid notifications from 2019 to 2025. Annual national notification rates ranged from 1,290 per 100,000 population in 2019 to 2,054 per 100,000 in 2025. Rate ratios relative to the reference ranged from 2.41 to 3.84. Every district-clustered 95% confidence interval lay above the reference, and all seven Holm-adjusted two-sided p values were below 0.002. In 2025, district notification rates ranged from 43 to 5,116 per 100,000 population. A doubling of the within-district clinical malaria notification rate was associated with a typhoid rate ratio of 1.44 (95% CI 0.87-2.39; p = 0.14).
Routine suspected typhoid notification rates exceeded the reference in every study year and varied widely between districts. The pattern may reflect true transmission, diagnostic classification, care seeking, reporting, or combinations of these processes. Standardized febrile-patient screening, sentinel blood culture, and register and eIDSR review in both high- and low-notification districts are needed to determine how routine notifications relate to culture-confirmed typhoid.

articles.titulo: Maternal Nopp140 ensures production of zygotic ribosomes in early larval mushroom body neuroblasts
articles.autores: Meher KA, DiMario PJ (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Stem cells and their progenitor offspring express copious amounts of nucleolar ribosome biogenesis factors (RBFs) and ribosomes. Various human ribosomopathies show different pathologies due to differential sensitivities of tissue-specific stem cells to mutations in ribosomal proteins (ribosomal stress) or RBFs (nucleolar stress). Previously, we showed that Type I/II neuroblasts (NBs) in developing Drosophila brains show sensitivity to nucleolar stress while mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) remain resilient. Here, we depleted the RBF, Nopp140, to investigate differential sensitivities of the various larval brain NBs to nucleolar stress. MBNBs showed larger and brighter nucleoli when labeled with anti-Nopp140-RGG reflecting higher demands for ribosome biogenesis when compared to Type I/II NBs. In Nopp140-/- larvae lacking zygotic Nopp140, MBNBs but not Type I/II NBs maintained deposits of maternal Nopp140 which contributed to zygotic ribosome formation. MBNBs exhibited higher zygotic ribosome density compared to Type I/II NBs in both wild type and Nopp140-/- larvae. Although the ribosome pool in MBNBs remained predominantly zygotic, they still retained maternally inherited ribosomes until the 1st instar larval stage. Thus, perdurance of maternal Nopp140 in Nopp140-/- MBNBs afforded resilience to nucleolar stress by enabling zygotic ribosome production while other Nopp140-/- NBs lacking maternal and zygotic Nopp140 showed sensitivity.

articles.titulo: Computational Discovery of Enzyme-targeted Insecticides and Acaricides: In Silico Strategies for Next-generation Mosquito and Tick Control
articles.autores: Vijay M, Pandey S, … Manjunathachar HV (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Vector-borne diseases impose a substantial burden on global public health and livestock productivity. Mosquitoes and ticks serve as major vectors of malaria, arboviral infections, and tickborne diseases, while some vector-associated conditions, including WHO-listed Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs), are also transmitted. The continued reliance on chemical insecticides and acaricides has accelerated the emergence of resistance, compromised the efficacy of existing control strategies, and underscored the urgent need for novel, mechanism-driven interventions. Recent advances in computational medicinal chemistry have transformed early-stage discovery by enabling structure- and ligand-based virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, free energy calculations, AI/ML, and pharmacophore-driven hit prioritization. These in silico approaches facilitate rapid exploration of chemical space, identification of enzyme-selective inhibitors, and early ADME and eco-safety profiling. This review focuses on enzymatic targets involved in neurophysiological and detoxification enzymes as promising molecular vulnerabilities in arthropod vectors. Key targets, such as acetylcholinesterase, glutathione S-transferases, carboxylesterases, cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, UDP-glycosyltransferases, and emerging metabolic targets, represent promising vulnerabilities for next-generation vector control strategies. By synthesizing current computational methodologies, this review integrates early ADME prediction, ecotoxicological profiling, and resistance modeling, highlighting the translational potential of in silico hits toward experimentally validated, resistance-aware vector control strategies.

articles.titulo: Bacteria-Derived Micro/Nanoparticles for Vaccine Design
articles.autores: Xu Y, Luo T, … Sun X (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Vaccines have profoundly reduced the global burden of infectious diseases and are increasingly being explored for cancer immunotherapy. However, developing vaccine platforms capable of simultaneously achieving efficient antigen delivery, precise immune modulation, and durable protective immunity remains a major challenge. Bacteria-derived micro/nanoparticles (BPs) have recently emerged as promising vaccine platforms that integrate the structural advantages of nanomaterials with the intrinsic immunostimulatory properties of bacterial components. Their micro-to-nanoscale dimension, pathogen-mimicking architecture, and capacity for multivalent antigen presentation facilitate efficient lymphatic trafficking, antigen-presenting cell targeting, and coordinated activation of both innate and adaptive immunity. Moreover, the endogenous pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) within BPs serve as built-in adjuvants, potentiating antigen cross-presentation, inducing trained immunity, and eliciting robust T-cell and B-cell responses. These unique structure-function relationships have accelerated the clinical translation of BP-based vaccines, with several candidates now in clinical trials or already commercialized. In this review, we discuss the fundamental mechanisms, engineering strategies, and clinical research progress of BPs in vaccine development, while critically emphasizing the current challenges in safety, mechanistic elucidation, and scalable manufacturing. We further outline future opportunities for harnessing BPs as precision-tailored platforms for next-generation immunization paradigms.

articles.titulo: Epigenetic Crosstalk Between BCG-Infected Macrophages and Naïve Monocytes: Potential Role of the Extracellular Vesicles.
articles.autores: Ellinger L, Alipoor SD, … Lerm M (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of death from infectious disease. Infected cells secrete extracellular vesicles (EVs), nanosized membrane-bound particles containing bioactive molecules known to mediate intercellular communication and may contribute to immune regulation during infection. We hypothesized that factors released by Mycobacterium bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-infected macrophages (MΦs), including EVs, could contribute to epigenetic remodeling of naïve monocytes and influence their response to subsequent Mtb infection. A transwell co-culture system enabled communication via soluble factors and EVs between BCG-infected MΦs and naïve monocytes undergoing differentiation into recipient MΦs. The recipient MΦs exhibited altered DNA methylation patterns compared to those co-cultured with untreated, Staphylococcus aureus-infected or hydrogen peroxide-exposed MΦs. These DNA methylation changes were accompanied by a trend toward lower GFP-based Mtb burden in vitro. BCG-infected MΦs released EVs with a distinct proteomic profile enriched in tuberculosis-related pathways. Exploratory integration of the EV proteomic and DNA methylation datasets from the recipient MΦs identified potential molecular associations, including a TNF-centered network enriched in phagosome and tuberculosis pathways. These findings indicate that exposure to the intercellular environment generated by BCG-infected MΦs, including EVs and soluble factors, is associated with DNA methylation changes and modulation of antimycobacterial responses in recipient cells. Further studies using purified EVs and targeted mechanistic approaches are required to define the relative roles of EVs and other soluble mediators.

articles.titulo: Trained immunity in sepsis from immune reprogramming to precision immunotherapy.
articles.autores: Liu N, Gan T, … Wang Z (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Sepsis represents a severe systemic inflammatory response to infection, with complex immune dysregulation at the core of its pathophysiology. Conventional therapies remain limited to effectively modulate immune status while controlling infection, contributing to high mortality rates and severe long-term complications.In recent years, trained immunity,a form of innate immune memory, has demonstrated novel potential for regulating immune responses through metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic regulation. This narrative review integrates mechanistic and translational evidence on trained immunity in sepsis, with particular emphasis on key signalling pathways, their contributions to immune dysregulation, and potential biomarkers. It further discusses emerging precision immunotherapy strategies.Targeting trained immunity and assesses their opportunities and challenges in clinical translation, with particular emphasis on personalised treatment design and safety evaluation.Finally, we consider the application prospects of trained immunity in the long-term chronic inflammation and immune dysfunction associated with sepsis. However, direct clinical evidence remains limited, and validated biomarkers for identifying trained immune states in patients with sepsis are currently lacking. Future multidisciplinary studies are therefore needed to define clinically relevant trained immune states and establish reliable biomarkers for precision immune intervention in sepsis.

articles.titulo: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis.
articles.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.autores: Jiang Q, Dikdan RJ, … Shi L (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine-leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.
articles.resumo_pt_v6: Em camundongos com TB, metabolômica dirigida e transcriptoma mostram que o controle agudo vem com ativação de mTORC1, glutaminólise, glicólise e metabolismo de arginina e serina; a infecção crônica reduz mTORC1, aumenta o catabolismo de BCAA e baixa a glutamina. Glutamina oral restaurou aminoácidos pulmonares, reforçou mTORC1 e reduziu moderadamente carga bacteriana e lesão; dados humanos reanalisados mostram queda de glutamina circulante na progressão.

articles.titulo: Dietary Hercynine Protects Intestinal Stem Cell Function During Epithelial Repair and Aging Through Insulin Signaling.
articles.autores: Zhang Q, Fu F, … Chen H (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Intestinal stem cell (ISC) dysfunction compromises epithelial repair and contributes to intestinal aging, yet naturally derived metabolites that preserve ISC homeostasis remain incompletely defined. Through metabolomic profiling of a standardized edible mushroom extract, we identified hercynine (HER) as the most abundant detected metabolite and investigated its role in intestinal repair and aging. In Drosophila, HER accelerated post-injury epithelial repair by promoting timely restoration of ISC/progenitor dynamics and epithelial differentiation. During physiological aging, mid-life HER supplementation preferentially attenuated age-associated ISC/progenitor dysfunction, accompanied by improved intestinal homeostasis, enhanced organismal fitness, and extended lifespan. Mechanistically, HER shifted aged ISC/progenitor transcriptomes toward a more youth-associated state, with genetic and pharmacological pathway-perturbation experiments supporting the functional involvement of insulin signaling in HER-mediated improvements in aged ISC/progenitor homeostasis. HER was also associated with remodeling of the gut microbiota during injury repair and aging; microbiota perturbation experiments suggested that this remodeling represented an accompanying response to HER treatment rather than the primary driver of ISC protection. In aged human small intestinal organoids, HER improved budding capacity, ISC/progenitor-associated activity, and epithelial differentiation, while reducing p-AKT levels, supporting a conserved epithelial response in a mammalian model. Together, these findings identify HER as a mushroom-derived metabolite that supports ISC-centered intestinal epithelial repair and mitigates intestinal aging, highlighting dietary metabolites as potential modulators of stem cell-associated epithelial homeostasis during tissue repair and aging.

articles.titulo: Krüppel regulates cell cycle exit and limits adult neurogenesis of mushroom body neural progenitors in Drosophila.
articles.autores: Chen D, Man J, … Kimata Y (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Neural progenitors typically exit the cell cycle during development, limiting adult neurogenesis. Here, we identify Krüppel (Kr) as a regulator of cell cycle exit and elimination of mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) in Drosophila. Neuroblast (NB)-specific Kr RNAi and the Irregular facet (KrIf-1) mutation prolong MBNB lifespan and enable continued adult neurogenesis. Despite low post-embryonic expression, pupal stage-specific Kr depletion or misexpression causes MBNB retention, revealing a role distinct from its established embryonic function. Persistent MBNBs retain the early temporal factor IGF2 mRNA-binding protein (Imp) and fail to fully induce the late temporal factors Syncrip (Syp) and Eip93F (E93). Imp co-depletion suppresses MBNB retention following Kr depletion, identifying Imp as a key downstream effector. Krüppel homolog 1 (Kr-h1), a hormone-responsive transcription factor, functionally antagonises Kr by suppressing E93 expression. Kr-h1 knockdown partially rescues MBNB retention caused by Kr depletion, whereas its overexpression drives tumour-like NB overgrowth. Together, these findings identify Kr as a lineage-specific regulator coordinating the Imp/Syp transition and E93 expression to promote timely MBNB termination. This work reveals how temporal regulators control neural progenitor lifespan and restrict adult neurogenesis, linking intrinsic developmental programmes with hormone-responsive pathways in the Drosophila brain.

articles.titulo: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Remodeling of the Cockroach Brain Following Envenomation by Parasitoid Wasp Ampulex compressa.
articles.autores: Miroliubov A, Lianguzova A, … Libersat F (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The parasitoid jewel wasp Ampulex compressa induces prolonged hypokinesia in its cockroach host, Periplaneta americana, by injecting venom into the central nervous system. Although acute behavioral effects are well characterized, molecular processes associated with persistent hypokinesia remain poorly understood. We combined transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics to characterize brain changes 24 h after envenomation. RNA-seq of the central brain region containing the central complex and adjacent tissue identified 331 differentially expressed genes: 267 upregulated and 64 downregulated. Increased expression of tyrosine decarboxylase-like and arrestin-domain genes, together with reduced expression of a putative tyramine/octopamine receptor, suggests altered regulation of aminergic signaling. Changes in synaptic vesicle and innexin transcripts further implicate chemical and electrical synaptic function. Immune, detoxification, and extracellular-matrix genes were also affected. Independent metabolomic analyses revealed significant increases in fumaric acid and sorbitol, consistent with altered energy metabolism. Tyramine, octopamine, glutamate, and GABA showed no significant differences after multiple-testing correction, although several showed greater inter-individual variation in stung cockroaches. Together, these findings identify changes in neuromodulatory signaling, synaptic organization, and metabolic support as candidate processes associated with persistent hypokinesia. Their contributions to behavioral suppression remain to be distinguished from downstream responses to reduced neural activity and tissue stress.

articles.titulo: Flashing light modulates insect behavior in a species-specific manner.
articles.autores: Ali MS, Luo X, … Holmes TC (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Light is a powerful tool to study animal behavior.1-3 In contrast to natural light, almost all artificial light exhibits flicker, but most work on insect behavioral responses to light flicker focuses on flicker perceptual detection. We tested photopreference light-choice behavior across a wide range of Drosophila species in response to rhythmically flickering light using custom FLASH (flickering light of actuatable spectral hues) instrumentation and find species-specific behavioral responses and altered time-of-day-ordered behaviors that are evoked by light frequencies far beyond perceptual flicker frequency. Mutant analysis shows that behavioral responses to FLASH rely on all known classes of phototransduction, including Cryptochrome and Rhodopsin-7 expressed directly in brain neurons and the eyes. FLASH behavioral responses are abolished following ablation of the pigment-dispersing factor (PDF)-positive lateral ventral neuron circadian light input hub and in circadian mutants. These results suggest means for designing ecologically friendly light devices for species-specific insect behavioral control.

articles.titulo: Beyond taste: internal nutrient sensing and endocrine roles of selected insect gustatory receptors.
articles.autores: Zhang W, Sun J, Mang D (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Gustatory receptors (GRs) are best known for detecting chemicals that influence insect feeding and behavior. Studies of selected receptors, predominantly sugar-responsive GRs, have also established roles in internal nutrient sensing and physiological regulation. Fructose-responsive receptors such as Drosophila melanogaster Gr43a and Bombyx mori BmGr9 illustrate how internal carbohydrate availability can influence feeding, endocrine signaling, and hematopoietic proliferation. Other sugar-responsive GRs have been implicated in gut peptide hormone signaling and metabolic regulation. Here, we examine the experimental evidence for these functions and distinguish established receptor-specific mechanisms from broader hypotheses concerning the GR family. We discuss how structural biology, single-cell approaches, and comparative functional studies can define the distribution and mechanisms of physiological GR functions. These findings motivate a framework connecting chemical sensing with internal physiological state, while their generality across GR lineages and contribution to ecological adaptation remain open questions.

articles.titulo: Volume Electron Microscopy of Cortical Organoids: Methods for Region Identification, Connectome Reconstruction, and Organelle Segmentation.
articles.autores: Dallere S, Mattioni A, … Boido M (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Volume electron microscopy (vEM) has become a powerful tool for 3D ultrastructural analysis of neural circuits, yet its application to human brain organoids remains limited, particularly for connectomic studies. Here, we established a comprehensive and scalable workflow for applying vEM to human cortical organoids, integrating correlative light and electron microscopy, large-area SEM (scanning electron microscopy) mosaic imaging, focused ion beam-SEM (FIB-SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) validation. By systematically comparing two embedding protocols in use, we demonstrated that the DeFelipe and Fairén (1993); Cano-Astorga et al. (2024a) method provides optimal compatibility with toluidine blue-stained semithin sectioning and enables reliable synapse segmentation and neurite tracing. In contrast, the Deerinck's protocol (2010) offers enhanced membrane contrast but limits postsynaptic density visualization. Using FIB-SEM imaging of peripheral, neuropil-like regions of cortical organoids, we achieved accurate 3D reconstruction of synapses, neurites and intracellular organelles, enabling quantitative assessment of synaptic apposition surfaces, neurite trajectories, and organelle distribution across defined cellular compartments. Together, our results demonstrate for the first time the feasibility of micro-connectomic reconstruction in human cortical organoids at nanometer resolution. This methodological framework expands the applicability of vEM to organoid systems and provides a robust foundation for future studies of human brain development, disease modeling, and therapeutic evaluation at the synaptic and subcellular level.

articles.titulo: Natural Infection Induces Antibodies Targeting Pfs230 Domains D1M and D7D8 with Potential for Malaria Transmission Blocking.
articles.autores: Harju T, Cao Y, Kumar N (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The natural immunogenicity of domain 1 (D1M) and domains 7 and 8 (D7D8) in Plasmodium falciparum transmission-blocking vaccine (TBV) candidate Pfs230 is assessed. Antibody reactivity by ELISA using endemic human sera from Zimbabwe (n = 301) and Thailand (n = 44) was evaluated. Regression analyses revealed significant positive correlations between responses to both domains. A 1-log increase in Pfs230-D1M reactivity predicted a 0.43- to 0.87-log increase in Pfs230-D7D8 reactivity across cohorts. Furthermore, Pfs230-D1M positivity increased the odds of Pfs230-D7D8 positivity by 59% to 89%. These data demonstrate that both Pfs230-D1M and Pfs230-D7D8 are highly immunogenic during natural infection, validating their potential as strong TBV candidates.

articles.titulo: Helical repeat protein mRSiC is required for rRNA fragment accumulation in T. gondii mitochondria.
articles.autores: Drakoulis N, Maschmann S, … Tetzlaff S (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Myzozoans, including apicomplexan parasites Plasmodium falciparum and Toxoplasma gondii, possess unusual mitochondrial genomes that only encode two to three respiratory chain subunits and extensively fragmented rRNAs forming a divergent mitoribosome. Heptatricopeptide repeat (HPR) proteins are expanded in myzozoans, with some functioning as mitoribosomal constituents. Additional HPR proteins have been proposed to function in post-transcriptional mitochondrial gene expression, though their specific roles remain unexplored. We present a phylogenetic analysis of HPR proteins that reveals extensive lineage-specific expansions, consistent with diversifications of mitochondrial gene expression systems within myzozoans. We further characterize mRSiC, a HPR found in T. gondii and its closest relatives. Using sRNA sequencing and RNA gel blot analyses, we show that mRSiC is required for the stabilization of two lineage-specific mitochondrial sRNAs, RNA33 and RNA42. Loss of mRSiC causes rapid depletion of these RNAs, followed by secondary reductions of rRNA fragments, defects in the respiratory chain, and impaired parasite proliferation. Together, these findings highlight the importance of HPRs in apicomplexan mitochondrial gene expression and illustrate how lineage-specific RNA-binding factors support highly derived mitochondrial expression systems.

articles.titulo: Hybrid Epidemiological-Neural Modelling of Dengue Under Climate-Socioeconomic Influence.
articles.autores: Adeniji A, Mahmood A, … He Z (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue transmission in climate-sensitive and socioeconomically heterogeneous settings arises from nonlinear interactions between environmental suitability, mosquito ecology, and human behaviour. Classical SEIR-type models offer mechanistic interpretability but are often constrained by observational noise and incomplete data, while purely data-driven approaches typically fail to respect underlying transmission dynamics. In this study, we introduce a hybrid epidemiological framework that embeds a temperature-unemployment driven SEIR-SEI model within a Physics-Informed Neural Network (SEIR-PINN). Using weekly dengue incidence data from Medellín, Colombia, we incorporate unemployment as a socioeconomic proxy that modulates transmission alongside climatic suitability. The Model performance was evaluated in two ways; the prediction of observed incidence, the SEIR-PINN achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.05 and R2 of 0.975, compared with MAE of 43.57 and R2 of 0.870 for a mechanistic SEIR-SEI baseline fitted under identical climatic and socioeconomic assumptions. Shuffled five-fold cross-validation provided held-out prediction of observed incidence within the 2009-2011 period, with mean MAE of 14.87 and mean R2 of 0.977 (out-of-fold MAE 14.89, R2 0.978). These held-out results interpolate within the observed epidemic and are not an assessment of prospective forecasting performance Importantly, the SEIR-PINN reconstructs latent human and mosquito compartments that remain biologically consistent across epidemic phases. By fusing mechanistic structure with data-adaptive flexibility, the proposed SEIR-PINN provides an interpretable framework for analysing the joint climatic and socioeconomic modulation of dengue transmission in an urban endemic setting. Although using Medellín as a single-city methodological case study, application of this framework to other dengue endemic settings requires external validation using additional locations, longer time periods, and independent datasets. The results therefore support the potential use of physics-informed hybrid models as interpretable tools for dengue surveillance and transmission-dynamics research, while recognising the need for further external validation across longer time periods and additional geographical regions.

articles.titulo: Mosquito Population Dynamics Across Successive Gonotrophic Cycles: A Structured Multiscale Mathematical Approach.
articles.autores: Nforba GDY, Teboh-Ewungkem MI, Ngwa GA (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: We develop a structured multiscale mathematical model for mosquito population dynamics that explicitly links gonotrophic-cycle processes to population-level demographic outcomes across multiple reproductive cycles. The model couples breeding-site movement, resting, oviposition, density-dependent recruitment, mortality, human biting, and repeated reproductive cycling, thereby quantifying contributions of mosquitoes that survive to complete multiple cycles. As a first step toward understanding the role of gonotrophic cycling in mosquito-borne disease transmission, we focus on mosquito demography, with the human population held at demographic equilibrium. We characterize the steady states of the model and their stability, derive a basic offspring number governing mosquito persistence, and investigate bifurcation behaviour and parameter sensitivity. The results show that incorporating additional gonotrophic cycles increases reproductive contributions and can qualitatively alter persistence predictions. Parameter regimes yielding extinction with one or two cycles can support persistence when a third cycle is included, while additional cycles can shift stable populations into oscillatory regimes at lower oviposition rates. Shortening the gonotrophic cycle can further promote persistence under low oviposition and modestly alter oscillation frequency and amplitude at higher oviposition. Sensitivity analysis identifies early gonotrophic-cycle processes, particularly first-cycle oviposition, successful blood feeding, and breeding-to-questing progression, as dominant regulators of the basic offspring number. More generally, oviposition, breeding-to-questing movement, biting, successful blood feeding, and return rates positively influence the basic offspring number, whereas stage-specific mortality acts negatively; the effects of later-cycle parameters are increasingly weighted by successful progression through preceding cycles. These results demonstrate that explicitly representing successive gonotrophic cycles can materially change predicted mosquito persistence, stability, and potential control targets.

articles.titulo: A national geocoded inventory of Aedes mosquitoes in Kenya: integrating published, archival, and digital sources across 124 years.
articles.autores: Muchiri SK, Mwangi LW, … Snow RW (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes, represent growing public health threats in Kenya and across sub-Saharan Africa. In the absence of licensed vaccines for either disease in Africa, targeted vector control remains the primary prevention strategy, making accurate knowledge of Aedes species distributions essential. Global inventories of Aedes species are severely under-representative for Kenya, with existing repositories documenting fewer than 200 unique locations. No comprehensive, geocoded national inventory integrating published, unpublished, and digital sources has previously been assembled.
Three complementary approaches were used to assemble a national geocoded inventory of Aedes species in Kenya including (i) a systematic review of peer-reviewed literature, theses, and conference abstracts; (ii) digitisation of unpublished archival reports from the Ministry of Health, Division of Insect-Borne/Vector-Borne Diseases (DIBD/DVBD), regional and municipal councils; and (iii) cross-referencing with Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and Walter Reed Biosystematics Unit's (WRBU) VectorMap repositories. Data were extracted using a standardised template, de-duplicated, and geocoded using Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates, Google Earth, or census enumeration area shapefiles. Aedes species were classified as principal or possible secondary vectors based on confirmed field detection and, for the principal vector, an established role in transmission during dengue and chikungunya outbreaks reported in Kenya.
A total of 1,802 time-site records were identified across 855 unique locations between 1901 and 2024, documenting 104 Aedes species. Unpublished archival records contributed 51% of all records, with peer-reviewed articles accounting for 43%. The principal vector, Aedes aegypti was the most widely documented species, reported at 522 unique locations. Eight possible secondary vectors with confirmed DENV and/or CHIKV detection were documented, with Aedes mcintoshi, Ae. ochraceus, and Ae. tricholabis the most frequently recorded. Geographic coverage was concentrated along the coast and western Kenya, with notable surveillance gaps in northern and northeastern regions.
This inventory represents the most comprehensive geocoded database of Aedes mosquito species ever assembled for Kenya, substantially exceeding the coverage of existing global repositories. It provides an essential empirical foundation for disease and vector surveillance, ecological niche modelling (ENM) and sub-national targeting of vector control interventions in Kenya.

articles.titulo: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels.
articles.autores: Bermann TL, Barbosa DAM, … da Luz Wallau G (30 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

articles.titulo: Developmental site type, larval productivity, and insecticide susceptibility of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
articles.autores: Zongo S, Toe HK, … Namountougou M (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Arboviral diseases, including dengue and chikungunya, are increasing in sub-Saharan Africa. This study assessed Aedes aegypti larval productivity across three container types and examined associations with abiotic parameters and insecticide resistance patterns in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. From July to September 2024, a semi-field experiment was conducted at the Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme. Tires, terracotta jars, and buckets were exposed outdoors for natural colonization. Larval abundance and six abiotic parameters (pH, temperature, salinity, conductivity, total dissolved solids, and redox potential) were recorded over 11 rounds. Susceptibility bioassays were performed on emerging Ae. aegypti adults using deltamethrin (0.03%), bendiocarb (0.2%), and malathion (1.5%). A total of 14,020 larvae were collected, of which 93.13% were Ae. aegypti. Tires (mean = 83.3 ± 10.8 larvae/container) and terracotta jars (mean = 50.7 ± 7.4 larvae/container) harbored significantly more larvae than buckets (mean = 22.5 ± 3.3 larvae/container); tires and jars did not differ significantly. Generalized linear mixed model analysis showed no significant effect of abiotic parameters, while container type was strongly associated with abundance. Ae. aegypti populations were resistant to deltamethrin in all container types (mortality 5.2%-17.9%) and to malathion in both tested container types (mortality 88.4%-88.8%). For bendiocarb, populations were resistant in plastic buckets (85.3% mortality), showed suspected resistance in tires (91.6%), and were susceptible in terracotta jars (98.6%). Vector control should prioritize the management of tires and terracotta jars, and widespread pyrethroid resistance highlights the need for alternative tools.

articles.titulo: Insecticide Resistance in Anopheles stephensi: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Native and Invasive Populations.
articles.autores: Eshetu D, Gadisa E, … Yan G (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The rapid spread of the invasive malaria vector Anopheles stephensi in Africa, coupled with increasing reports of insecticide resistance, presents an emerging challenge for malaria vector control. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare insecticide resistance profiles and underlying resistance mechanisms between native Asian and invasive African populations and assessed their implications for insecticide resistance management.
PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, WHO IRIS, and gray literature sources were searched using terms related to An. stephensi, insecticide susceptibility, and resistance mechanisms. Data were extracted into Excel, critically appraised using an adapted Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-analysis software. The protocol was registered in Prospero International Registrar for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis in April 2025 (ID: CRD420251007131).
Thirty-one studies published between 2000 and 2025 were included. Pooled mortality was lower in invasive than native populations for the pyrethroids assessed in both ranges, including deltamethrin (72.6% vs. 83.5%), permethrin (68.3% vs. 89.0%), and lambda-cyhalothrin (47.0% vs. 87.0%), as well as for DDT (36.0% vs. 47.7%). Mortality was also lower in invasive populations for bendiocarb and propoxur, although propoxur was assessed in only one native-range study. Between-study heterogeneity varied substantially. Target-site mutations were reported at low frequencies; L1014F ranged from 1.4% to 32.9% in native populations and was detected in one study in invasive-range (5.7%), while L1014S (21.4-35%) was reported only in native-range. Metabolic resistance mechanisms involved cytochrome P450s (CYP4 and CYP6 families), glutathione S-transferases (GSTe2 and GSTe4), and esterases, including esterase E4 and carboxylesterase-6. No acetylcholinesterase-1 (ace-1) mutations were reported.
Anopheles stephensi exhibits resistance to multiple insecticide classes across its native and invasive ranges, with lower pooled mortality observed in the invasive range. Available evidence indicates an important contribution of metabolic detoxification, while target-site resistance markers, including vgsc L1014F/L1014S, were detected at lower frequencies and remain poorly characterized in invasive populations. High between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation and highlights the need for standardized phenotypic and molecular surveillance to guide locally tailored insecticide resistance management as An. stephensi continues to spread in Africa.

articles.titulo: Population genomics of the Anopheles farauti complex reveals a distinct regime of malaria vector evolution in the southwest Pacific
articles.autores: Autores não informados
articles.resumo_original: Abstract: The southwest Pacific has one of the highest per-capita malaria burdens outside Africa, yet how its malaria mosquitoes evolve is largely unknown. In African vectors, insecticide resistance evolves rapidly in large, connected populations carrying abundant standing variation. Southwest Pacific vectors show little to no biochemical resistance despite decades of insecticide-based control. We analyse 495 genomes from six taxa of the Anopheles farauti complex, which includes the region's major vectors. The complex radiated rapidly in the late Pleistocene concomitant to the peopling of Near Oceania. Thereafter, post-glacial sea-level rise and climate change fragmented its populations into recently colonised island isolates. Successive environmental and colonisation bottlenecks left a legacy of extraordinary inbreeding, most marked in island populations of the coastal specialist An. farauti sensu stricto, where sustained low effective population size has allowed deleterious alleles to be purged effectively; the inland generalists An. hinesorum and An. oreios retain more variation. After five decades of chemical control we recover a single resistance sweep, at Gste2, alongside recent selection at species-specific chemosensory gene repertoires. Severe inbreeding and the loss of standing variation have not prevented ecological success, challenging assumptions about how much variation and connectivity a vector population needs to thrive. This work establishes the first genomic foundation for this major vector system of endemic species through a biogeographically diverse region of the world.

articles.titulo: Overcoming Dengue Underreporting: A Machine Learning Framework for Automated Dengue Notification Based on Electronic Medical Records.
articles.autores: Sornsurin W, Suwannik W, … Ingsrisawang L (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hospital notification of dengue cases is frequently delayed, contributing to underreporting. At Thai provincial hospitals the bottleneck is administrative, not diagnostic: delayed discharge coding and clerical steps mean notifications are submitted late or omitted. Existing machine learning (ML) studies require clinician-annotated features absent in passive electronic medical records (EMRs). We propose a dual-pathway EMR framework for ML-based pre-population of surveillance reports. We analyzed 1031 dengue-suspected encounters (508 notifiable) from Surin Hospital, Thailand (2019-2022). Pathway A combines EMR data with manually documented clinical features; Pathway B uses only passive EMR data. Using an 80/20 stratified split, we tested 7 ML methods across 11 feature sets (77 combinations) with SHAP-guided feature elimination and 10-fold cross-validation. On the primary split, Pathway A (CatBoost) achieved an F1 score of 96.62%, 95.10% sensitivity, and 98.10% specificity (10-seed mean F1 95.7% ± 1.4%). Pathway B (LightGBM) achieved an F1 score of 84.42%, 94.12% sensitivity, 75.24% specificity, and a projected negative predictive value of 99.1% at 10% prevalence; 10-seed performance was lower (F1 78.5% ± 4.3%; sensitivity 89.1%). An exploratory LSTM-16 stacking model (F1 83.99%; precision 79.49%) performed best in precision and specificity among Pathway B. Test F1 SD across 10 seeds was ≤5.0% in 75 of 77 combinations. Within this cohort, passive EMR modeling achieved 91-94% sensitivity on the primary split (85-89% across seeds) without additional data collection, supporting the feasibility of ML-based notification in resource-constrained hospitals. Whether this reduces dengue underreporting must be established in prospective, multi-center studies.

articles.titulo: Oropouche fever in a changing tropical world: emergence, diagnostics and surveillance preparedness for India.
articles.autores: Thangavelu K, Murugaiyan M (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arthropod-borne virus causing Oropouche fever. OROV is transmitted predominantly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Although historically confined to South America, imported cases have been reported, highlighting its expanding geographic range and global public health relevance. Currently, there are no commercially available diagnostic assays for laboratory confirmation of OROV infection. In addition, no specific antiviral therapy or licensed vaccine is available. The recent emergence of cases outside traditional endemic areas further emphasizes the urgent need to address critical knowledge gaps. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on OROV virology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum and diagnostic challenges. We further contextualize OROV within the Indian setting, where competent Culicoides vectors are present, and discuss the importance of incorporating OROV into targeted surveillance and travel-related screening frameworks to facilitate early detection, reduce diagnostic misclassification and strengthen one-health preparedness in regions currently considered non-endemic.

articles.titulo: An Anti-diabetic drug Liraglutide inhibits Zika Virus Infection by Suppressing AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis.
articles.autores: Chiu TJ, Lu TW, … Lee JC (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is a global health-threatening illness that causes severe neurological complications, including microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Currently, no approved antiviral therapeutics or vaccines are available for treating ZIKV infections. Using cell-based and mouse experiments, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist clinically used to treat diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, on viral replication, cell viability, and host metabolic signaling pathways. We found that liraglutide exhibited significant antiviral activity in a dose-dependent manner, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 5.5 ± 0.6 μM for viral RNA replication suppression, without cytotoxicity at the effective concentration. Furthermore, liraglutide treatment extended the lifespan of ZIKV-infected AG129 mice and achieved an approximately 15-fold reduction in viremia. Mechanistically, liraglutide enhanced 5' adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and then increased the phosphorylation of transducer of regulated CREB activity protein 2 (TORC2), thereby downregulating expression of rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzymes, specifically phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and glucose-6-phosphatase. The antiviral activity of liraglutide was attenuated by both AMPK inhibitor Compound C and siRNA-mediated AMPK knockdown, supporting the claim that AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis contributes to liraglutide's anti-ZIKV activity. Given its clinical availability, liraglutide represents a promising therapeutic option for immediate repurposing for managing patients infected with ZIKV.

articles.titulo: Extracellular Polyphosphate at the Host-Pathogen Interface: Emerging Roles in Virulence and Therapeutic Opportunity.
articles.autores: Tennakoon A, Shrestha SK, Rijal R (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Polyphosphate (polyP) is a conserved linear polymer of orthophosphate residues linked by phosphoanhydride bonds. Although polyP has long been studied for its intracellular roles in phosphate storage, energy metabolism, and stress adaptation, growing evidence indicates that extracellular polyP also influences host-pathogen interactions. In a subset of well-characterized bacterial systems, including mycobacteria and Neisseria species, extracellular or surface-associated polyP has been directly linked to impaired phagosome maturation, altered macrophage activation, reduced complement-mediated killing, and reduced neutrophil antimicrobial activity, whereas in other pathogens, polyP supports virulence primarily via intracellular mechanisms. PolyP chain length governs biological activity: long-chain bacterial polyP is largely immunosuppressive, whereas short-chain host polyP promotes procoagulant and inflammatory signaling, although context dictates specific outcomes. Here, we examine models of polyP externalization, detail how extracellular polyP impairs phagosome maturation, reprograms macrophages, and inhibits complement, evaluate interbacterial and probiotic barrier functions, and consider therapeutic opportunities targeting polyP metabolism.

v6.implicacao: Polifosfato (tema sob Malária / Plasmodium) e Piloto de imageamento de polifosfato em inflamação hemorrágica: o comprimento de cadeia passa a ser variável obrigatória na leitura de polyP curto do hospedeiro; vale também para a colaboração de polyP em osso e MSC.

articles.titulo: Down-Regulation of eIF3L Is Associated with Decreased Susceptibility of Helicoverpa armigera to Cry1Ac.
articles.autores: Li N, Zhang C, … Liang G (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Large-scale cultivation of transgenic Bt crops has led to target pest resistance to Bt proteins, especially Cry1Ac. Under persistent selection pressure, Helicoverpa armigera has evolved resistance to Bt proteins in both laboratory and field populations, highlighting an urgent need to comprehensively elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying pest Bt resistance. Previous studies have confirmed that the eukaryotic translation initiation factor eIF2 plays a critical role in regulating Bt resistance. Our prior RNA-seq data showed significant differences in the expression level of eIF3L between susceptible and Cry1Ac-resistant strains of H. armigera. In this study, we further observed that the mRNA level of eIF3L was significantly reduced in larvae surviving Cry1Ac exposure. More importantly, heterologous expression of eIF3L increased the susceptibility of Sf9 cells to Cry1Ac. Consistently, knockdown of eIF3L was associated with reduced mortality in H. armigera larvae exposed to Cry1Ac. Together, our in vivo and in vitro results suggest that eIF3L is involved in Cry1Ac toxicity. Furthermore, eIF3L affects the expression of the Cry1Ac receptor genes CAD, ABCC2, and ABCC3. Collectively, these results indicate that down-regulation of eIF3L is associated with decreased susceptibility of H. armigera to Cry1Ac, providing novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying insect resistance to Bt proteins.
