articles.titulo: Travelers and Human-Animal Pathogen Transmission: A One Health Review of Zoonotic and Reverse Zoonotic Diseases.
articles.autores: Charoensakulchai S, Nuntanajaroenkul N, … Onwan M (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
International travel can accelerate the geographic spread of zoonotic pathogens and, under certain circumstances, contribute to epidemic or pandemic dissemination. Travelers may also transmit human pathogens to wildlife at tourism interfaces, acting as intermediaries in zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission.
Archived WHO and ECDC reports were screened for major zoonotic outbreaks in which international travel contributed to cross-border spread. PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies of human-to-wildlife transmission involving tourists, visitors, or travelers and traveler behaviors that could facilitate transmission.
Among 14 major zoonotic outbreaks, travelers commonly acted as spreaders following initial animal-to-human spillover by importing infections into new regions, sometimes resulting in onward transmission. This pattern was prominent with respiratory infections such as SARS, MERS, influenza, and COVID-19 and vector-borne infections such as Oropouche and Zika. Twenty-one studies reported possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human-wildlife tourism interfaces. Pathogens included respiratory viruses, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, enteric pathogens, and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Affected wildlife included great apes, primates, elephants, felines, carnivorans, ungulates, avians, reptiles, and urban-adapted wildlife in national parks, zoological parks, rehabilitation centers, and semi-urban parks. Five additional studies documented risky tourist behaviors, including close approach to, physical contact with, and feeding and visiting wildlife while having respiratory symptoms, and inadequate vaccination against measles, influenza, and polio.
Travelers can influence transmission bidirectionally by disseminating zoonotic pathogens and exposing wildlife to human pathogens. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization alongside conventional traveler protection.

articles.titulo: Quality assessment of malaria microscopy in Ouagadougou laboratories, Burkina Faso: accuracy of thick and thin blood smears.
articles.autores: Sawadogo PM, Kaboré JAT, … Zida A (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria microscopy remains the reference method for parasite detection in many low-resource settings, but its accuracy depends on slide preparation, staining quality, and reader performance.
This study aimed to assess the accuracy of routine malaria microscopy in selected laboratories in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
We conducted a cross-sectional study in four laboratories in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, and re-examined 1000 malaria blood smears initially read by 29 laboratory providers using independent expert microscopy. The slides examined were the same as those used for routine diagnosis to ensure no bias remains in the interpretation of the results.-Routine microscopy was performed using single reading, while expert microscopy was performed using double reading to comply with the WHO standard.
Twenty-nine microscopy providers participated, of whom 79.3% (23/29) were biomedical technicians, 17.2% (5/29) trainees, and 3.4% (1/29) biologists. Routine microscopy classified 184/1000 slides (18.4%) as positive and 816/1000 (81.6%) as negative, whereas expert re-reading identified 115/1000 (11.5%) as positive and 885/1000 (88.5%) as negative. Overall concordance was 88.1% (95% CI 85.9-90.0%), with a sensitivity of 78.3% (95% CI 69.9-84.8%), specificity of 89.4% (95% CI 87.2-91.2%), positive predictive value of 48.9% (95% CI 41.8-56.1%), and negative predictive value of 96.9% (95% CI 95.5-97.9%). Inter-reader agreement between routine and expert classification was moderate (Cohen's kappa = 0.54). Inaccurate routine readings were significantly associated with lack of refresher training and shorter slide-reading time.
Routine malaria microscopy performance in the participating laboratories was limited by false-positive readings, highlighting the need for strengthened quality assurance and continuous competency-based training.

articles.titulo: From Emerging Vectors to Missed Fevers: Why Fragile Health Systems Need Integrated Fever-Vector Preparedness.
articles.revista: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.autores: Abdi DA, Abdi Yusuf A, … Ahmed Mohamed A (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Climate change, urbanization, population mobility, and expanding mosquito vectors are reshaping infectious-disease risks in fragile health systems, where surveillance, diagnosis, and response often remain fragmented. This Policy Analysis argues that preparedness should move beyond isolated pathogen- or vector-specific programs toward an integrated fever-vector model. Undifferentiated fever should serve as the clinical entry point linking environmental intelligence, entomological surveillance, sentinel fever surveillance, tiered laboratory testing, and public health response. Such integration could improve recognition of arboviral infections overlooked in malaria-centered systems, support earlier outbreak detection, and guide targeted vector control and diagnostic preparedness. Somalia and the wider Horn of Africa illustrate the urgency of this shift because climate shocks, displacement, weak laboratory systems, and emerging urban vector-borne risks increasingly converge. The priority is not a more technologically complex system, but a connected and sustainable preparedness architecture capable of linking emerging vectors with febrile illnesses presenting in routine care.

articles.titulo: Evolutionary relatedness is a partially reliable predictor of host-associated microbiome composition.
articles.autores: Buffin K, Sabree Z (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Multicellular animals emerged into a microbial world, and they continue to be influenced by sympatric bacterial species. Host-associated microbiomes are recognized as critical contributors to their living domicile's success. Detailing how microbiomes are assembled and maintained by their hosts has important implications for animal health, agricultural productivity, and biodiversity interventions across the tree of life. Tens to 100s of bacterial genera are frequently detected in animal microbiomes, with some being uniquely and consistently detected in specific host species. Such discoveries have informed theories like phylosymbiosis that assert that host-associated microbiomes often reflect host species relatedness. We explored the predictive limits of this theory by performing a multi-scale dissimilarity-based comparative analyses using publicly available microbiomes drawn from 113 insect species spanning 14 insect orders. We detected a moderate inter-order phylosymbiotic signal (Mantel test: r = 0.392, P < 0.001) that was weakened (r = 0.173, P < 0.001) when the Blattodea were excluded from the analysis. Intra-order level phylosymbiotic signals varied widely for lepidopteran, hymenopteran, hemipteran, and blattodean host species microbiomes. Strong signals were often explained by obligate endosymbionts and/or nestmate-acquired gut bacteria, rather than by the total microbiomes. In short, host species-defining bacterial genera often represented a small fraction of the total observed microbial diversity in their respective insect host species, and these genera were well-integrated into host behaviors and/or physiologies that facilitated reliable intra- and inter-generational transmission. In contrast, microbiome compositional variability was so high in some insect orders that attempts to reflect host speciation events using their microbiomes were impossible.IMPORTANCEWhile all animals have microbiomes, the principles determining their composition remain an incomplete story. We leveraged the diversity of Insecta, arisen from 400 My of evolution, to evaluate if microbiome evolution is synchronized with the evolutionary history of their associated hosts. We found that host evolution plays a limited role in predicting microbiome composition, particularly due to the non-uniformity of host-microbial symbioses across insects. This result is in stark contrast to studies of similar scope in vertebrate organisms that spanned much less evolutionary time (i.e., up to 50 My). While insects of the order Blattodea, in particular, harbor exceptionally diverse microbiomes, many insect microbiomes are characterized by few bacterial genera. Our results suggest that host evolutionary history is but one of many factors, including differences in microbiome transmission modality, influencing insect microbiome evolution.

articles.titulo: Circadian rhythm regulates immune cell function and participates in the development and progression of metabolic diseases.
articles.autores: Yang Y, Zheng S, … Zhu J (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The circadian rhythm is an intrinsic ~24-hour timing system that plays a crucial role in regulating immune functions and maintaining metabolic homeostasis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how the circadian clock influences five key immune cell types-macrophages, dendritic cells, B cells, T cells, and natural killer cells-affecting processes such as phagocytosis, antigen presentation, cytokine secretion, cell migration, antibody production, and cytotoxicity, along with their underlying molecular mechanisms. This review also examines the effects of circadian disruption on metabolic disorders-including obesity, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, and atherosclerosis-mediated by immune cell pathways. Key mechanisms include adipose tissue macrophage polarization, rhythmic IL-17A secretion by γδ T cells, and the temporal regulation of the Th17/Treg cell balance. Additionally, we address current challenges in fully elucidating these mechanisms and translating them into clinical applications, emphasizing promising avenues such as multi-omics integration, biomarker identification, and chrono-immunotherapy, while noting that the latter remains supported primarily by retrospective and hypothesis-generating evidence. Overall, this review seeks to provide a comprehensive framework for the emerging field of circadian immunometabolism and to facilitate the development of time-based precision strategies for managing metabolic diseases.

articles.titulo: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in the tumor host macroenvironment: organ crosstalk, treatment trajectories, and net clinical benefit.
articles.autores: Jia MJ, Zhou J, … Liang FQ (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome links metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease, yet oncology commonly treats these conditions as separate comorbidities. This review examines CKM as a measurable component of the tumor host macroenvironment that may influence treatment tolerance and competing mortality. We integrate adipose, cardiorenal, and immune-metabolic pathways; clonal hematopoiesis is considered as a candidate link between inflammation, vascular injury, and treatment exposure, rather than a CKM staging criterion. Cancer and its treatment can also alter CKM status through organ injury and catabolism. Population studies associate higher CKM stages with cancer incidence and adverse host outcomes, but evidence for cancer-specific mortality and treatment efficacy remains inconsistent or limited. The central question is therefore whether CKM captures biologically meaningful host variation that changes tumor natural history, treatment tolerance, or both. Our oncology-adapted phenotyping framework retains the original American Heart Association CKM stages and adds organ reserve and activity, tumor and treatment context, and longitudinal change. It applies to both patients with active cancer and survivors, without introducing a new stage or stage-specific treatment recommendation. We outline assessment from pretreatment to survivorship and distinguish established cardiorenal indications from exploratory anticancer effects of CKM therapies. Net clinical benefit requires joint assessment of tumor control, treatment delivery, cardiorenal events, function, and patient priorities. Prospective validation is needed before the added phenotypes can guide cancer-treatment selection.

articles.titulo: Electrical, mechanical, and morphological properties of nano-filled HTV-SR/EPDM blends under AC corona aging.
articles.autores: Saleem MZ, Noorden ZA, … Algamili AS (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Among the various factors, corona discharge is recognized as one of the most threatening to degrade polymeric insulators. Over time, corona-induced deterioration has become a more dominant phenomenon in extra- and ultrahigh-voltage transmission lines. Therefore, this study investigates the aging effects on optimally balanced weight-percentage samples of high-temperature-vulcanized silicone rubber/ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (HTV-SR/EPDM) incorporating boron nitride (BN) and silicon carbide (SiC) fillers to identify the most desirable composition for resistance to degradation. The nano-sized fillers were loaded at 1, 3, and 5 wt.%. The test samples were subjected to an AC corona discharge for 72 h, utilizing a multi-needle high-voltage electrode and a plane-grounded electrode arrangement. The deterioration characteristics of the blend materials, both before and after aging, were evaluated through electrical, morphological, and mechanical analyses encompassing volume conductivity, dielectric response, scanning electron microscopy, tensile strength, and hardness measurements. The results revealed that at 8 kV stress across 30-60 °C, corona exposure increased the volume conductivity of 3 wt.% BN nanocomposites by only 25.8%-36.5%, whereas the unfilled blend experienced a much higher increase of 45.3%-88.3%. After corona exposure, high-loading nanocomposites retained up to 42.4% greater tensile strength than the degraded unfilled blend. The surface roughness was relatively lower for the filled blend samples following the corona discharge. Overall, the blend sample with 3 wt.% of BN demonstrated consistent behavior under all investigated conditions, indicating better corona-aging retardation. It has been shown that the incorporation of nano-sized fillers retards material degradation, thereby enhancing the performance of polymeric insulation.

articles.titulo: Assessing the role of single human chromosome 21 gene orthologues on amyloid-β toxicity in fly models.
articles.autores: Wenz K, Lau H, … Niccoli T (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Individuals with Down syndrome face a high risk of early-onset Alzheimer's disease. While an additional copy of the amyloid beta precursor protein gene (APP) is a primary trigger, other human chromosome 21 (Hsa21) genes are known to modulate amyloid-β1-42 (Aβ42) pathology and response. However, the relative impact of single genes during early neurodevelopment or in adult neurons remains unclear. To systematically evaluate the contribution of single gene effects, we overexpressed conserved Hsa21 Drosophila orthologues in an adult-restricted model of Aβ42 adult locomotor toxicity and found no single gene was able to modulate this biology. To evaluate developmental effects, we expressed these Hsa21 orthologues in the developing fly eye. We found that overexpression of the Hsa21 orthologues Pten/TPTE, Sik2/SIK1, plp/PCNT, pnt/ETS2 and O-fut2/POFUT2 significantly exacerbated Aβ42-induced rough eye phenotypes. Crucially, overexpression of pnt and O-fut2 was sufficient to drive severe neurodegeneration even in the absence of Aβ42. Our findings suggest that direct modulation of Aβ42 adult locomotor toxicity downstream of APP by single Hsa21 orthologues in adult neurons is limited in our model. Instead, overexpression of genes such as pnt/ETS2 and O-fut2/POFUT2 can disrupt early neurodevelopment, which may establish long-lasting vulnerabilities that impact on the later effect of Aβ42, underscoring the critical role of early brain development in later Down Syndrome Alzheimer's disease progression.

articles.titulo: Cortisol-Producing Adrenocortical Adenomas Drive a Unique Cytokine and Steroid Profile that Suppress Macrophage Immunity.
articles.autores: Crastin A, David Onesimu EL, … Ronchi CL (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) in patients with adrenocortical adenoma is associated with increased infection-related morbidity and mortality, although the mechanisms underpinning immunity dysfunction remain poorly defined. Given the central role of macrophages in innate immunity and immune-metabolic coordination, we investigated whether circulating factors in overt Cushing's syndrome (CS) and MACS alter macrophage inflammatory and metabolic function.
Primary human macrophages were polarised toward an inflammatory M1-like phenotype and treated with serum from patients with CS (n=6), MACS (n=10), or inactive endocrine adenoma. Cytokine secretion, polarisation markers, phagocytic capacity, mitochondrial viability, oxidative phosphorylation, and glycolysis were assessed and correlated with clinical and biochemical characteristics.
CS serum significantly reduced TNF-α and IL-6 secretion, and increased mitochondrial viability while promoting features consistent with anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization. CS serum also markedly suppressed oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis, and ATP production. MACS serum elicited a similar but attenuated profile, characterized by trends toward suppression of inflammatory and metabolic activation, consistent with early glucocorticoid-driven immune remodelling. Across all samples, serum-free cortisol concentrations correlated negatively with macrophage inflammatory cytokine production and positively with anti-inflammatory markers.
Patients with CS and MACS possess unique glucocorticoid and cytokine profiles that drive suppression of macrophage inflammatory and metabolic function. These findings provide mechanistic evidence that even mild cortisol excess in MACS may contribute to early innate immune remodelling that predisposes to infection and impaired inflammatory resilience.

articles.titulo: Schwann Cells Mount an Early Injury Response in Sarm1 Knockout Nerves, and Glial Sarm1 Loss Delays Axon Degeneration.
articles.autores: Stepanova E, Hunter-Chang S, … Deppmann C (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Schwann cells (SCs) transition into a Repair state after peripheral nerve injury, but their early injury response remains poorly understood. To characterize SC injury responses before axon fragmentation and in the absence of axonal SARM1 activity, we profiled WT and global Sarm1-knockout nerves within the first day after transection by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. We observed a substantial transcriptional injury response, enrichment of a putative intermediate SC state, and increased oxidative phosphorylation gene expression across injured SC states. These genotype-associated differences may reflect the absence of SARM1-dependent axonal signals, Sarm1 loss within SCs, or contributions from other cell types; they do not establish cell-autonomous control of the repair-state transition. We then asked whether glial Sarm1 influences axon degeneration when neuronal SARM1 is intact. We detect Sarm1 transcripts in SCs that increase after nerve injury. Reducing SC or glial Sarm1 delayed axon degeneration in co-cultures of Sarm1-knockout SCs with wild-type neurons, Sarm1 conditional knockout in Sox10 positive cells in mice, and Drosophila with pan-glial dSarm knockdown. Together, our findings characterize early SC injury states in nerves lacking SARM1-dependent axon degeneration and support a glial contribution to axon degeneration kinetics.

articles.titulo: How acidic compounds in human sweat open a mosquito ion channel.
articles.autores: Pantheerayil S, Kumar J (2 autores)

articles.titulo: miR-493 and miR-995-3p negatively regulate TSSK1 and affect male fertility in Zeugodacus cucurbitae.
articles.autores: Han HL, Zhai XD, … Wei D (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: MicroRNAs are crucial upstream regulators of reproductive development across insect species. In this study, we identified two testis-highly expressed miRNAs, the novel miR-493 and the known miR-995-3p, that directly target the testis-specific serine/threonine kinase 1 (ZcTSSK1) in Zeugodacus cucurbitae (Coquillett). Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) assays showed that miR-493, miR-995-3p, and ZcTSSK1 co-localized in the testicular transformation region. Overexpression of miR-493 and miR-995-3p significantly reduced the total sperm count and sperm viability, and decreased the offspring hatching rate. Moreover, RNAi-mediated knockdown of ZcTSSK1 reduced sperm count and sperm viability, decreased total bound phosphate groups in testes, elevated the proportion of apoptotic cells, and induced abnormal sperm morphology. These phenotypes closely mirrored those induced by miRNA overexpression. Collectively, these results indicate that miR-493 and miR-995-3p regulate ZcTSSK1 to modulate global protein phosphorylation in the testis and the differentiation of spermatids into mature sperm, thereby playing a crucial role in spermatogenesis in Z. cucurbitae. This study clarifies the essential role of the miR-493/miR-995-3p-ZcTSSK1 regulatory module in spermatogenesis and male fertility of Z. cucurbitae, and provides a molecular basis for exploring reproduction-targeted genetic control strategies against tephritid pests.

articles.titulo: Structural and biochemical characterization of ligand binding, oxidative modulation and inhibitory mechanisms of human inorganic pyrophosphatase 1.
articles.revista: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology
articles.autores: Mawani JS, Gnann AD, … Dowling DP (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Human inorganic pyrophosphatase 1 (hsPPA1) is a ubiquitous metalloenzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of cytoplasmic inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) into inorganic phosphate (Pi). hsPPA1 maintains cellular phosphorus homeostasis by removing the PPi released during the synthesis of biomolecules, thus making biosynthetic reactions thermodynamically favorable. Therefore, hsPPA1 is critical to cellular metabolism, and its upregulation and overexpression in cancer-cell proliferation and metastasis make hsPPA1 a promising enzyme target for the development of anticancer drugs. Here, we report X-ray crystal structures of hsPPA1 in multiple liganded states: with magnesium ions, with lithium ions and a fluoride-inhibited structure complexed with magnesium and pyrophosphate ions. These structures show that hsPPA1 adopts the conserved oligonucleotide/oligosaccharide (OB) fold, and substrate binding induces subtle conformational changes in the active-site residues. The structure of hsPPA1 with lithium ions bound, combined with functional studies, showed that Li+ can bind in the same sites as the M1 and M2 magnesium ions and inhibit the enzyme. In addition, functional assays on the variants of the proposed catalytic base residue (Asp118) and phosphate ions revealed details of the chemical mechanism of hsPPA1 and the dual effects of phosphate on hsPPA1 activity. Finally, we report on the effect of magnesium concentrations and reducing agent on hsPPA1 activity. These findings reveal a deeper understanding of hsPPA1 at the molecular level and establish a framework for structure-based inhibitor design.

articles.titulo: Glycosylation of the Premembrane Protein Is Required for Dengue Virus Replication in Both C6/36 and Vero Cells
articles.autores: Reneer ZB, Dong S, … Baric RS (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne, positive sense, single-stranded RNA virus that includes four serotypes (DENV1-4) that are further divided into distinct genotypes within a serotype. DENV causes approximately 100 million human infections each year. DENV virions encode a capisd surrounded by a lipid bilayer that encodes two glycoproteins, E and prM. During virion maturation, the premembrane protein (prM) is cleaved to form a mature virion, which includes partially mature and fully mature particles. The maturity state of the DENV virion affects both the infectivity of DENVs and the ability of antibodies to neutralize the virus. The prM glycoprotein is glycosylated and highly conserved across all DENVs. In particular, the N-linked glycosylation site at position 69 is present in over 99% of DENV genomes. In this manuscript, we investigated the importance of the N69 glycosylation site by generating both DENV2 and DENV4 loss-of-function viruses. These N69 glycosylation knockout viruses were generated by introducing a single amino acid mutation at site 69. Neither mutant virus had detectable titers despite multiple passages in vitro. To further investigate the importance of the glycosylation site, we generated another variation in which the N-linked glycosylation site was repositioned to a site proximal to residue 69. One of these proximal-glycosylation mutants showed viral replication at levels that approached wild-type (WT) DENV strains. Overall, this study demonstrated the importance of retaining an N-linked glycan on the prM protein at position 69 for DENV infectivity of mosquito cells and that inserting a glycosylation site in close proximity to position 69 may restore infectivity in some DENV4 strains.

articles.titulo: Identification and Characterization of Wenshan Mosquito Virus, a Putative Novel Bisegmented RNA Virus from Mosquitoes in Yunnan Province, China
articles.autores: Sun X, Li C, … Niu G (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-associated viruses pose significant public health threats globally, with Yunnan Province in southwestern China representing a critical hotspot for arboviral emergence. In this study, 2612 female mosquitoes belonging to three species (Culex tritaeniorhynchus, Anopheles sinensis, and Culex quinquefasciatus) were collected from Wenshan during summer 2023. Viral metatranscriptomic analysis identified a novel bisegmented positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, designated Wenshan mosquito virus (WSMV). Its genome comprises 4741 nucleotides across two segments: Segment 1 (3127 nt) encodes an S39 family peptidase and an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), while Segment-2 (1614 nt) encodes a capsid protein and a hypothetical protein. Pairwise nucleotide identity analysis revealed 87.62% and 86.96% identity with Hubei mosquito virus 2 (HMV-2) for Segments 1 and 2, respectively. Given the absence of established species demarcation criteria for this lineage, WSMV is described as a putative novel virus within the HMV-2-related group. Phylogenetic analyses using a common taxon set placed WSMV consistently with HMV-2 across both segments. WSMV was detected in Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Anopheles sinensis pools (MIR 2.08 and 1.54 per 1000, respectively), but not in the limited number of Culex quinquefasciatus pools tested; the host range of WSMV therefore remains to be fully defined. This study expands knowledge of mosquito-associated viral diversity in Yunnan's border regions and provides a molecular foundation for future investigations.

articles.titulo: Population Genetics-Informed Design and Deployment of Genetic Mosquito Control Strategies
articles.autores: Hill E, Raban R, … Akbari OS (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Population genomics can improve the design, deployment, and monitoring of genetic mosquito control strategies by revealing how genetic variation, population structure, and movement influence intervention outcomes. Here, we present a decision-oriented framework for integrating population-genetic information into conventional sterile insect technique (SIT), female-specific release of insects carrying a dominant lethal (fsRIDL), CRISPR-based precision-guided SIT (pgSIT), homing gene drives, and Wolbachia-based population suppression and modification strategies. Although these approaches differ in their mechanisms and intended outcomes, their effectiveness can be influenced by population connectivity, immigration, and local ecological conditions. Additional constraints are intervention-specific, including functional resistance alleles that can compromise homing gene drives, mating competitiveness and sex-sorting requirements for incompatible insect technique (IIT), and reproductive compatibility, maternal transmission, and pathogen-blocking efficacy for Wolbachia population modification. We describe how population-genomic surveys, functional assays, movement measurements, contained experiments, and spatial modeling can guide target selection, release-stock preparation, deployment planning, and surveillance. Importantly, we distinguish demonstrated field outcomes, including mosquito suppression and reductions in dengue incidence following Wolbachia-based interventions, from gene-drive outcomes that remain limited to laboratory and contained studies. We emphasize that genomic data alone cannot establish biological compatibility, predict field efficacy, or demonstrate epidemiological benefit. Instead, population-genetic measurements should inform locally parameterized models, predefined performance endpoints, and testable decision criteria evaluated against independent observations. Integrating population genomics with intervention-specific validation and prospective monitoring provides a practical framework for translating genetic mosquito control technologies toward responsible field deployment.

articles.titulo: Cuticle-Mediated Insecticide Resistance in Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex Mosquitoes: A Systematic Review
articles.autores: Bouledroua R, Briolant S, … Almeras L (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Control of vector mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae), particularly species belonging to the genera Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex, remains essential to limit the transmission of vector-borne diseases, but is made more difficult by the increasing level of resistance to insecticides. Among the mechanisms involved, the role of the mosquito's cuticle is receiving increasing attention. A systematic literature review was conducted in PubMed and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, resulting in the inclusion of 56 studies specifically addressing cuticle-associated insecticide resistance in mosquitoes. Available data indicate that cuticular resistance is not based on a single mechanism, but rather on various structural and biochemical modifications that can alter insecticide penetration and interact with other resistance pathways. Although several cuticle-related characteristics have been proposed as potential markers of resistance, their relevance depends on mosquito species, developmental stages, populations, and insecticides, underscoring the need for integrated approaches that combine structural, molecular, chemical, and functional analyses. Beyond resistance, the cuticle and its exuviae also provide valuable biological information that can facilitate mosquito identification and vector surveillance. Overall, a better understanding of the properties of the mosquito cuticle could improve the characterization of the resistance while expanding the use of cuticle-derived information in medical entomology.

articles.titulo: Viral Immunomodulation as a Potential Driver of Trained Immunity: Emerging Mechanisms of Innate Immune Memory and Antiviral Protection
articles.autores: John SP, Fraser IDC (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The discovery of trained immunity has challenged the longstanding view that immunological memory is restricted to the adaptive immune system. Trained immunity refers to the capacity of innate immune cells to undergo long-term functional reprogramming following exposure to microbial, endogenous, or environmental stimuli, resulting in enhanced responses to subsequent challenges. Trained immunity is mediated by epigenetic and metabolic remodeling, including changes in chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and cellular metabolism. Recent studies further demonstrate that these memory-like properties can also be established in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), providing a basis for their long-term persistence. While Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) and β-glucan are the best-characterized inducers of trained immunity, increasing evidence indicates that viral infections and viral vaccines can also induce durable innate immune reprogramming. Epidemiological studies have demonstrated heterologous protective effects associated with vaccinia, measles, and oral polio vaccines, while cytomegalovirus infection and severe SARS-CoV-2 infection have been linked to long-lasting alterations in innate immune function. Notably, many of these viruses possess potent immune evasion mechanisms that suppress interferon signaling, modulate NF-κB activation, disrupt antigen presentation, and alter myeloid cell function. We propose that viral immune evasion and immunomodulatory strategies may promote trained immunity by triggering compensatory metabolic, epigenetic, and transcriptional reprogramming that persists after resolution of infection. This review summarizes the historical development and molecular basis of trained immunity and examines emerging evidence linking viral infections and viral vaccines to innate immune memory. We further discuss the potential roles of virus-induced autophagy and long non-coding RNAs as mechanistic bridges connecting viral infection, immune reprogramming, and trained immunity. Understanding how viral infections shape innate immune memory may provide new opportunities for antiviral therapies, vaccine design, and broad-spectrum immune protection.

articles.titulo: Diabetes Mellitus and Infection Susceptibility: An Immunometabolic Interface
articles.autores: Al Zeir F, Hamdi M, … Seed Ahmed M (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a rapidly growing global health burden and a major driver of infection-related morbidity and mortality. Chronic hyperglycemia disrupts both innate and adaptive immunity through impaired complement activity, dysfunctional dendritic cells and natural killer cells, altered macrophage polarization and efferocytosis, and neutrophil defects including reduced chemotaxis, impaired phagocytosis, and dysregulated NETosis. These immune abnormalities, compounded by endothelial dysfunction and microvascular disease, increase susceptibility to severe and recurrent infections such as urinary tract infections, tuberculosis, pneumonia, skin and soft tissue infections, and invasive fungal diseases. Emerging evidence also supports a bidirectional relationship in which infections may precipitate or aggravate DM via mechanisms including molecular mimicry, β-cell injury, chronic inflammation, and gut microbiota dysbiosis, contributing to insulin resistance and β-cell dysfunction. Recurrent infections and frequent exposure to broad-spectrum antibiotics, together with altered pharmacokinetics, chronic wounds with biofilm formation, and prolonged healthcare exposure, create strong selective pressure for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in diabetic populations. Using clinical and scientific based evidence, this review explores mechanisms linking DM, infection risk, and AMR, highlighting implications for the diagnosis, therapy, stewardship, and vaccination, as well as outlines key research gaps including improved AMR surveillances stratified by diabetes status and integrated predictive models incorporating glycemic control, host factors, and microbial genomics.

articles.titulo: Site-specific acylation of type-I interferon pathway components couples cellular metabolism to antiviral immunity
articles.autores: Liu C, Nie A, … Zheng H (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling through the IFNAR-JAK-STAT axis is essential for antiviral immunity, and its output is determined, not only by the canonical phosphorylation and ubiquitination events that transmit and terminate the signal, but by additional modifications whose substrates are intermediates of cellular metabolism. Protein acylation, in which metabolite-derived acyl groups are transferred to lysine and cysteine residues, therefore constitutes a point at which the metabolic state contributes to the strength, duration and transcriptional output of the interferon response. Rather than survey these chemistries in isolation, we trace acylation through the pathway it regulates: from the IFNAR receptor complex and its associated kinases, through STAT activation and assembly of the ISGF3 complex, to the nuclear and effector functions of interferon-stimulated genes. At each tier, modification of defined residues alters protein stability, localization, complex assembly or transcriptional activity, and in some cases it does so in opposing directions. The resulting analysis of the data does not support acylation as a uniformly positive or negative regulator of IFN-I signaling; rather, the direction of effect is a function of the residue modified, the identity of the acyl donor and the metabolic context in which the modification is positioned, such that a single pathway component can be sensitized or desensitized depending on which sites are occupied. We develop this conclusion through the crosstalk between acylation and the canonical PTMs - competition at shared residues, and shared writers and erasers whose substrate preference shifts with metabolite availability - and through the settings in which this layer is subverted: viral manipulation of host acylation machinery, and the metabolic states of aging and metabolic disease.

articles.titulo: Mitochondrial dynamics in orthoflavivirus infection: insights from human and mosquito hosts
articles.autores: Stevens M, Miesen P (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses alternate between vertebrates and mosquitoes, where they establish distinct infection outcomes. In humans, infection is acute and associated with immune activation and cellular damage, whereas in mosquitoes, viruses persist lifelong without overt pathology. Mitochondria, as central regulators of metabolism, signaling, and immunity are emerging as key determinants of these distinct responses. Here, we discuss how mitochondrial dynamics and inter-organelle communication may shape orthoflavivirus replication and infection outcome.

articles.titulo: Trained Macrophages Propagate Glycolysis-Dependent Inflammation in Human Airway Epithelial and Fibroblast Cells Mediated by the Synergistic Action of IL-1β and TNF
articles.autores: Connolly SA, Murphy DM, … Basdeo SA (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Trained immunity, a form of innate immune memory that enhances subsequent pro-inflammatory responses in myeloid cells, has been well described; however, its impact on lung structural cells remains unknown. As airway epithelial and fibroblast cells are key regulators of respiratory immunity, we hypothesized that they may be affected downstream of trained innate immune responses, thereby amplifying lung inflammation. We aimed to define the effects of soluble mediators from 'trained' macrophages on the immune functions of lung epithelial and fibroblast cells and determine the mechanisms that drive this inflammatory amplification loop during trained immunity. Alveolar epithelial cells (A549) and lung fibroblasts (MRC-5) were treated with conditioned medium from untrained or IFN-γ trained macrophages stimulated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis or unstimulated controls. Soluble factors from trained macrophages significantly increased IL-6, IL-8, and ICAM-1 in A549 and MRC-5 cells, compared with controls. A key role for IL-1β in driving these responses was identified using a blocking antibody. Addition of recombinant IL-1β and TNF showed that these cytokines synergise to promote inflammation in alveolar epithelial cells and lung fibroblasts. Trained macrophages, with their enhanced production of IL-1β and TNF, also drove matrix metalloproteinases, tissue factor, and thrombin generation in airway epithelial and fibroblast cells. Crucially, the synergistic effects of IL-1β and TNF were abrogated by 2-deoxyglucose. This suggests that crosstalk between innate immune signals and airway epithelial and fibroblast cells which drive inflammation is mechanistically mediated by glycolysis. These findings will help to inform the design of therapeutics targeting immunometabolism and immunothrombosis. Furthermore, our data identify the innate immune-epithelial/fibroblast cell network as a tractable target for host-directed therapies.

articles.titulo: Targeted metabolic reprogramming of CD8 T cells restores immune regulation in lupus
articles.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.autores: Oba S, Humbel MH, … Tsokos GC (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by pathogenic humoral autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking T cell dysfunction to aberrant B cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a CD8+ T cell-intrinsic metabolic defect that promotes humoral immune dysregulation in lupus. CD8+ T cells from patients with SLE exhibited elevated CD38 expression associated with reduced intracellular NAD+ levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cytotoxic capacity. Pharmacologic inhibition of CD38 with the small-molecule inhibitor MK-0159 restored NAD+ metabolism and rescued cytotoxic function in human CD8+ T cells ex vivo. To selectively target this pathway in vivo, we developed anti-CD8 antibody-conjugated nanoparticles encapsulating MK-0159. In lupus-prone MRL/lpr mice, CD8-targeted delivery enhanced granzyme B expression, improved degranulation, reduced plasmablast responses and autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and renal pathology. Importantly, targeted delivery restored CD8+ T cell function without broad immune perturbation. These findings identify CD38-driven NAD+ depletion as a reversible immunometabolic checkpoint limiting CD8+ T cell cytotoxic competence and support a model in which targeted restoration of cytotoxic fitness contributes to the control of humoral autoimmunity in SLE.

articles.titulo: A gut-brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
articles.autores: Cui X, Meiselman MR, … Yapici N (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut-brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop-a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut-brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

articles.titulo: IsoVEM: Accurate and robust isotropic reconstruction with defects section inpainting for volume electron microscopy
articles.autores: He J, Zhang Y, … Sun F (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Volume electron microscopy (vEM) provides 3D nanoscale imaging of biological ultrastructure but faces a key limitation: anisotropic resolution, where the axial detail is markedly inferior to the lateral detail. Existing deep learning solutions lack stability, compromise structural continuity, and fail to address practical slice defects. We present IsoVEM, a robust deep learning method for high-fidelity isotropic vEM reconstruction. Utilizing a video Transformer architecture, IsoVEM captures long-range cross-slice dependencies to maintain structural continuity and delivers accurate reconstructions under significant anisotropy. This helps overcome a major bottleneck in large-scale, high-throughput ultrastructural analysis. As a self-supervised model, IsoVEM requires no pre-existing isotropic training data and generalizes well, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques across four vEM modalities. In a landmark application, IsoVEM successfully resolves the complete 3D ultrastructure of mouse sperm in seminiferous tubules, yielding unprecedented insights into organelle assembly and maturation.

articles.titulo: Large deletion variants in a Plasmodium falciparum ookinete protein gene and associations with different endemic populations and mosquito vectors
articles.autores: Palmer S, Fogang B, … Conway DJ (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The Plasmodium falciparum PIMMS43 gene encodes an ookinete protein that is important for mosquito infection. Here, large indel variants within the coding sequence are identified and their frequencies in natural infections of humans and mosquitoes are investigated. Comparing long-read genome sequences in a small panel of P. falciparum strains and related species revealed a 150 bp deletion in the central part of the gene in several strains, including the standard 3D7 reference genome. Mapping of short-read genome sequence data from 524 P. falciparum infections from 9 different countries to full-length PIMMS43 showed that the 150 bp deletion and an alternative 90 bp deletion were common structural variants. Across African populations, the 150 bp deletion had a mean allele frequency of 32% and the 90 bp deletion had a mean frequency of 12%, with significant geographical variation. Targeted genotyping of 30 oocysts from naturally infected mosquitoes in Tanzania using nested PCR showed overall deletion-variant frequencies similar to those observed in human infections in the same country. Although sample size was limited, differences in the variant frequencies in oocysts from Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles funestus suggest potential vector-specific selection. The findings highlight the importance of surveying structural genomic variation and its potential role in parasite adaptation.

articles.titulo: Temperature-sensitive N^6^-methyladenosine interactions prime the malaria parasite for transmission
articles.autores: Mussgnug S, Vignolini T, … Baumgarten S (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original: To infect a mosquito vector, malaria parasites differentiate into male and female semi-quiescent gametocytes that can re-initiate development within seconds after transmission. The rapid switch from gametocytes to gametes relies on multiple environmental changes, yet the molecular events driving this developmental transition remain unclear. Here, using high-resolution RNA and ribosome profiling, we identify the mRNA modification N6-methyladenosine (m6A) as an essential mechanism to restructure protein synthesis during Plasmodium falciparum transmission. We show that male parasites rapidly repress translation of m6A-methylated transcripts after mosquito uptake via the binding of YTH.2, a reader protein with an m6A-binding domain. This repressive interaction is temperature sensitive and requires the temperature drop accompanying human-to-mosquito transmission. Hence, m6A primes the transcriptome during semi-quiescence for a post-transcriptional response that is activated by an environmental shift. These data reveal how unicellular organisms incorporate external stimuli for lifecycle progression, providing potential avenues to combat malaria.

articles.titulo: Spatiotemporal Modeling of Aedes aegypti in La Guajira: An Approach Based on Environmental Suitability (MaxEnt) and Temporal Dependence (ARIMA)
articles.autores: Marceló-Díaz C, Charry L, … Santamaría E (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Environmental, climatic, and socioeconomic conditions coexist in La Guajira, northwestern Colombia, which may be conducive to dengue (DENV) transmission. However, knowledge gaps remain regarding the distribution and temporal dynamics of its primary vector, Aedes aegypti. In this study, the potential distribution and autoregressive temporal persistence of Aedes aegypti in the municipality of Manaure were assessed by incorporating climatic variables into maximum entropy (MaxEnt) and autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models with the goals of identifying areas of entomological risk and supporting vector surveillance. First, occurrence records were obtained from published literature, the National Institute of Health's collection of medically important insects, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), and field surveys to model environmental suitability. Nineteen WorldClim v2.1 bioclimatic variables were initially considered to model the potential distribution using MaxEnt, and model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Second, the temporal dynamics of Ae. aegypti were assessed over one year in two neighborhoods that exhibited high and low DENV incidence using Prokopack aspirators for indoor sampling. The MaxEnt models exhibited good predictive performance (AUC > 0.8), and the annual temperature range (BIO7) was identified as the most influential predictor. To address the temporal dynamics, a total of 2313 mosquitoes (53% females) were collected. The La Cruzada (LC) neighborhood exhibited greater temporal dependence (φ1 = 0.679; p < 0.001) than the Altos de Salinas (AS) neighborhood did (φ1 = 0.309; p = 0.02), whereas rainfall that occurred one to two weeks earlier was positively associated with an increase in female abundance in both neighborhoods. The integration of spatial and temporal models facilitated the identification and prioritization of risk areas. At the spatial level, MaxEnt identified patterns that were consistent with the ecology of the vector at the state level; in municipalities in which entomological risk is highest, time series analyses could be conducted to improve forecasts and planning for the integrated management of arboviruses transmitted by the Ae. aegypti mosquito.

articles.titulo: Community Diversity and Predictive Distribution of Japanese Encephalitis Virus Vectors Across North Borneo Sabah Malaysia
articles.autores: Safree ASA, Karim KA, … Ong SQ (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Japanese encephalitis (JE) is an important but neglected tropical disease that remains endemic in Borneo, Malaysia. Effective management and monitoring of the disease require information about the mosquito vector; however, data on the ecology and spatial distribution of Culex mosquitoes associated with Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) are limited. This study characterized Culex community composition across multiple districts in Sabah and predicted the spatial distribution of major vector species using species distribution modeling (SDM). Mosquitoes were collected from Tawau, Semporna, Sandakan, and Kudat using CDC light traps, BG-Sentinel traps, and human-baited double nets during peak activity periods. Community diversity and species composition were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Detrended Correspondence Analysis (DCA), while multiple machine learning algorithms were evaluated for SDM performance. A total of 3,169 mosquitoes were identified, with Cx. quinquefasciatus and Cx. vishnui as the dominant taxa. DCA revealed distinct habitat associations among vector species, with Cx. vishnui strongly associated with coastal environments, while Cx. tritaeniorhynchus, the principal JEV vector, was more frequently associated with forested habitats. SDM projections identified highly suitable habitats for Cx. tritaeniorhynchus along the western coast and northern Kudat, while the predicted distribution of Cx. quinquefasciatus closely overlapped with densely populated urban and peri-urban areas in western Sabah. These findings demonstrate substantial spatial heterogeneity in Culex vector distribution across Sabah and highlight ecological hotspots where intensified vector surveillance, targeted control measures, and JE prevention strategies should be prioritized.

articles.titulo: Global Patterns and Future Changes in West Nile Virus Risk Under Climate Change
articles.autores: Zhang J, Zhao X, … Jiang F (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Over the past two decades, West Nile virus (WNV) has spread to many countries and caused substantial losses to life and property worldwide, while climate change has further influenced its transmission by affecting its vectors. To understand the global distribution of WNV and changes in its risk, 2039 occurrence records were collected and a MaxEnt model was used to simulate the current and future potential risk distribution. Temperature seasonality, annual mean temperature, precipitation of the coldest quarter, and precipitation seasonality contributed relatively strongly to the spatial distribution simulation of WNV, together accounting for 83.3%. Overall high-risk areas showed a certain banded pattern, mainly concentrated between 25 °N and 55 °N in the Northern Hemisphere and between 25 °S and 35 °S in the Southern Hemisphere. Under global climate change, the area classified as high potential risk by the MaxEnt model is projected to expand. In the 2050s and 2070s, the average area classified as high potential risk is projected to increase by 0.133 × 106 km2 and 0.106 × 106 km2, respectively, representing increases of 7.705% and 6.161%. The best prevention strategy is mosquito control, especially in areas at high risk for WNV. These results may help identify areas where enhanced WNV surveillance and vector control warrant further consideration under climate change.

articles.titulo: Comparative Analysis of Innate Immune Modulation Between BeAn19991 and ISCDC-2024 Oropouche Virus Strains
articles.autores: Accordini S, Gianesini N, … Caldrer S (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Oropouche virus (OROV) has re-emerged as a significant public health threat during the 2023-2025 outbreak, characterized by an unprecedented geographic expansion beyond endemic regions. The virus has been detected in various regions, including the Caribbean, as well as in Europe and the United States, among travelers from Central and South America. This epidemic was associated with the expansion of a novel reassortant strain, which may exhibit enhanced viral fitness and immune evasion properties. Although orthobunyaviruses are known to counteract interferon responses, the specific strategy adopted by OROV remains incompletely understood. In this study, we compared the in-vitro behavior of the prototype strain BeAn19991 and a 2024 isolate representing the reassortant virus responsible for the 2023-2025 epidemic (ISCDC-2024), focusing on innate immune response. We examined the sensitivity of the two strains to IFN-β antiviral activity and their ability to induce type I IFN in fibroblast. Furthermore, we characterized the innate immune response triggered by in-vitro infection of PBMCs from healthy donors. Although the two viral strains exhibited a similar plateau in viral RNA accumulation and comparable sensitivity to exogenous IFN-β, the IFN-β induction in fibroblasts was delayed, with higher levels induced by ISCDC-2024 than by BeAn19991. Moreover, the two strains displayed distinct innate immune profiles in PBMCs: BeAn19991 predominantly induced a robust antiviral IFN-driven response, whereas ISCDC-2024 infection was associated with an IL-6-dominated inflammatory pattern. Overall, these findings highlight distinct phenotypic features of the contemporary reassortant isolate and suggest strain-specific differences in the modulation of innate immunity, potentially reflecting distinct immune evasion strategies. If confirmed, this hypothesis could have significant implications for infection transmission, viral persistence and disease severity, highlighting the need for continuous surveillance and functional characterization of emerging OROV strains to drive public health interventions and antiviral countermeasures.

articles.titulo: Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
articles.autores: Richardson RB, Kikawa C, … Evans MJ (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

articles.titulo: Discovery of Ebselen Analogs as Novel Inhibitors of Polyphosphate Metabolism to Attenuate Virulence and Show Combination Benefit with Meropenem in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
articles.autores: Wang Y, Zhou Z, … Deng X (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major opportunistic pathogen responsible for severe hospital-acquired infections. The challenge in treating these infections is exacerbated by increasing antibiotic resistance. Polyphosphate kinases (PPKs), specifically PPK1 and PPK2, play a critical role in the virulence, stress response, and antibiotic tolerance of P. aeruginosa, making it a compelling target for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we describe the discovery and development of ebselen analogs as novel inhibitors against PPK1Pa and PPK2Pa. Biochemical and cellular assays revealed that ebselens interfere with the polyphosphate homeostasis within the bacterium. EB-1 and EB-18 treatment significantly reduced intracellular polyP levels, mirroring the phenotypic effects observed in Δppk strains, including impaired biofilm formation, reduced motility, and attenuated production of pyoverdine and pyocyanin. Notably, EB-1 and EB-18 showed combination benefit with meropenem against P. aeruginosa in the Galleria model, supporting their potential as an adjunctive agent to improve the antibacterial efficacy of meropenem. Most representative compounds, including EB-1 and EB-18, showed no detectable cytotoxicity in the tested mammalian cells. These findings underscore ebselen analogs as promising dual-specific PPK inhibitors, establishing a valuable strategy for the development of adjunct therapies via the PPK-mediated anti-virulence pathways.

articles.titulo: Chikungunya-associated encephalitis in a neonate and an older child: A two-case series from northern Thailand
articles.autores: Kusontammarat P, Kunanitthaworn N, … Sudjaritruk T (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chikungunya-associated encephalitis is an uncommon but serious neurological complication in children. We report two pediatric cases of CHIKV-associated encephalitis from Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. The first case was a term male neonate with vertically acquired infection following maternal peripartum chikungunya. He developed high-grade fever and diffuse limb edema on day 5 of life, followed by lethargy, poor feeding, and decreased spontaneous movements. CHIKV RNA was detected in both serum and CSF, supporting CHIKV-associated encephalitis. The second case involved a previously healthy 11-year-old boy with community-acquired mosquito-borne infection who presented with acute febrile encephalopathy, lower-extremity myalgia, generalized rash, conjunctival injection, and brief hand spasms. His mother and several neighbors had recently recovered from chikungunya. Although CSF analysis showed no pleocytosis and brain MRI was unremarkable, CHIKV RNA was detected in serum and CSF. Both patients recovered completely with supportive care without neurological sequelae. These cases illustrate that CHIKV-associated encephalitis may occur in both neonates and older children following vertical and community-acquired transmission, respectively. During outbreaks, clinicians should consider CHIKV infection in children presenting with acute encephalitis, particularly neonates born to mothers with peripartum infection and children living in endemic areas. Early recognition, laboratory confirmation, and appropriate supportive care are essential to optimize neurological outcomes.

articles.titulo: A Parasite-Rich Microeukaryome Shows Tribe-Structured Covariation with the Bacteriome in Non-Urban Mosquitoes (Culicinae) from Colombia
articles.autores: Cuervo-Tinjacá G, Marín-Suárez J, … Gómez-Palacio A (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The eukaryotic component of the mosquito microbiota, which includes parasites, remains poorly characterized, partly because amplicon surveys suffer from host co-amplification and primer bias. To describe their microeukaryome, we re-analysed total-RNA sequencing libraries from non-urban Culicinae collected in Antioquia, Colombia, whose virome and bacteriome were previously characterized. Ribosomal 18S and 28S reads were mined from 26 pooled samples representing 18 morphotypes and four tribes. The curated 18S matrix comprised 1350 reads across 45 taxonomic features, and a rank-aware inventory retained 29 non-redundant lineages. Stramenopiles (Gyrista and Bigyra) accounted for 43.0% of curated 18S reads and Microsporidia for 20.0%. Seven features with best-hit labels of insect parasites occurred in 15 samples; Amblyospora was supported at the genus level, whereas a Coelomomyces-labelled signal was corroborated by 28S evidence only at the order Blastocladiales. Community composition differed among tribes after rarefaction; in non-rarefied data, this difference depended mainly on an Aspergillus-labelled feature of uncertain provenance. In 21 matched samples, microeukaryome and bacteriome ordinations were concordant (Procrustes correlation = 0.507; p = 0.0047), but not within tribes, and no concordance with the virome was detected. These results provide a baseline for the microeukaryome of non-urban Neotropical Culicinae and its tribe-structured covariation with the bacteriome.

articles.titulo: Gut Microbiota Restructuring and Elizabethkingia Enrichment in Aedes albopictus Larvae Under Pyriproxyfen Exposure
articles.autores: Xie LH, Xu SY, … Chen H (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aedes albopictus transmits dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its expanding range, together with widespread insecticide resistance, threatens the sustainability of chemical vector control. Pyriproxyfen (PPF) is an insect growth regulator used in mosquito control, but the relationship between gut bacteria and larval responses to PPF remains poorly characterized. We combined 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with culture-dependent isolation to characterize gut bacterial communities in Ae. albopictus following acute PPF exposure and identify candidates for functional investigation. The 24 h median lethal concentration (LC50) for the Fuzhou population was 10.27 mg/L. Community profiles were compared among Fuzhou larvae dying at 2× LC50, surviving at 5× LC50, and receiving solvent alone; solvent-treated Foshan laboratory larvae served as an external population reference. Bacterial richness and Shannon diversity were lower in both exposed Fuzhou groups than in the Fuzhou solvent-treated control, and community structure differed among the four groups (PERMANOVA, R2 = 0.797, p = 0.001). Elizabethkingia accounted for 35.0% of bacterial reads in survivors, compared with 22.8% in non-survivors and 7.6% in Fuzhou solvent-treated controls, with significantly higher relative abundance in survivors than in either comparison group. Culture-dependent isolation from survivors yielded 29 isolates representing nine genera, including three isolates assigned to Elizabethkingia anophelis by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Concordant sequencing and culture-based evidence, together with the recovery of viable isolates, positions Elizabethkingia as a tractable entry point into this question, opening a route to ask whether the larval microbiota can be managed to preserve the efficacy of pyriproxyfen-based control as resistance to other insecticide classes spreads.

articles.titulo: Tetracycline Exposure Disrupts Gut Microbiota and Immune-Antioxidant Homeostasis in Honey Bees
articles.autores: Hao M, Wang X, … Liu Y (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Antibiotic exposure can perturb the gut microbiota of honey bees, but its associations with host physiological responses remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the effects of tetracycline exposure on survival, locomotor activity, gut bacterial communities, and immune- and antioxidant-related gene expression in Apis mellifera workers maintained under controlled laboratory cage conditions. Tetracycline exposure at 100, 300, and 450 μg/mL reduced worker survival in a concentration-dependent manner, while 100 μg/mL increased daytime locomotor activity without affecting sucrose consumption. Tetracycline also altered gut bacterial community structure, with marked reductions in several core taxa, particularly Snodgrassella and Bartonella, whereas Commensalibacter, Lactobacillus Firm4 and Firm5 increased, especially at the highest concentration. Changes in immune- and antioxidant-related gene expression were more pronounced in the gut than in the head. Moreover, Snodgrassella abundance was positively correlated with Relish expression in the head and with Apidaecin and CAT expression in the gut. These findings demonstrate that tetracycline exposure reduces honey bee survival and is associated with coordinated alterations in gut bacterial communities and host physiological responses.

articles.titulo: Intrinsic Variations in Stress Resistance and Host-Microbiome Interactions Influence Neurodegenerative Disease-Associated Phenotypes in Drosophila Models
articles.autores: Yue X, Dulac A, … Birman S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Drosophila is widely used to model human diseases, including metabolic and neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease (PD). Disease-induced changes in locomotion and stress resistance are typically assessed against healthy control flies, such as the white-eyed strain w1118, used as a reference for normal physiology and behavior. We compared two independent w1118 lines and found striking differences in their susceptibility to oxidative stress induced by the PD risk factor paraquat and nutrient starvation. Axenic rearing increased oxidative stress resistance in the susceptible line but not the resistant one, without affecting starvation resistance. We found that the stress-sensitive line had higher levels of Clostridiales bacteria and the endosymbiont Wolbachia in its gut microbiota and lower immune effector expression (antimicrobial peptides, lysozymes) in the head and gut. In a genetic PD model, the stress-resistant background strongly attenuated the locomotor defects mediated by the pan-neuronal expression of human mutant α-synuclein but not when expression was restricted to the dopaminergic neurons of the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster. These findings implicate the microbiome and immune effectors as modifiers of PD penetrance and suggest that accounting for such hidden variability could increase consistency in neurodegenerative disease modeling in Drosophila.

articles.titulo: Dissecting the Lethal Mechanism of Silencing TcSP3 in Tetranychus cinnabarinus Eggs Reveals a Biosafety-Favorable RNAi Target
articles.autores: Chen X, Zeng S, … Lu W (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Serine proteases are essential for development and physiology in arthropods. We previously showed that RNAi-mediated silencing of the serine protease gene TcSP3 induces embryonic lethality in the carmine spider mite, Tetranychus cinnabarinus, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. Here, we adopted an integrated strategy-transcriptome sequencing, RT-qPCR validation, and gene-specific RNAi-to pursue two distinct but complementary objectives: (i) to map the downstream transcriptional response to TcSP3 silencing and thereby identify candidate RNAi targets and (ii) to functionally interrogate the leading candidate, TcHKB, in order to infer the lethal mechanism. We additionally performed a preliminary evaluation of the environmental biosafety of the resulting candidate dsTcHKB for RNAi-based mite management. TcSP3 silencing altered 495 genes (464 upregulated and 31 downregulated). Six downregulated candidate genes were validated; among these, silencing TcHKB resulted in the highest egg mortality (53.57%), accompanied by malformation and incomplete development, whereas silencing TcbHLH and Tcngn-1 caused 34.99% and 22.93% mortality. Sequence homology and domain prediction indicate that TcHKB encodes a Sp5-like transcription factor of the Sp/KLF family, suggesting that TcHKB may indirectly affect developmental signaling. The downregulation of TcHKB is therefore proposed as a possible, yet unverified, explanation for the observed embryonic lethality; direct measurements of Sp5, β-catenin, or Wnt pathway activity are still required to confirm this link. For translational application, we also conducted a preliminary biosafety evaluation of dsTcHKB. Under our tested conditions, sequence alignment showed no extensive homology between dsTcHKB and genes of the predatory mite N. barkeri, and direct bioassays detected no adverse effects on its survival, hatchability, or development; the dsRNA additionally degraded almost completely on cowpea leaves within three days. These initial observations address two specific risk aspects-environmental dissipation on cowpea leaves and non-target effects on N. barkeri-but do not yet establish general safety. This study suggests a plausible mechanism for TcSP3/TcHKB-mediated lethality and identifies TcHKB as a candidate RNAi target warranting further biosafety assessment.

articles.titulo: BeetleFormer: A Sequence Transformer for Identifying Effective Double-Stranded RNAs in the Red Flour Beetle, Tribolium castaneum
articles.autores: Xu J, Zhang W, … Yang J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Selecting double-stranded ribonucleic acid (dsRNA) reagents remains a bottleneck in insect gene-function research and RNA interference (RNAi)-based pest management. We developed BeetleFormer to learn sequence patterns associated with RNAi screening outcomes in Tribolium castaneum. The model integrates multiscale convolutions, long-range attention, complementary-strand symmetry and sequence descriptors. Following previous dsRNA prescreening research, 14,821 iBeetle reagents meeting mortality or phenotype criteria were used as positives and 14,825 messenger RNA (mRNA) fragments as negative samples. Source genes and overlapping sequences were separated across training, validation and testing. On 6083 test sequences, BeetleFormer achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.978, accuracy 0.913 and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.831, compared with 0.888, 0.817 and 0.636 for an adapted convolutional-recurrent comparator. Ablations supported local processing and strand symmetry; AUC remained 0.976 after exact-length matching. External testing on 20 published dsRNAs and 20 mRNA negatives yielded AUC 0.928. Model interpretation revealed terminally concentrated sequence sensitivity and organized learned representations. These findings establish an improved sequence-based prescreen that turns genome-scale RNAi observations into candidate-selection evidence, supporting functional-genomics experiments and the development of RNAi-based pest control.

articles.titulo: RNA Interference for Insect Pest Management: Linking dsRNA Structure-Function Relationships, Delivery Biology, and Field Performance
articles.autores: Murtaza G, Qayyum N, … Smagghe G (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: RNA interference (RNAi) is a sequence-guided approach to insect pest management, but its efficacy depends on more than the choice of an essential target gene. The biological activity of exogenously applied double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is shaped by its molecular properties, extracellular stability, interactions with delivery materials, cellular uptake, intracellular trafficking, and access to the RNAi machinery. This review examines these linked determinants and considers how differences in insect physiology contribute to variation in RNAi susceptibility. We discuss target-gene selection and sequence specificity alongside nuclease activity, gut barriers, endosomal processing, and systemic transport. Particular attention is given to nanomaterial-based formulations, including chitosan, liposomes, and layered double hydroxides, as well as microbial, symbiont-mediated, host-induced gene silencing (HIGS), and spray-induced gene silencing (SIGS) platforms. Their potential benefits are assessed in relation to formulation reproducibility, production costs, environmental fate, non-target exposure, and regulatory requirements. By connecting dsRNA structure-function relationships with delivery biology and application performance, this review identifies mechanistic questions and validation steps that must be addressed to develop reliable RNAi-based tools. RNAi is best regarded as a complementary component of integrated pest management, with field deployment requiring species-specific optimization and evidence-based environmental assessment.

articles.titulo: Infection with the Entomopathogenic Fungus Metarhizium robertsii Suppresses Cellular Immunity and Activates Humoral Antibacterial Responses in Spodoptera frugiperda
articles.autores: Zhang M, Wang J, … Liu X (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda, is a globally distributed agricultural pest. Metarhizium robertsii is an entomopathogenic fungus (EPF) with great application potential for the biological control of S. frugiperda. Nevertheless, to date, there have been no reports describing the interactions between M. robertsii and the immune system of S. frugiperda. In the present study, we investigated the pathogenicity of M. robertsii against S. frugiperda and demonstrated that this fungus exhibits high virulence toward the pest. M. robertsii infection induces apoptosis and necrosis in hemocytes of S. frugiperda, which, in turn, reduces circulating hemocyte abundance. Fungal infection also impairs the spreading capacity of plasmatocytes. These adverse effects on hemocytes collectively lead to a marked suppression of host cellular immune responses, including phagocytosis, nodulation, and encapsulation. Meanwhile, M. robertsii infection upregulates the expression of prophenoloxidase genes in hemocytes, resulting in significantly elevated phenoloxidase activity in host hemolymph. Transcription of antimicrobial peptide genes is also increased in the fat body following fungal challenge. Upregulation of these humoral antibacterial response-related genes enhances the antibacterial activity of hemolymph. This study reveals the mechanistic basis underlying immune interactions between M. robertsii and S. frugiperda and deepens our understanding of the pathogenic mechanisms employed by EPF.

articles.titulo: Functional Characterization of Prothoracicotropic Hormone in Larval Development and Diapause of Ostrinia furnacalis
articles.autores: Cao S, Jia J, … Ma H (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Prothoracicotropic hormone (PTTH) is a secretory neuropeptide initiating insect metamorphosis via ecdysteroid synthesis. While the PTTH-ecdysone axis is well-established in development, its specific role in diapause regulation and the underlying mechanisms in agricultural pests like Ostrinia furnacalis are less understood. To address this, we identified O. furnacalis' PTTH gene (OfPTTH) and investigated its spatiotemporal expression and function using RNAi and 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) rescue assays. Our findings show that OfPTTH expression was lowest during diapause, significantly increasing upon its termination, and exhibiting an extended developmental periodicity during diapause. OfPTTH-silencing was associated with reduced expression of ecdysone-signaling genes, leading to broad physiological disruptions including altered ecdysone and juvenile hormone signaling, inhibited insulin/IGF signaling, suppressed lipid metabolic reprogramming (triglyceride accumulation), and decreased heat shock protein expression. These events ultimately caused larval diapause-like developmental arrest, pupation failure, and mortality. Exogenous 20E treatment promoted pupation in OfPTTH-knockdown larvae and restored the expression of several downstream ecdysone-signaling genes, suggesting that impaired 20E signaling contributes to the observed developmental abnormalities. This study supports an important role of the PTTH-20E axis in O. furnacalis development and diapause-associated regulation and provides a basis for further evaluation of OfPTTH as a potential target for RNAi-based pest management.
