articles.titulo: Knockdown of ncm Induces Significant Mortality of Phyllotreta striolata
articles.autores: Chen K, Ren H, … Chen M (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The striped flea beetle, Phyllotreta striolata, is one of the most destructive pests in Brassicaceae plants worldwide. RNA interference (RNAi) has been proven to be a promising alternative strategy for pest control, especially for P. striolata, since its larvae feed on roots and the adults feed on leaves. Gene ncm is critical for insect physiological process, as it is responsible for processing precursor mRNA into mature mRNA. In this study, we cloned and characterized the ncm gene (Psncm) from P. striolata. Additionally, we found silencing Psncm either by microinjection or oral delivery led to the high mortality of P. striolata adults. Moreover, the onset of feeding refusal was observed on day 3 in Psncm-silenced P. striolata. Finally, a total of 875 differentially expressed genes were identified in dsPsncm-injection treatment, among which 322 were upregulated and 553 were downregulated. Additionally, these genes were mainly clustered in "metabolism" and "organism systems" pathways. Consistent with the transcriptome analysis, metabolomics analysis revealed that silencing of Psncm was associated with significant alterations in multiple metabolic pathways. These results suggest that Psncm is a potential candidate for RNAi-based pest management, although further functional validation, field delivery, dsRNA stability, non-target safety, and resistance risk assessment are needed.

articles.titulo: Structural and Compositional Characterization of a Human Adipose Allograft for Soft Tissue Volume Restoration
articles.autores: Bouamar H, Fanniel V, … Hill S (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Subcutaneous adipose tissue loss from trauma, congenital deformity, aging, or weight loss can compromise facial contour, symmetry, and soft-tissue support, making volume restoration a central target in soft-tissue reconstruction. Current approaches include autologous fat grafting, dermal fillers, and decellularized adipose matrices, each having distinct limitations related to tissue harvesting, material composition, durability, or absence of adipocyte structure. To address these limitations, dermaClaeTM was developed as a ready-to-use, minimally manipulated nonviable human structural adipose allograft for small volume applications in delicate areas, such as the face. This study characterizes the structural and compositional properties of dermaClae using histology, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and biochemical assays to evaluate tissue structure, composition, and extracellular matrix (ECM) components relevant to tissue integration and remodeling. Histological and SEM analyses demonstrated adipocytes surrounded by collagen-rich connective tissue. Adipocyte cross-sectional area demonstrated overlapping distributions with native adipose tissue. Total collagen, laminin α4, proteoglycans, and elastin levels were all measured in dermaClae at concentrations higher than native adipose tissue. Retained adipocyte structures contribute to tissue bulk, cushioning, and support, while the ECM provides a structural framework relevant to incorporation and remodeling. Together, these characteristics may position dermaClae as a potential natural alternative to current approaches for facial reconstruction.

articles.titulo: Surface Engineering of Organosilica Nanoparticles Modulates Cellular Uptake, Cytotoxicity, and Mechanobiological Responses
articles.autores: Mun EA, Zhaisanbayeva BA, … Khutoryanskiy VV (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: Surface chemistry is a major determinant of nanoparticle-cell interactions, yet their influence on mechanobiological properties of cells remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the cytotoxic and mechanobiological effects of thiolated and PEGylated organosilica nanoparticles and evaluated whether cortical stiffness could serve as a complementary measure of nanoparticle-cell interactions. Methods: We evaluated thiolated organosilica nanoparticles (Si NP-SH) and two PEGylated nanoparticles (Si NP-PEG750 and Si NP-PEG5000) in non-cancerous human pulmonary fibroblasts (HPF) and cancerous human pulmonary adenocarcinoma (A549) cells. We assessed cellular viability and nanoparticle uptake after exposure and used atomic force microscopy to measure cellular cortical stiffness. Additionally, nanoparticle effects on neuroblast proliferation and mitotic progression were examined in Drosophila melanogaster larval brain explants. Results: HPF cells were markedly less sensitive to all nanoparticle formulations across the tested concentration range, whereas A549 cells showed dose-dependent sensitivity, with thiolated nanoparticles producing the earliest and greatest reduction in viability. Despite a comparable uptake of Si NP-SH and Si NP-PEG750, the thiolated nanoparticles produced greater toxicity, whereas Si NP-PEG5000 showed lower uptake but intermediate toxicity. Atomic force microscopy measurements demonstrated significant cortical softening in Si NP-SH-treated A549 cells, while HPF cells were unaffected. All nanoparticles reduced Drosophila melanogaster neuroblast proliferation in a similar order: Si NP-SH > Si NP-PEG750 > Si NP-PEG5000. Conclusions: The biological activity of organosilica nanoparticles is predominantly dependent on accessibility and intracellular reactivity of surface thiols rather than uptake alone. PEGylation shields thiol reactivity, with higher PEG molecular weight additionally reducing nanoparticle uptake. The consistency of viability, uptake, cortical stiffness, and neuroblast proliferation identifies AFM-derived cortical stiffness as a valuable complementary measurement of nanoparticle-induced stress.

articles.titulo: Effects of Oral and Volatile Peppermint Oil Exposure on Feeding and Hypopharyngeal Gland Development in Young Worker Honey Bees (Apis mellifera)
articles.autores: Kim YH, Kim JM, … Oh D (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Protein nutrition during early adulthood is closely associated with hypopharyngeal gland (HPG) development in worker honey bees, but whether peppermint oil (PO) influences this physiology and whether its effects depend on exposure route remain unclear. Newly emerged Apis mellifera workers were exposed for up to six days to dietary PO (0.05%, w/w), volatile PO (0.05% in paraffin oil, v/v), both routes, or control conditions. Protein-patty mass disappearance and recorded deaths were monitored daily, while body and head weight, HPG acinus area, feeding- and nutrient-associated gene expression in the brain and fat body, HPG mrjp1 expression, and MRJP1 protein abundance were assessed at designated sampling points. PO-exposed cages showed greater cumulative protein-patty mass disappearance and significantly altered feeding- and nutrient-associated gene expression, although individual molecular responses varied among exposure routes. All PO-treated groups had larger HPG acinus areas than controls on days 4 and 7; mrjp1 expression was significantly higher in PO-F on day 4 and in all PO-treated groups on day 7. MRJP1 protein abundance was also increased in all PO treatments. Volatile exposure showed numerically higher mortality on observation day 3, but cumulative mortality did not differ significantly from the control. These results indicate that dietary and volatile PO exposure were associated with changes in feeding-related measures and HPG development in young worker honey bees.

articles.titulo: Gut microbiome stability and mycotoxin degradation confer aflatoxin B1 tolerance in Folsomia candida (Collembola)
articles.autores: Wang K, Zhang Y, … Xu Y (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a potent carcinogen that contaminates food and feed, causing significant economic losses and health problems in animals. Soil-dwelling arthropods such as Collembola often coexist with molds and are thought to tolerate toxic fungi, yet their responses to mycotoxins remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of AFB1 on Folsomia candida. We found that AFB1 exposure caused dose-dependent increases in mortality, reductions in body size, and declines in reproductive output of this species. Remarkably, the growth retardation induced by AFB1 was largely alleviated upon removal of AFB1 from the diet. Analysis of gut microbial communities showed that high concentrations of AFB1 had little effect on overall community composition; the gut microbiota was dominated by the phyla Pseudomonadota and Bacillota and by the genera Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, and Enterobacter. Metagenomic profiling suggested that Wolbachia possesses the potential capability against AFB1. Furthermore, a large proportion of culturable gut bacterial isolates were found to be tolerant of AFB1 and could degrade it to varying degrees. Thus, while high AFB1 levels negatively affect F. candida's fitness, they do not perturb its gut bacterial community and its ability to degrade AFB1, indicating an adaptation of this host-microbiome system to AFB1 exposure.
Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a widespread mycotoxin that threatens food safety and animal health, but how soil animals tolerate AFB1 remains poorly understood. We show that the soil springtail F. candida is highly tolerant to AFB1 even though high doses reduce survival, growth, and reproduction. Notably, AFB1 exposure caused little change in gut microbial community structure. In addition, many gut bacterial isolates tolerated AFB1 and degraded it in vitro. These results suggest that microbiome stability and microbial detoxification capacity may help F. candida persist in mycotoxin-contaminated environments. Our study also highlights toxin-tolerant soil animals as a potential source of microorganisms and functions for aflatoxin biodegradation.

articles.titulo: Defining the Diphyllin Pharmacophore for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral V-ATPase Inhibition by Structure-Guided Scaffold Modifications
articles.autores: Elkabbany A, Sanford LM, … Davisson VJ (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The threat of emerging viral diseases presents a critical societal need for broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. A key contribution to antiviral options would be a broad-spectrum agent that can treat a wide variety of viral diseases. Vacuolar H-ATPase (V-ATPase), a host proton pump critical for endosomal acidification, serves an essential role in facilitating the entry of multiple viruses. Diphyllin, a naturally occurring V-ATPase inhibitor, displays potent antiviral activity but is limited by suboptimal drug-like properties, including selectivity and metabolic instability. Molecular modeling enabled the identification of a conserved binding site on the V-ATPase a-subunit consisting of three distinct sub-pockets. Docking analyses of ninety-five known diphyllin derivatives demonstrated that active analogs effectively occupy all three subpockets, informing a structure-based design approach. A library of novel diphyllin analogs with modifications to a single-ring system showed 50-fold increases in potency for antiviral activity against Ebola, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, and Chikungunya viruses and exhibiting improvements in metabolic stability and permeability.

articles.titulo: Are Viruses a Cause of Urinary Tract Infections? A Narrative Review
articles.autores: Gebremedhin KB, Amogne W, … Eguale T (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Urinary tract infections (UTIs), often associated with the lower urinary tract, are a major public health problem. Traditionally, urine has been believed to be sterile in healthy individuals, but increasing evidence shows that the urinary tract may contain a variety of viruses even in healthy populations. Bacteria remain the major etiologic agents of UTIs, but growing evidence points to viruses as emerging causes. This narrative review focuses on six viruses: adenoviruses, cytomegalovirus (CMV), BK virus (human polyomavirus), severe acute respiratory syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Zika virus, and West Nile virus. West Nile virus has been detected in urine without clear evidence of causing UTIs; however, the other five viruses reviewed in this narrative discuss have been associated with UTIs and may lead to various complications. Management of viral UTIs is mainly supportive, with reduced immunosuppression, symptom alleviation, prevention of complications, and monitoring of response to therapy. Key interventions include managing secondary bacterial infections, ensuring adequate hydration, using analgesics for pain and discomfort, and closely monitoring for treatment failure or recurrence. Effective prevention and control of viral infections also rely on broader public health strategies, including vaccination, sanitation, surveillance, early diagnosis, and appropriate treatment. Additional approaches may include prophylaxis, preemptive therapy, virus-specific treatments, and donor-recipient serostatus matching. Regular monitoring and careful adjustment of immunosuppressive therapy are also important, as no effective vaccine is available except for Ad4/Ad7 and SARS-CoV-2, and definitive preventive strategies are currently unavailable. Future research should focus on developing safe and effective antivirals and vaccines to prevent and treat viral UTIs and their complications.

articles.titulo: California West Nile Virus Forecasting Challenge 2024
articles.autores: Sánchez C HM, Danforth ME, … León TM (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: West Nile virus (WNV) is the primary cause of mosquito-borne disease in California and the continental United States. Between 2003 (its year of introduction to California) and 2024, over 8200 symptomatic human cases, including 5083 severe neuroinvasive cases and 406 deaths, have been reported. In California, 52 out of 58 counties have had a reported WNV case. Following the example set by prior national WNV forecasting challenges, the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) launched the 2024 forecasting challenge with the aim of predicting symptomatic cases each month during the typical WNV season for a select group of high-burden counties in California: Placer, Sacramento, Solano, San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Fresno, Tulare, Kern, San Bernardino, Los Angeles, Orange, and Riverside. County-month predictions were solicited as probability bins and evaluated by the logarithmic score. The 2024 WNV season in California had low activity, with 131 cases statewide (85 in challenge counties), compared with a ten-year median of 334 cases statewide (236 cases in challenge counties). Overall, the ensemble outperformed all individual models, and machine learning models were the best-performing model class. Forecasts performed better for counties with lower historical variance in case activity.

articles.titulo: Circular RNAs in metabolic reprogramming and therapy resistance in prostate cancer: emerging links to the tumor immune microenvironment
articles.autores: Zhou P, Zhang F, … Song G (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Therapy resistance in prostate cancer can emerge at different disease stages; castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is one clinically important state, and resistance to individual therapies may overlap but is not synonymous with CRPC. Metabolic reprogramming-including changes in glycolysis, de novo lipogenesis, glutamine metabolism, and mitochondrial homeostasis-has been implicated in prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance, although the strength of evidence varies across pathways and treatment settings. CircRNAs have been reported to modulate selected metabolic nodes in prostate cancer, although direct links between circRNA-associated metabolic changes and acquired therapy resistance are established only in a subset of studies. This review evaluates circRNAs as candidate regulators of selected metabolic processes in therapy-resistant prostate cancer. Mechanistically, individual circRNAs have been associated with selected metabolic changes through proposed miRNA-mediated interactions and, in some reports, peptide translation or protein scaffolding. These metabolic changes could, in principle, intersect with immunometabolic programmes such as lactate-associated suppression, lipid-linked macrophage states, and adenosine signalling; however, direct evidence that individual circRNAs control these immune-cell processes in CRPC remains limited, as detailed in the evidence tiers later in this review. Therapy-specific resistance networks are organised for enzalutamide/androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, PARP inhibitors and radiotherapy, distinguishing metabolism-dependent axes from signalling, mitotic, DNA-repair and exosome-propagated routes. Beyond mechanistic insights, circRNAs hold promise as non-invasive liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as druggable targets amenable to antisense oligonucleotide silencing, mimic delivery, and engineered circRNA vaccines. Major barriers to clinical translation include incomplete multi-therapy metabolic maps, sparse stage-resolved evidence across the hormone-sensitive→CRPC→neuroendocrine continuum, and unresolved delivery, safety, and regulatory challenges. Overall, current evidence supports circRNA-associated metabolic vulnerabilities as a promising preclinical research framework; however, circRNA-targeted metabolic interventions for therapy-resistant prostate cancer have not yet been clinically validated.

articles.titulo: Evaluating the Insecticidal Potential of Solanum lycocarpum and Curatella americana Leaf Extracts: Histopathological Effects on Culex quinquefasciatus Larvae
articles.autores: Caetano NDS, Meireles BA, … Cassel M (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study evaluated the larvicidal potential and histopathological impacts of ethanolic extracts from Solanum lycocarpum and Curatella americana against third-instar Culex quinquefasciatus larvae. Laboratory bioassays were conducted to assess mortality and behavioral effects. While no direct larval mortality occurred in this study, lethargy was observed three hours post exposure in treatments involving the highest concentrations (T7 and T8). After specimens were fixed in 70% ethanol, standard histological analysis revealed concentration-dependent changes across both plant extracts. Significant structural alterations were observed in the salivary glands, gastric caeca, Malpighian tubules, and the anterior, mid, and posterior intestines, with the most severe damage appearing to increase with higher extract concentrations. These disruptions affected tissues involved in feeding and development, potentially offering an indirect mechanism for vector control.

articles.titulo: Modulation of MOF Catalytic Activity to Exploit Cystine Dependency for Immunometabolic Therapy
articles.autores: Lv L, Xiang X, … Liu H (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tumor immunometabolism plays an important role in tumor progression and immune cell activity and is therefore critical to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy. Modulation of immunometabolism to boost cancer immunotherapy is mostly based on targeting tumor cell metabolism, which often fails to address the tumor-promoting functions maintained by stromal cells. In contrast, targeting a metabolic checkpoint shared by tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can potentially overcome this limitation but has been relatively underexplored. Herein, a locally delivered, ultrasound activatable nanocatalytic platform is reported for immunometabolic cancer therapy. The platform is composed of sulfasalazine and a gallium-modified Fe-TCPP metal-organic framework nanozyme codelivered in an oxidized sodium alginate-based hydrogel. Ultrasound-activated gallium-modified Fe-TCPP boosts electron transfer, peroxide activation, and reactive oxygen species production while disrupting iron balance. Simultaneously, sulfasalazine inhibits SLC7A11-mediated cystine uptake in CAFs and tumor cells, reducing matrix remodeling and weakening the tumor's antioxidant defense. This dual approach increases oxidative stress, reshapes the tumor microenvironment, induces immunogenic tumor cell death with ferroptotic traits, matures dendritic cells, and strengthens CD8+ T-cell responses. Consequently, it suppresses tumor growth in an immunocompetent osteosarcoma model and remains effective in a patient-derived OSCC xenograft model. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting shared SLC7A11-mediated cystine dependence integrates stromal remodeling, tumor redox disruption, and antitumor immune activation.

articles.titulo: MOSAIC: Integrating Computer-Vision-Assisted Counting and Multimodal Large Language Models for Species Identification in Mosquito Surveillance
articles.autores: Kuchavaram M, Huang Y, … Bandi ND (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Municipal mosquito control programs depend on timely counts and species identification, yet these tasks take staff time, require scarce expertise, and are often handled in separate tools. We developed MOSAIC (Mosquito Observations and Surveillance using AI for Communities), a web platform bringing trap collections, photographs, counts, laboratory results, and expert review into a single record and turning them into weekly trap priorities. We evaluated it with the vector control program of Corpus Christi, Texas, USA. Counting uses classical computer vision (OpenCV) without a trained model; for identification, we compared multimodal large language models (LLMs) with a laboratory-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) and tested LLMs given a local species list, taxonomic knowledge, and labeled examples. OpenCV counts were within two mosquitoes of the operators' blind counts for 69% of 175 collections. On citizen-science photographs, the zero-shot LLM was correct on 89% of the genera it named but named a genus for 83% (overall accuracy 74%, versus 77% for the CNN). Across three runs, added knowledge and examples raised mean forced-choice species accuracy from 17 to 20% to 63-70%, but when abstention was allowed, the models named a species for only 23-49% of specimens. Automated tools can assist surveillance while experts confirm the outputs.

articles.titulo: Characterization of the Gametocytocidal and Putative Transmission-Blocking Activity of Chlorotonil A Against Plasmodium falciparum
articles.autores: Schäfer TM, de Carvalho LP, … Held J (16 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background: Chlorotonil A, a keto-macrolide produced by the myxobacterium Sorangium cellulosum, has potent antibiotic and antimalarial activities. Notably, chlorotonil A is active against both asexual and sexual blood-stage malaria parasites, making it a promising candidate for the development of an antimalarial treatment that also reduces parasite transmission to mosquitoes. Objectives: Here, we characterize the gametocytocidal and transmission-reducing activity of chlorotonil A. Methods and results: Using direct membrane feeding assays with Plasmodium falciparum isolates from a malaria-endemic area in Gabon, we show that chlorotonil A reduces oocyst infection prevalence and intensity in Anopheles gambiae (Kisumu) mosquitoes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that chlorotonil A is a particularly fast-acting gametocytocidal compound in vitro. Fluorescence and transmission electron microscopy revealed that chlorotonil A impairs membrane integrity and induces intracellular vacuolization after 6 h of drug exposure, with accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and intracellular acidification after 24 h. Conclusions: Our findings show that chlorotonil A has the potential for development as a dual-active antimalarial.

articles.titulo: From low to high transmission: diversity-dependent responses of Plasmodium falciparum population structure to transmission intensity
articles.revista: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci
articles.autores: Suarez-Salazar D, Corredor-Espinel V, … Santos-Vega M (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Genetic surveillance is increasingly used to characterize malaria transmission, yet genetic patterns can respond nonlinearly to transmission intensity and depend on diversity already present in parasite populations. To isolate these effects from migration, selection, treatment and host immunity, we developed a neutral stochastic agent-based model of a closed human-mosquito transmission system integrating SEIS (susceptible-exposed-infectious-susceptible) epidemiological dynamics with neutral Plasmodium falciparum haplotypes and mosquito-stage recombination, without mutation or de novo allele generation. By independently varying human biting availability (amax) and initial genetic diversity (π0), we examined their joint effects on infection complexity, recombination and parasite population structure across a continuous transmission gradient. Infection prevalence and within-host infection complexity increased rapidly across low-to-intermediate transmission, whereas the effective recombination ratio and the number of recombinant haplotypes continued to increase across a broader range. Higher transmission was also associated with greater retention of human-stage parasite population genetic diversity (πH) and more even haplotype-frequency distributions, while initial genetic diversity constrained attainable genetic outcomes. Similar late-time population structures could be approached through different transient dynamics. Parasite population structure therefore reflects the interaction between transmission intensity and the genetic conditions on which transmission and recombination act, providing mechanistic expectations for interpreting malaria genetic surveillance patterns across heterogeneous transmission settings. This article is part of the theme issue 'Ecological and evolutionary interactions between parasites across scales'.

articles.titulo: Investigating Lethality of Mayaro Virus, O'nyong-nyong Virus, Ross River Virus, and Una Virus in an Immunodeficient Murine Model
articles.autores: Gardner CL, Pieterse L, … Burke CW (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Arthritogenic alphaviruses are mosquito-borne viruses characteristically associated with severe rheumatic disease and febrile illness. While this group of arboviruses house significant epidemic potential due to expanding competent vectors, host plasticity, and recombination events increasing infectivity, the median lethal dose (LD50) for many members remains limited or non-existent, thus restraining medical countermeasure (MCM) investigations. Mayaro virus (MAYV), o'nyong-nyong virus (ONNV), Una virus (UNAV), and Ross River virus (RRV) are four arthritogenic alphaviruses with epidemic potential. However, at the time of our study, no literature examining LD50 values for each virus in IFNAR-deficient mice, an effective model for characterizing disease severity and thus MCM potential, was available. In this study, we subcutaneously inoculated IFNAR-deficient mice with ranged doses of MAYV, ONNV, UNAV, or RRV to determine the LD50. However, we were unsuccessful upon finding complete lethality across all ranged doses for each virus. We further validated MCM potential in our MAYV model by prophylactically treating mice with neutralizing antibody (nAb) and examining clinical scores, weight loss, and survival rates. Our study serves as the first to examine the lethality of UNAV, MAYV, and RRV infection in an IFNAR-deficient mouse model and provides crucial lethal dose reference material for future MAYV, ONNV, UNAV, and RRV studies.

articles.titulo: Antiviral Strategies Against Dengue Virus: Viral Targets, Host Pathways, and Chinese Herbal Medicines
articles.autores: Liang Q, Liu K, … Shan C (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue is caused by four antigenically distinct dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and remains a major global public health threat. It is endemic in more than 100 countries and territories, primarily in tropical and subtropical regions. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 390 million DENV infections occur annually, with nearly half of the world's population at risk of infection. Complex virus-host interactions and disease mechanisms continue to complicate antiviral development. No dengue-specific antiviral therapy has been approved. This review summarizes recent advances in anti-DENV therapeutics, including inhibitors targeting viral proteins, host factors, and virus-host interactions. In addition, it highlights the antiviral potential of Chinese herbal medicines and their bioactive compounds, and discusses priorities for their further development.

articles.titulo: Long-Term Nitrogen and Phosphorus Control and Microbial Responses by Tea-Bag-Encapsulated MgO-Modified Biochar at the Sediment-Water Interface
articles.autores: Ding Y, Chai B, … He L (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Internal phosphorus release from sediments is an important limiting factor in the remediation of eutrophic water bodies. Tea-bag-encapsulated MgO-modified biochar has advantages in phosphorus adsorption, microbial attachment, and convenient recovery, but its long-term phosphorus control effect and associated microbial responses at the sediment-water interface remain unclear. In this study, a 124-day sediment-water simulation experiment combined with metagenomic sequencing was conducted to evaluate its effects on nitrogen and phosphorus removal, water environmental changes, and microbial phosphorus-cycling functions. The results showed that the removal efficiencies of phosphate, total phosphorus, ammonia nitrogen, and total nitrogen in the treatment group reached 88%, 67%, 90%, and 40%, respectively. After application, the BET specific surface area of the material decreased from 47.85 to 20.18 m2/g, obvious surface deposits appeared, and phosphorus enrichment was detected, indicating that the material continuously participated in interfacial phosphorus fixation. Meanwhile, the relative abundances of Anaerolinea and Nitrospira increased from 5.71% to 10.08% and from 0.72% to 1.06%, respectively. Functional gene analysis showed that the relative abundances of genes related to phosphorus sensing, transport, and polyphosphate metabolism changed, suggesting that the functional potential related to phosphorus acquisition and storage was adjusted. Since this study was based on a small-scale long-term simulation system, the contribution of the material was mainly interpreted through the stage-specific differences between BC and BT, material characterization, and microbial functional responses, while the independent effects of time-varying factors such as temperature and redox conditions still require further controlled experiments. Overall, the sustained phosphorus control effect of tea-bag-encapsulated MgO-modified biochar was mainly associated with interfacial material fixation, microbial community changes, and adjustments in phosphorus cycling functional potential.

articles.titulo: MAALEM-Btmosquito: A Novel Floating Granular Bti Formulation for Aedes aegypti Control in Domestic Water-Storage Containers
articles.autores: Villegas A, Sanchez J, … Soberón M (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Integrated management of Aedes aegypti, the primary urban vector of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, requires effective, environmentally safe larvicides with sufficient residual activity for operational use. We developed and evaluated MAALEM-Btmosquito, a novel floating granular formulation based on Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis (Bti), designed to maintain larvicidal activity under routine water use and partial water replacement in domestic water containers. Outdoor semi-field bioassays were conducted in 20 L buckets and 200 L drums under three water-replacement regimes (0%, 10%, and 50%). Groups of 25 late third- and early fourth-instar Ae. aegypti larvae were exposed at successive post-treatment intervals, and mortality was assessed at 24 and 48 h over 30 days. MAALEM-Btmosquito caused 100% mortality at 24 h on the first day and maintained >94.5% larval mortality throughout the study. Overall mean 24 h mortality across treatments was 98.8%, with treatment means ranging from 94.7% (95% CI, 91.9-96.5) to 99.7% (95% CI, 98.5-99.9). The greatest reduction in activity was observed in 20 L containers subjected to 50% water replacement. Operational performance was evaluated during three application cycles involving more than 700 households in Puente de Ixtla, Morelos, Mexico. The Breteau Index decreased by 72.6%, 64.6%, and 81.1%, while the mean egg count per ovitrap decreased from 93.2 ± 76.10 before the first MAALEM-Btmosquito application to 25.4 ± 20.44 eggs after completion of the field interventions. Because the community evaluation was conducted without a concurrent untreated control area, these field observations are associative and cannot be attributed solely to MAALEM-Btmosquito. Potential confounding factors include seasonality, rainfall, other vector-control activities, and household water-use behavior. Together with the controlled semi-field results, these findings support the potential of MAALEM-Btmosquito as a larvicide for integrated mosquito vector management.

articles.titulo: Serum itaconate levels and treatment-related changes in polymyalgia rheumatica: a prospective observational study
articles.autores: Li Z, Wu Y, … Wu M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Itaconate (ITA) is an immunometabolic regulator, but its circulating levels and treatment-associated changes in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) remain unclear. This study investigated serum ITA levels across treatment states and their longitudinal associations with inflammatory markers and glucocorticoid (GC) exposure.
This prospective observational study included 161 serum samples from 108 participants, comprising 20 healthy control (HC), 30 treatment-naïve (TN), and 111 treatment-exposed (TE) samples. Serum ITA was quantified by LC-MS/MS. Between-group differences were assessed using age- and sex-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Paired changes were evaluated in 11 patients, and longitudinal associations were examined across 42 TE-to-TE intervals from 27 patients using regression models with patient-clustered robust standard errors.
Adjusted geometric mean ITA concentrations were 4.170 ng/mL (95% CI, 3.132-5.553) in HC, 0.907 ng/mL (0.719-1.143) in TN, and 3.885 ng/mL (3.427-4.405) in TE. ITA levels were significantly lower in TN than in HC and TE (both P<0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed between TE and HC (P = 0.656). Among 11 paired patients, ITA increased in 10 at the first post-treatment follow-up, with median concentrations rising from 1.408 to 5.394 ng/mL (P = 0.0049). Across all 42 treated intervals, changes in ITA were not significantly associated with changes in ESR (P = 0.622). However, among 21 intervals involving abnormal ESR, an inverse association was observed after adjustment for concurrent GC dose changes (β=-0.601, 95% CI, -1.000 to -0.201; P = 0.006; Holm-adjusted P = 0.018).
Serum ITA was markedly reduced in TN PMR and increased following treatment initiation. Its exploratory inverse association with ESR changes in intervals involving abnormal ESR suggests treatment-associated immunometabolic variation that warrants further investigation.

articles.titulo: Lachnospiraceae and the Host Immune System: Mechanisms, Disease Associations and Precision-Oriented Intervention
articles.autores: Mao D, Yang Q, … Ji H (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The family Lachnospiraceae is among the most abundant obligately anaerobic taxa in the healthy human gut. Its core function-fermentation of dietary fibre to produce short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), chiefly butyrate-makes it a key node linking diet, the microbiota and host immunity. Altered Lachnospiraceae abundance is associated with inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer and autoimmune conditions, but the underlying molecular layers, causal structure and intra-family heterogeneity have yet to be integrated. This review addresses a single question: how do Lachnospiraceae shape and constrain host immunity? It first summarises the family's taxonomy, metabolism and ecology, and then examines the relevant mechanisms along four partly overlapping axes of immune crosstalk: the mucosal barrier and epithelial innate immunity, metabolite-mediated immune signalling, immune sensing of bacterial structural components and the shaping of adaptive immunity, together with a fifth, prospective and still exploratory layer of immune tolerance and trained immunity, which is presented as an open question rather than as an established mechanism. Four features distinguish this review from earlier overviews of the family: an explicit evidence hierarchy applied claim by claim; strict separation of findings obtained for Lachnospiraceae from those obtained for related taxa; explicit grading of intervention studies according to whether the family was manipulated, depleted or merely measured; and restriction of the trained-immunity layer to an open question. Associations with immune-related diseases are then assessed by disease category, followed by culturomics, genetic tools, live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) and polysaccharide-based, precision-oriented interventions. The central conclusion is that the immunological effects of Lachnospiraceae are strongly strain-specific and disease-context-dependent; family-level associations therefore cannot be extrapolated directly to strain-level causal effects.

articles.titulo: Immune-Mediated Endothelial Injury in Cardiometabolic-Cardiovascular Disease
articles.autores: Wang Q, Liu L, … Li Y (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cardiometabolic disease, encompassing hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and dyslipidemia, is the predominant driver of cardiovascular disease (CVD) morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the vascular endothelium sits at the transition from metabolic derangement to overt cardiovascular events, serving as both sensor and transducer of metabolic injury. This review synthesizes evidence that aberrant immune responses act as contributory drivers of endothelial injury in cardiometabolic disease. These responses span innate pattern-recognition receptor activation, neutrophil-mediated cytotoxicity, monocyte/macrophage polarization imbalance, adaptive T- and B-cell dysregulation, and trained immunity. The inflammation they represent is therapeutically actionable at the level of cardiovascular events. Whether endothelial protection mediates that benefit has not been directly tested, and reverse causation and parallel metabolic-inflammatory loops are not excluded. We trace how the canonical innate sensing cascades (Toll-like receptor 4-nuclear factor κB, the NLRP3 inflammasome, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes) converge on endothelial activation. We then examine how oxidative stress at the immune-metabolic interface, including NADPH oxidase-derived reactive oxygen species, endothelial nitric oxide synthase uncoupling, mitochondrial damage-associated molecular pattern release, and oxidized phospholipid accumulation, amplifies this convergence. Finally, we describe how junctional disassembly, glycocalyx degradation, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition execute barrier disruption. We then assess mechanism-linked circulating biomarkers and multi-marker integration strategies, anchoring the framework in clinical trials that have established anti-inflammatory therapy in selected patient populations while the mechanistic steps linking these interventions to endothelial protection remain incompletely tested. We close by consolidating this evidence into a graded inventory that separates candidate circulating readouts from intervention and real-world evidence, and by marking where the mechanistic chain from pathway to readout to therapy remains unclosed. Whether these pathways can be translated into mechanism-informed risk stratification awaits prospective evidence and standardized measurement.

articles.titulo: Dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia: a scoping review of program design, uptake, and safety surveillance
articles.autores: Enriquez MGL, Villanueva-Uy LM, … Acuin MES (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue vaccine programs in Southeast Asia differ in target groups, delivery, financing, eligibility, and safety monitoring, and the evidence is scattered across peer-reviewed and grey literature.
To map evidence on dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia, focusing on program design, uptake, and safety surveillance, and to identify practical insights for future vaccination policies, implementation frameworks, and clinical guidelines in the region.
Scoping review.
Southeast Asia. Population Populations eligible for or receiving dengue vaccination.
The review followed JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, Google Scholar, WPRIM, WHO IRIS, Google, and government and regulatory websites, and checked reference lists, for sources published from 2015 to 2026 on program design, uptake, or safety surveillance. Two reviewers screened records independently. Evidence was mapped by country and concept and synthesized narratively.
Database searches were last updated on September 8, 2026, and grey-literature and supplementary searches on November 1, 2026. Of 366 database records and 220 grey-literature links, 33 sources were included; a supplementary search added 12 (total 45). Evidence was found for six countries and none for Brunei, Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, or Timor-Leste. The Philippines ran a large, publicly funded, school-based CYD-TDV program; Indonesia combined private access with a provincial TAK-003 pilot; Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam relied mainly on private delivery. Safety surveillance was best documented in the Philippines, Malaysia, and Singapore. Uptake data were sparse: fewer than half of the >830,000 Filipino children given CYD-TDV completed three doses before the program was suspended, and the Indonesian pilot reported about 90% coverage. No uptake data were found for private-sector delivery. Nine sources were modeling or economic studies, which inform planning but do not document implementation.
Dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia varies in delivery, financing, and safety monitoring, and is unevenly documented, especially for uptake. Standardized monitoring and reporting of real-world vaccination programs are needed.
