articles.titulo: Pathogen surveillance by agnostic high-throughput sequencing in sand flies collected in the country of Georgia
articles.autores: Paskey AC, Thomas QK, … Bishop-Lilly KA (19 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Sand flies are known vectors of human pathogens that cause acute febrile illness (AFI). Understanding the pathogen landscape within these insects is crucial for biosurveillance and prevention of infectious diseases in U.S forces deployed to regions where sand flies are present.
We used agnostic high-throughput sequencing to perform genomic surveillance for the presence of known human pathogens associated with AFI and novel relatives thereof in sand flies (Psychodidae: Phlebotominae) collected in the country of Georgia between August 2017 and August 2023. A total of 102 sand fly pools, containing 1-37 specimens each and in some cases sorted by sex, were homogenized. Of those, 86 produced Illumina RNA libraries suitable for sequencing. The resulting data were queried in an entirely pathogen agnostic manner: sequencing reads were processed through two bioinformatic pipelines, VirusSeeker 2.0 and MetaDetector, to perform quality control steps, de novo assembly, and a DIAMOND analysis on reads and assembled contigs. Manual analysis was performed to identify expected pathogens and any other pathogens of notable abundance. Results with similarity to pathogens of human or veterinary importance, as well as low confidence results represented by a low number of reads were also subjected to in-depth analysis.
This pathogen-agnostic assessment revealed both expected and unexpected results. We detected novel viruses consistent with insect vector viromes, including novel orthomyxoviruses that could merit further exploration and some vesiculovirus sequences that may represent endogenous viral elements. Although Leishmania was an expected finding, it was not detected with high confidence. A significant unexpected result was the detection of Rickettsia felis, a pathogen typically vectored by fleas and occasionally mosquitoes, in two separate pools, with 51% of the genome covered in one pool. Furthermore, we identified two distinct and complete novel phlebovirus genomes. Their genome divergence from previously known phleboviruses is so significant that they are not predicted to be amplified using any of the five published phlebovirus assays.
These results are achieved through a combination of agnostic sequencing and detailed bioinformatic analyses, enabling the detection of novel viruses and an expansion of our understanding of vector-borne disease ecology.

articles.titulo: Redox-regulated immunomodulatory mechanisms of mycophenolate mofetil in a lupus-like disease
articles.autores: Zhong J, Zhu W, … Liu B (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Lupus-like autoimmune disease remains a severe, hard-to-manage complication after allogeneic immune cell transfer, with limited targeted therapies. While mycophenolate mofetil shows observable clinical benefit, its immunometabolic mechanisms in tissue-resident macrophages remain poorly defined. In this established murine lupus-like disease model, recipient mice received splenocytes from lupus-prone donors, with parallel comparisons between reactive oxygen species (ROS)-deficient, ROS-normal and conditional APOBEC3 knockout groups. We applied standardized in vivo mycophenolate mofetil dosing and ex vivo mycophenolic acid treatment, alongside high-resolution magnetic particle profiling, flow cytometry, ELISA, histology and RNA sequencing for systematic assessment. Mycophenolate mofetil significantly induced macrophage functional reprogramming, suppressed antigen-specific immune activation, lowered interferon-γ and IgG2b autoantibody levels, and alleviated pulmonary fibrosis, while APOBEC3-mediated cytosine deamination in macrophages was regulated by ROS signaling. These findings indicate that mycophenolate mofetil ameliorates lupus-like autoimmunity via ROS-dependent and independent DNA regulatory pathways, providing a new mechanistic basis for improving inflammation-directed immunomodulatory strategies.

articles.titulo: Multistate Dengue Fever Outbreak in Sudan Amid Ongoing Conflict: A Descriptive Epidemiological Analysis
articles.autores: Azhary A, Hajhamed NM, … Siddig EE (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
This study is a descriptive epidemiological analysis of a multistate dengue fever outbreak in Sudan during a period of intense armed conflict and mass displacement.
This study is an analysis of national surveillance data conducted using reports collected between August 2024 and July 2025. Variables, including case counts, fatalities, and internally displaced persons (IDPs) per state, were calculated and analyzed with R software 4.2.2 (Version 2025.05.1 + 513).
A total of 13,371 cases and 21 fatalities were reported across 10 states. Notably, Khartoum State, a conflict-affected region, recorded the highest number of cases (n = 8040), while Kassala reported the highest number of deaths (n = 9). Kassala State documented the highest number of dengue cases among IDPs (472), followed by Khartoum (69).
The findings highlight the need for strengthened dengue surveillance and vector control in conflict-affected settings, where disruption of health services may complicate outbreak prevention and response.
Not applicable.

articles.titulo: Formulation of Glycerol-Based Emulsion Containing Myrica gale L. Essential Oil for Enhanced Repellent Activity
articles.autores: Whyms SE, Kroll G, … Walsh JJ (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: Glycerol-based emulsions containing Myrica gale L. essential oils (EOs) were developed and evaluated for stability, volatilisation behaviour and in vivo mosquito repellent activity. Preliminary GC-MS characterisation of the oils demonstrated complex chemical profiles comprised mainly of a mixture of mono- and sesquiterpenes. Methods: Emulsions containing 10% oil were prepared at two surfactant concentrations (2.5 and 5%) and differing ratios of glycerol to water as the non-polar phase. The optimal system was determined to be 10% oil and 2.5% surfactant (i.e., cetearyl alcohol and cetearyl glucoside) in 100% glycerol as assessed over a 91-day storage period by changes in particle size, polydispersity and zeta potential. This formulation approach was subsequently applied to three proven insect repellent M. gale EOs. Volatilisation behaviour was investigated using headspace GC-MS analysis of selected marker compounds (α-pinene, camphene, β-pinene, myrcene, α-phellandrene, 3-carene, p-cymene, γ-terpinene). Results: M. gale-based emulsions demonstrated significantly improved volatilisation over time, compared with the EO coarsely dispersed in a lotion base. This enhanced partitioning behaviour correlated well with increased protection times observed in an arm-in-cage repellent assay against Aedes aegypti mosquitos. It was found that all formulated M.gale EOs, F_EO15M (CPT = 40.05 min, p = 0.032), F_EO21C (CPT = 42.023 min, p = 0.01) and F_EO15C (CPT = 99.478 min, p < 0.0001), performed significantly better than their non-formulated counterparts EO15M (CPT = 11.45 min), EO21C (CPT = 13.053 min) and EO15C (CPT = 33.02 min). Conclusion: This study describes for the first time an effective, topical M. gale-loaded emulsion for the improvement of insect repellent activity.

articles.titulo: Unveiling skin mycobiome-immune dynamics: The role of fungi in trained immunity and immune reprogramming during skin diseases
articles.autores: Riera-Leal L, Riera-Leal A, … Ortiz-García YM (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Human skin and mucosal surfaces harbor complex fungal communities, collectively termed the mycobiome, that can influence local and systemic immune homeostasis despite their relatively low abundance. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the composition and dynamics of cutaneous and mucosa-associated mycobiota at oral, nasal, and vaginal sites across the lifespan, highlighting Malassezia and Candida as dominant genera in specific niches. Age, anatomical site, hormonal status, barrier integrity, and environmental exposures shape these communities and their interactions with co-resident bacteria, archaea, and viruses. Particular emphasis is placed on fungal recognition and the mechanisms underlying trained innate immunity, while distinguishing experimental evidence from the incompletely defined effects of physiological colonization. Fungal components are recognized by receptors including Dectin-1, Dectin-2, Mincle, Langerin, Toll-like receptors, and NK cell receptors, activating pathways that coordinate antifungal defense. Experimental exposure to fungi or β-glucans can induce metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in innate immune cells, involving PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling, increased aerobic glycolysis, and altered chromatin states that support enhanced responses to subsequent challenges. Related antifungal pathways regulate cytokine production, Th17 responses, and inflammasome activation, with outcomes ranging from protective immunity to chronic inflammation and tissue damage, depending on the host and tissue context. Finally, we discuss fungal virulence strategies, interkingdom interactions, and their reported associations with inflammatory, infectious, and neoplastic diseases.

articles.titulo: A Preliminary Virome Survey of Arctic and Sub-Arctic Tundra Mosquitoes (Aedes, Subgenus Ochlerotatus): Viral Diversity and Phylogenetic Affinities in Three Pooled Regional Samples
articles.autores: Lee SY, Lee YM, … Chae N (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rapid Arctic warming may increase mosquito abundance and alter host interactions, yet tundra mosquito-associated viral communities remain poorly characterized. We report viral sequences from pooled mosquitoes of three Arctic and sub-Arctic regions: Alaska (Aedes punctor group, n = 4), Canada (Ae. nigripes, n = 4), and Greenland (Ae. nigripes, n = 10). For each site, pooled specimens were sequenced from total nucleic acids and viral families were assigned only from amino-acid-level hits. Fourteen families were detected (7, 7, and 4 per pool), dominated by Iflaviridae, Narnaviridae, and Orthototiviridae (approximately 99%, 71%, and 93% of virus-assigned reads, respectively). Baculoviridae and Orthototiviridae were shared across all pools, though baculovirus may reflect environmental or dietary exposure rather than active infection. Maximum-likelihood phylogenies placed the recovered sequences within mosquito-associated lineages related to Fennoscandian relatives: a near-complete Alaskan iflavirus sequence (9850 bp) clustered with Finnish Pedersore iflaviruses, while Canadian and Greenlandic totiviruses and a narna-like virus were related to but divergent from Fennoscandian references. A Canadian chu-like virus-like sequence was the most divergent (27.9% amino-acid identity). These results link tundra mosquito-associated viral sequences to Fennoscandian lineages, some closely related but others substantially divergent. Despite single pooled libraries per region, this study offers an initial baseline for Arctic tundra mosquito viromes and underscores the need for future individually sequenced surveys under standardized protocols.

articles.titulo: Forest Pest Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv11 with Intraspecific Classification Strategy
articles.autores: Liang X, Xiang J, … Zou D (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Forest pest detection has challenges such as the high similarity in appearance among different species, which leads to feature confusion. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv11 forest pest detection model with a fine-grained intraspecific classification strategy. The bottleneck of identification caused by the diversity of internal morphologies is effectively alleviated via constructing a dataset with adults, larvae, and nymphs, i.e., using intraspecific classification strategy. This model incorporates a CBA (Convolution-BatchNorm-AReLU) module, Scale-based Dynamic (SD) loss, and an Adaptively Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) module. The CBA module integrates an attention mechanism to dynamically adjust the gradient, which alleviates vanishing gradients and accelerates the convergence of model parameters. SD loss adaptively balances localization and scale loss based on a target scale, which reduces IoU fluctuations and enhances cross-scale robustness. Resolution conflicts and optimizing semantic alignment are alleviated by introducing the ASFF module to achieve learnable spatial multi-scale feature fusion. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv11 model outperforms existing methods, with Precision, Recall, AP50-90, and F1 score reaching 97.19%, 97.20%, 88.25%, and 97.17%, respectively. In practical applications, the proposed model can accurately capture subtle differences in the microscopic features of the same pest during different life cycles. This research project can accurately identify the types and occurrence stages of pests, match targeted control measures, avoid the use of excessive pesticides, and significantly reduce the cost of control and environmental pollution.

articles.titulo: Amino acid metabolic checkpoints in microglia: emerging regulators of Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis
articles.autores: Xu F, Li H, … Zhang M (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Microglial immunometabolic reprogramming is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but amino acid metabolism has received less integrated attention than glucose and lipid metabolism. This Mini Review examines tryptophan-kynurenine, arginine, and glutamine pathways because they connect amino acid flux or amino acid-derived metabolites with microglial redox control, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial function, and amyloid handling. We use the term amino acid metabolic checkpoints narrowly for a molecular regulatory node that has a demonstrable link to amino acid availability, transport, metabolic flux, or an amino acid-derived ligand and whose perturbation changes a defined microglial function. Broad domains such as mitochondrial fitness and phagolysosomal competence are treated as functional outputs rather than checkpoints. The glutamine-NLRP3 literature illustrates why directionality and experimental context are essential: glutaminase inhibition can promote mitophagy and suppress NLRP3 activation, whereas NLRP3 loss or chronic pharmacological inhibition increases glutamine/glutamate-related metabolism, mitochondrial activity, and Aβ clearance. These findings support bidirectional coupling rather than a simple model in which glutaminolysis is uniformly pathogenic. Evidence for tryptophan- and arginine-related nodes is biologically compelling but more heterogeneous in cell type and disease context. A checkpoint framework that explicitly grades direct versus indirect evidence may therefore help prioritize cell- and stage-specific immunometabolic intervention in AD.

articles.titulo: Anatomical transformation through the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition in megalopteran insects
articles.autores: Zhao C, Huang M, … Liu X (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The adaptation of aquatic insects to freshwater habitats is a key question for understanding insect evolution. Many aquatic insects undergo significant morphological and physiological changes during the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition. However, changes of internal anatomical structures and organs with the process of transformation have yet to be comprehensively investigated.
Here we document the anatomical transformations of the skeletal-muscular system, nervous system, digestive system, and tracheal system during the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition in an aquatic insect species Protohermes xanthodes Navás, 1914 (Megaloptera: Corydalidae), using micro-CT and 3D reconstruction. Notably, unlike the rapid, concentrated breakdown of other organ systems, the tracheal system undergoes a prolonged, stepwise, and tightly orchestrated disintegration-reconstruction process during the major developmental stages. The digestive system is markedly modified but without complete disintegration across these stages. For predation and sensation under water, the larvae possess powerful mandibles and prothoracic muscles, and short but well-developed antennal nerves. In addition, the well-developed mesothoracic, metathoracic, and abdominal muscles at the filament base of the larvae enable underwater swimming.
This study provides new insights into the dynamic adaptations during the aquatic-terrestrial transition in Corydalidae (Megaloptera) and sheds light on coordinated evolution across multiple functional systems in response to environmental pressures.

articles.titulo: Efficacy and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated plasmodium falciparum malaria in South Sudan: a multi-site therapeutic efficacy study, 2024-2025
articles.autores: Ayuen DS, Dau AD, … Malual MD (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
South Sudan has one of the highest malaria burdens per capita in Africa, and artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ) and artemether-lumefantrine (AL) are first- and second-line treatments for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria. However, despite the emergence of Artemisinin partial resistance (ART-R) and AL failure at some sites in the region, no therapeutic efficacy study (TES) has been conducted since the introduction of ASAQ and AL two decades ago. Our TES aimed to assess the efficacy of ASAQ and AL across four sites in South Sudan.
This study was conducted in Juba, Bor, Wau, and Yambio. Children aged 6 months to 59 months with microscopically confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum monoinfection were assigned to ASAQ or AL and followed for 28 days to assess treatment response. The primary endpoint was the Kaplan-Meier PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on Day 28. Day 3 parasite positivity was used as a measure of early treatment response.
We enrolled 390 children across all arms; 10.3% overall were lost to follow-up, ranging from 0% in Bor to 24.1% in Juba-ASAQ, and 350 (89.7%) were included in the per-protocol analysis. Kaplan-Meier uncorrected ACPR was: 96.2% (95% CI: 89.2-99.2) in Juba-AL, 95.6% (95% CI: 87.6-99.1) in Juba-ASAQ, 97.7% (95% CI: 92.6-99.7) in Bor (ASAQ) and 93.3% (95% CI: 86.1-97.5) in Yambio (AL). Kaplan-Meier PCR-corrected ACPR exceeded 90% in all sites except Wau: 98.7% (95% CI: 92.9-100.0) in Juba-AL, 100.0% (95% CI: 94.5-100.0) in Juba-ASAQ, 100.0% (95% CI: 95.8-100.0) in Bor (ASAQ) and 98.8% (95% CI: 93.5-100.0) in Yambio (AL). In Wau, only 34 participants were evaluable at Day 28, and no treatment failures were observed. Day 3 parasite positivity was elevated at Bor (13.8%), exceeding the WHO 10% threshold used as an indicator of suspected ART-R. No adverse events were reported.
ASAQ and AL remain highly efficacious against uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in South Sudan, supporting the continuation of the current treatment policy. The high Day 3 positivity rate at Bor warrants enhanced molecular surveillance and repeat efficacy monitoring. This study establishes a baseline for national TES surveillance.
consultas: plasmodium OR arbovirus OR dengue OR zika

articles.titulo: The Genome Exposome Microbiome-Phenome (GEM-P): a conceptual framework for social bees
articles.autores: Cutajar S, Alberoni D, … Mifsud D (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The gut microbiome of social bees is a small, specific set of symbionts that contributes to nutrition, detoxification, immune function and behaviour, with effects on colony performance and resilience. In recent years, the field has expanded, but studies still analyse host genetics and environmental exposures separately and often rely on correlations between microbes and health traits. This makes it difficult to distinguish between instances in which microbiome differences primarily reflect host or environmental factors and instances in which they may contribute mechanistically to bee health. A key challenge is context dependence: similar microbiome shifts may be associated with different trait outcomes depending on life stage and task, exposure history, and colony transmission structure. We present the Genome Exposome Microbiome-Phenome (GEM-P) framework as an integrative organisational framework for social bees. GEM-P treats genome, lifetime exposures (exposome), and the gut microbiome as interacting components shaping phenotypes at both individual and colony scales. Phenotypes can, in turn, modify subsequent exposures and microbiome states. We use GEM-P to map evidence on genetic filtering, exposomal drivers, microbiome assembly and function, and phenotypic outcomes, and to highlight study designs that help distinguish among alternative biological pathways without requiring comprehensive multi-omics approaches. GEM-P provides a practical way to generate pathway-specific hypotheses and interpret microbiome-phenotype associations across contexts. KEY POINTS: • An integrative framework linking genome, exposome, gut microbiome, and phenome in social bees. • Highlights scale, timing, and social transmission as sources of context dependence. • Supports pathway-specific hypotheses and sampling designs that help distinguish alternative explanations for microbiome-phenotype associations.

articles.titulo: MiR-277 Drives Sexually Dimorphic Development in Ericerus pela Through Differential Regulation of Dlg1 and Lar
articles.autores: Chen X, Ling X, … Chen H (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Insects exhibit diverse developmental strategies, yet the molecular basis of sexual dimorphism in metamorphosis remains largely elusive. The white wax scale insect Ericerus pela (hereafter, WWS) displays extreme sexual dimorphism: females undergo paurometamorphosis (four stages), while males undergo hyperpaurometamorphosis (five stages). Although miR-277 is highly expressed in both sexes, its functional role in this process was unknown. Here, we demonstrate that miR-277 drives sexually dimorphic development through differential regulation of two distinct targets. Combining gain- and loss-of-function assays, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and RNA interference, we show that miR-277 suppresses Discs large 1 (Dlg1) in females, disrupting cellular signaling and causing growth retardation and morphological abnormalities. In males, miR-277 inhibits tyrosine-protein phosphatase Lar (Lar), a receptor tyrosine phosphatase linked to nervous system development; knockdown of Lar severely impairs male metamorphosis but does not affect females. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized, sex-specific miRNA regulatory switch: miR-277 concurrently modulates a cell-growth pathway in females and a neurodevelopmental pathway in males, thereby generating divergent developmental outcomes. Our study provides the mechanistic insight into miRNA-mediated sexual dimorphism in insects and advances the understanding of how post-transcriptional regulators shape metamorphic diversity.

articles.titulo: Broad-Scale Landscape Structure Shapes Anopheline Assemblages in an Amazonian Deforestation Frontier
articles.autores: Santos TC, Ilacqua RC, … Laporta GZ (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Previous work in this Amazonian deforestation frontier identified a broad-scale landscape signal for malaria-vector abundance and infected-anopheline occurrence, generating the hypothesis that the anopheline assemblage itself may be organized by landscape structure. Here, we tested whether anopheline richness, total abundance, Nyssorhynchus darlingi abundance and multispecies assemblage structure are associated with landscape composition, configuration and spatial extent. We analyzed 365 anophelines from 22 landscapes and eight species using Bayesian count and hierarchical multispecies models. Predictors represented forest cover, secondary forest, water, exposed soil, forest configuration and river proximity across 3, 5 and 7 km2. The 7 km2 scale received the strongest support across responses. Forest cover consistently increased richness and community abundance, exposed soil reduced abundance-based responses, and forest edge density contributed to the best multispecies model. These findings indicate that broad-scale landscape structure organizes anopheline assemblages that may underlie malaria transmission in Amazonian frontier regions.

articles.titulo: Aedes aegypti breeding patterns and arboviral risks influenced by complex social-climate dynamics in the semi-arid areas of Bouaké, central Côte d'Ivoire (West Africa)
articles.autores: Dibo JDK, Touré M, … Zahouli JZB (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue (DEN) is rapidly expanding across yellow fever (YF)-endemic settings in Côte d'Ivoire (West Africa). However, data on how climate and social conditions influence local Aedes vector populations and disease transmission are still lacking, particularly in climatic transition zones. Thus, we assessed the driving effects of seasonality and social behaviours on Aedes aegypti occurrence and DEN and YF epidemic risks across variously urbanised landscapes in the semi-arid climate areas of Bouaké, central Côte d'Ivoire.
From September 2023 to August 2024, we sampled Aedes larvae and pupae in aquatic habitats among 3,600 households in urban, peri-urban and rural areas during rainy and dry seasons. We conducted a community-based survey to assess knowledge and practices related to potable water and solid waste management, mosquito breeding prevention and vector-borne disease risk in the households. Larval and pupal indices were compared between the study areas over behavioural and seasonal variations.
Ae. aegypti widely predominated across all study areas, with proportions > 99% (n = 64488). Larval breeding in aquatic habitats and related arboviral risks were driven by the local community behaviours and seasonality in all areas, and showed higher magnitude in the urban. DEN and YF epidemic risk indices exceeded the standard World Health Organisation (WHO) thresholds in all areas, with density figures of 6-9 in the urban and 4-8 in the peri-urban and rural areas. Out of 23,074 wet containers inspected, tires were the most productive pupal breeding grounds in the urban areas, while medium containers were the largest providers of pupae in the peri-urban and rural areas. Larval occurrences among household containers were associated with water storage practices and seasonal variations. Outdoor and discarded containers were more infested with Aedes larvae during rainy seasons. Domestic water-holding containers abundantly harboured larvae during dry seasons associated with longer water storage duration and frequent supply interruptions and drought. Unexpectedly, local community education and awareness of mosquito risks and DEN and YF causes were not translated into behavioural change for protective effect. Rainfall-behaviour cycles supported the strong presence of Ae. aegypti and high epidemic risks of DEN and YF year-round in all areas, with more pronounced effects in the urban areas.
In the semi-arid areas of Bouaké, the patterns of Ae. aegypti larval breeding among household water-holding containers are locally influenced by the complex and dynamic interactions between community behaviours and climate. Compensatory effects of rainfall-water storing dynamics sustain Ae. aegypti density figures and DEN and YF epidemic risks above the WHO-established thresholds over a year, mainly in the urban areas. Thus, community-driven awareness and vector control actions are required to attenuate climate impacts on arboviral epidemic risks in the semi-arid areas of Côte d'Ivoire and other West African countries.

articles.titulo: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Japanese Encephalitis Virus Infection in Mammals
articles.autores: Zhang S, Luo H, … Liang G (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus and the leading cause of viral encephalitis in many regions of Asia. Owing to its pronounced neurotropism, JEV infection can result in severe neurological disease with high mortality, while 30-50% of survivors develop permanent neurological sequelae. Although substantial progress has been made over the past few decades, the molecular mechanisms underlying JEV infection, neuroinvasion, and host-mediated pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the understanding of JEV pathogenesis from both viral and host perspectives. We discuss the key events during JEV infection in mammalian hosts, including viral attachment and entry, replication and dissemination, viral determinants of virulence, blood-brain barrier penetration, and the mechanisms underlying central and peripheral nervous system injury. We further compare currently available experimental models for JEV research, including mouse models, porcine models, and human brain organoid systems, highlighting their respective applications, advantages, and limitations in investigating JEV pathogenesis. Collectively, this review provides an integrated overview of the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing JEV infection and neuropathogenesis, identifies current knowledge gaps, and discusses future research priorities that may facilitate the development of effective antiviral and neuroprotective strategies against Japanese encephalitis.

articles.titulo: The Potassium Channel Gene BmTWK7 Contributes to Cocoon-Spinning Behavior in Bombyx mori
articles.autores: Sun X, Tan Y, … Sima Y (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Potassium channels regulate membrane potential, cellular excitability, and neurotransmission, yet potential behavioral and physiological roles in the silkworm (Bombyx mori) remain unclear. Here, the roles of BmTWK7 (TWiK family of potassium channels protein 7), a gene encoding a two-pore-domain potassium (K2P) channel, were investigated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout. BmTWK7 deficiency reduced the larval heart rate and altered dorsal vessel contraction patterns, supporting a regulatory role in cardiac function. BmTWK7-deficient larvae exhibited altered cocoon-spinning behavior, including a tendency toward an expanded wandering range, altered temporal patterns of spinning rate in males, higher cocooning positions, larger spinning areas, increased cocoon floss, and a higher frequency of incomplete cocoons. BmTWK7 deficiency was further associated with reduced head GABA levels, widespread downregulation of brain GABA-related genes, and increased brain Ca2+ fluorescence. Together, these findings support the role of BmTWK7 in regulating cocoon-spinning behavior and cardiac activity, while its deficiency was associated with altered GABAergic homeostasis and increased brain Ca2+ signals, highlighting broader roles of K2P channels in insect behavior and physiology.

articles.titulo: Eight-year malaria trend in Estie District, Ethiopia: implications for malaria elimination
articles.autores: Adugna T (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original:
In Ethiopia, malaria is one of the leading health and socioeconomic problems even though significant numbers of malaria cases were reduced in the last two decades. The health facilities' retrospective studies offer valuable insights into how to carry out evidence-based interventions in particular areas and assess the effectiveness of ongoing malaria control initiatives. However, the trend of malaria prevalence has not been studied so far in the Estie locality; therefore, this study was designed to evaluate the eight-year trend of malaria in the Estie district, Ethiopia.
A retrospective study was conducted to determine the occurrence of malaria over the past eight years (2015-2022) from the peripheral blood smear examinations reported in the laboratory logbooks of the Mekane Eyesus hospital and health center, Ethiopia. To show the trends of infection rate patterns in months, years, sexes, age groups, residential settings, and seasons, descriptive statistics were used. Tables and figures were used to display results.
Of 49,215 clinically malaria-suspected individuals, only 15.6% (7674) microscopically confirmed malaria cases were reported in the district. The rate of infection was much higher in males (81.9%) and rural communities (71.3%) than females (18.1%) and urban communities (28.7%), respectively (p < 0.01). The most frequently identified Plasmodium species was Plasmodium falciparum (p < 0.01). The highest peak of malaria cases was recorded in age groups between 15 and 44 years in the autumn season (September, October, and November), which is considered the peak malaria transmission period in Ethiopia after the heavy rain in July and August.
Despite large fluctuations in malaria incidence over the last eight years, malaria has remained a public health problem in the research area. Malaria is particularly likely to reappear between 2021 and 2022, which is extremely concerning. Furthermore, in the study location, P. falciparum is the predominant species, followed by P. vivax in a rural population. As a result, the use of ongoing intervention strategies should be reviewed. Uninterrupted efforts and increased malaria control and prevention activities are critical to considerably lowering the malaria burden in the research area. Unless these issues are addressed, the country's goal of eradicating malaria would be significantly hampered.

articles.titulo: Salicylamides as RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase Inhibitors with Antiviral Activity against West Nile and Zika Viruses
articles.autores: Río ND, Rodríguez-Tacón Á, … Pérez-Pérez MJ (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-transmitted orthoflaviviruses constitute an escalating global threat to public health, for which no approved antiviral therapies exist. Here, we identify the salicylanilide derivative S1 as a West Nile virus (WNV) RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase (RdRp) inhibitor. Chemical optimization of S1 yielded compound S7, which inhibited WNV RdRp activity and displayed antiviral efficacy in Vero cells (EC50 of 3.0 μM; CC50 > 100 μM). S7 and related analogues inhibited Zika virus (ZIKV) RdRp, and this enzymatic inhibition translated into antiviral activity in cell-based assays. Compared with niclosamide, as reference salicylanilide, compound S7 exerted lower impact on mitochondria, reduced cytotoxicity and no induction of apoptosis. Molecular modelling support binding within the polymerase N-pocket, with key contributing residues being highly conserved in both WNV and ZIKV polymerases. Site-directed mutagenesis further supported the importance of N-pocket residues for S7 binding. Therefore, the S7-scaffold constitutes a promising antiviral chemotype against orthoflaviviruses.

articles.titulo: The Molecular Potassium Code: Extracellular K^+^ Sensing, Allosteric Ion Selectivity, KCC2 Thermodynamics, and the Dynamic Control of Neural Inhibition
articles.autores: Dumitrescu D, Dumitru AV, … Rădoi MP (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Neuronal excitability can be controlled by the level of potassium (K+) outside a neuron through both its effects on the cell membrane's electrical properties and its influence on ion transport across the membrane. Recent studies have also shown that certain ligand-gated ion-channel receptors can be modulated by the levels of K+ outside the neuron. Therefore, understanding how each mechanism contributes to the generation of inhibitory signals requires the ability to differentiate between them. This study represents a review that integrates evidence using various methods, including electrophysiology, structural studies, thermodynamics, and optical measurements, to propose a framework called the molecular potassium code that explains how neurons respond to varying levels of K+ in their environment. The framework describes three ways that neurons interact with changing levels of K+: how these changes shift their K+ equilibrium potential and membrane voltage; how they alter the thermodynamic driving force for KCC2-mediated cotransport of K+ and Cl-; and how receptor-dependent modulation occurs at specific receptors when documented. Changes in activation, desensitization, pharmacological sensitivity, and permeation characteristics have been measured in Drosophila DmAlka channels; however, the atomic details of K+ recognition by these channels remain unclear. Human GlyRα2 variants engineered or edited to allow for assessment of K+-associated responses under elevated K+ conditions did not provide sufficient evidence for physiological recruitment of these receptors in mammals. Additionally, the presence and function of astrocytes, as well as geometric factors such as size, shape, and orientation, affect local concentrations of K+. Therefore, the framework described here provides multiple approaches that scientists can use to measure and interpret different mechanisms contributing to the generation of inhibitory signals in the nervous system.

articles.titulo: Future of Parasitology Symposium 2026: perspectives from the next generation
articles.autores: Beher B, Ali M, … Rosado J (5 autores)

articles.titulo: Prevention of Experimental Severe Malaria
articles.autores: Rishiq A, Birman I, … Golenser J (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background: Severe malaria, including cerebral malaria and malaria-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome, remains associated with high mortality despite anti-plasmodial and supportive therapies. This study evaluates whether a drug combination can prevent severe malaria complications in a well-defined experimental model. The combination includes an anti-plasmodial artemisinin derivative, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor originally developed for anti-angiogenic cancer therapy, and the general immunosuppressant dexamethasone. Methods: C57BL/6 mice were infected with Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA sub1a strain). Disease progression was assessed using MRI, histology, and liver enzyme analysis and by monitoring parasitemia and survival. The drugs administered included the anti-plasmodial agent artemisone (Art), dexamethasone (Dex), a systemic immunosuppressant, and apatinib (Apa) and sunitinib, both angiogenesis inhibitors. Additional experiments were performed in infected Ncr1-deficient and Tigit-KO transgenic mice (which show decreased or increased activation of NK cells, respectively). Results: PbA infection in C57bl/6 mice induced mild cerebral pathology, severe pulmonary inflammation with edema and microhemorrhages, and elevated liver enzymes, followed by death within a week post-infection, despite relatively low parasitemia on the day of death. Early treatment with Art, starting two- or three days post-infection (PI), killed the parasites and led to complete recovery. Dex, Apa, and sunitinib, initiated at the same early time points PI, prevented acute mortality. However, about two weeks later, these mice developed high parasitemia and succumbed to the disease. Late treatment (starting five days PI) with the individual compounds was ineffective. In contrast, late combined treatment with Dex, Apa, and Art eliminated the plasmodia and rescued most mice. Infection of Ncr1-deficient or Tigit-KO mice resulted in rapidly fatal disease with a course similar to that in mice with the same genetic background, indicating that partial immunosuppression or immune enhancement is insufficient to inhibit malaria progression and that NK cells do not necessarily play a role in the pathology. Conclusions: Multi-target therapy using anti-plasmodial, immunomodulatory, and anti-angiogenic agents has the potential to prevent severe malaria complications and improve survival outcomes.

articles.titulo: Exploratory Survey of Fungal Communities and Cultivable Yeasts Associated with Mosquito Larval Habitats in Italy
articles.autores: Cappelli A, Damiani C, … Ricci I (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Fungi represent recurrent components of mosquito-associated microbial communities, but the larval mycobiota remains far less documented than its bacterial counterpart. Here, we conducted an exploratory survey of fungal communities associated with mosquito larvae collected across central and north-eastern Italy during 2022 and 2023, collecting Aedes albopictus, Aedes koreicus and Culex pipiens larvae and related breeding waters. A subset of 16 larval pools and five water samples was analysed via ITS metabarcoding, while 23 samples were subjected to culture-dependent isolation. Metabarcoding revealed fungal assemblages dominated by Ascomycota and Basidiomycota and Rozellomycota sensu lato, with prominent yeast genera such as Wickerhamomyces, Kurtzmaniella, Candida, Rhodotorula and Metschnikowia. Cultivation yielded 21 yeast isolates assigned to seven distinct species: Candida parapsilosis, Metschnikowia pulcherrima, Barnettozyma californica, Schwanniomyces vanrijiae, Sporobolomyces roseus, Wickerhamomyces anomalus and Rhodotorula paludigena. Overlap between cultured yeast genera and metabarcoding profiles confirmed the complementary nature of the two approaches. This study documents fungal associations in three relevant mosquito species and provides, to our knowledge, the first ITS metabarcoding-based description of the mycobiota in field-collected Ae. koreicus larvae. Although the constrained sampling design precludes definitive inferences regarding host specificity or geographic patterns, the findings provide a baseline for larger studies of mosquito-associated fungal diversity.

articles.titulo: Implications of the trade-offs between negative density-dependence and Allee effects for vector control
articles.autores: Kipingu AM, Kiware S, … Viana M (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Understanding population dynamics is fundamental for predicting species persistence and extinction, yet remains challenging because of the complex interplay among ecological, environmental, and anthropogenic factors. Population dynamics are regulated by intrinsic processes, such as negative density-dependence, driven by factors, including resource competition during larval development, and Allee effects, which can arise through mechanisms such as mate limitation at low population densities. While negative density-dependence is well-understood, Allee effects have received comparatively less attention despite important implications for conservation and population management. For disease vectors, both negative density-dependence and Allee effects can influence whether populations persist, rebound following control, or are driven to elimination. In malaria mosquitoes, negative density-dependence at the larval stages is well-known to regulate population growth, whereas Allee effects have not been empirically demonstrated, and their potential implications and interactions with negative density-dependence remain poorly understood. This study addresses this gap using a population simulation model to evaluate the trade-offs between negative density-dependence and potential mate-finding Allee effects and their implications for vector control. It is possible that, depending on the vector control strategy, Allee effects could become important at low densities and push populations closer to extinction.
A stochastic stage-structured population simulation model representing a simplified mosquito life cycle was developed. Negative density-dependence and mate-finding Allee effects were incorporated as processes affecting larval survival and total fecundity, respectively. Their effects were examined by varying the strength of both processes independently and jointly, under different vector control scenarios: control, sustained and shorter-term interventions (here, immolating larvicides) that reduced larval population.
When considered separately, neither negative density-dependence nor mate-finding Allee effects had a substantial long-term effect on population persistence, although negative density-dependence substantially altered equilibrium abundance. However, their combined effects accelerated population decline and increased the likelihood of extinction as the strength of both processes increased. Because Allee effects operate on low population abundances, sustained interventions were able to reduce mosquito populations to levels, where Allee effects became important, thereby increasing the probability of extinction. In contrast, short-term interventions led to population rebound, driven by negative density-dependence as formulated in the simulation.
Understanding less-studied regulatory processes such as Allee effects can support vector control by identifying stages of the vector life cycle that are either resilient or vulnerable to interventions. The results suggest that, if present, the mate-finding Allee effects and density-dependent resource competition considered in this study could potentially be leveraged to accelerate vector control and support the elimination of vector-borne diseases, such as malaria.

articles.titulo: Indium Stress in Plants: Toxicity Mechanisms, Physiological Adaptation, and Emerging Mitigation Strategies
articles.autores: Ali B, Rehman M, … Gan Y (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Indium is widely used in high-tech industries and renewable energy applications; however, its increasing environmental release from industrial activities and electronic waste recycling poses a growing threat to agricultural ecosystems. In response to this growing challenge, this review comprehensively synthesizes the biogeochemical fate of indium and its phytotoxic effects, focusing on soil dynamics and root retention, physiological and molecular mechanisms of toxicity, and emerging mitigation strategies. In soils, indium exhibits remarkably low mobility and strong root retention, resulting in severe growth inhibition. It profoundly disrupts nutrient homeostasis, particularly that of phosphorus, magnesium, and iron, thereby triggering excessive production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS). Consequently, indium toxicity induces lipid peroxidation, photosynthetic dysfunction, caspase-like programmed cell death, and premature cell-wall lignification. While multi-omics evidence reveals that plants attempt to counter this toxicity via phosphate-starvation signaling, autophagy, and antioxidant defenses, acute redox imbalance often overwhelms these intrinsic defense mechanisms. To contextualize these findings, we highlight indium's distinct biogeochemical behavior relative to other metal contaminants and technology-critical elements, thereby integrating systems-level insights into plant stress responses. Additionally, we evaluate promising mitigation strategies, emphasizing biochar amendments, root exudate regulation (e.g., flavonols), and beneficial nanomaterials, including silicon- and selenium-based materials, titanium dioxide nanoparticles, and emerging heteroatom-doped carbon dots, for enhancing plant resilience. Ultimately, we propose that the development and field validation of these targeted mitigation strategies will be essential for safeguarding sustainable crop productivity in indium-contaminated agroecosystems.

articles.titulo: Reticulon-3 at the Interface of Hepatitis C and Dengue Virus Infection: Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Transfer and Emerging Antiviral Vulnerabilities
articles.autores: Noumi T, Bitazar R, … Bukong TN (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Positive-sense RNA viruses are commonly classified by genome organization, entry route, tissue tropism, and clinical syndrome, but these categories do not explain how viruses construct protected replication niches or route infectious material between cells. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) provides a shared platform for viral translation, replication-organelle formation, membrane curvature, lipid remodeling, innate immune regulation, and vesicular trafficking. Within this framework, reticulon-3 (RTN3) has emerged as a candidate regulator linking ER-based RNA-virus replication to the generation of infectious extracellular-vesicle cargo. Hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV) provide complementary experimental settings for evaluating this model despite their distinct transmission routes, tissue tropisms, disease courses, and immune pathophysiology. HCV most clearly demonstrates that exosome-enriched fractions can transfer replication-competent viral RNA with defined host cofactors, whereas DENV provides an acute infection model for examining related transfer phenotypes. Both viruses nevertheless replicate within remodeled ER membranes and can transfer infection-competent material in a vesicle-associated form. Functional perturbation studies implicate RTN3 in the output of infection-associated vesicle preparations, but do not yet establish direct recognition of viral RNA or its incorporation into endosomal intraluminal vesicles. RTN3 can also restrict HCV replication through NS4B interactions, suggesting that its effects vary by endpoint and may reflect distinct functions at different stages of infection. Related membrane-remodeling and vesicle-associated processes in Zika virus, West Nile virus, enteroviruses, SARS-CoV-2, and hepatitis A virus illustrate broader exploitation of host membrane organization, but replication-membrane phenotypes and vesicle-associated dissemination in these systems do not establish an RTN3-dependent infectious EV pathway. In selected models, EV-enriched preparations contain protected viral cargo and transfer biological activity to recipient cells; neither particle enrichment nor infectivity alone resolves the carrier's identity. Advances in isolation and characterization, including density-gradient or size-exclusion separation, immunoaffinity selection, particle and marker profiling, membrane-protection assays, and recipient-cell infectivity testing, now permit more rigorous identification of defined vesicle populations, protected cargo, and biological activity. Nevertheless, RTN3 should not be considered a universal RNA-virus dependency, nor should extracellular-vesicle release be assumed to generate uniformly infectious populations. Instead, HCV and DENV support functional involvement of RTN3 in vesicle-associated output, while the molecular connection between ER organization and selective cargo enclosure remains unresolved. Defining these shared and virus-specific dependencies may reveal host-virus interfaces suitable for broad-spectrum or resistance-resilient intervention, provided that infection-selective reliance, a measurable therapeutic window, and preservation of essential host-cell functions can be demonstrated.

articles.titulo: Enhanced Protection by Fluoride Varnish with Nano-Sized Sodium Trimetaphosphate Against Enamel Erosive Wear: An In Situ Study
articles.autores: Paiva MF, Delbem ACB, … Pessan JP (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To assess the effects of fluoride varnishes containing micrometric or nano-sized sodium trimetaphosphate (TMPmicro or TMPnano, respectively) on erosive tooth wear (ETW) in situ.
In this randomized, double-blind, crossover study, 14 participants wore palatal devices containing bovine enamel blocks (n=4/device), which received each of the four varnish treatments in separate experimental periods: Placebo (Pla - without F/TMP); 5% NaF (5NaF); 5NaF + 5% TMPmicro (5-TMPmicro); and 5NaF + 5% TMPnano (5-TMPnano). After 6 h of intraoral exposure and varnish removal, the blocks underwent four daily erosive challenges ex vivo for five days (ERO, 0.05 M citric acid, pH 3.2, 90 s), while two blocks were additionally subjected to abrasion by brushing (ERO+ABR). Profilometry, surface hardness (SH), cross-sectional hardness (ΔKHN) and computed X-ray micro tomography (gHAp × cm⁻³ × µm) were performed. Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA and Holm-Sidak's test (p<0.05).
ETW, integrated mineral loss and depth of mineral loss of the remaining eroded enamel showed a consistent treatment ranking under both conditions, with the greatest protection observed for 5-TMPnano, followed by 5-TMPmicro, 5NaF, and Pla. Compared with 5NaF, ETW was reduced by 20-22% with 5-TMPmicro and 40-50% with 5-TMPnano under ERO and ERO+ABR. A similar pattern was observed for hardness in depth (ΔKHN at 5-30 µm from the enamel surface), except between 5-TMPmicro and 5-TMPnano. Compared with 5NaF, SH loss was significantly lower for both TMP-containing varnishes under ERO, but only for 5-TMPnano under ERO+ABR.
F varnish supplemented with TMP significantly reduced ETW in situ, and nano-sized TMP provided additional protection.
The addition of TMP to 5% NaF varnishes, especially as nanoparticles, may enhance their protective effect against enamel erosive wear.

articles.titulo: Transcriptomic analyses reveal how parasites exploit plasticity in caste and brain development of social wasps
articles.autores: Vacca NA, Padilla-Choy V, … Uy FMK (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The evolution of castes in social insects is one of the most spectacular examples of phenotypic plasticity. However, this adaptive plasticity could instead be exploited by parasites to develop an extended phenotype. We characterize the timing and molecular changes induced by enigmatic twisted-wing insects to manipulate developing social wasps. These parasites reprogram short-lived female workers into phenotypes that are long-lived like queens, while hindering ovary development and cooperative behavior. Using differential gene expression analyses across developmental stages of naturally infected and uninfected brood coupled with experimental infections, we uncovered that parasites manipulate the developmental plasticity that determines caste bias.
Parasite larvae infected most host larval instars. Across development, we identified 2341 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between uninfected workers and gynes (future queens), 529 DEGs between infected and uninfected workers, and 2672 DEGs between infected workers and uninfected gynes. However, robust differences in the number of DEGs were unique to each host stage. Specifically, candidate genes linked caste bias to insulin and juvenile hormone pathways, immune responses, and neural development. Controlling for the effect of nutrition and social interactions in development through our infection experiment revealed that the parasites consistently targeted caste bias and neural genes. Finally, infecting long-lived gyne brood that is not targeted in nature showed minimal manipulation.
Our findings reveal how stage-specific targeting of caste plasticity initiates the reprogramming of hosts towards the long-lived extended phenotype. We propose leveraging emerging host-parasite systems to unravel the molecular mechanisms underlying adaptive developmental plasticity.

articles.titulo: Hemozoin-Targeting and Glutathione-Responsive Theranostic Prodrug Platform for Targeted Malaria Therapy
articles.autores: Tayde D, Ali S, … Pramanik SK (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria remains a major global health challenge, while the efficacy of artemisinin-based combination therapies is increasingly threatened by emerging resistance, treatment failure, and dose-limiting toxicity. Here, we report a stimulus-responsive antimalarial prodrug designed to exploit parasite-specific biochemical and physicochemical features. A hemozoin-targeting, reduction-responsive dihydroartemisinin (DHA) prodrug, DHA-SS-SmCp, was constructed by conjugating DHA to a luminescent Sm(DBM)3PHEN-NH2 complex through a glutathione (GSH)-cleavable disulfide linker. The prodrug spontaneously assembled into stable, monodisperse nanoparticles (534 ± 10 nm; PDI ≈ 0.084), enabling nanoparticle-mediated delivery and imaging. The reductive intracellular environment promotes disulfide cleavage and efficient DHA release, while the paramagnetic Sm complex facilitates association with hemozoin-rich parasite compartments. This integrated design provides both stimulus-responsive drug activation and parasite-associated imaging capabilities. In a Plasmodium yoelii N67-infected mouse model, DHA-SS-SmCp administered at 30 mg/kg DHA equivalent achieved complete parasite clearance, whereas free DHA at the same dose did not. By integrating redox-triggered activation, hemozoin affinity, luminescent imaging, and self-assembled nanodelivery, this study establishes a chemically programmed prodrug platform for selective antimalarial therapy and provides a framework for developing parasite-responsive therapeutics.

articles.titulo: Bone turnover and phosphate metabolism in children with Prader-Willi syndrome: results from two tertiary centers
articles.autores: Cheleș AD, Nicoară DM, … Mărginean O (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by impaired growth, altered body composition, and reduced bone mineral accrual. However, the relationships between skeletal maturation, bone turnover, and phosphate homeostasis during childhood remain insufficiently understood. This study explored bone turnover, somatotropic function, skeletal maturation, and phosphate metabolism in children with PWS compared with healthy peers. In this two-center retrospective case-control study, 40 children and adolescents with molecularly confirmed PWS and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were evaluated between January 2016 and May 2026. Anthropometric measurements, bone age, somatotropic axis parameters, bone turnover markers, and indices of phosphate metabolism were analyzed using multivariable-adjusted models, correlation analyses, regression models, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses. Compared with controls, children with PWS showed a pattern of lower circulating bone turnover markers characterized by significantly lower osteocalcin, C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen, bone-specific alkaline phosphatase, and insulin-like growth factor I, together with a reduced molar insulin-like growth factor I/insulin-like growth factor-binding protein-3 ratio and delayed skeletal maturation. Phosphate metabolism was characterized by higher serum phosphorus, tubular reabsorption of phosphate, and tubular maximum reabsorption of phosphate per glomerular filtration rate, accompanied by lower fibroblast growth factor 23, ionized calcium, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D. Within the PWS group, bone turnover markers correlated with bone age. In exploratory analyses, growth hormone treatment status was not significantly associated with insulin-like growth factor I or major bone turnover markers; however, interpretation was limited by incomplete information regarding treatment dose, duration, age at initiation and adherence. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis identified bone age delay (AUC = 0.847) and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (AUC = 0.842) as the strongest discriminators of PWS versus control status within the study population. Children and adolescents with PWS showed cross-sectional differences in skeletal maturation, bone turnover, and phosphate homeostasis compared with healthy controls. These findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in longitudinal studies incorporating detailed growth hormone exposure, bone density, and body composition assessments.
