articles.titulo: Combined Spinosad and Pyriproxyfen in Toxic Sugar Baits Enhances Suppression of Culex quinquefasciatus
articles.autores: Alomar AA (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Combining insecticides with different biological activities may improve the effectiveness of toxic sugar baits (TSBs) for adult mosquito control. This study evaluated the lethal and sublethal effects of spinosad, pyriproxyfen, and their combination in TSBs against adult Culex quinquefasciatus. Concentration-response assays showed concentration-dependent mortality for both insecticides. Pyriproxyfen had lower LC50 estimates than spinosad, with values of 2.61 and 1.60 ppm for females and males, respectively, compared with 4.84 and 3.58 ppm for spinosad. Sublethal exposure to either insecticide reduced longevity, fecundity, and fertility, while adult size was unaffected. The combined treatment produced the greatest reductions in longevity, fecundity, and fertility compared with either insecticide alone. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining spinosad and pyriproxyfen in TSB formulations to enhance suppression of adult Cx. quinquefasciatus. Further studies are needed to investigate potential interactions between these insecticides and evaluate their combined effectiveness under field conditions.

articles.titulo: Acupuncture Integration in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS): A Comprehensive Evidence-Based Review
articles.autores: Yang W, Xu J, … Zheng Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols have significantly improved perioperative outcomes; however, challenges including opioid-related adverse effects, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), delayed gastrointestinal recovery, and chronic post-surgical pain remain incompletely resolved. These limitations are closely linked to perioperative neuroimmune and autonomic dysregulation, which current pharmacologic strategies do not adequately address. This review examines acupuncture and acupoint-based stimulation modalities, including electroacupuncture and transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation, as adjunctive interventions within ERAS pathways. Current evidence suggests that these modalities may reduce postoperative pain and opioid consumption, decrease PONV incidence, and support gastrointestinal recovery in selected perioperative settings, with generally acceptable safety when delivered by trained practitioners. Mechanistic investigations suggest that these effects may involve modulation of spinal nociceptive processing, vagal anti-inflammatory pathways, and autonomic balance. Despite heterogeneity in study design and intervention protocols, the cumulative evidence supports the potential role of acupuncture as an adjunctive perioperative strategy, particularly for PONV and selected recovery outcomes. Acupuncture may serve as a mechanism-informed adjunct within ERAS pathways, with stronger conclusions requiring large, high-quality randomized controlled trials using standardized protocols and clinically meaningful endpoints.

articles.titulo: From Bacterial Persistence to Granuloma Failure: Mechanisms of LTBI Reactivation as a Framework for Tuberculosis Prevention and Treatment
articles.autores: Zhang L, Sun W, … Gong W (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Latent tuberculosis infection constitutes the principal reservoir from which tuberculosis (TB) disease emerges, yet the molecular transition from durable containment to reactivation remains incompletely resolved. Reactivation is not a single bacterial "awakening" event or a nonspecific consequence of immunosuppression. Instead, we propose a hypothesis-generating threshold framework across an interconnected pathogen-host-microenvironment system. This narrative review integrates evidence on Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence and resuscitation programs, including metabolic remodeling, resuscitation-promoting factors, cell-wall turnover, and metal acquisition, with defects in adaptive and innate immunity, immunometabolic control, cytokine networks, aging, comorbid disease, and epigenetic regulation. We further examine the granuloma as a spatially heterogeneous ecosystem in which hypoxia, necrosis, vascular dysfunction, fibrosis, extracellular-vesicle communication, and intercellular crosstalk may influence bacterial control. Evidence from human longitudinal and cross-sectional studies is distinguished from non-human primate, other animal, in vitro, and cross-system evidence. The proposed balance between bacillary resuscitation potential and local containment capacity has not been prospectively validated in humans or defined by a numerical clinical cutoff. Pathogen-, host-, and lesion-directed approaches are therefore discussed as research priorities. They are not alternatives to recommended TB preventive treatment for eligible individuals or antimicrobial treatment of TB disease. Prospective human validation is required before the framework can inform biomarker-guided intervention or patient stratification.

articles.titulo: Characterization of Pathogenic Features of Dengue Virus Serotypes 1-4 in the AG129 Mouse Model
articles.autores: Cai C, Ding K, … Sun Q (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: An AG129 mouse infection model with four DENV isolates was established to systematically characterize the early pathogenic phenotypes of these strains. DENV-1 caused 100% mortality by 15 dpi, with sustained viremia, widespread multi-organ injury, and persistent leukopenia. DENV-4 exhibited peak viremia at 4 dpi and unique neurovirulence, presenting exclusive hind-limb paralysis, severe pulmonary hemorrhage, and characteristic cerebral parenchymal lesions. DENV-2 and DENV-3 induced only transient mild viremia and focal tissue alterations without mortality. Hematological and biochemical alterations, as well as occasional splenic hemosiderin deposition, were noted among infected animals. This preclinical dataset offers insights into serotype-specific DENV pathogenesis and may aid future evaluation of broad-spectrum antivirals and tetravalent vaccine candidates.

articles.titulo: Discovery of Indazole-Based Dual-Pharmacophore Inhibitors of Dengue and Zika Proteases as Promising Antivirals
articles.autores: Singh SK, Potluri V, … Prasad PK (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Flavivirus outbreaks caused by dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) remain a major global health challenge, with no FDA-approved antivirals available. Herein, we designed, synthesized, and evaluated indazole-based dual pharmacophore motifs targeting NS2B-NS3 serine proteases, essential for viral replication. Enzymatic assays revealed nanomolar to sub-micromolar potency, with strong selectivity over host serine proteases, minimizing off-target risks. Biophysical studies showed ligand-induced thermal stabilization, while kinetic and dialysis analyses confirmed a reversible, competitive, non-covalent inhibition mechanism. In DENV-infected Vero CCL-81 cells, several leads exhibited potent antiviral activity with low cytotoxicity. Notably, compound C8 demonstrated low-nanomolar enzyme inhibition against both viruses, translating to complete viral suppression in cells (EC50 = 0.5 μM) with a good selectivity index, underscoring its therapeutic potential. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported these findings, revealing key active-site interactions consistent with potency and specificity. Collectively, these results highlight indazole-based dual-pharmacophore inhibitors as promising anti-flaviviral leads.

articles.titulo: Stochastic dynamics of a multi-stage dengue model with vaccination and saturated incidence rates
articles.autores: Rajasekar SP, Priya MM (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Complex population movements and inherent disruptive environmental factors render it more challenging to analyse the pathogenic dengue virus. Research on epidemic mathematical frameworks may assist in protecting the economy and public health in addition to predicting the dengue epidemic's development pattern. Influenced by this, we discuss the six-dimensional ShVhIhRh-SvIv dengue stochastic epidemic model. For this stochastic system, we first verify the existence and uniqueness of a positive global solution. Next, we construct the suitable Lyapunov function to analyse the existence and uniqueness of a stationary distribution with ergodic features by Khasminskii's method. To investigate the statistical report for the existing stationary distribution by using a probability density function. This yields, the expression of the probability density function near quasi-endemic equilibrium of log-normal properties is solved by the Fokker-Planck equation. Furthermore, sufficient conditions are derived to eradicate and control the dengue transmission. Subsequently, numerical simulations are executed to validate the mathematical predictions, and the impact of environmental disturbances and key parameters on dengue transmission is taken into account as well.
consultas: plasmodium OR arbovirus OR dengue OR zika

articles.titulo: Assessment of the coverage, use rate and physical integrity of long-lasting insecticide nets after scaling up of their distribution in Gujarat, India
articles.autores: Baharia RK, Vadhel A, … Yadav CP (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs) are a key tool for control and elimination of malaria, by providing protection from the bite of infected mosquitoes. To support its malaria elimination goal by 2030, Gujarat distributed LLINs across 33 districts in 2019. However, sustained effectiveness depends on consistent use and proper maintenance.
A household-based cross-sectional survey was conducted in the Anand, Kutch, Panchmahal, and Surendranagar districts of the state of Gujarat in India. A Standard WHO questionnaire was used to assess LLIN coverage, usage, and maintenance. A total of 4719 households were surveyed. Net ownership, usage patterns, physical integrity (Hole size, washing and dry pattern), and maintenance practices were evaluated.
LLIN ownership was high (93.8%), but consistent usage was lower (51.9%). Seasonal variation in adherence was observed, with 86.5% of households using LLINs year-round and 91.8% using them while sleeping outdoors. Maintenance practices varied: 76.5% of households washed their nets regularly, but 51.6% dried them in direct sunlight, which may reduce their efficacy. Physical durability was compromised, with 27.3% of nets developing holes due to wear and misuse. Additionally, 23.6% of households repurposed LLINs for activities such as fishing or livestock protection.
Despite high coverage, gaps in consistent usage, proper care, and net durability remain challenges. Addressing these through community education, discouraging alternative net use, and improving sleeping conditions is essential to maximize the impact of LLINs. Strengthening behavioral interventions and maintenance practices will enhance LLIN effectiveness and contribute to Gujarat's malaria elimination efforts.

articles.titulo: Recent advances in the glioma tumor microenvironment (TME): cellular interactions, signaling networks, and therapeutic opportunities
articles.autores: Moqbel AQ, Ghani MU, … Ke X (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Gliomas are treatment-resistant primary brain tumors, with glioblastoma (GBM) representing the most aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma. Their progression reflects the interplay between tumor-intrinsic alterations and the surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME). The TME comprises immune, stromal, vascular, and extracellular matrix (ECM) components, which together shape tumor growth, invasion, immune evasion, and treatment response. In GBM, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), microglia, astrocytes, and endothelial cells interact with tumor cells through cytokine, chemokine, growth-factor, and extracellular-vesicle signaling, influencing tumor behavior and antitumor immunity. Hypoxia, vascular dysfunction, and ECM remodeling further shape this environment by altering tumor metabolism, angiogenesis, immune activity, and glioma-cell invasion. Molecular alterations, including EGFR activation, IDH mutations, BRAF alterations, and PTEN loss, also influence TME organization across glioma subtypes and contribute to differences in disease progression and treatment response. Despite advances in standard treatment, recurrence and therapeutic resistance remain major challenges, particularly in GBM. These challenges have driven interest in TME-directed strategies, including immunotherapy, anti-angiogenic therapy, metabolic interventions, vaccines, and myeloid-targeted approaches. Although several strategies have shown promise in preclinical models and clinical studies, their therapeutic efficacy remains variable. This review provides an integrated analysis of the glioma TME, with particular emphasis on GBM. We examine how immune, vascular, metabolic, ECM, and tumor-intrinsic factors interact to shape disease progression and treatment response. We also discuss emerging TME-targeted therapies and experimental models that deepen mechanistic understanding of glioma biology and may guide the development of more precise and effective treatments.

articles.titulo: The Holobiont Bioreactor: Microbiome Dynamics, Biosafety Paradoxes, and Ecological Engineering in Black Soldier Fly Bioconversion
articles.autores: Dabravolski SA, Pavshintsev VV, … Mitkin NA (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens L.) has emerged as a cornerstone technology for the circular economy, valorising organic waste into high-value insect protein and biofertiliser. The efficiency, safety, and adaptability of this bioconversion process are fundamentally dictated by the complex interplay between the insect host and its gut microbiome, which together function as an integrated 'holobiont bioreactor'. This reactor is characterised by partially vertically transmitted core taxa and a dynamic, horizontally acquired microbial community. This review critically synthesises high-impact original research identified through a systematic literature search published predominantly between 2021 and 2026, incorporating foundational landmark studies, to provide a mechanistic overview of this holobiont's function. We first dissect the architecture of the BSFL microbiome, examining the 'nature vs. nurture' debate of egg-associated vertical inheritance versus horizontal acquisition and highlighting the critical, yet often overlooked, role of the fungal mycobiome. We then explore the larval gut as a spatio-temporally compartmentalised bioreactor, where extreme physicochemical gradients and host-microbe metabolic crosstalk drive nutrient extraction and immunity. A central focus is placed on the 'Bioremediation vs. Biosafety Paradox', wherein the system's capacity to degrade chemical xenobiotics and sanitise pathogens is contrasted with its propensity to amplify antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and bioaccumulate contaminants like heavy metals and microplastics under specific substrate and exposure conditions. Finally, we evaluate the frontier of microbiome engineering from the deployment of native probiotics and synthetic microbial consortia (SynComs) to enhance performance to the use of prebiotics for mitigating ammonia emissions. This synthesis reveals that while BSFL technology holds immense promise, its industrial maturation is constrained by significant methodological limitations in the current literature. We conclude by advocating for a field-wide shift towards integrated multi-omics and viability-based analytical frameworks to ensure the development of safe, efficient, and regulatory-compliant bioconversion systems.

articles.titulo: Environmental indicators and large-scale climatic variability associated with malaria incidence in southeastern Iran: a 23-year negative binomial analysis
articles.autores: Dehghan A, Rahimi M, … Hanafi-Bojd AA (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria transmission is influenced by climatic and environmental conditions, but the relative contributions of large-scale climate variability and local environmental factors remain unclear in southeastern Iran. We assessed associations between ENSO, remotely sensed environmental indicators, monsoon precipitation, and malaria incidence during 2001-2023.
Monthly malaria surveillance data from eight counties in southeastern Iran (2001-2023) were analyzed using a retrospective ecological longitudinal design. Predictors included Niño 3.4 ENSO, NDVI, NDWI, and LST, with candidate lags evaluated based on model fit, estimated effects, and epidemiological plausibility. The primary analysis used a negative binomial mixed-effects model (NB-GLMM) with a log link, population offset, calendar-month adjustment, a four-degree-of-freedom nonlinear temporal trend, and county-level random intercepts. A quadratic term for six-month lagged LST was included to assess nonlinearity. County-specific models and random-slope analyses were used to assess spatial heterogeneity, while monsoon precipitation was analyzed separately using cumulative June-September rainfall in Chabahar, Saravan, and Sarbaz.
In the final province-wide model, six-month lagged LST showed a significant nonlinear, U-shaped association with malaria incidence, with the estimated minimum occurring at approximately 0.32 standard deviations above the mean LST. ENSO (IRR = 1.01, 95% CI 0.95-1.08; p = 0.653), NDVI (IRR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18; p = 0.888), and NDWI (IRR = 1.21, 95% CI 0.91-1.60; p = 0.192) were not independently associated with malaria incidence. County-specific analyses showed heterogeneous environmental associations, while formal random-slope analyses supported significant between-county heterogeneity for ENSO, NDVI, and NDWI but not LST. Monsoon-season precipitation was not significantly associated with annual malaria incidence in the analyzed counties. Environmental associations were substantially attenuated after adjustment for nonlinear long-term temporal variation.
Lagged LST showed a nonlinear province-wide association with malaria incidence, whereas ENSO, NDVI, and NDWI showed no independent associations. The attenuation of environmental associations after nonlinear temporal adjustment highlights the importance of accounting for long-term epidemiological trends. County-level heterogeneity indicates that environmental associations are context-dependent. The observed associations should not be interpreted as causal effects.

articles.titulo: Plant-Mediated Silver Nanoparticles for Aedes aegypti Control: Larvicidal Efficacy and Mechanisms
articles.autores: Seeniponnalagu S, Rajendran K, … Gurusamy D (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aedes aegypti L. in Hasselquist (Diptera: Culicidae) is a major vector of dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and other arboviral diseases. Increasing insecticide resistance and environmental concerns highlight the need for sustainable vector-control strategies. Phytochemical-mediated silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are promising bio-larvicidal agents because plant-derived metabolites contribute to nanoparticle formation, stabilization, and biological activity. This review provides a mechanistic and comparative assessment of green-synthesized AgNPs for A. aegypti control. It examines the roles of phytochemicals, including phenolics, flavonoids, terpenoids, and alkaloids, in nanoparticle synthesis and discusses how particle size, morphology, surface chemistry, and synthesis conditions influence larvicidal efficacy. Comparative analysis indicates that reported larvicidal activity varies with extract composition, nanoparticle characteristics, larval stage, exposure duration, and bioassay conditions, limiting direct comparisons of lethal concentrations across studies. Across the studies reviewed, plant-extract composition and synthesis-dependent nanoparticle characteristics emerge as important determinants of activity; however, their effects are difficult to separate from differences in larval stage, exposure duration, tested dose, and bioassay protocol. These methodological and material discrepancies elucidate the variability in reported lethal concentrations and the frequent unreliability of direct efficacy rankings across studies. Major toxicity mechanisms, including reactive oxygen species generation, oxidative stress, membrane disruption, enzyme inhibition, DNA damage, and apoptosis, are examined, with consideration of the distinction between experimentally demonstrated and proposed mechanisms in A. aegypti. The review also evaluates dose-response relationships and potential effects on non-target organisms and aquatic ecosystems. The contribution of plant metabolites to larvicidal activity and the relative roles of nanoparticles and released silver ions remain important research gaps. Challenges in standardization, reproducibility, scale-up, environmental safety, regulatory approval, and field validation are highlighted. Future research should prioritize harmonized synthesis and bioassay protocols, mechanistic validation, comprehensive ecological risk assessment, and field evaluation to support the responsible development of phytogenic AgNPs for mosquito control.

articles.titulo: Protein Lactylation in Sepsis-Associated Acute Lung Injury: Evidence and Controversies
articles.autores: Sun X, Zhang S, … Mao Z (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (SA-ALI/ARDS) is an important complication of sepsis involving disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier and immunometabolic dysregulation. Lysine lactylation (Kla) may link metabolic states to transcriptional regulation and protein function. However, blood lactate, global Kla abundance, and the function of lactylation at specific sites are not interchangeable. This review organizes the evidence by cell type, histone and non-histone substrate, and modification site, and separately evaluates modification identification, functional perturbation, lung injury phenotypes in animal models, and observations in patients. Current studies do not show a uniform direction of effect: some lactylation events have been associated with glycocalyx degradation, ferroptosis, inflammatory amplification, and intercellular injury signaling, whereas other studies report protective feedback. Differences in models and levels of intervention limit direct comparisons. Evidence for context dependence is emerging, but dependencies on time, concentration, and disease stage have not been adequately validated. Histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) in patient samples provides a candidate biomarker signal; its independent clinical value and the efficacy of lactylation-targeted interventions remain to be established. Future work should prioritize cell- and site-specific causal validation and connect these studies with standardized assays in patient samples and external clinical validation.

articles.titulo: Phosphorus concentration from low-phosphorus wastewater using embedded phosphorus removal biofillers coupled with anaerobic cyclic phosphorus release: performance evaluation and microbiological analysis
articles.autores: Song W, Yang H (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: To achieve high-concentration phosphorus (P) enrichment at low influent PO43--P concentrations while minimizing carbon source consumption, a reactor with embedded phosphorus removal biofillers (EBPAOs) was constructed in this study. Batch experiments were conducted to investigate the effect of the high-P solution formed by multiple anaerobic enrichment cycles on P release by EBPAOs. When the PO43--P concentration in the anaerobic P release liquid was below 200 mg/L, P release by EBPAOs was unaffected. As the PO43--P concentration increased, P release was gradually inhibited and nearly ceased at 400 mg/L. This is because the high P concentration weakened the transmembrane gradient of orthophosphate (ortho-P) and impeded its efflux, whereas the hydrolysis of intracellular polyphosphate (poly-P) remained unaffected. Under the coupled operation of aerobic continuous feeding (influent PO43--P 4 mg/L) and anaerobic P release cycling, the anaerobic phosphorus concentrate liquid (PCL) concentration reached 232.66 ± 1.20 mg/L after 13 cycles, achieving a concentration factor of 58.17, while the aerobic effluent PO43--P concentration was only 0.14 ± 0.06 mg/L. The relative abundance of Candidatus_Accumulibacter increased from 53.29% to 67.08%. Genes related to the pentose phosphate pathway were downregulated, whereas those related to the Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas pathway, polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) synthesis, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle were upregulated, enhancing PHA synthesis and adequate ATP supply. The ratio of anaerobic COD consumption to anaerobic P release (CODup/Prel) was 3.28 ± 0.03. These results indicate that this technology can achieve efficient P enrichment and stable P discharge control in low-P wastewater.

articles.titulo: Effect of metformin on HIV reservoir, inflammation and cell differentiation in non-diabetic older people with HIV: a two-year placebo-controlled pilot trial (Metforaging)
articles.autores: Gutiérrez-García L, Esteban-Cantos A, … Arribas JR (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
People with HIV (PWH) on long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART) exhibit persistent inflammation, immune activation, and a stable HIV reservoir, contributing to non-AIDS age-related comorbidities. Metformin, an indirect mTOR inhibitor with immunometabolic properties, is a candidate geroprotective agent. We assessed its long-term immunological and virological impact in non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥50 years.
Metforaging is a phase II, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in which 35 non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥ 50 years received metformin or placebo for 96 weeks. At baseline and week 96, we quantified blood T-cell, monocyte, B-cell and NK subsets, inflammation and immune checkpoint biomarkers, total HIV DNA, intact/defective proviruses, and cell-associated HIV RNA (CA-RNA). Between-group effects were estimated by baseline-adjusted ANCOVA.
At week 96, CD8+ TEMRA T cells increased with placebo but remained stable under metformin (adjusted mean difference -5.2%, 95% CI -8.5 to -2.0; p=0.003), with a modest increase in CD8+ effector memory T cells (p=0.044). No between-group differences were detected in soluble inflammation or immune checkpoint biomarkers, immune checkpoint mRNA expression, or HIV reservoir markers (total HIV DNA, intact and defective proviruses, CA-RNA).
In non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥50 years, 96 weeks of metformin appeared to attenuate CD8+ T-cell terminal differentiation with no between-group differences detected in systemic inflammation or the HIV reservoir. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.

articles.titulo: Same cell or separate sections? Cross-method identity evidence in the telocyte and Cajal-like cell literature: a sampled meta-research survey
articles.autores: Tudose RC, Varga I, … Rusu MC (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Telocytes and Cajal-like cells are identified by telopode ultrastructure or by markers and genetic labels read at light-microscope resolution; these identifications are equivalent only when they are joined in the same cell. We measured how often they join. From a metadata-defined frame of 908 records, a method-enriched census of the 18 whose abstracts declared an immunoelectron, correlative or volume-electron method and an equal-probability sample of 100 of the other 890 (87 obtained) were charted independently by two readers, the census by three. Each method-pair identity claim was classified as direct (same cell), population-level, inferred or unsupported. Readers mainly disagreed on immunolabelled cells showing the characteristic shape: depending on the reader, 25.6% or 55.3% of sampled papers reached a same-cell link. Because the marker draws the outline against which the shape is read, a post hoc rule set that pairing aside as co-registered but not independent, leaving 10.3% (8/78) and 15.8% (12/76; kappa, 0.54 between readings). At most two sampled papers made such a link at electron-microscope resolution and at most four reported numerical apertures; none of the 25 and 24 links pairing electron microscopy with light-level immunolabelling was direct; we found no extractable marker-versus-ultrastructure performance estimate among the charted papers. Seven census papers reached a direct electron-resolution link in the adopted file, four by immunoelectron labelling, so the link is technically feasible. In the sample, the bridge that makes a marker-defined population ultrastructurally defined was almost never built; reports should state the material pairing, the optics and the cell-level evidence.

articles.titulo: Heterologous expression of recombinant dengue virus C-prM-E structural antigens from all four serotypes in the red microalga Porphyridium purpureum
articles.autores: Utomo DIS, Bayu A, … Putra MY (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The dengue virus (DENV) remains a significant global health threat, and the currently available vaccines exhibit concerns regarding safety, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness. Microalgae represent an innovative method for producing proteins that do not occur naturally. They are Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS), easily scalable, and capable of inducing post-translational modifications in eukaryotes. This study illustrates the effective heterologous expression of recombinant dengue virus capsid-premembrane-envelope (C-prM-E) structural antigen constructs representing all four DENV serotypes (DV1-DV4) in the red microalga Porphyridium purpureum through Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation. Gene constructs containing capsid-premembrane-envelope (CprME) polyprotein fragments with C-terminal epitope tags were cloned into pCAMBIA1301 vectors and subsequently introduced into P. purpureum. PCR amplification confirmed the successful chromosomal integration of all four serotype constructs, yielding the anticipated 2.5-kb amplicons. The SDS-PAGE analysis revealed protein bands at around 85 kDa, consistent with the expected molecular weight of the processed CprME-derived proteins. We employed both anti-DENV-2 and anti-FLAG antibodies in a western blot assay to demonstrate that the recombinant antigens were identical and interacted with the immune system across all serotypes. These findings indicate that P. purpureum is an effective system for expressing DENV antigens, paving the path for the development of cost-effective, plant-derived dengue vaccine candidates. This microalgal platform may facilitate the large-scale production of tetravalent dengue vaccines, particularly in regions where dengue is prevalent and resources are scarce.

articles.titulo: Mussel Biodeposits as a Qualitative Sentinel Proxy for Environmental Plastic Contamination in Freshwater Ecosystems
articles.autores: Schirinzi GF, Geneselli I, … Ponti J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The identification of plastic particles below 10 µm in the environment is a challenge. Freshwater molluscs, widely used as model organisms for biomonitoring of water pollution, are able to filtrate large volume of water and naturally concentrate contaminants in their excretions. Based on this observation, this work aims to describe a method to collect and detect smaller plastic particles in feces and pseudofeces after animals' exposure to polyethylene terephthalate micro/nanoparticles, expected to be present in the environment at the end of its uncontrolled life cycle. Our findings, mainly based on Raman spectroscopy for polymer identification and electron microscopy, can be considered a qualitative to semi-quantitative proof of concept that can be further developed to build up a new system to collect plastics using molluscs, naturally exposed to environmental contaminants, without sacrificing them. In addition, the use of feces and pseudofeces of filtering organisms could be the solution to concentrate environmental plastics and confirm their presence.

articles.titulo: Potential roles of soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise in modulating the oral microbiome-host axis in obesity and diabetes: microbial dysbiosis, inflammation, and immunometabolic signaling
articles.autores: Chen D (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are complex metabolic disorders increasingly associated with alterations in the oral microbiome, chronic low-grade inflammation, dysregulated immunometabolic signaling, and systemic metabolic dysfunction. Although regular exercise is a cornerstone intervention for improving metabolic health, interindividual variability in exercise responsiveness has prompted interest in complementary nutritional strategies. Emerging evidence suggests that soy proteins and soy-derived isoflavones may influence metabolic and immune pathways relevant to exercise adaptation, potentially involving microbial and host-mediated mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes current experimental and clinical evidence regarding the potential roles of soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise in modulating the oral microbiome-host axis in obesity and diabetes. Particular attention is given to oral microbial dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, inflammatory and immune signaling, insulin resistance, glucose and lipid metabolism, vascular dysfunction, and systemic immunometabolic responses. We distinguish direct evidence from the oral microbiome from indirect evidence derived from the gut microbiome, systemic metabolic studies, and preclinical models. Although some findings suggest convergence of soy-derived bioactives and exercise on overlapping microbial and host pathways, such convergence should not be interpreted as experimentally established synergy. The potential contribution of microbial biotransformation of soy isoflavones and subsequent microbial-host interactions is also considered as an emerging, but incompletely characterized, mechanism linking dietary bioactives with systemic metabolic health. Overall, the available evidence supports a hypothesis-generating framework in which soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise may contribute to complementary modulation of microbial ecology and host immunometabolic signaling; however, direct human evidence linking these interventions to oral microbiome changes remains extremely limited. Most mechanistic evidence derives from gut microbiome research, systemic metabolic outcomes, and preclinical models and therefore cannot be directly extrapolated to the oral microbiome-host axis. Further well-controlled human studies are needed to determine whether combined soy and exercise interventions can reproducibly modify oral microbial communities and whether such changes are associated with clinically meaningful metabolic outcomes in obesity and T2DM.

articles.titulo: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment
articles.autores: Othayoth J, Bist JS, … Bist P (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.

articles.titulo: Nanotechnology-enabled modulation of immune cell ferroptosis for empowering cancer immunotherapy
articles.autores: Zhou T, Guo S, … Li M (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ferroptosis has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome therapy resistance and reshape the tumor-immune microenvironment. Beyond direct tumor killing capabilities, ferroptosis functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic regulator, capable of enhancing antitumor immunity through immunogenic cell death while also impairing immune effector functions under excessive oxidative stress. However, research has predominantly centered on tumor-cell ferroptosis, while its roles in regulating the fate and function of key immune cells remain less explored, including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), dendritic cells (DCs), T cells, and natural killer (NK) cells. Here, we review recent advances in nanomaterial-enabled ferroptosis regulation that enable coordinated modulation across tumor and immune compartments. We emphasize the coordinated roles of lipid metabolic reprogramming and iron homeostasis in establishing cell-type-specific susceptibility to ferroptosis, thereby contributing to heterogeneous immune responses within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Drawing on recent evidence of the context-dependent effects of nanomaterial-mediated ferroptosis on immune responses, we critically discuss material design strategies that enable cell-selective targeting and spatiotemporal control, aiming to promoting ferroptosis in tumor and immunosuppressive cells while protecting antitumor immune cells. Collectively, this review establishes a mechanistic framework connecting immune-cell ferroptosis with nanomedicine design and highlights key directions for developing more precise and durable ferroptosis-based cancer immunotherapies.

articles.titulo: Short-Term Climate Variability and Its Association with Dengue Transmission in the Southern United States
articles.autores: Bowles T, Deshpande G, … Oni T (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue fever has re-emerged in parts of the Southern United States (U.S.), raising concerns about how short-term climate variability may influence transmission risk. This ecological study evaluates whether changes in mean annual temperature and total annual precipitation between 2020 and 2024 were associated with shifts in dengue incidence across seven Southern U.S. states. Dengue case data were obtained from CDC ArboNET, and climate data from NOAA monitoring systems. Incidence rates were standardized using U.S. Census population estimates, and associations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation and longitudinal mixed-effects models. All study states experienced increases in mean annual temperature over the five-year period, while precipitation patterns varied. Dengue incidence rose across all states, with Florida showing the most substantial increase. Moderate correlations were observed between temperature change and dengue incidence (rs = 0.54) and between precipitation change and dengue incidence (rs = 0.71), though neither reached statistical significance. Longitudinal mixed-effects models identified a statistically significant positive association between temperature and both cumulative incidence and locally acquired incidence. These findings suggest that modest short-term climate shifts may be associated with variations in dengue dynamics in the Southern U.S., underscoring the need for expanded surveillance and longer-term analyses to better characterize these emerging vector-borne disease risks.

articles.titulo: A genomic toolkit for surveillance and elimination of the principal malaria vectors in Southeast Asia
articles.autores: Dennis TPW, Vantaux A, … St Laurent B (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original: While substantial progress has been made toward malaria elimination in Southeast Asia, major challenges remain. The principal mosquito vectors, Anopheles dirus and Anopheles minimus, inhabit diverse ecological niches and exhibit a wide range of behavioural and physiological insecticide resistance phenotypes, complicating vector control efforts. In Africa, genomic surveillance has transformed our understanding of vector evolution and resistance, supported by open-access tools and data. Comparable resources for Southeast Asian vectors remain limited. Here, we release Adir1.0, a curated, analysis-ready catalog of 540 An. dirus whole-genome sequences, accessible for interactive cloud-based analysis via the malariagen-data-python application programming interface (API). Alongside, we provide an updated Amin1.0 API to enhance functionality and usability, enabling integrated analyses across historical and new datasets. We demonstrate these resources by performing the first exploratory population genomic analysis of An. dirus from Bangladesh, Thailand, and Cambodia, revealing population structure, candidate regions of physiological resistance, and genomic structural variation. Together, these resources provide a foundation for genomic surveillance studies to inform vector control and malaria elimination strategies in Southeast Asia.

articles.titulo: Expanding Kelch13 Artemisinin Resistance Markers Are Associated with Higher Malaria Incidence in Uganda
articles.autores: van Wyk S, Gwasupika J, … Barnes KI (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Artemisinin partial resistance (ART-R)-associated Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 mutations are expanding across Africa. However, their population-level consequences remain poorly understood, particularly in settings of moderate-to-high malaria transmission. We investigated associations between Kelch13 and partner drug mutation prevalence and monthly confirmed malaria incidence across 16 Ugandan districts from 2017 to 2022, using integrated molecular, epidemiological, climatic, malaria-control, and antimalarial resistance data and negative binomial regression. Combined prevalence of WHO-validated and candidate Kelch13 mutations increased over the study period. Each 10-percentage-point increase in Kelch13 prevalence was associated with a 13.1% higher incidence after multivariable adjustment (aIRR, 1.131; 95% CI, 1.090-1.174). Furthermore, each 10-percentage-point increase in pfcrt K76T prevalence was associated with a 24.2% higher malaria incidence. As expected, ITN distribution ≥ 80%, IRS coverage ≥ 90%, and higher altitude were associated with lower incidence, whereas temperatures of 25-30 °C, relative humidity of 60-80%, and higher precipitation were associated with higher incidence. The persistence of these associations after adjustment suggests that expanding ART-R-associated parasite populations are independently associated with malaria incidence. The relationship may be bidirectional. These findings support interpreting ART-R within its ecological and intervention context and integrating molecular, epidemiological, and malaria-control surveillance to safeguard antimalarial efficacy.

articles.titulo: Development of a Calreticulin-Based Endogenous Control for Use in Culex restuans RT-qPCR Assays in Massachusetts
articles.autores: Stamborski N, Rich CM, … Rich SM (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hematophagous arthropods and associated pathogens are becoming more prevalent globally. With limited treatment options, prevention is the top priority to reduce disease. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) has emerged as a standard detection method for many laboratories, but it has several drawbacks. Degraded sample quality, failed RNA preparations, and the presence of reaction inhibitors can lead to false negative results, introducing the need for a positive control. Existing control methods rely on adding exogenous nucleotides during amplification reactions, which may not reflect the quality of the sample. Incorporating assays to detect endogenous mosquito mRNA transcripts provides assurance that sample quality is sufficient for the downstream amplification of pathogen RNA. In the present study, we applied the Rapid Amplification of cDNA Ends (RACE) technique to obtain a full-length calreticulin cDNA sequence from the Culex restuans mosquito, collected in Massachusetts, USA. We then used the newly discovered cDNA sequence to design primers and probes spanning the first exon-exon junction of the calreticulin gene, which allowed for specific and accurate RNA transcript detection in an RT-qPCR assay. This assay detected the presence of calreticulin transcripts in extracted pools of mosquito RNA. This approach may be further developed to include other relevant mosquito species and, with extensive validation, may have potential for use as an endogenous control in arbovirus surveillance.

articles.titulo: Caffeine Prolongs Survivability and Significantly Modulates Cytokine Levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-18 and IL-10 in Plasmodium berghei ANKA-infected ICR Mice
articles.autores: Noriman AZ, Mohd Abdul Razak MR, … Hassan WRM (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Caffeine, a bioactive compound in Theobroma cacao, exhibits various pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory properties. Malaria is an inflammatory-related disease caused by Plasmodium spp. Severe infection of this disease can cause cerebral malaria, which is characterised by neuroinflammation. An in vitro study of caffeine suggested that it possesses anti-malarial properties. However, caffeine's potential in both anti-malarial and cytokine-modulating properties through in vivo have yet to be explored. This study investigated the anti-malarial and cytokine-modulating effects of caffeine in P. berghei ANKA-infected ICR mice. Anti-malarial activity of caffeine at 5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg body weight was given via intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection, and the chemosuppressive percentage (percentage of parasitaemia inhibition) was calculated based on Peter and Robinsons's study in 1992. In addition, the cytokine-modulating effect was determined using the ELISA method. Chemosuppressive test at 5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg b.w. of caffeine in the P. berghei ANKA-infected ICR mice exhibited 64.18 ± 9.17, 39.93 ± 5.63 and 21.86 ± 5.57%, respectively. Notably, the lowest concentration, 5 mg/kg b.w. of caffeine was able to prolong significantly (p < 0.05) the survivability of malaria-infected ICR mice for 17 days as compared to infected mice (12 days). This effective dose of caffeine revealed a significant reduction in cytokine levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-18 and IL-10 by 1.08-, 1.12-, 1.12- and 1.15-folds, respectively, as compared to malaria-infected mice. Collectively, 5 mg/kg b.w. of caffeine exhibited good chemosuppressive, modulated levels of inflammatory cytokines and prolonged survivability of P. berghei ANKA-infected ICR mice. Hence, caffeine can be a plausible candidate for the development of anti-malarial therapeutic drugs.

articles.titulo: Genome-Wide Characterization of ABCG Transporters Involved in Anthranilic Diamide Insecticide Tolerance in Spodoptera exigua (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
articles.autores: You C, Duan R, … Ji X (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The beet armyworm, Spodoptera exigua (Hübner), has developed pronounced resistance to nearly all major classes of insecticides, posing a persistent threat to global agricultural productivity. The ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters, particularly members of the G subfamily, mediate the transmembrane efflux of xenobiotics and are increasingly implicated in insecticide tolerance, but the functional roles of the ABCG subfamily in S. exigua remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified 17 SeABCG genes and systematically characterized their spatiotemporal expression patterns and insecticide-responsive profiles. Most SeABCGs were broadly expressed across developmental stages and tissues, although with notable quantitative variation. Among the insecticide-responsive candidates, SeABCG3, SeABCG8, and SeABCG10 were significantly upregulated after treatment with cyantraniliprole and chlorantraniliprole and were highly expressed in detoxification tissues; these three genes were therefore selected for functional studies. Functional characterization through RNAi confirmed that SeABCG3, SeABCG8, and SeABCG10 contribute to tolerance against cyantraniliprole and chlorantraniliprole. Furthermore, molecular docking results revealed that SeABCG3, SeABCG8, and SeABCG10 exhibit potential binding affinity for both cyantraniliprole and chlorantraniliprole. These findings provide the first functional characterization of ABCG transporters in S. exigua and identify SeABCGs as crucial factors contributing to tolerance to anthranilic diamide insecticides.

articles.titulo: Visualizing Disintegration Pathways of Orally Disintegrating Tablets in Water and Thickened Media Using Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-Ray CT
articles.autores: Noji M, Fujita Y, … Harada T (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: Orally disintegrating tablets (ODTs) are often used for patients with dysphagia; however, their co-administration with "thickened water" in clinical settings can delay disintegration and potentially reduce therapeutic efficacy. While wicking networks formed by superdisintegrants facilitate rapid disintegration, we hypothesized that viscous polymers in thickened water cause "pore clogging" within these networks. Although conventional macroscopic evaluations have demonstrated this delay, direct visualization of the underlying microstructural changes remains unexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to elucidate the microstructural mechanisms of disintegration delay. Methods: Simplified model ODTs containing either a wicking-type (crospovidone [CP]) or a swelling-type (sodium starch glycolate [SSG]) disintegrant were prepared. Their microstructures and disintegration behaviors were evaluated by cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (Cryo-FIB-SEM), three-dimensional (3D) X-ray computed tomography (CT), and disintegration tests under simulated gastric conditions (pH 1.2). Results: Cryo-FIB-SEM revealed that CP-containing tablets formed numerous channel-like pores that promoted capillary action upon contact with water, whereas SSG-containing tablets formed larger, isolated macropores. X-ray CT analysis demonstrated distinct low-density regions associated with penetration-induced structural changes in both formulations. In CP-containing tablets, these regions extended throughout the channel network, whereas in SSG-containing tablets they were largely confined to the tablet surface. Consequently, the disintegration of CP-containing tablets in simulated gastric fluid was significantly delayed compared to that of SSG-containing tablets. Conclusions: The findings are consistent with a pore-clogging mechanism in which penetration of a viscous medium interferes with the liquid transport pathways responsible for rapid tablet disintegration. Combined Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-ray CT imaging provided direct morphological evidence of disintegrant-dependent structural responses in viscous media and offers a new framework for mechanistic investigation of tablet disintegration processes.

articles.titulo: Transient Suppression of Head CYP9Q3 Transcripts Is Associated with Thiacloprid and Tau-Fluvalinate Susceptibility in Apis mellifera
articles.autores: Katsavou E, Vlogiannitis S, … Vontas J (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Neonicotinoid toxicity to honeybees varies among active ingredients, with the insects being tolerant to thiacloprid but sensitive to imidacloprid. The selective toxicity has been hypothesized to be due to differences in metabolic detoxification by cytochrome P450s. In vitro experiments revealed that CYP9Q3 efficiently metabolises thiacloprid but not imidacloprid, consistent with the toxicity data. Honeybee tolerance to tau-fluvalinate, a pyrethroid acaricide used against Varroa destructor, has also been linked to P450-mediated detoxification. To address the role of CYP9Q3 in vivo in Apis mellifera, we used an RNA interference approach based on double-stranded RNA delivery through the median ocellus of adults to transiently suppress expression of CYP9Q3 in the head. Following confirmation of CYP9Q3 suppression by qPCR, fixed-dose topical bioassays were conducted with the neonicotinoids imidacloprid and thiacloprid and the pyrethroid tau-fluvalinate. Suppression of CYP9Q3 was associated with increased mortality following exposure to thiacloprid and tau-fluvalinate, whereas no increase was observed with imidacloprid. These findings provide in vivo functional evidence supporting the role of CYP9Q3 in honeybee tolerance to thiacloprid and tau-fluvalinate. The RNAi approach offers a valuable tool for investigating the functions of cytochrome P450 enzymes and other genes expressed in the honey bee head that are involved in insecticide susceptibility.
